````text
/**
 * Everything the dashboard renders, in one request: agent settings, LinkedIn
 * connection health, the approval queue, recent history, the rejection log,
 * LLM budget, and any ambiguous sends awaiting a human.
 */
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getAccountStatus } from "../../../lib/accounts";

import { getRequestAgent } from "../../../lib/request-agent";
import { ALL_CATEGORY_IDS, CATEGORIES } from "../../../lib/categories";
import { hasEncryptionKey } from "../../../lib/crypto";
import { query } from "../../../lib/db";
import {
  LINKEDIN_DAILY_REQUESTS,
  MANUAL_DAILY_CAP,
  MAX_AUTO_CAP,
  liveModeEnabled,
  listAmbiguousSends,
  sendsToday,
} from "../../../lib/distribute";
import { POST_COLUMNS, serializePost, type PostRow } from "../../../lib/post-view";
import { getTodayCalls } from "../../../lib/llm";
import { memoryDegraded } from "../../../lib/memory";
import { describeDays, formatInZone, localClock } from "../../../lib/schedule";
import {
  ensureSlotsMigrated,
  listSlots,
  MAX_LEAD_MINUTES,
  MAX_SLOTS,
  MIN_LEAD_MINUTES,
  MISSED_AFTER_MINUTES,
  schedulerHealth,
  slotTimeline,
  watchdogHealth,
} from "../../../lib/slots";
import { MAX_HASHTAGS, PRESETS } from "../../../lib/style";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

export async function GET() {
  try {
    const agent = await getRequestAgent();
    if (!agent) {
      return NextResponse.json({
        initialized: false,
        config: { liveMode: liveModeEnabled(), encryptionKey: hasEncryptionKey() },
      });
    }

    const [
      slots,
      account,
      posts,
      rejections,
      schedule,
      llm,
      ambiguous,
      sent,
      timeline,
      scheduler,
      watchdog,
    ] = await Promise.all([
      // Migrating a pre-slots agent used to be AWAITED before this batch, which
      // cost a whole extra round trip on every single request to a database
      // that is not in the same country — for a check that has been a no-op
      // since the first time it ran. It needs the agent id and nothing else, so
      // it belongs in the fan-out.
      ensureSlotsMigrated(
        agent.agentId,
        agent.postTimeLocal,
        agent.timezone,
        agent.autoPublish,
      ).catch((err) => {
        console.warn("[status] slot migration skipped:", err);
        return [];
      }),
      getAccountStatus(agent.agentId),
      // Ordered by when it GOES OUT rather than when it was written: with
      // several drafts waiting at once, the one with the nearest deadline is
      // the one that needs reading. Unscheduled drafts sort last.
      // Queue and history in ONE round trip. Two queries over the same table,
      // differing only in which statuses they want, cost two trips to a
      // database that is not in the same country; this fetches both windows at
      // once and splits them below.
      query<PostRow>(
        `(SELECT ${POST_COLUMNS} FROM posts
           WHERE agent_id = $1 AND status IN ('draft', 'approved', 'failed', 'unknown', 'missed')
           ORDER BY scheduled_for ASC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC)
         UNION ALL
         (SELECT ${POST_COLUMNS} FROM posts
           WHERE agent_id = $1 AND status = 'published'
           ORDER BY published_at DESC NULLS LAST, seq DESC LIMIT 20)`,
        [agent.agentId],
      ),
      query<{ title: string; url: string; reason: string; scores_json: Record<string, number>; created_at: Date }>(
        `SELECT title, url, reason, scores_json, created_at FROM rejections
          WHERE agent_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 15`,
        [agent.agentId],
      ),
      query<{ last_run_at: Date | null; next_run_at: Date | null; cycle_count: number }>(
        "SELECT last_run_at, next_run_at, cycle_count FROM scheduler_state WHERE agent_id = $1",
        [agent.agentId],
      ),
      getTodayCalls().catch(() => []),
      listAmbiguousSends(agent.agentId),
      sendsToday(agent.agentId, agent.timezone),
      slotTimeline(agent.agentId, 7),
      schedulerHealth(),
      watchdogHealth(),
    ]);

    // Split the single posts fetch back into its two windows.
    const queue = posts.filter((p) => p.status !== "published");
    const history = posts.filter((p) => p.status === "published");

    // The next run comes from the SLOTS, not from scheduler_state. That row's
    // next_run_at was derived from the legacy agents.post_time_local, which
    // slots replaced — so it reported a confident time for a schedule nothing
    // was reading, and the dashboard showed an hour that matched no slot the
    // user had ever set. It is now written as NULL and this reads the real one.
    const nextSlotRun = slots
      .filter((s) => s.enabled && s.nextRunAt)
      .map((s) => new Date(s.nextRunAt!))
      .sort((a, b) => a.getTime() - b.getTime())[0];
    const nextRunAt = nextSlotRun ?? null;

    const [review] = await query<{next_delivery_at:Date|null;config:unknown}>(`SELECT o.next_delivery_at,o.config FROM onboarding o JOIN agents a ON a.owner_id=o.user_id WHERE a.id=$1`,[agent.agentId]);
    const [dailyPost] = review ? await query<PostRow>(`SELECT ${POST_COLUMNS} FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND review_date=$2`,[agent.agentId,localClock(agent.timezone).date]) : [];
    return NextResponse.json({
      reviewDelivery: review ? {nextDeliveryAt:review.next_delivery_at?.toISOString()??null,config:review.config,post:dailyPost ? serializePost(dailyPost) : null,testMode:process.env.BYLINE_TEST_MODE==='true'} : null,
      initialized: true,
      agent,
      account,
      config: {
        liveMode: liveModeEnabled(),
        encryptionKey: hasEncryptionKey(),
        memoryDegraded: memoryDegraded(),
        maxAutoCap: MAX_AUTO_CAP,
        maxHashtags: MAX_HASHTAGS,
        presets: Object.entries(PRESETS).map(([id, p]) => ({
          id,
          label: p.label,
          blurb: p.blurb,
          style: p.style,
        })),
        // Served rather than hardcoded per client. Both the Flutter app and the
        // web dashboard used to carry their own id -> label maps, so adding a
        // category meant editing three files and an unlisted id rendered as a
        // raw slug like "compute-silicon" until someone noticed.
        categories: ALL_CATEGORY_IDS.map((id) => ({
          id,
          label: CATEGORIES[id].label,
          blurb: CATEGORIES[id].blurb,
          groupLabel: CATEGORIES[id].groupLabel,
        })),
      },
      // Two separate allowances, reported separately — conflating them is what
      // made a day of manual posting look like the agent was out of budget.
      budget: {
        autoUsed: sent.auto,
        autoCap: agent.autoPublishCap,
        manualUsed: sent.manual,
        manualCap: MANUAL_DAILY_CAP,
        linkedinDailyRequests: LINKEDIN_DAILY_REQUESTS,
      },
      schedule: {
        lastRunAt: schedule[0]?.last_run_at?.toISOString() ?? null,
        nextRunAt: nextRunAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
        nextRunLocal: nextRunAt ? formatInZone(nextRunAt, agent.timezone) : null,
        cycleCount: schedule[0]?.cycle_count ?? 0,
      },
      // The timetable, and what each slot actually did over the last week —
      // including the days it stayed silent, which is what stops a deliberate
      // silence from looking like a broken cron.
      slots: slots.map((s) => ({
        ...s,
        daysLabel: describeDays(s.daysMask),
        nextRunLocal: s.nextRunAt ? formatInZone(new Date(s.nextRunAt), agent.timezone) : null,
      })),
      timeline,
      // Whether the cron is alive at all. Without this, a stopped scheduler and
      // a day when nothing cleared the bar look identical from the app.
      scheduler,
      // And whether the thing that watches the cron is alive. It runs on GitHub
      // Actions, which disables scheduled workflows in a repository with no
      // commits for 60 days — so the safety net can be switched off by a quiet
      // couple of months with nothing anywhere saying so. A stale timestamp
      // here is the only visible symptom.
      watchdog,
      slotLimits: {
        maxSlots: MAX_SLOTS,
        minLeadMinutes: MIN_LEAD_MINUTES,
        maxLeadMinutes: MAX_LEAD_MINUTES,
        missedAfterMinutes: MISSED_AFTER_MINUTES,
      },
      queue: queue.map(serializePost),
      history: history.map(serializePost),
      rejections: rejections.map((r) => ({
        title: r.title,
        url: r.url,
        reason: r.reason,
        scores: r.scores_json,
        createdAt: r.created_at.toISOString(),
      })),
      llm,
      ambiguous,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("[status] failed:", err);
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: "status_failed", detail: String((err as Error)?.message ?? err).slice(0, 200) },
      { status: 500 },
    );
  }
}

````

## Source: app/api/style/preview/route.ts

````text
/**
 * Style preview: run a candidate voice config over real material and return
 * the result, WITHOUT saving anything.
 *
 * The controls in the settings panel are abstract — "structure: mixed",
 * "emoji: sparing" — and nobody can predict what those produce in combination.
 * Guessing, saving, then waiting until tomorrow's cycle to find out is a
 * terrible loop, so this closes it: pick settings, press preview, read the
 * post, adjust.
 *
 * It rewrites the author's most recent post rather than inventing a story,
 * because the interesting question is "what would MY posts look like in this
 * voice", not "can the model write something". Uses a reviewed setup sample or
 * an author-supplied example when the archive is empty.
 *
 * Costs one LLM call, so it is button-triggered and never runs on keystroke.
 */
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getPersona, voiceReferencesFor } from "../../../../lib/agents";
import { getRequestAgent } from "../../../../lib/request-agent";
import { query } from "../../../../lib/db";
import { assemblePost, checkLength, hookOf } from "../../../../lib/format";
import { parseStyle } from "../../../../lib/style";
import { polishCustomPost } from "../../../../lib/writer";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
// polishCustomPost, plus a possible repair call.
export const maxDuration = 120;

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const agent = await getRequestAgent();
  if (!agent) return NextResponse.json({ error: "not_initialized" }, { status: 400 });

  const [persona, voice] = await Promise.all([
    getPersona(agent.agentId),
    voiceReferencesFor(agent),
  ]);
  if (!persona) return NextResponse.json({ error: "persona_not_ready" }, { status: 409 });

  let body: { style?: unknown; text?: string };
  try {
    body = (await request.json()) as typeof body;
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "bad_request" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  if (!body || typeof body !== 'object' || Array.isArray(body)) return NextResponse.json({error:'Check your preview settings.'},{status:400});

  // Merge the candidate over the SAVED style, matching how PATCH /api/settings
  // applies a patch — otherwise the preview shows a different voice than the
  // one you would actually get by saving.
  const style = parseStyle({
    ...agent.style,
    ...(body.style && typeof body.style === "object" && !Array.isArray(body.style) ? body.style : {}),
  });

  let source = typeof body.text === "string" ? body.text.trim() : "";
  let sourceLabel = "your draft";
  if (!source) {
    const recent = await query<{ text: string; id: string }>(
      `SELECT text, id FROM posts WHERE agent_id = $1 ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1`,
      [agent.agentId],
    );
    if (recent[0]) {
      source = recent[0].text;
      sourceLabel = 'your most recent post';
    } else {
      const [setup]=await query<{text:string}>(`SELECT o.preview->>'text' AS text FROM onboarding o JOIN agents a ON a.owner_id=o.user_id WHERE a.id=$1 AND o.accepted_revision=o.preview_revision AND o.preview IS NOT NULL`,[agent.agentId]);
      source = setup?.text || voice.samples[0]?.text || '';
      sourceLabel = setup?.text ? 'your reviewed setup sample' : 'your writing sample';
      if (!source) return NextResponse.json({error:'preview_source_required',detail:'Add a writing sample or save a draft to preview your voice.'},{status:409});
    }
  }

  // The preview has to run the SAME prompt the real writer runs, samples and
  // all. A preview that consults only the style toggles would look convincing
  // and still not be what saving this voice actually produces.
  const result = await polishCustomPost(persona, source, style, voice);
  if (!result.ok) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "preview_failed", detail: result.reason }, { status: 502 });
  }

  // Show it exactly as LinkedIn would receive it, hashtags and all — the
  // hashtag count is one of the settings being previewed.
  const sampleTags = (result.data.hashtags ?? []).slice(0, style.hashtagCount);
  const assembled = assemblePost({
    body: result.data.text,
    hashtags: sampleTags,
    maxHashtags: style.hashtagCount,
  });

  return NextResponse.json({
    ok: true,
    sourceLabel,
    before: source,
    after: assembled,
    hook: hookOf(assembled),
    length: checkLength(assembled),
    style,
    servedBy: result.data.servedBy,
  });
}
````

## Source: app/api/watchdog/route.ts

````text
/**
 * The outside observer. Checks the standing health properties and pushes if
 * one of them has gone bad.
 *
 * This is separate from the cron tick for one structural reason: **a dead
 * scheduler cannot report its own death.** If the tick is what notices a
 * stalled tick, then the exact failure that most needs an alert — the cron
 * stopping — is the one that produces silence. So this endpoint is driven by a
 * DIFFERENT machine on a different schedule (a GitHub Action, see
 * .github/workflows/watchdog.yml) and the two can only fail together if both
 * providers are down at once.
 *
 * Authenticated by the same CRON_SECRET header as the tick, and answers 404 on
 * a mismatch so it does not advertise that it exists.
 *
 * Everything it can report is throttled in lib/push.ts. A stalled scheduler is
 * still stalled thirty minutes later, and an alert that repeats every half hour
 * is an alert that gets muted — after which it may as well not exist.
 */
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getAccountStatus } from "../../../lib/accounts";
import { getPrimaryAgent } from "../../../lib/agents";
import { checkCredentials, notify, pushConfigured } from "../../../lib/push";
import { deadFeeds } from "../../../lib/feedhealth";
import { apiVersionAge } from "../../../lib/linkedin";
import { recordWatchdog, schedulerHealth } from "../../../lib/slots";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

/** Warn this far ahead of the 60-day LinkedIn token expiry. */
const TOKEN_WARNING_DAYS = 7;

function authorized(request: Request): boolean {
  const expected = process.env.CRON_SECRET;
  if (!expected) return false;
  const provided = request.headers.get("x-cron-secret") ?? "";
  if (provided.length !== expected.length) return false;
  let diff = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < expected.length; i++) diff |= provided.charCodeAt(i) ^ expected.charCodeAt(i);
  return diff === 0;
}

export async function GET(request: Request) {
  if (!authorized(request)) return new NextResponse("Not Found", { status: 404 });

  // ?deep=1 additionally proves the push credentials WORK rather than merely
  // exist, by exchanging a real access token and sending nothing. Off by
  // default: the scheduled run happens every half hour and does not need to
  // talk to Google to answer "is the scheduler alive".
  const params = new URL(request.url).searchParams;

  if (params.get("deep") === "1") {
    const credentials = await checkCredentials();
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: credentials.ok, deep: true, push: credentials });
  }

  // ?test=1 sends a real notification to every registered device. The only way
  // to prove the last link — this server, to Google, to a specific handset —
  // and the first genuine alert is the wrong moment to find out it was never
  // connected. Reports the device count, so "nothing arrived" can be told apart
  // from "nothing was sent because no device has ever registered".
  if (params.get("test") === "1") {
    const target = await getPrimaryAgent();
    if (!target) return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, reason: "not_initialized" });
    const delivered = await notify(target.agentId, { kind: "test" });
    return NextResponse.json({
      ok: delivered > 0,
      test: true,
      delivered,
      detail:
        delivered > 0
          ? `sent to ${delivered} device(s)`
          : "no device accepted it — either none has registered, or the credentials are wrong (try deep=1)",
    });
  }

  // Before the checks, and regardless of what they find. This records that the
  // WATCHDOG ran — the one thing nothing else in the system can observe.
  await recordWatchdog();

  const agent = await getPrimaryAgent();
  if (!agent) return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, checked: false, reason: "not_initialized" });

  const [health, account, dead] = await Promise.all([
    schedulerHealth(),
    getAccountStatus(agent.agentId),
    deadFeeds(),
  ]);

  const alerts: string[] = [];

  if (!health.healthy) {
    alerts.push("scheduler_stalled");
    await notify(agent.agentId, {
      kind: "scheduler_stalled",
      // Null means it has never ticked at all, which on a fresh deployment is
      // normal for a few minutes and after that is the same problem.
      minutes: health.minutesSince ?? health.staleAfterMinutes,
    });
  }

  // Reported while there is still time to act. Once needsReauth is true nothing
  // can publish at all, so the useful alert is the one before that.
  if (account.connected && (account.needsReauth || (account.daysRemaining ?? 99) <= TOKEN_WARNING_DAYS)) {
    alerts.push("token_expiring");
    await notify(agent.agentId, { kind: "token_expiring", days: account.daysRemaining ?? 0 });
  }

  // Feeds die quietly — one warning per cycle in a log nobody reads — and the
  // symptom is a reading list that halves over two years with no alert.
  if (dead.length > 0) {
    alerts.push("feed_dead");
    await notify(agent.agentId, { kind: "feed_dead", names: dead.map((f) => f.name) });
  }

  // The one guaranteed breakage with no natural warning: the pinned API version
  // is retired on LinkedIn's schedule, and without this the first sign is a
  // post that failed to send.
  const version = apiVersionAge();
  if (version?.stale) {
    alerts.push("api_version_stale");
    await notify(agent.agentId, {
      kind: "api_version_stale",
      version: version.version,
      months: version.months,
    });
  }

  return NextResponse.json({
    ok: true,
    checked: true,
    pushConfigured: pushConfigured(),
    deadFeeds: dead.map((f) => f.name),
    apiVersion: version ? { version: version.version, months: version.months } : null,
    scheduler: { healthy: health.healthy, minutesSince: health.minutesSince },
    linkedin: { connected: account.connected, daysRemaining: account.daysRemaining ?? null },
    alerts,
  });
}

````

## Source: app/globals.css

````text
/*
 * Ink & Filament — the web half of the design system. See /DESIGN.md.
 *
 * The same tokens the Flutter app carries in lib/theme.dart, so the two
 * surfaces are one product rather than two that happen to share an API. Every
 * value below is referenced, never inlined at a call site.
 *
 * THE LAYOUT RULE, which is what changed:
 *
 *     Copy sits on the page. A box means an object you act on.
 *
 * The stylesheet this replaces gave every region an identical bordered panel,
 * so nothing had hierarchy and the post — the one thing on screen worth
 * reading — was a third of the box it sat in, competing with badges, five score
 * meters and a rationale. Sections are separated by rhythm and a ruled heading
 * now; a border means a draft, a slot, or a sheet.
 */

@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Barlow+Condensed:wght@500;600;700&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;600;700&family=IBM+Plex+Sans:wght@400;500;600&display=swap");

:root {
  /* --- ground. Warm-neutral ink, not blue-black: blue-black is what every
     dark dashboard reaches for, and it turns the accents into status LEDs. */
  --ink: #0e0d0b;
  --ink-2: #161512;
  --ink-3: #1e1c18;
  --rule: #2a2721;
  --rule-strong: #3b372f;

  /* --- ink on the page. Every value clears 4.5:1 on --ink. */
  --paper: #f2efe9; /* 16.9:1 */
  --paper-dim: #b3ada2; /* 8.7:1 */
  --paper-faint: #8a857b; /* 5.3:1 — replaces #6b7484, which failed AA at 12px */

  /* --- the three accents. Colour answers ONE question: which clock is this on?
     A slot that judged its candidates and chose silence gets no colour at all;
     correct behaviour must never look like an alarm. */
  --filament: #ff8a3d; /* on the desk — still yours to change */
  --daylight: #45c8dc; /* out in the world — published, cleared, healthy */
  --flare: #ff4d5e; /* broken — missed, failed, expired */

  --filament-wash: #2a1b0f;
  --daylight-wash: #0e2a30;
  --flare-wash: #2c1214;
  --on-filament: #1a0e04;

  /* --- rhythm. Nothing between these values. */
  --s1: 0.25rem;
  --s2: 0.5rem;
  --s3: 0.75rem;
  --s4: 1rem;
  --s5: 1.5rem;
  --s6: 2rem;
  --s7: 3rem;

  /* Tighter than the old 6/10/16: a large radius reads consumer, a small one
     reads instrument. */
  --radius-sm: 4px;
  --radius: 8px;
  --radius-lg: 14px;

  /* Three faces, three jobs, no overlap. Condensed for structure because a
     column is narrow and a newsroom deck always was; the sans for anything read
     as language; the mono for anything that is a figure. */
  --cond: "Barlow Condensed", "Archivo Narrow", "Roboto Condensed", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
  --sans: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  --mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Code", Consolas, monospace;

  --fs-micro: 0.75rem;
  --fs-sm: 0.8125rem;
  --fs-base: 0.9375rem;
  --fs-copy: 1.0625rem; /* the post. The most readable thing on screen. */
  --fs-lg: 1.375rem;
  --fs-xl: 2rem;
  --fs-clock: 2.75rem;

  --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 50%), 0 12px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 28%);
  --max-width: 1220px;
  --measure: 68ch; /* the reading measure. Copy never runs wider. */
}

* {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

html,
body {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}

body {
  background: var(--ink);
  color: var(--paper);
  font-family: var(--sans);
  font-size: var(--fs-base);
  line-height: 1.55;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}

/* Numbers that sit in columns, or change in place, must not jitter. A countdown
   whose digits change width reflows while you read it. */
.tabular,
.counter,
.meter + span {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}

a {
  color: var(--daylight);
  text-decoration: none;
}
a:hover {
  text-decoration: underline;
}

:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--filament);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ layout */

.shell {
  max-width: var(--max-width);
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: var(--s6) var(--s4) var(--s7);
}

/* The masthead: who this is, what state it is in. A rule under it rather than a
   box around it. */
.masthead {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: flex-end;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--s4);
  padding-bottom: var(--s4);
  margin-bottom: var(--s5);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
}

.masthead h1 {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: var(--cond);
  font-size: var(--fs-xl);
  font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  line-height: 1.05;
}

.masthead .sub {
  margin: var(--s1) 0 0;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

/* Desk on the left, the things you set once on the right. The desk is wider
   because reading the draft carefully IS the job. */
.columns {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.6fr) minmax(0, 1fr);
  gap: var(--s6);
  align-items: start;
}

@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .columns {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
    gap: var(--s5);
  }
}

.stack {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--s6);
  min-width: 0;
}

.sidebar {
  gap: var(--s6);
}

.row {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s2);
}

.spread {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--s3);
}

.spacer {
  flex: 1;
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- sections */

/*
 * `.panel` is no longer a box. It is a SECTION: a ruled heading, then content
 * on the page ground. Kept under the old name so the markup did not have to be
 * rewritten to get the new hierarchy.
 */
.panel {
  display: block;
  min-width: 0;
}

.panel > h2,
.panel > h3,
.panel-head {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s3);
  margin: 0 0 var(--s3);
  font-family: var(--cond);
  font-size: 0.8125rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.09em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

/* The rule runs from the label to the edge — that is what separates a section
   without boxing it. */
.panel > h2::after,
.panel > h3::after,
.panel-head::after {
  content: "";
  flex: 1;
  height: 1px;
  background: var(--rule);
}

.panel > p,
.panel > .hint {
  max-width: var(--measure);
}

.hint {
  margin: var(--s2) 0 0;
  font-size: var(--fs-micro);
  line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

.sub {
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ marks */

/*
 * A state word. Colour marks the ABNORMAL case only: `running`, `live` and
 * `approval mode` are the ordinary state of a healthy agent, and three chips
 * lit in three colours on an ordinary day is three colours saying nothing.
 */
.badge {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s1);
  padding: 3px var(--s2) 4px;
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--ink-3);
  font-family: var(--cond);
  font-size: 0.71875rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.09em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--paper-faint);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.badge.good,
.badge.live {
  background: var(--daylight-wash);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--daylight) 50%, transparent);
  color: var(--daylight);
}

.badge.warn {
  background: var(--filament-wash);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--filament) 50%, transparent);
  color: var(--filament);
}

.badge.bad {
  background: var(--flare-wash);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--flare) 50%, transparent);
  color: var(--flare);
}

.dot {
  width: 6px;
  height: 6px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: currentcolor;
}

/* A condition of the page, not a card: a bar on the left rather than a border
   all the way round, so it does not read as one more thing to act on. */
.notice {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: var(--s3);
  padding: var(--s3);
  margin-bottom: var(--s3);
  border-left: 2px solid var(--filament);
  border-radius: 0 var(--radius-sm) var(--radius-sm) 0;
  background: var(--filament-wash);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--filament);
}

.notice.bad {
  border-left-color: var(--flare);
  background: var(--flare-wash);
  color: var(--flare);
}

.notice.good {
  border-left-color: var(--daylight);
  background: var(--daylight-wash);
  color: var(--daylight);
}

.notice p {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

.notice strong {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 2px;
  color: inherit;
  font-weight: 600;
}

.error-text {
  margin: var(--s2) 0 0;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--flare);
}

.empty {
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--s6) 0;
  max-width: var(--measure);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------- post */

/*
 * The one place the layout rule bends: a draft IS a box, because it is a thing
 * you act on. Inside it the copy sits on the surface with nothing around it.
 */
.post {
  padding: var(--s4);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--ink-2);
}

.post + .post {
  margin-top: var(--s3);
}

/* The slug line: where this came from and what state it is in, above a
   hairline, the way a slug line sits above copy. */
.post-meta {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s2);
  padding-bottom: var(--s3);
  margin-bottom: var(--s4);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-micro);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

.post-text {
  margin: 0;
  max-width: var(--measure);
  font-size: var(--fs-copy);
  line-height: 1.62;
  color: var(--paper);
  white-space: pre-wrap;
}

.post-text + .post-text {
  margin-top: 0;
}

/* Not hidden — the text above the fold is the whole post as far as most readers
   are concerned, so what follows is simply quieter. */
.below-fold {
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

/*
 * THE SIGNATURE. LinkedIn cuts a post at 210 characters and hides the rest
 * behind "see more"; drawing that boundary is the single most useful thing this
 * screen does that LinkedIn's own composer does not. So it is drawn as a cut —
 * dashed, in the warm accent, because the fold is a thing you can still act on
 * — with the count of what is hidden set in the gutter.
 */
.fold {
  position: relative;
  height: 1px;
  /* Chrome's UA stylesheet gives `hr` overflow:hidden, which clipped the label
     below to the rule's own 1px box and rendered it as a smear. */
  overflow: visible;
  margin: var(--s4) 0;
  border: 0;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(
    to right,
    color-mix(in srgb, var(--filament) 42%, transparent) 0 4px,
    transparent 4px 8px
  );
}

/* The label comes from the markup so it can carry the count of what is hidden;
   a static ::before could only ever say "see more". */
.fold::before {
  content: attr(data-below);
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  left: 0;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
  padding-right: var(--s3);
  background: var(--ink-2);
  line-height: 1;
  white-space: nowrap;
  font-family: var(--cond);
  font-size: 0.71875rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.09em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--filament);
}

.rationale {
  margin: var(--s4) 0 0;
  padding-left: var(--s3);
  max-width: var(--measure);
  border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

/* The judge's criteria. Thin, quiet, and never competing with the copy. */
.scores {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--s2);
  margin-top: var(--s3);
  max-width: 30rem;
}

.judgement {
  margin-top: var(--s4);
  padding-top: var(--s4);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
}

.judgement > summary {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s2);
  min-height: 32px;
  cursor: pointer;
  list-style: none;
  font-family: var(--cond);
  font-size: 0.71875rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.09em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

.judgement > summary::-webkit-details-marker {
  display: none;
}

.judgement > summary::before {
  content: "▸";
  font-family: var(--sans);
  transition: transform 180ms ease;
}

.judgement[open] > summary::before {
  transform: rotate(90deg);
}

.judgement > summary .total {
  margin-left: auto;
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  letter-spacing: 0;
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

.judgement .rationale {
  margin-top: var(--s3);
}

.score {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 8rem 1fr 2rem;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s3);
  font-size: var(--fs-micro);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

.meter {
  display: block;
  height: 3px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--ink-3);
  overflow: hidden;
}

.meter > i {
  display: block;
  height: 100%;
  background: var(--daylight);
}

.post-actions {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s2);
  padding-top: var(--s4);
  margin-top: var(--s4);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- controls */

button {
  min-height: 40px;
  padding: 0 var(--s4);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--paper);
  font-family: var(--sans);
  font-size: var(--fs-base);
  font-weight: 500;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease, color 180ms ease;
}

button:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--ink-3);
  border-color: var(--paper-faint);
}

button:disabled {
  color: var(--paper-faint);
  border-color: var(--rule);
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

button.primary {
  background: var(--filament);
  border-color: var(--filament);
  color: var(--on-filament);
  font-weight: 600;
}

button.primary:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--filament) 88%, white);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--filament) 88%, white);
}

button.primary:disabled {
  background: var(--ink-3);
  border-color: var(--rule);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

button.danger {
  color: var(--flare);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--flare) 45%, transparent);
}

button.danger:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--flare-wash);
  border-color: var(--flare);
}

button.ghost {
  border-color: transparent;
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

button.ghost:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--ink-3);
  border-color: var(--rule);
  color: var(--paper);
}

input,
select,
textarea {
  width: 100%;
  padding: var(--s3);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--ink-3);
  color: var(--paper);
  font-family: var(--sans);
  font-size: var(--fs-base);
  line-height: 1.5;
}

input::placeholder,
textarea::placeholder {
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

textarea {
  min-height: 11rem;
  resize: vertical;
  font-size: var(--fs-copy);
  line-height: 1.62;
}

textarea.compact {
  min-height: 5.5rem;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  line-height: 1.5;
}

input:focus-visible,
select:focus-visible,
textarea:focus-visible {
  outline: none;
  border-color: var(--filament);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--filament);
}

label.field {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: var(--s4);
  min-width: 0;
}

label.field > span {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: var(--s2);
  font-family: var(--cond);
  font-size: 0.71875rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.09em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

/* A row of choices, visible without opening a menu — on the voice editor,
   comparing them IS the task. */
.chips {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: var(--s2);
}

.chip {
  min-height: 40px;
  padding: 0 var(--s4);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--ink-2);
  color: var(--paper-dim);
  font-family: var(--sans);
  font-size: var(--fs-base);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease, color 180ms ease;
}

.chip:hover {
  border-color: var(--paper-faint);
  color: var(--paper);
}

.chip[data-on="true"],
.chip[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background: var(--filament-wash);
  border-color: var(--filament);
  color: var(--paper);
  font-weight: 600;
}

/* Title, explanation, switch. */
.toggle {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--s4);
  padding: var(--s3) 0;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
}

.toggle .label {
  min-width: 0;
}

.toggle .label strong {
  display: block;
  font-size: var(--fs-base);
  font-weight: 500;
  color: var(--paper);
}

.toggle .label span {
  display: block;
  margin-top: 2px;
  font-size: var(--fs-micro);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

.switch {
  flex: none;
  width: 44px;
  min-height: 26px;
  height: 26px;
  padding: 0;
  border-radius: 999px;
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  background: var(--ink-3);
  position: relative;
  transition: background-color 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease;
}

.switch::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 3px;
  left: 3px;
  width: 18px;
  height: 18px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--paper-faint);
  transition: transform 180ms ease, background-color 180ms ease;
}

.switch[data-on="true"] {
  background: var(--filament-wash);
  border-color: var(--filament);
}

.switch[data-on="true"]::after {
  transform: translateX(18px);
  background: var(--filament);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- compose */

.dropzone {
  padding: var(--s5);
  border: 1px dashed var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: transparent;
  text-align: center;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
  transition: border-color 180ms ease, background-color 180ms ease;
}

.dropzone[data-over="true"] {
  border-color: var(--filament);
  background: var(--filament-wash);
  color: var(--filament);
}

.thumbs {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: var(--s2);
  margin-top: var(--s3);
}

.thumb {
  position: relative;
  width: 84px;
  height: 84px;
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
}

.thumb img {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
  display: block;
}

.thumb button {
  position: absolute;
  top: 2px;
  right: 2px;
  min-height: 24px;
  height: 24px;
  padding: 0 var(--s2);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--ink);
  border-color: transparent;
  color: var(--flare);
  font-size: var(--fs-micro);
}

.preview {
  margin-top: var(--s4);
  padding: var(--s4);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--ink-2);
}

.counter {
  font-size: var(--fs-micro);
  color: var(--paper-faint);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ lists */

.list-compact {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--s2);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--paper-dim);
}

.list-compact li {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--s3);
  padding: var(--s2) 0;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
}

.list-compact li:last-child {
  border-bottom: 0;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------- gate and setup */

.gate,
.setup {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  min-height: 100dvh;
  padding: var(--s5);
}

.gate .panel,
.setup .panel,
.gate form,
.setup form {
  width: 100%;
  max-width: 26rem;
}

.setup form {
  max-width: 34rem;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- reduced motion */

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *,
  *::before,
  *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}

````

````text
import type { Metadata, Viewport } from "next";

import "./globals.css";

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "LinkedIn agent",
  description:
    "A daily editorial agent for music tech, hardware and emerging tech — drafts, judges, and publishes to LinkedIn.",
  // Private control surface; keep it out of search results.
  robots: { index: false, follow: false },
};

export const viewport: Viewport = {
  width: "device-width",
  initialScale: 1,
  colorScheme: "dark",
};

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
````
