## Source: lib/breeth.ts

````text
/**
 * Breeth memory client — thin typed wrapper over https://api.thebreeth.com/v1.
 *
 * ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT:
 * Breeth is an ENHANCEMENT layer, never a hard dependency. Postgres is the
 * source of truth for posts, rejections, and scheduler state. If Breeth is
 * unreachable, quota-exceeded, or slow, the agent must keep publishing on
 * schedule using Postgres-only fallback memory. Nothing on a user-facing
 * request path may ever await a Breeth call. A dead memory service degrades
 * the quality of the agent's judgment, never its availability.
 *
 * Consequences encoded here:
 * - No function in this module ever throws across the module boundary; every
 *   call resolves to a discriminated BreethResult the caller must inspect.
 * - 8s AbortController timeout on every request.
 * - One retry with backoff on 500s and network errors only. 402
 *   (payment_required) and 429 (quota_exceeded) are hard stops: never
 *   retried, flip the module into degraded mode (see isDegraded()).
 * - POST /v1/episodes is NOT idempotent — a blind retry of a non-network
 *   failure would double-write, so only transport-level failures retry.
 */

const BASE_URL = "https://api.thebreeth.com/v1";
// Reads (search/health) stay tight; episode writes measured ~16.5s in the
// smoke test, so they get a longer leash. Episodes only ever run inside the
// background cycle (300s budget) — never on a user-facing request path.
const TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000;
const WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
const RETRY_BACKOFF_MS = 750;

export type BreethResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; reason: string };

export interface EpisodeWriteData {
  ok?: boolean;
  entities?: number;
  relationships?: number;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

export interface SearchEdge {
  edge_uuid: string;
  source_node: string;
  target_node: string;
  fact: string;
  name: string;
  intent_meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
  _tier?: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

// Flips true after a hard-stop error (402 payment_required / 429
// quota_exceeded) and stays true for the life of the process: once quota or
// billing is exhausted, further calls this billing period are pointless.
let degraded = false;

export function isDegraded(): boolean {
  return degraded;
}

const HARD_STOP_STATUSES = new Set([402, 429]);

async function request<T>(
  path: string,
  body: Record<string, unknown>,
  timeoutMs: number = TIMEOUT_MS,
): Promise<BreethResult<T>> {
  const key = process.env.BREETH_API_KEY;
  if (!key) return { ok: false, reason: "missing_api_key" };

  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= 1; attempt++) {
    if (attempt > 0) {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_BACKOFF_MS));
    }

    const controller = new AbortController();
    const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);

    try {
      const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: {
          Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`,
          "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
        signal: controller.signal,
      });

      if (res.ok) {
        return { ok: true, data: (await res.json()) as T };
      }

      let slug = `http_${res.status}`;
      try {
        const err = (await res.json()) as { error?: string };
        if (err.error) slug = err.error;
      } catch {
        // non-JSON error body; keep the http_<status> slug
      }

      if (HARD_STOP_STATUSES.has(res.status)) {
        degraded = true;
        console.error(`[breeth] hard stop ${res.status} ${slug} — degraded mode on, no retry`);
        return { ok: false, reason: slug };
      }

      if (res.status >= 500 && attempt === 0) {
        continue;
      }

      // 400/401/403 etc. — caller error or auth problem; retrying won't help.
      return { ok: false, reason: slug };
    } catch (err) {
      const reason =
        err instanceof Error && err.name === "AbortError" ? "timeout" : "network_error";
      if (attempt === 0) continue;
      return { ok: false, reason };
    } finally {
      clearTimeout(timer);
    }
  }

  return { ok: false, reason: "unreachable" };
}

/**
 * Write a prose memory. `extractIntent` is an explicit caller decision:
 * true for writes carrying an editorial decision, false for plain content.
 * NOT idempotent — calling twice with the same content creates two episodes.
 */
export async function writeEpisode(opts: {
  agentId: string;
  content: string;
  extractIntent: boolean;
}): Promise<BreethResult<EpisodeWriteData>> {
  return request<EpisodeWriteData>(
    "/episodes",
    {
      content: opts.content,
      group_id: `agent-${opts.agentId}`,
      extract_intent: opts.extractIntent,
    },
    WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS,
  );
}

/** Hybrid BM25 + vector + graph retrieval, scoped to the agent's namespace. */
export async function search(opts: {
  agentId: string;
  query: string;
  limit?: number;
}): Promise<BreethResult<SearchEdge[]>> {
  const result = await request<{ edges?: SearchEdge[] }>("/search", {
    query: opts.query,
    group_id: `agent-${opts.agentId}`,
    limit: opts.limit ?? 10,
  });
  if (!result.ok) return result;
  return { ok: true, data: result.data.edges ?? [] };
}

/**
 * Breeth documents no health endpoint, so this is the cheapest authenticated
 * round-trip available: a 1-edge search in a reserved namespace. Note it
 * counts against the monthly retrieval quota — call it sparingly.
 */
export async function healthCheck(): Promise<BreethResult<{ reachable: true; latencyMs: number }>> {
  const started = Date.now();
  const result = await request<unknown>("/search", {
    query: "healthcheck",
    group_id: "agent-healthcheck",
    limit: 1,
  });
  if (!result.ok) return result;
  return { ok: true, data: { reachable: true, latencyMs: Date.now() - started } };
}
````

````text
/**
 * The categories chosen at init. They do three jobs:
 *   1. select which discovery feeds are consulted,
 *   2. give the judge a category-fit criterion to score against,
 *   3. supply the hashtag vocabulary the writer draws from.
 *
 * A category is a standing editorial interest, not a keyword filter — the
 * judge decides what actually belongs, the same way it decides everything
 * else in this pipeline.
 */

/**
 * Adding a category is deliberately ADDITIVE. Existing ids never change meaning
 * enough to alter what an agent already watching them receives, and no feed is
 * ever moved from an old category to a new one — moving `arxiv-cs.SD` out of
 * music-tech-software to a new audio-dsp category would silently stop an agent
 * that never touched its settings from seeing DSP papers at all.
 *
 * That rule is why there is no separate "audio DSP" category despite the
 * overlap being real: it cannot be carved out of music-tech-software without
 * either changing what an existing agent receives, or fetching the same arXiv
 * feed twice per cycle.
 */
import { SUBJECT_GROUPS, subjectId } from './category-catalogue';

export type CategoryId = string;
type LegacyCategoryId =
  | "music-tech-software"
  | "music-tech-hardware"
  | "emerging-tech"
  | "ai-ml"
  | "dev-tooling"
  | "hardware-embedded"
  | "compute-silicon"
  | "marketing" | "hr" | "finance" | "healthcare" | "business";

export interface Category {
  id: CategoryId;
  label: string;
  /** Fed to the judge and writer: what genuinely belongs under this heading. */
  blurb: string;
  /** Lower-case prose fragment, joined into the agent's scope line. See describeCategories. */
  scope: string;
  /** Candidate hashtags. The writer picks at most two; more reads as reach-farming. */
  hashtags: string[];
  group?: string;
  groupLabel?: string;
  /** A targeted discovery query, never a generic parent feed. */
  query?: string;
}

const LEGACY_CATEGORIES: Record<LegacyCategoryId, Category> = {
"marketing": {"id": "marketing", "label": "Marketing", "scope": "marketing strategy and customer research", "blurb": "Evidence-backed developments in marketing strategy and customer research. Explain implications without inventing facts, personal experience, or giving individualized advice.", "hashtags": ["Marketing", "CustomerExperience", "ContentStrategy"]},
"hr": {"id": "hr", "label": "People & HR", "scope": "workplace culture and people management", "blurb": "Evidence-backed developments in workplace culture and people management. Explain implications without inventing facts, personal experience, or giving individualized advice.", "hashtags": ["HumanResources", "Leadership", "WorkplaceCulture"]},
"finance": {"id": "finance", "label": "Finance", "scope": "financial services and economic developments", "blurb": "Evidence-backed developments in financial services and economic developments. Explain implications without inventing facts, personal experience, or giving individualized advice.", "hashtags": ["Finance", "Economics", "Banking"]},
"healthcare": {"id": "healthcare", "label": "Healthcare", "scope": "healthcare systems and public health research", "blurb": "Evidence-backed developments in healthcare systems and public health research. Explain implications without inventing facts, personal experience, or giving individualized advice.", "hashtags": ["Healthcare", "PublicHealth", "HealthResearch"]},
"business": {"id": "business", "label": "Business", "scope": "business strategy and entrepreneurship", "blurb": "Evidence-backed developments in business strategy and entrepreneurship. Explain implications without inventing facts, personal experience, or giving individualized advice.", "hashtags": ["Business", "Entrepreneurship", "BusinessStrategy"]},

  "music-tech-software": {
    id: "music-tech-software",
    label: "Music tech — software",

export const CATEGORIES: Record<CategoryId, Category> = Object.assign(
  Object.create(null), LEGACY_CATEGORIES,
  Object.fromEntries(SUBJECT_GROUPS.flatMap(([group, groupLabel, subjects]) =>
    subjects.split('|').map(label => {
      const id = subjectId(group, label);
      return [id, {id, label, group, groupLabel, scope: `${label.toLowerCase()} (${groupLabel.toLowerCase()})`,
        blurb: `Developments specifically about ${label.toLowerCase()} within ${groupLabel.toLowerCase()}. The source must substantively address this subject: a passing mention or a broadly related industry story does not qualify. Explain concrete findings and implications using source evidence; never invent results, personal experience, or individualized advice.`,
        query: `"${label}"`, hashtags: [...new Set([label.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, ''), groupLabel.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, ''), 'ProfessionalDevelopment'])]} satisfies Category];
    }))),
);
export const ALL_CATEGORY_IDS = Object.keys(CATEGORIES);
export const MAX_SELECTED_CATEGORIES = 12;
/** Preserve the scope of existing installations whose saved category list was empty. */
export const LEGACY_CATEGORY_IDS:CategoryId[]=['music-tech-software','music-tech-hardware','emerging-tech','ai-ml','dev-tooling','hardware-embedded','compute-silicon'];

export function isCategoryId(v: unknown): v is CategoryId {
  return typeof v === "string" && Object.hasOwn(CATEGORIES, v);
}

export function parseCategories(v: unknown): CategoryId[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(v)) return [];
  const seen = new Set<CategoryId>();
  const dropped: unknown[] = [];
  for (const item of v) {
    if (isCategoryId(item)) seen.add(item);
    else dropped.push(item);
  }
  // Say so rather than swallowing it. A category removed from this file
  // disappears from every agent that had it selected, and silently narrowing
  // what someone watches looks exactly like discovery quietly getting worse.
  if (dropped.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`[categories] ignoring ${dropped.length} unknown id(s): ${JSON.stringify(dropped)}`);
  }
  return [...seen];
}

/**
 * The agent's editorial scope, in prose, derived from the categories it is
 * actually watching.
 *
 * This is the ONE description of what the agent covers. It is stored on
 * agents.domain, rendered in the app header, and fed to the persona expander —
 * so the header, the chips and the prompts cannot disagree with each other.
 *
 * It used to be a free-text sentence typed once at setup and never touched
 * again, which is how an agent whose music categories had been switched off
 * kept describing itself as writing about music technology, and kept being
 * judged as though it did.
 */
export function describeCategories(ids: CategoryId[]): string {
  const active = ids.length > 0 ? ids : LEGACY_CATEGORY_IDS;
  // Comma-joined rather than "a, b and c": several scopes already contain an
  // "and" of their own, and a second one reads as a single run-on interest.
  return active.map((id) => CATEGORIES[id].scope).join(", ");
}

/** Order-insensitive comparison — the persona only cares WHICH categories, not their order. */
export function sameCategorySet(a: CategoryId[], b: CategoryId[]): boolean {
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  const set = new Set(a);
  return b.every((id) => set.has(id));
}

/** Prompt block describing the active categories, shared by judge and writer. */
export function categoryBlock(ids: CategoryId[]): string {
  const active = ids.length > 0 ? ids : LEGACY_CATEGORY_IDS;
  return [
    "ACTIVE CATEGORIES (a post must belong to exactly one):",
    ...active.map((id) => `- ${id} — ${CATEGORIES[id].label}: ${CATEGORIES[id].blurb}`),
    // Without this the broad catch-all absorbs everything: an LLM handed both
    // "emerging-tech" and "ai-ml" will file a paper on inference batching under
    // the general heading roughly half the time, which makes the specific
    // category look broken and its hashtags never appear.
    "Assign the MOST SPECIFIC active category that genuinely fits. Only fall back to a broad one when no narrower category applies.",
  ].join("\n");
}

export function hashtagsFor(id: CategoryId | null | undefined): string[] {
  return id && id in CATEGORIES ? CATEGORIES[id].hashtags : [];
}
````

````text
/**
 * Deterministic verification of a draft against the author's own voice
 * settings.
 *
 * Every rule in lib/style.ts is stated in the prompt and, until this file
 * existed, verified nowhere. isDraft() in writer.ts only checked that the JSON
 * had the right shape and the text was over 100 characters, so a model that
 * returned 400 words against a 220-word cap, opened with a banned phrase, or
 * pasted the source URL into the body produced a draft nobody flagged.
 *
 * That is the wrong division of labour. A language model is good at writing and
 * unreliable at counting; code is the reverse. So the prompt asks, and this
 * checks — and when the check fails the writer gets ONE repair call naming the
 * exact violation, which works far better than restating the rule louder.
 *
 * Nothing here is a matter of taste. Every rule is either arithmetic (word
 * counts, character limits) or a fact about LinkedIn (it renders no markdown;
 * hashtags and source links are appended by lib/format.ts and duplicate if the
 * body carries its own).
 */
import { FOLD_CHARS,MAX_BODY_CHARS,assemblePost,checkLength } from "./format";
import { BULLET_MARK, type StyleConfig } from "./style";

export interface Violation {
  /** Short stable id, for logs and for counting which rules models break. */
  rule: string;
  /** Written at the model: names the failure and what to do about it. */
  detail: string;
}

/** Emoji, including the pictographic ranges people actually use on LinkedIn. */
const EMOJI = /\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u;
const EMOJI_GLOBAL = /\p{Extended_Pictographic}/gu;

export function countWords(text: string): number {
  return text.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
}

/**
 * The first sentence — the part that has to land before the fold.
 *
 * Checking the whole first LINE would be wrong for prose, where an opening
 * paragraph of 2-4 sentences routinely runs past 210 characters by design.
 * What actually matters is whether the opening claim survives truncation.
 */
export function firstSentence(text: string): string {
  const firstLine = text.trim().split("\n")[0] ?? "";
  const match = /^[\s\S]*?[.!?](?=\s|$)/.exec(firstLine);
  return (match?.[0] ?? firstLine).trim();
}

export function critique(
  text: string,
  style: StyleConfig,
  options: {
    usedQuote?: boolean;
    /**
     * The tags the model returned. OMITTED means "not checked" — the caller
     * has no tag list to judge, which is different from a post with none.
     */
    hashtags?: string[];
    sourceUrl?: string;
  } = {},
): Violation[] {
  const out: Violation[] = [];
  const body = text.trim();
  const lines = body.split("\n").map((l) => l.trim());

  // ---- length
  const words = countWords(body);
  const finalLength=checkLength(assemblePost({body,hashtags:options.hashtags,sourceUrl:options.sourceUrl,maxHashtags:style.hashtagCount}));
  if(!finalLength.withinLimit||body.length>MAX_BODY_CHARS)out.push({rule:'linkedin_length',detail:`The body is ${body.length} characters and the assembled post is ${finalLength.escapedChars}. Keep the body within ${MAX_BODY_CHARS} characters and the complete post within LinkedIn's 3000-character limit after its source and hashtags are added. Use short words and short sentences while keeping ${style.minWords}-${style.maxWords} words; aim near ${style.minWords}. Do not drop the source or tags.`});
  if (words < style.minWords) {
    out.push({
      rule: "too_short",
      detail: `The post is ${words} words. Your setting is ${style.minWords}-${style.maxWords}. Add substance — another concrete detail or consequence — rather than padding.`,
    });
  } else if (words > style.maxWords) {
    out.push({
      rule: "too_long",
      detail: `The post is ${words} words. Your setting is ${style.minWords}-${style.maxWords}. Cut to length, removing the least specific sentences first.`,
    });
  }

  // ---- banned phrases
  const lowered = body.toLowerCase();
  for (const phrase of style.bannedPhrases) {
    if (lowered.includes(phrase.toLowerCase())) {
      out.push({
        rule: "banned_phrase",
        detail: `Contains the banned phrase "${phrase}". Remove it and say the thing directly.`,
      });
    }
  }

  // ---- emoji policy
  const emojiCount = (body.match(EMOJI_GLOBAL) ?? []).length;
  if (style.emoji === "none" && emojiCount > 0) {
    out.push({
      rule: "emoji_forbidden",
      detail: `Contains ${emojiCount} emoji. This author uses none at all — remove every one.`,
    });
  } else if (style.emoji === "sparing") {
    if (emojiCount > 2) {
      out.push({
        rule: "emoji_excess",
        detail: `Contains ${emojiCount} emoji against a limit of 2. Keep at most the two that genuinely replace a word.`,
      });
    }
    if (EMOJI.test(lines[0] ?? "")) {
      out.push({
        rule: "emoji_in_hook",
        detail: "An emoji appears in the first line. The hook must be words only.",
      });
    }
  }

  // ---- markdown. LinkedIn renders none of it; the characters publish literally.
  if (/\*\*[^*]+\*\*|__[^_]+__/.test(body)) {
    out.push({
      rule: "markdown_bold",
      detail:
        "Contains markdown bold (** or __). LinkedIn renders no markdown — the asterisks appear literally on screen. Remove them.",
    });
  }
  if (/`[^`]+`/.test(body)) {
    out.push({
      rule: "markdown_code",
      detail: "Contains backticks. They publish as literal backtick characters. Remove them.",
    });
  }
  if (/^#{1,6}\s/m.test(body)) {
    out.push({
      rule: "markdown_heading",
      detail: "Contains a markdown heading. LinkedIn has no headings — write it as a sentence.",
    });
  }
  if (/^\s*(?:[-*]\s|\d+\.\s)/m.test(body)) {
    out.push({
      rule: "markdown_list",
      detail: `Contains a markdown list marker ("-", "*" or "1."). These publish literally. Use "${BULLET_MARK} " if the section needs bullets, or write it as prose.`,
    });
  }

  // ---- structure
  const bulletLines = lines.filter((l) => l.startsWith(BULLET_MARK)).length;
  if ((style.structure === "bullets" || style.structure === "mixed") && bulletLines < 3) {
    out.push({
      rule: "missing_bullets",
      detail: `Your structure setting is "${style.structure}" but the post has ${bulletLines} bullet lines. It needs at least 3, each starting with "${BULLET_MARK} " on its own line.`,
    });
  }
  if ((style.structure === "prose" || style.structure === "short-lines") && bulletLines > 0) {
    out.push({
      rule: "unexpected_bullets",
      detail: `Your structure setting is "${style.structure}", which has no bullets, but the post has ${bulletLines}. Rewrite them into the flow.`,
    });
  }

  // ---- the fold
  const hook = firstSentence(body);
  if (hook.length > FOLD_CHARS) {
    out.push({
      rule: "hook_past_fold",
      detail: `The opening sentence is ${hook.length} characters and LinkedIn hides everything past about ${FOLD_CHARS}, so it is cut mid-thought. Make the first sentence land the claim on its own.`,
    });
  }

  // ---- things lib/format.ts appends, which duplicate if the body carries them
  if (/https?:\/\/\S+/.test(body)) {
    out.push({
      rule: "url_in_body",
      detail:
        "The body contains a URL. The source link is appended automatically — including it here publishes it twice.",
    });
  }
  if (/(^|\s)#\w+/.test(body)) {
    out.push({
      rule: "hashtag_in_body",
      detail:
        "The body contains a hashtag. Hashtags are appended automatically — including them here publishes them twice.",
    });
  }

  // ---- hashtag count
  //
  // The setting reads "N tags" and means exactly N. It used to be enforced as a
  // ceiling in one direction only: the prompt asked for "0-N" and lib/format.ts
  // trimmed anything above N, so setting ten and receiving three looked like
  // the setting being ignored, and nothing anywhere noticed.
  if (options.hashtags !== undefined) {
    const tags = options.hashtags.length;
    if (tags !== style.hashtagCount) {
      out.push({
        rule: "hashtag_count",
        detail:
          style.hashtagCount === 0
            ? `Returned ${tags} hashtag(s). This author uses none — return an empty array.`
            : `Returned ${tags} hashtag${tags === 1 ? "" : "s"} and the author's setting is exactly ${style.hashtagCount}. ` +
              (tags < style.hashtagCount
                ? `Add ${style.hashtagCount - tags} more that genuinely fit this post — single words, no duplicates, no near-duplicates of each other.`
                : `Drop the ${tags - style.hashtagCount} least relevant.`),
      });
    }
  }

  // ---- the signature
  if (!style.signature && options.usedQuote) {
    out.push({
      rule: "unexpected_signature",
      detail:
        "This author has no signature line configured, but the post reports using a quote. Remove it.",
    });
  }

  return out;
}

/**
 * How bad a draft is, as one comparable number.
 *
 * Counting violations alone is too coarse to choose between two drafts. A post
 * 30 words short and a post 2 words short both have exactly one violation, so a
 * repair that moved from the first to the second scored no better than the
 * original and was discarded — which is why a narrow word range almost never
 * landed inside it. Distance breaks the tie, in words and in tags.
 */
export function severity(text: string, style: StyleConfig, violations: Violation[]): number {
  const words = countWords(text);
  const outOfRange =
    words < style.minWords
      ? style.minWords - words
      : words > style.maxWords
        ? words - style.maxWords
        : 0;
  const tagGap = violations.find((v) => v.rule === "hashtag_count") ? 1 : 0;
  // Violations dominate; distance only separates drafts that break the same
  // number of rules. Capped so one wild draft cannot outrank an extra violation.
  return violations.length * 1000 + Math.min(999, outOfRange) + tagGap;
}

/**
 * Turn violations into one repair instruction.
 *
 * Deliberately specific and finite: naming the exact failures repairs far more
 * reliably than repeating the whole constraint block, which the model has
 * already read once and ignored.
 */
export function repairInstruction(violations: Violation[]): string {
  return [
    "Your draft broke rules the author set. Fix EVERY item below and return the same JSON shape.",
    "Keep the facts, the argument and the source material exactly as they are — this is an edit, not a rewrite.",
    "",
    ...violations.map((v, i) => `${i + 1}. ${v.detail}`),
  ].join("\n");
}

/** One-line summary for logs: "too_long, banned_phrase". */
export function summarize(violations: Violation[]): string {
  return violations.map((v) => v.rule).join(", ");
}
````

````text
/**
 * Token encryption at rest (AES-256-GCM).
 *
 * A LinkedIn access token IS the ability to post as you for the next 60 days.
 * Neon backups, a leaked connection string, or a shared read-replica should
 * not hand that over, so tokens are encrypted before they touch a column and
 * decrypted only in the request that needs them.
 *
 * Unlike the external-service clients in this codebase, these functions THROW
 * on misconfiguration. A missing or malformed key is an operator error that
 * must be loud at connect time, not a degraded mode that silently writes
 * plaintext credentials.
 *
 * Generate a key with:
 *   node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"
 */
import { createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";

const ALGO = "aes-256-gcm";
const IV_BYTES = 12; // GCM standard nonce length
const TAG_BYTES = 16;
const PREFIX = "v1:";

function key(): Buffer {
  const raw = process.env.TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY;
  if (!raw) {
    throw new Error(
      "TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set — refusing to store a LinkedIn token. " +
        'Generate one with: node -e "console.log(require(\'crypto\').randomBytes(32).toString(\'base64\'))"',
    );
  }
  // Accept base64 or hex; both are natural things to paste into a .env.
  const buf = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(raw.trim())
    ? Buffer.from(raw.trim(), "hex")
    : Buffer.from(raw.trim(), "base64");
  if (buf.length !== 32) {
    throw new Error(
      `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY must decode to 32 bytes (got ${buf.length}). Use a fresh base64 32-byte key.`,
    );
  }
  return buf;
}

/** True if a usable key is configured — for honest status reporting, never for control flow around storage. */
export function hasEncryptionKey(): boolean {
  try {
    key();
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export function encrypt(plaintext: string): string {
  const iv = randomBytes(IV_BYTES);
  const cipher = createCipheriv(ALGO, key(), iv);
  const ct = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(plaintext, "utf8"), cipher.final()]);
  return PREFIX + Buffer.concat([iv, cipher.getAuthTag(), ct]).toString("base64");
}

export function decrypt(payload: string): string {
  if (!payload.startsWith(PREFIX)) {
    throw new Error("ciphertext is not in the expected v1 format");
  }
  const buf = Buffer.from(payload.slice(PREFIX.length), "base64");
  if (buf.length <= IV_BYTES + TAG_BYTES) throw new Error("ciphertext is truncated");
  const decipher = createDecipheriv(ALGO, key(), buf.subarray(0, IV_BYTES));
  decipher.setAuthTag(buf.subarray(IV_BYTES, IV_BYTES + TAG_BYTES));
  return Buffer.concat([
    decipher.update(buf.subarray(IV_BYTES + TAG_BYTES)),
    decipher.final(),
  ]).toString("utf8");
}
````

````text
import { withAgentUsage } from './ai-usage';
/**
 * One cycle, end to end:
 *   discover -> recall memory -> judge (1 LLM call, batched) ->
 *   persist rejections -> [write (1 LLM call) -> save draft] ->
 *   record episodes.
 *
 * Runs behind a Postgres advisory lock (transaction-scoped, so it survives
 * Neon's pgbouncer pooling and is released even if the process dies) — the
 * cron ticks and any manual trigger all pass through here, so overlapping
 * triggers can never double-fire.
 *
 * The important difference from the feed-publishing original: a cycle produces
 * a DRAFT. It no longer publishes anything at all. That used to happen inline
 * here when auto_publish was set, which meant the moment a post was written was
 * also the moment it was sent — leaving no window in which a human could read
 * it. Sending is now a separate pass (publishDuePosts in lib/distribute.ts)
 * driven by the post's own scheduled_for, and the gap between the two is the
 * review window that lib/slots.ts exists to create.
 *
 * A failed cycle is a logged non-event: it never throws, never corrupts state,
 * and the next slot tries again.
 */
import {
  getAgentSettings,
  getPersona,
  refreshPersonaIfStale,
  voiceReferencesFor,
  type AgentSettings,
} from "./agents";
import type { CategoryId } from "./categories";
import { getPool, query } from "./db";
import { discover } from "./discovery";
import { hookOf } from "./format";
import { judgeCandidates, PUBLISH_THRESHOLD } from "./judge";
import { notify } from "./push";
import { formatInZone } from "./schedule";
import { recall, rememberPublish, rememberRejections } from "./memory";
import { nextDailyRun } from "./schedule";
import {
  claimSlotRun,
  listDueSlots,
  rescheduleSlot,
  settleSlotRun,
  withSlotLock,
  type DueSlot,
} from "./slots";

import { writePost, type PriorPost } from "./writer";

/** Nothing published in this long widens discovery (more sources, higher caps). */
const STALE_HOURS = 48;
/** A cycle that found nothing usable retries this soon rather than losing the day. */
const RETRY_MINUTES = 120;

export interface CycleResult {
  agentId: string;
  ran: boolean;
  drafted: boolean;
  /** Always false now — cycles draft, they never send. Kept so callers and logs
   *  that read this field do not silently break. */
  published: boolean;
  postId?: string;
  seq?: number;
  skippedReason?: string;
  stats?: { n: number; min: number; max: number; mean: number };
  servedBy?: string[];
}

/** What a slot contributes to a cycle: its categories, and where the post lands. */
export interface CycleContext {
  onProgress?: (stage: 'discovering' | 'judging' | 'writing' | 'saving') => Promise<void>;
  reviewDate?: string;
  suppressNotification?: boolean;
  /** Overrides the agent's categories when non-empty. */
  categories?: CategoryId[];
  slotId?: string;
  slotDate?: string;
  /** Stamped onto the draft as posts.scheduled_for — when it should go out. */
  scheduledFor?: Date;
}

/**
 * Record that a cycle ran. Bumps last_run_at and the counter, nothing else.
 *
 * It used to also write scheduler_state.next_run_at, computed from the legacy
 * agents.post_time_local — a column slots replaced and nothing consults any
 * more. So the dashboard cheerfully displayed a "next run" that no longer
 * corresponded to anything: a time derived from a dead setting, for a scheduler
 * that had stopped reading it. next_run_at is now cleared, and the real answer
 * comes from the slots themselves.
 */
async function recordCycleRan(agentId: string): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO scheduler_state (agent_id, last_run_at, next_run_at, cycle_count)
     VALUES ($1, now(), NULL, 1)
     ON CONFLICT (agent_id) DO UPDATE
       SET last_run_at = now(), next_run_at = NULL,
           cycle_count = scheduler_state.cycle_count + 1`,
    [agentId],
  );
}

/** The cycle body. Assumes the advisory lock is already held. */
async function runCycle(agentId: string, context: CycleContext = {}): Promise<CycleResult> {
  const servedBy: string[] = [];
  const settings = await getAgentSettings(agentId);
  if (!settings) return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "unknown_agent" };
  if (settings.paused) {
    // Still reschedule, so unpausing does not require a manual kick.
    await recordCycleRan(agentId);
    return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "paused" };
  }

  // The identity is derived from the categories, so it is rebuilt here if they
  // have moved since it was last built. Doing it at the top of the cycle rather
  // than in the settings handler means a run of category taps costs one rebuild
  // instead of one per tap, and the rebuild lands before the prompts that read it.
  await refreshPersonaIfStale(agentId);

  const persona = await getPersona(agentId);
  if (!persona) {
    return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "persona_not_ready" };
  }
  const name = persona.input.name;

  // STALE GUARD: nothing written for 48h+ -> widen discovery. The threshold is
  // never lowered to force a post; the input gets fixed instead.
  const newest = await query<{ newest: Date | null }>(
    "SELECT max(created_at) AS newest FROM posts WHERE agent_id = $1",
    [agentId],
  );
  const newestAt = newest[0]?.newest?.getTime() ?? 0;
  const staleFeed = Date.now() - newestAt > STALE_HOURS * 3_600_000;
  if (staleFeed) {
    console.warn(
      `[cycle] agent=${agentId} stale (newest ${newestAt ? new Date(newestAt).toISOString() : "never"}) — widening discovery`,
    );
  }

  // 1. Discover. A slot may narrow the agent's categories to its own — that is
  // what stops three posts a day all sounding like the same beat — but it can
  // never widen them beyond what the agent is watching.
  const slotCategories = (context.categories ?? []).filter((c) => settings.categories.includes(c));
  const activeCategories = slotCategories.length > 0 ? slotCategories : settings.categories;
  await context.onProgress?.('discovering');
  const discovered = await discover({ categories: activeCategories, wide: staleFeed });

  // Hard dedup: never re-judge a URL already written about (drafts included —
  // a rejected draft still consumed the story).
  const usedUrls = new Set(
    (
      await query<{ sources_json: string[] }>("SELECT sources_json FROM posts WHERE agent_id = $1", [
        agentId,
      ])
    ).flatMap((r) => r.sources_json ?? []),
  );

  // Rejection cooldown: a URL scored and rejected in the last 24h does not get
  // to burn a judging slot again. After 24h it may be re-judged — timeliness
  // genuinely changes.
  const cooldownUrls = new Set(
    (
      await query<{ url: string }>(
        "SELECT DISTINCT url FROM rejections WHERE agent_id = $1 AND created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'",
        [agentId],
      )
    ).map((r) => r.url),
  );

  const candidates = discovered.filter((c) => !usedUrls.has(c.url) && !cooldownUrls.has(c.url));
  console.log(
    `[cycle] agent=${agentId} pool: ${discovered.length} discovered, ${discovered.length - candidates.length} filtered, ${candidates.length} to judge`,
  );

  if (candidates.length === 0) {
    await recordCycleRan(agentId);
    return { agentId, ran: true, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "no_candidates" };
  }

  // 2. Recall prior coverage (Breeth, falling back to Postgres fingerprints).
  const topics = candidates.slice(0, 8).map((c) => c.title).join("; ");
  const judgeMemory = await recall(agentId, topics);
  const priorFingerprints =
    judgeMemory.source === "postgres"
      ? []
      : (
          await query<{ fingerprint: string }>(
            "SELECT fingerprint FROM posts WHERE agent_id = $1 ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 20",
            [agentId],
          )
        ).map((r) => r.fingerprint);

  // 3. Judge — ONE batched call for all candidates.
  //
  // The recent category mix goes in with them. Judging every candidate purely
  // on its own merits reads well in isolation and narrows the profile over
  // time: whichever category yields the strongest stories takes every cycle.
  // Drafts count, not just published posts — a draft has already consumed the
  // subject whether or not the author ever approved it.
  const recentCategories = (
    await query<{ category: CategoryId | null }>(
      `SELECT category FROM posts
        WHERE agent_id = $1 AND category IS NOT NULL
        ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 12`,
      [agentId],
    )
  ).flatMap((r) => (r.category ? [r.category] : []));

  await context.onProgress?.('judging');
  const judged = await judgeCandidates(
    persona,
    activeCategories,
    candidates,
    judgeMemory,
    priorFingerprints,
    recentCategories,
  );
  if (!judged.ok) {
    console.warn(`[cycle] agent=${agentId} judging failed: ${judged.reason}`);
    await recordCycleRan(agentId);
    // A mechanical failure, not a quiet day. "below_threshold" and
    // "no_candidates" are deliberately NOT reported: a silent day is correct
    // behaviour, and an alert for it would train you to ignore the ones that
    // are not.
    await notify(agentId, { kind: "cycle_failed", detail: `judge:${judged.reason}` });
    return { agentId, ran: true, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: `judge:${judged.reason}` };
  }
  if (judged.data.servedBy) servedBy.push(judged.data.servedBy);
  const scored = judged.data.scored;

  const totals = scored.map((s) => s.total);
  const stats = {
    n: totals.length,
    min: Math.min(...totals),
    max: Math.max(...totals),
    mean: Math.round((totals.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / totals.length) * 100) / 100,
  };

  const winner = scored[0].total >= PUBLISH_THRESHOLD ? scored[0] : null;
  const rejected = winner ? scored.slice(1) : scored;

  // 4. Persist every rejection with its per-criterion scores and a reason.
  const cycleId =
    (
      await query<{ cycle_count: number }>(
        "SELECT cycle_count FROM scheduler_state WHERE agent_id = $1",
        [agentId],
      )
    )[0]?.cycle_count ?? 0;
  for (const r of rejected) {
    await query(
      `INSERT INTO rejections (agent_id, cycle_id, title, url, scores_json, reason)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)`,
      [
        agentId,
        cycleId + 1,
        r.title,
        r.url,
        JSON.stringify({ ...r.scores, total: r.total }),
        winner ? r.reason : `${r.reason} (top score ${r.total} below ${PUBLISH_THRESHOLD} threshold)`,
      ],
    );
  }

  if (!winner) {
    await recordCycleRan(agentId);
    console.log(`[cycle] agent=${agentId} nothing cleared ${PUBLISH_THRESHOLD} — silent day (max ${stats.max})`);
    return { agentId, ran: true, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "below_threshold", stats, servedBy };
  }

  // 5. Write the draft.
  const writeMemory = await recall(agentId, winner.title);
  const priorRows = await query<{
    id: string;
    fingerprint: string;
    opening: string;
    used_quote: boolean;
  }>(
    `SELECT id, fingerprint, left(text, 90) AS opening, used_quote
       FROM posts WHERE agent_id = $1 ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 10`,
    [agentId],
  );
  const priorPosts: PriorPost[] = priorRows.map((p) => ({
    id: p.id,
    fingerprint: p.fingerprint,
    opening: p.opening,
    usedQuote: p.used_quote,
  }));

  // Few-shot voice references, from the same helper the composer's rewrite and
  // the voice preview use. They were separate before, and the composer's copy
  // simply did not exist — so "Rewrite with AI" ran on the style toggles alone
  // and ignored the author's samples entirely.
  const voice = await voiceReferencesFor(settings);

  // The signature ration counts PUBLISHED posts only. Counting drafts would let
  // a quote in something the author discarded consume the budget, silently
  // suppressing the signature for days afterwards.
  const quotesInLastFivePublished = (
    await query<{ used_quote: boolean }>(
      `SELECT used_quote FROM posts
        WHERE agent_id = $1 AND status = 'published'
        ORDER BY published_at DESC NULLS LAST, seq DESC
        LIMIT 5`,
      [agentId],
    )
  ).filter((r) => r.used_quote).length;

  const runnersUp = scored.slice(1, 3);
  await context.onProgress?.('writing');
  const draft = await writePost({
    persona,
    style: settings.style,
    winner,
    runnersUp,
    memory: writeMemory,
    priorPosts,
    samples: voice.samples,
    editNotes: voice.editNotes,
    publishedQuotesInLastFive: quotesInLastFivePublished,
  });

  if (!draft.ok) {
    console.warn(`[cycle] agent=${agentId} writing failed: ${draft.reason}`);
    await recordCycleRan(agentId);
    return { agentId, ran: true, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: `writer:${draft.reason}`, stats, servedBy };
  }
  if (draft.data.servedBy) servedBy.push(draft.data.servedBy);

  await context.onProgress?.('saving');
  const inserted = await query<{ id: string; seq: number }>(
    `INSERT INTO posts (agent_id, seq, text, rationale, sources_json, fingerprint, scores_json,
                        continuity, cycle_id, status, kind, category, hashtags_json, used_quote,
                        slot_id, scheduled_for, review_date,slot_date)
     SELECT $1, byline_next_seq($1), $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, 'draft', 'auto', $9, $10, $11,
            $12, $13, $14,$15
     ON CONFLICT(agent_id,slot_id,slot_date) WHERE slot_date IS NOT NULL
       DO UPDATE SET slot_date=EXCLUDED.slot_date
     RETURNING id, seq`,
    [
      agentId,
      draft.data.text,
      draft.data.rationale,
      JSON.stringify([winner.url]),
      draft.data.fingerprint,
      JSON.stringify({ ...winner.scores, total: winner.total }),
      draft.data.continuity,
      cycleId + 1,
      winner.category,
      JSON.stringify(draft.data.hashtags ?? []),
      draft.data.used_quote,
      context.slotId ?? null,
      context.scheduledFor?.toISOString() ?? null,
      context.reviewDate ?? null,
      context.slotDate ?? null,
    ],
  );
  const postId = inserted[0]?.id;
  const seq = inserted[0]?.seq;

  // NOTE: nothing is published here, deliberately. This used to auto-publish
  // inline, which collapsed writing and sending into one instant and left no
  // window to read the draft. Sending is now publishDuePosts() in
  // lib/distribute.ts, driven by the scheduled_for stamped just above.
  console.log(
    context.scheduledFor
      ? `[cycle] agent=${agentId} ${postId} drafted for ${context.scheduledFor.toISOString()}`
      : `[cycle] agent=${agentId} ${postId} drafted — unscheduled, waiting in the queue`,
  );

  // 6. Editorial memory — the publish episode carries intent.
  await rememberPublish(agentId, name, {
    title: winner.title,
    rationale: draft.data.rationale,
    runnersUp: runnersUp.map((r) => r.title),
  });
  await rememberRejections(
    agentId,
    name,
    rejected.slice(0, 3).map((r) => ({ title: r.title, reason: r.reason })),
  );

  await recordCycleRan(agentId);

  // Announced from HERE rather than from the cron route, so every path that
  // produces a draft says so: the scheduled tick, "Run a cycle now" from the
  // phone, and a forced single-agent run. It was wired into the tick alone,
  // which meant the one case where somebody was definitely holding the phone
  // and waiting — pressing the button — was the one case that stayed silent.
  //
  // The hook, not the post: a notification is a reason to open the app, not a
  // place to read a draft.
  if (seq !== undefined && !context.suppressNotification) {
    await notify(agentId, {
      kind: "draft_ready",
      seq,
      hook: hookOf(draft.data.text).slice(0, 120),
      at: context.scheduledFor ? formatInZone(context.scheduledFor, settings.timezone) : null,
    });
  }

  console.log(
    `[cycle] agent=${agentId} scored n=${stats.n} min=${stats.min} max=${stats.max} mean=${stats.mean} drafted=${postId} servedBy=${servedBy.join(",") || "n/a"}`,
  );
  return { agentId, ran: true, drafted: true, published: false, postId, seq, stats, servedBy };
}

/**
 * Advisory-locked wrapper. Uses a transaction-scoped lock
 * (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock) on a dedicated client: safe through Neon's
 * transaction-mode pooler, and auto-released on COMMIT/ROLLBACK or death.
 * A session-scoped lock would silently not work here — do not "simplify" it.
 */
export async function runCycleWithLock(agentId: string, force = false, context: CycleContext = {}): Promise<CycleResult> {
  return withAgentUsage(agentId,()=>runCycleLocked(agentId,force,context));
}
async function runCycleLocked(agentId: string, force = false, context: CycleContext = {}): Promise<CycleResult> {
  const pool = getPool();
  if (!pool) return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "no_database" };

  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");
    const lock = await client.query<{ locked: boolean }>(
      "SELECT pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(42, hashtext($1)) AS locked",
      [agentId],
    );
    if (!lock.rows[0].locked) {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "locked" };
    }

    // Re-check dueness INSIDE the lock so two ticks cannot both pass it.
    if (!force) {
      const due = await client.query(
        `SELECT 1 FROM scheduler_state s
           JOIN agents a ON a.id = s.agent_id
          WHERE s.agent_id = $1 AND a.active AND NOT a.paused
            AND (s.next_run_at IS NULL OR s.next_run_at <= now())`,
        [agentId],
      );
      if (due.rows.length === 0) {
        await client.query("ROLLBACK");
        return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: "not_due_or_paused" };
      }
    }

    const result = await runCycle(agentId, context).catch((err): CycleResult => {
      console.error(`[cycle] agent=${agentId} crashed:`, err);
      return { agentId, ran: true, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: String(err) };
    });

    await client.query("COMMIT"); // releases the advisory lock
    return result;
  } catch (err) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK").catch(() => {});
    console.error(`[cycle] lock wrapper failed for agent=${agentId}:`, err);
    return { agentId, ran: false, drafted: false, published: false, skippedReason: String(err) };
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

/**
 * Generate for one due slot, under that slot's own lock.
 *
 * Order matters here and each step is load-bearing:
 *   1. A slot noticed far past its time is marked missed and rescheduled
 *      WITHOUT generating. Publishing a 09:00 thought at lunchtime is worse
 *      than staying quiet, and we would rather show you that it happened.
 *   2. The run is claimed via the (slot_id, run_date) primary key, so however
 *      many ticks overlap, a slot generates at most once per local day.
 *   3. The slot is rescheduled in a `finally`, so a crash inside the pipeline
 *      cannot leave next_run_at in the past and wedge the slot into retrying
 *      forever.
 */
/**
 * Is something already on its way out at or before this slot's moment?
 *
 * A slot exists to make sure something gets published at that time — not to
 * make sure the AGENT wrote it. If a post is already scheduled to go out by
 * then, generating another one produces two posts competing for one moment and
 * spends two LLM calls to create the problem.
 *
 * Deliberately counts only SCHEDULED posts. An unscheduled draft is not going
 * anywhere on its own, and treating it as "the queue has content" would let one
 * forgotten draft silence the agent permanently — a far worse failure than an
 * occasional extra post, and one nobody would diagnose quickly.
 */
async function queueAlreadyCovers(agentId: string, scheduledFor: Date): Promise<number | null> {
  const rows = await query<{ seq: number }>(
    `SELECT seq FROM posts
       WHERE agent_id = $1
         AND status IN ('draft', 'approved')
         AND scheduled_for IS NOT NULL
         AND scheduled_for <= $2
         AND scheduled_for > now() - interval '5 minutes'
       ORDER BY scheduled_for
       LIMIT 1`,
    [agentId, scheduledFor.toISOString()],
  );
  return rows[0]?.seq ?? null;
}

export async function runSlotCycle(due: DueSlot, manual=false): Promise<CycleResult> {
  return withAgentUsage(due.slot.agentId,()=>runSlotCycleInternal(due,manual));
}
async function runSlotCycleInternal(due: DueSlot, manual=false): Promise<CycleResult> {
  const { slot, runDate, scheduledFor } = due;
  const base: CycleResult = {
    agentId: slot.agentId,
    ran: false,
    drafted: false,
    published: false,
  };

  return withSlotLock(
    slot.id,
    async () => {
      const [existing]=await query<{seq:number}>(`SELECT seq FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND slot_id=$2 AND
        (slot_date=$3::date OR seq IN(SELECT post_seq FROM slot_runs WHERE slot_id=$2 AND run_date=$3::date)) LIMIT 1`,[slot.agentId,slot.id,runDate]);
      if(existing) {
        await settleSlotRun(slot.id,runDate,'drafted',{postSeq:existing.seq});
        await rescheduleSlot(slot,due.timezone,new Date(Math.max(Date.now(),scheduledFor.getTime())));
        return {...base,ran:true,drafted:true,seq:existing.seq};
      }
      if (!(await claimSlotRun(due,manual))) {
        return { ...base, skippedReason: "already_ran_today" };
      }

      try {
        if (due.missed && !manual) {
          await settleSlotRun(slot.id, runDate, "missed", {
            detail: `Noticed more than ${MISSED_AFTER_LABEL} after ${slot.localTime}; not published late.`,
          });
          console.warn(`[cycle] slot=${slot.id} ${slot.localTime} MISSED for ${runDate}`);
          return { ...base, skippedReason: "missed" };
        }

        // Nothing to write if something is already queued for this moment —
        // whether the author composed it by hand or an earlier run produced it.
        // Recorded as a silent slot with the reason, because the timetable
        // showing a gap it cannot explain is the thing this app refuses to do.
        const [native]=await query('SELECT 1 FROM agents WHERE id=$1 AND owner_id IS NOT NULL',[slot.agentId]);
        const covered = native ? null : await queueAlreadyCovers(slot.agentId, scheduledFor);
        if (covered !== null) {
          await settleSlotRun(slot.id, runDate, "silent", {
            detail: `Post #${covered} is already queued for this slot — nothing new was written.`,
          });
          console.log(
            `[cycle] slot=${slot.id} ${slot.localTime} already covered by p${covered} — skipping generation`,
          );
          return { ...base, ran: true, skippedReason: "queue_already_covers" };
        }

        if(process.env.BYLINE_TEST_MODE==='true') {
          const {generateSetupSample,defaultSetup}=await import('./onboarding');
          const [setup]=await query<{config:typeof defaultSetup}>(`SELECT o.config FROM onboarding o JOIN agents a ON a.owner_id=o.user_id WHERE a.id=$1`,[slot.agentId]);
          const sample=await generateSetupSample({...defaultSetup,...setup?.config});
          const [demo]=await query<{seq:number}>(`INSERT INTO posts(agent_id,seq,text,rationale,sources_json,fingerprint,status,kind,slot_id,slot_date,scheduled_for)
            VALUES($1,byline_next_seq($1),$2,'Local demonstration; no AI call',$3,$4,'draft','auto',$5,$6,$7)
            ON CONFLICT(agent_id,slot_id,slot_date) WHERE slot_date IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET slot_date=EXCLUDED.slot_date RETURNING seq`,
            [slot.agentId,sample.text,JSON.stringify(sample.sources),`local-slot:${slot.id}:${runDate}`,slot.id,runDate,
              manual&&scheduledFor.getTime()<=Date.now()?null:scheduledFor]);
          await settleSlotRun(slot.id,runDate,'drafted',{postSeq:demo.seq});
          return {...base,ran:true,drafted:true,seq:demo.seq};
        }
        const result = await runCycleWithLock(slot.agentId, true, {
          categories: slot.categories,
          slotId: slot.id,
          slotDate: runDate,
          scheduledFor: manual && scheduledFor.getTime()<=Date.now() ? undefined : scheduledFor,
          onProgress: async stage => {
            await query('UPDATE slot_runs SET stage=$3 WHERE slot_id=$1 AND run_date=$2',[slot.id,runDate,stage]);
          },
        });

        if (result.drafted) {
          await settleSlotRun(slot.id, runDate, "drafted", { postSeq: result.seq });
        } else if (result.skippedReason === "below_threshold") {
          // The silent day, made legible. Without the score the app can only
          // show a gap, which is indistinguishable from a broken cron.
          await settleSlotRun(slot.id, runDate, "silent", {
            detail: result.stats
              ? `Nothing cleared ${PUBLISH_THRESHOLD} — best was ${result.stats.max} across ${result.stats.n} candidates.`
              : "Nothing cleared the threshold.",
          });
        } else {
          await settleSlotRun(slot.id, runDate, "failed", { detail: result.skippedReason });
        }
        return result;
      } finally {
        const [run]=await query<{outcome:string;attempts:number}>(
          'SELECT outcome,attempts FROM slot_runs WHERE slot_id=$1 AND run_date=$2',[slot.id,runDate]);
        const retry=run && ['failed','silent'].includes(run.outcome) && run.attempts<3 && scheduledFor.getTime()>Date.now();
        if(!retry)await rescheduleSlot(slot, due.timezone, new Date(Math.max(Date.now(), scheduledFor.getTime()))).catch((err) =>
          console.error(`[cycle] slot=${slot.id} reschedule failed:`, err),
        );
      }
    },
    { ...base, skippedReason: "locked" },
  );
}

const MISSED_AFTER_LABEL = "45 minutes";

/**
 * The generation pass: every slot whose review window has opened.
 *
 * Serialized rather than parallel, matching the tick's existing reasoning —
 * cycles share a per-model LLM rate limit, so running them concurrently just
 * produces 429s and a cascade down to the weaker models.
 */
export async function runDueSlots(): Promise<CycleResult[]> {
  const due = await listDueSlots();
  const results: CycleResult[] = [];
  for (const item of due) {
    results.push(
      await runSlotCycle(item).catch((err): CycleResult => {
        console.error(`[cycle] slot=${item.slot.id} crashed:`, err);
        return {
          agentId: item.slot.agentId,
          ran: true,
          drafted: false,
          published: false,
          skippedReason: String(err),
        };
      }),
    );
  }
  return results;
}
````

````text
/**
 * Single pg Pool per lambda instance. Neon requires TLS; the connection
 * string carries ?sslmode=require (see DEPLOY.md).
 *
 * Serverless notes:
 * - ensureSchema checks an additive schema-hash ledger once per instance.
 *   A transaction lock serializes migrations. Hosted releases can require
 *   the explicit migration command instead of applying changes on first use.
 * - No DATABASE_URL means stub mode (local dev before Neon exists) — callers
 *   must handle a null pool rather than crash.
 */
import { Pool } from "pg";
import { SCHEMA_SQL } from "./schema";
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';

/**
 * Pool and schema state live on globalThis, NOT in module scope.
 *
 * `next dev` re-evaluates a module every time a route that imports it is
 * recompiled — which happens constantly while editing. With these as plain
 * module variables, every recompile built a BRAND NEW pool (fresh TLS
 * handshakes to Neon) and re-ran the entire 14KB, 45-statement schema script
 * over the network before the first query could proceed. That is most of why
 * a simple PATCH took six seconds locally: almost none of it was the work.
 *
 * globalThis survives module re-evaluation, so the pool and the schema promise
 * are created once per PROCESS. Production is unaffected either way — a lambda
 * evaluates the module once — so this costs nothing there and transforms
 * local development.
 */
interface DbGlobals {
  pool: Pool | null;
  schemaReady: Promise<void> | null;
  schemaVersion?: string;
}
const g = globalThis as unknown as { __linkdinDb?: DbGlobals };
g.__linkdinDb ??= { pool: null, schemaReady: null };
const state = g.__linkdinDb;

export function getPool(): Pool | null {
  if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) return null;
  if (!state.pool) {
    state.pool = new Pool({
      connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
      // Raised from 3. Every read endpoint fans out a dozen independent
      // queries through Promise.all, and with three connections those ran four
      // rounds deep — turning one network round trip of latency into four
      // against a database that is not in the same country. Neon's pooled
      // endpoint is built for far more than this.
      max: 10,
      idleTimeoutMillis: 30_000,
      // Neon's free tier autosuspends after ~5 idle minutes and a cold start
      // regularly takes 5-10 seconds. A 5s ceiling meant the FIRST request
      // after any quiet spell failed with "Connection terminated due to
      // connection timeout" — the database was not down, we just gave up while
      // it was still waking.
      connectionTimeoutMillis: 20_000,
      // Keeps the socket alive through NAT/idle timeouts on long-lived
      // serverless instances, which is the other source of "Connection
      // terminated unexpectedly".
      keepAlive: true,
    });
    state.pool.on("error", (err) => {
      console.error("[db] idle client error:", err.message);
    });
  }
  return state.pool;
}

/** Applies the schema once per instance; safe to call on every access. */
export async function ensureSchema(): Promise<boolean> {
  const p = getPool();
  if (!p) return false;
  const version=createHash('sha256').update(SCHEMA_SQL).digest('hex');
  if(state.schemaVersion!==version) {state.schemaReady=null;state.schemaVersion=version;}
  if (!state.schemaReady) {
    const started = Date.now();
    state.schemaReady = (async()=>{
      const c=await p.connect();
      try {
        await c.query('BEGIN');
        await c.query('SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(729311)');
        if(process.env.BYLINE_REQUIRE_MIGRATIONS==='true') {
          const exists=await c.query("SELECT to_regclass('byline_schema_versions') AS name");
          if(!exists.rows[0].name)throw new Error('Database migration required before this release can serve requests.');
        } else {
          await c.query('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS byline_schema_versions(version TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())');
        }
        const applied=await c.query('SELECT 1 FROM byline_schema_versions WHERE version=$1',[version]);
        if(!applied.rowCount) {
          if(process.env.BYLINE_REQUIRE_MIGRATIONS==='true')throw new Error('Database migration required before this release can serve requests.');
          await c.query(SCHEMA_SQL);
          await c.query('INSERT INTO byline_schema_versions(version) VALUES($1)',[version]);
        }
        await c.query('COMMIT');
      } catch(e) {await c.query('ROLLBACK').catch(()=>{});throw e;}
      finally{c.release();}
        console.log(`[db] schema ensured in ${Date.now() - started}ms`);
      })()
      .catch((err) => {
        state.schemaReady = null; // allow retry on the next access
        throw err;
      });
  }
  await state.schemaReady;
  return true;
}

/**
 * Thin helper so call sites stay one-liners. Throws on query failure.
 *
 * T is deliberately unconstrained: a named `interface` has no implicit index
 * signature, so a `Record<string, unknown>` bound would reject every row type
 * declared as an interface and push call sites toward inline object literals.
 * The cast below is unchecked either way — the constraint bought no safety.
 */
/** A failure to reach the database at all, as opposed to a rejected statement. */
function isConnectionError(err: unknown): boolean {
  const message = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err);
  return (
    message.includes("Connection terminated") ||
    message.includes("timeout expired") ||
    message.includes("ECONNRESET") ||
    message.includes("ETIMEDOUT")
  );
}

export async function query<T = Record<string, unknown>>(
  sql: string,
  params: unknown[] = [],
): Promise<T[]> {
  const p = getPool();
  if (!p) throw new Error("DATABASE_URL not configured");
  await ensureSchema();

  try {
    const result = await p.query(sql, params);
    return result.rows as T[];
  } catch (err) {
    // Retry ONLY read-only statements, and only when the connection itself
    // failed. A write that dies mid-flight is ambiguous — it may have
    // committed — and blindly re-running one here would undermine the
    // idempotency the publish ledger depends on. A SELECT has no such risk.
    const readOnly = /^\s*select\b/i.test(sql);
    if (!readOnly || !isConnectionError(err)) throw err;

    console.warn(`[db] connection failed on a read, retrying once: ${(err as Error).message}`);
    const result = await p.query(sql, params);
    return result.rows as T[];
  }
}
````

````text
/**
 * Candidate discovery — keyless sources only, for reliability.
 * Every source is fetched with its own timeout and try/catch: one dead feed
 * must never abort the cycle. Title + summary is enough; no article-body
 * fetching (cheap and reliable beats complete).
 *
 * Feeds are grouped by the category they usually serve. The grouping only
 * decides which feeds get FETCHED for a given agent — the judge assigns each
 * candidate its final category, because a synth-plugin story turns up on a
 * hardware blog often enough that trusting the source would mislabel it.
 *
 * `verified: false` marks feeds that could not be reached from the build
 * environment (its network blocks several hosts) and are therefore unproven
 * rather than known-good. They cost one logged warning per cycle if dead.
 * Run `npm run check:feeds` from your own network to see the real picture.
 *
 * Previously checked sources retain their verification flags. New sources
 * remain unverified until runtime feed health establishes their availability.
 */
import type { CategoryId } from "./categories";
import { CATEGORIES, LEGACY_CATEGORY_IDS as ALL_CATEGORY_IDS, MAX_SELECTED_CATEGORIES } from "./categories";
import { decodeEntities } from "./entities";
import { boundedText } from './http-body';
export type FeedRecorder = (name:string, outcome:{ok:true;items:number}|{ok:false;error:string})=>Promise<void>;

export interface Candidate {
  title: string;
  url: string;
  summary: string;
  source: string;
  /** The category its source usually serves — a hint for the judge, not a verdict. */
  categoryHint: CategoryId;
  publishedAt?: string;
}

const FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000;
const MAX_CANDIDATES = 26;
const MAX_CANDIDATES_WIDE = 34;
const FRESH_HOURS = 72;
const SPARSE_FRESH_HOURS = 7 * 24;

/**
 * Slots guaranteed per active category, and the ceiling that stops the judge
 * prompt growing without bound.
 *
 * The interleave shares the cap evenly, so a fixed 26 means three categories
 * get eight or nine candidates each and seven get barely three — deep enough to
 * choose from in the first case, a coin toss in the second. The cap therefore
 * grows with how many categories are actually active, and only then.
 *
 * The ceiling matters because every candidate is scored in ONE batched call:
 * past roughly forty the prompt starts crowding the model's output budget and
 * the whole batch can come back truncated and unusable.
 */
const PER_CATEGORY_FLOOR = 5;
const HARD_CANDIDATE_CAP = 40;

export interface DiscoverOptions {
  /** Which categories the agent actually cares about. Empty = all of them. */
  categories?: CategoryId[];
  /** Stale-feed guard: more sources and higher caps when nothing published recently. */
  wide?: boolean;
  /** Cloud deployments reserve requests for writing and notification delivery. */
  maxFetches?: number;
  maxFeeds?: number;
}

type FeedFetch=(url:string,init:RequestInit)=>Promise<Response>;
/** Count redirect hops too; automatic redirects can silently exhaust Workers Free. */
export function boundedFeedFetch(limit:number):FeedFetch {
  let used=0;
  return async (url,init)=>{
    for(let hop=0;hop<3;hop++) {
      if(used>=limit)throw new Error('Source request budget reached');
      used++;
      const response=await fetch(url,{...init,redirect:'manual'});
      if(![301,302,303,307,308].includes(response.status))return response;
      const location=response.headers.get('location');
      await response.body?.cancel();
      if(!location)throw new Error('Feed redirect has no destination');
      const next=new URL(location,url);
      if(!['https:','http:'].includes(next.protocol))throw new Error('Invalid feed redirect');
      url=next.href;
    }
    throw new Error('Feed redirected too many times');
  };
}

async function fetchText(url: string,request:FeedFetch=fetch): Promise<string> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS);
  try {
    const res = await request(url, {
      signal: controller.signal,
      headers: { "User-Agent": "linkedin-creator/1.0 (+personal publishing agent)" },
    });
    if (!res.ok) {await res.body?.cancel();throw new Error(`http ${res.status}`);}
    return await boundedText(res, 512 * 1024);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

function stripHtml(s: string): string {
  return decodeEntities(
    s.replace(/<!\[CDATA\[([\s\S]*?)\]\]>/g, "$1").replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " "),
  ).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
}

function clip(s: string, n: number): string {
  return s.length <= n ? s : s.slice(0, n - 1).trimEnd() + "…";
}

// ---- Hacker News (Algolia, JSON, keyless) — emerging tech
async function fromHackerNews(wide: boolean,request?:FeedFetch): Promise<Candidate[]> {
  const body = await fetchText(
    `https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search_by_date?tags=story&hitsPerPage=${wide ? 20 : 12}`,request,
  );
  const data = JSON.parse(body) as {
    hits: {
      title?: string;
      url?: string;
      story_text?: string;
      objectID: string;
      created_at?: string;
    }[];
  };
  return data.hits
    .filter((h) => h.title)
    .map((h) => ({
      title: stripHtml(h.title!),
      url: h.url || `https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=${h.objectID}`,
      summary: clip(stripHtml(h.story_text ?? h.title!), 400),
      source: "hackernews",
      categoryHint: "emerging-tech" as CategoryId,
      publishedAt: h.created_at,
    }));
}

// ---- Generic RSS/Atom parser (regex-based, deliberately tolerant)
function parseFeed(
  xml: string,
  source: string,
  categoryHint: CategoryId,
  limit: number,
): Candidate[] {
  const items = xml.match(/<(?:item|entry)[\s>][\s\S]*?<\/(?:item|entry)>/g) ?? [];
  const out: Candidate[] = [];
  for (const item of items.slice(0, limit)) {
    const title = stripHtml(item.match(/<title[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/title>/)?.[1] ?? "");
    // Atom: <link href="..."/>; RSS: <link>...</link>; arXiv: <id>...</id>
    const url =
      item.match(/<link[^>]*href="([^"]+)"/)?.[1] ??
      stripHtml(item.match(/<link[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/link>/)?.[1] ?? "") ??
      stripHtml(item.match(/<id>([\s\S]*?)<\/id>/)?.[1] ?? "");
    const summary = stripHtml(
      item.match(
        /<(?:description|summary|content)[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/(?:description|summary|content)>/,
      )?.[1] ?? "",
    );
    const publishedAt = stripHtml(
      item.match(/<(?:pubDate|published|updated)>([\s\S]*?)<\/(?:pubDate|published|updated)>/)?.[1] ??
        "",
    );
    if (title.length >= 8 && url.startsWith("http")) {
      out.push({ title, url, summary: clip(summary || title, 400), source, categoryHint, publishedAt });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function arxivUrl(cat: string, n: number): string {
  return `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=cat:${cat}&start=0&max_results=${n}&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending`;
}

interface Feed {
  name: string;
  url: string;
  category: CategoryId;
  limit: number;
  wideLimit: number;

/**
 * Normally use 72 hours, extending to one week only for sparse categories.
 * Unparsable dates are kept and passed to the judge as supplied by the feed.
 */
function isFresh(c: Candidate, hours = FRESH_HOURS): boolean {
  if (!c.publishedAt) return true;
  const t = Date.parse(c.publishedAt);
  if (Number.isNaN(t)) return true;
  return Date.now() - t <= hours * 3_600_000;
}

/**
 * Interleave by category so one prolific feed cannot monopolise the judging
 * slots. Without this, MusicRadar's 50-item feed would crowd out every arXiv
 * paper before the judge ever saw one.
 */
function interleaveByCategory(candidates: Candidate[], cap: number): Candidate[] {
  const buckets = new Map<CategoryId, Candidate[]>();
  for (const c of candidates) {
    const bucket = buckets.get(c.categoryHint) ?? [];
    bucket.push(c);
    buckets.set(c.categoryHint, bucket);
  }
  const lists = [...buckets.values()];
  const out: Candidate[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; out.length < cap; i++) {
    let added = false;
    for (const list of lists) {
      if (i < list.length) {
        out.push(list[i]);
        added = true;
        if (out.length >= cap) break;
      }
    }
    if (!added) break;
  }
  return out;
}

/** Source routing is shared with catalogue coverage checks. No network work here. */
export function feedsForCategories(active: CategoryId[], wide = false): Feed[] {
  const activeSet = new Set(active);
  return [
    ...FEEDS.filter(f => activeSet.has(f.category) && (wide || !f.wideOnly)),
    ...active.filter(id => CATEGORIES[id]?.query).slice(0, MAX_SELECTED_CATEGORIES).map(id => ({
      name: `subject:${id}`, category: id, limit: 8, wideLimit: 12, verified: false,
      url: `https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(CATEGORIES[id].query! + ' when:7d')}&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US:en`,
    })),
  ];
}

export function balanceFeeds(feeds:Feed[],active:CategoryId[],limit:number):Feed[] {
  const groups=active.map(c=>feeds.filter(f=>f.category===c));
  const selected:Feed[]=[];
  for(let i=0;selected.length<limit;i++) {
    let added=false;
    for(const group of groups)if(group[i]&&selected.length<limit){selected.push(group[i]);added=true;}
    if(!added)break;
  }
  return selected;
}

/** Pull candidates across the agent's active categories, newest first. Partial results are normal. */
export async function discover(recordFeedResult: FeedRecorder, options: DiscoverOptions = {},
  runSource: (name:string, work:()=>Promise<Candidate[]>)=>Promise<Candidate[]> = (_name,work)=>work(),
): Promise<Candidate[]> {
  const wide = options.wide ?? false;
  const active =
    options.categories && options.categories.length > 0 ? options.categories : ALL_CATEGORY_IDS;
  const activeSet = new Set(active);
  const results: Candidate[] = [];
  const request=options.maxFetches===undefined?fetch:boundedFeedFetch(options.maxFetches);

  if (activeSet.has("emerging-tech")) {
    try {
      const hits = await runSource('hackernews',()=>fromHackerNews(wide,request));
      results.push(...hits);
      await recordFeedResult("hackernews", { ok: true, items: hits.length });
    } catch (err) {
      const message = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err);
      console.warn("[discovery] hackernews failed:", message);
      await recordFeedResult("hackernews", { ok: false, error: message });
    }
  }

  const available = feedsForCategories(active, wide);
  const feeds=options.maxFeeds===undefined?available:balanceFeeds(available,active,options.maxFeeds);

  // Fetched concurrently: ~13 feeds at 8s each would blow the cycle budget serially.
  await Promise.all(
    feeds.map(async (feed) => {
      const url = wide && feed.wideUrl ? feed.wideUrl : feed.url;
      const limit = wide ? feed.wideLimit : feed.limit;
      try {
        const items = await runSource(feed.name,async()=>parseFeed(await fetchText(url,request), feed.name, feed.category, limit));
        results.push(...items);
        // Zero parsed items counts as a failure, not a quiet day: parseFeed does
        // not filter by date, so even a dormant blog returns its old entries.
        // Zero means the format changed or the response was not a feed at all —
        // which is what a redesigned site's 200-with-an-HTML-error-page looks like.
        await recordFeedResult(feed.name, { ok: true, items: items.length });
      } catch (err) {
        const message = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err);
        console.warn(`[discovery] ${feed.name} failed:`, message);
        await recordFeedResult(feed.name, { ok: false, error: message });
      }
    }),
  );

  // Dedupe by URL, drop stale items, newest first, then balance across categories.
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const unique = results.filter((c) => {
    if (seen.has(c.url)) return false;
    seen.add(c.url);
    return true;
  });
  const fresh = unique.filter(c => isFresh(c));
  // Quiet categories need a useful pool over weekends too. Supplement only
  // categories with fewer than five recent stories, using at most a week's
  // material. The judge still sees the actual date and applies the same bar.
  const sparse = new Set(active.filter(category =>
    fresh.filter(c => c.categoryHint === category).length < PER_CATEGORY_FLOOR));
  fresh.push(...unique.filter(c => sparse.has(c.categoryHint) &&
    !isFresh(c) && isFresh(c, SPARSE_FRESH_HOURS)));
  fresh.sort((a, b) => (Date.parse(b.publishedAt ?? "") || 0) - (Date.parse(a.publishedAt ?? "") || 0));

  const base = wide ? MAX_CANDIDATES_WIDE : MAX_CANDIDATES;
  const cap = Math.min(HARD_CANDIDATE_CAP, Math.max(base, active.length * PER_CATEGORY_FLOOR));
  const balanced = interleaveByCategory(fresh, cap);
  console.log(
    `[discovery] ${balanced.length} selected (cap ${cap} for ${active.length} categories) of ${fresh.length} fresh / ${unique.length} unique, from ${new Set(balanced.map((c) => c.source)).size} sources${wide ? " (WIDE mode)" : ""}`,
  );
  return balanced;
}
````
