/**
 * The publish path: a stored post -> a post on the member's LinkedIn feed.
 *
 * Everything here is built around one failure mode being much worse than the
 * others. A post that fails to publish is a nuisance you fix and retry. A post
 * that publishes TWICE is on a real person's profile in front of their
 * colleagues and cannot be quietly undone. So:
 *
 *   1. A row in `distributions` with a UNIQUE idempotency key is claimed
 *      BEFORE the API call. Only the caller that wins that insert may publish.
 *      Concurrent cron ticks, a double-clicked button and a retried request
 *      all collapse into one attempt.
 *
 *   2. Failures are split into DEFINITE and AMBIGUOUS.
 *      - Definite (LinkedIn answered with a 4xx): the post did not go out. The
 *        claim is released so a fixed retry can proceed.
 *      - Ambiguous (timeout, network error, 5xx): we do not know whether
 *        LinkedIn accepted it. The claim is KEPT FOREVER and the post is
 *        flagged for a human to check. We cannot resolve this automatically —
 *        reading your own posts back requires r_member_social, a restricted
 *        scope this app does not have — and guessing wrong means double
 *        posting.
 *
 *   3. A daily cap backstops any logic error upstream. LinkedIn's own limit is
 *      150 member requests/day; the point of a much lower cap is that if this
 *      code ever loops, it burns 3 posts and stops, not 150.
 */
import { getUsableToken, recordAccountError, recordAccountOk } from "./accounts";
import { query, getPool, ensureSchema } from "./db";
import { assemblePost, checkLength } from "./format";
import { createPost, postPermalink, type PostImage } from "./linkedin";
import { safeTimeZone } from "./schedule";
import { settleSlotRun } from "./slots";
import { MAX_HASHTAGS } from "./style";
import { refreshEditNotes } from "./voice";

/**
 * Two budgets, because the two risks are completely different.
 *
 * The AGENT publishing on its own is the dangerous one: a logic error there
 * runs unattended against a real profile, so its allowance is small and set by
 * the user (agents.auto_publish_cap, 1-3).
 *
 * A HUMAN pressing Publish has already made the decision, so the only real
 * limit is LinkedIn's: 150 requests per member per day, shared with image
 * uploads and token calls. MANUAL_DAILY_CAP is a loop-breaker well inside that
 * — it exists to catch a retry storm, not to second-guess the author.
 */
export const MANUAL_DAILY_CAP = Number(process.env.MANUAL_DAILY_CAP ?? 40);

/** LinkedIn's documented per-member ceiling, for reporting headroom. */
export const LINKEDIN_DAILY_REQUESTS = 150;

/**
 * Hard bounds on the agent's own allowance. Matches MAX_SLOTS in lib/slots.ts —
 * the cap is derived from how many slots the author actually scheduled, so the
 * two ceilings have to agree or a legal fifth slot would fail at send time.
 */
export const MAX_AUTO_CAP = 5;

export type PublishSource = "auto" | "manual";
export interface ReviewedPost {text:string;hashtags:string[];media:string[]}

export type DistributeResult =
  | { ok: true; postUrn: string; permalink: string }
  | { ok: false; reason: string; needsReauth?: boolean; ambiguous?: boolean; alreadyClaimed?: boolean };

interface PostRow {
  seq: number;
  text: string;
  status: string;
  category: string | null;
  media_json: string[];
  sources_json: string[];
  hashtags_json: string[];
  /** Joined from agents — the hashtag cap has to match what the author chose. */
  style_json: unknown;
  auto_publish_cap: number | null;
  /** Joined from agents — the cap is counted against the author's calendar day. */
  timezone: string | null;
  auto_eligible: boolean;
}

/** Publishing is disabled entirely unless this is explicitly turned on. */
export function liveModeEnabled(): boolean {
  return process.env.LINKEDIN_LIVE === "true" && process.env.BYLINE_TEST_MODE !== "true";
}

/**
 * Sends so far TODAY in the operator's own timezone, split by who initiated them.
 *
 * Deliberately a calendar day rather than a rolling 24 hours. The rolling
 * version is subtly wrong the moment more than one post is scheduled per day:
 * a post sent at 21:00 yesterday is still inside a rolling window when the
 * 09:00 slot fires this morning, so a later slot gets refused with
 * `auto_cap_reached` for no reason a human could see. "Three posts a day" means
 * three per calendar day, and the day that matters is the author's, not UTC's.
 *
 * The boundary is computed in Postgres so DST transitions are handled by the
 * timezone database rather than by arithmetic here. safeTimeZone guards the
 * input because `AT TIME ZONE` throws on an unknown zone.
 */
export async function sendsToday(
  agentId: string,
  timezone?: string | null,
): Promise<{ auto: number; manual: number }> {
  const zone = safeTimeZone(timezone);
  const rows = await query<{ source: string; n: string }>(
    `SELECT source, count(*)::text AS n FROM distributions
      WHERE agent_id = $1 AND status = 'sent'
        AND settled_at >= (date_trunc('day', now() AT TIME ZONE $2) AT TIME ZONE $2)
      GROUP BY source`,
    [agentId, zone],
  );
  const by = new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.source, Number(r.n)]));
  return { auto: by.get("auto") ?? 0, manual: by.get("manual") ?? 0 };
}

async function loadImages(mediaIds: string[], agentId: string): Promise<PostImage[]> {
  if (mediaIds.length === 0) return [];
  const rows = await query<{ id: string; linkedin_urn: string; alt_text: string | null }>(
    "SELECT id, linkedin_urn, alt_text FROM media_assets WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]) AND agent_id=$2 AND status = 'uploaded'",
    [mediaIds, agentId],
  );
  // Preserve the author's ordering — ANY() gives no ordering guarantee, and on
  // a multi-image post the sequence is a deliberate choice.
  const byId = new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.id, r]));
  return mediaIds
    .map((id) => byId.get(id))
    .filter((r): r is NonNullable<typeof r> => !!r)
    .map((r) => ({ imageUrn: r.linkedin_urn, altText: r.alt_text ?? undefined }));
}

/**
 * Publish one stored post. Safe to call twice: the second call returns
 * `alreadyClaimed` without touching LinkedIn.
 */
export async function publishPost(
  agentId: string,
  seq: number,
  source: PublishSource = "manual",
  reviewed?: ReviewedPost,
): Promise<DistributeResult> {
  const rows = await query<PostRow>(
    `SELECT p.seq, p.text, p.status, p.category, p.media_json, p.sources_json, p.hashtags_json,
            a.style_json, a.auto_publish_cap, a.timezone,
            (a.active AND NOT a.paused AND p.scheduled_for <= now()
             AND (p.hold_until IS NULL OR p.hold_until <= now())
             AND (p.cleared_at IS NOT NULL OR
               (a.auto_publish AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM post_slots s WHERE s.id=p.slot_id AND s.auto_publish)))) AS auto_eligible
       FROM posts p JOIN agents a ON a.id = p.agent_id
      WHERE p.agent_id = $1 AND p.seq = $2`,
    [agentId, seq],
  );
  const post = rows[0];
  if (!post) return { ok: false, reason: "post_not_found" };
  if (source === 'auto' && !post.auto_eligible) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'The schedule, approval or pause setting changed before this send.' };
  }
  if(reviewed&&(!['draft','approved','failed','missed'].includes(post.status)||post.text!==reviewed.text||JSON.stringify(post.hashtags_json??[])!==JSON.stringify(reviewed.hashtags)||JSON.stringify(post.media_json??[])!==JSON.stringify(reviewed.media))) {
    return {ok:false,reason:'This post changed on another device. Refresh and review it again.'};
  }
  if (post.status === "published") return { ok: false, reason: "already_published", alreadyClaimed: true };
  if (!['draft', 'approved', 'failed', 'missed'].includes(post.status)) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'This post cannot be published in its current state. Refresh and review it in My Posts.' };
  }

  // Explicit isolated testing only; this branch never calls LinkedIn.
  if (process.env.BYLINE_TEST_MODE === 'true' && process.env.BYLINE_LOCAL_ONLY === 'true') {
    await query(`UPDATE posts SET status='published',published_at=now(),rationale='Local approval simulation; not posted to LinkedIn' WHERE agent_id=$1 AND seq=$2 AND status<>'published'`,[agentId,seq]);
    return {ok:true,postUrn:`local-simulation:${agentId}:${seq}`,permalink:''};
  }

  if (!liveModeEnabled()) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "live_mode_disabled — set LINKEDIN_LIVE=true to publish for real" };
  }

  // The agent's allowance and the author's are counted separately, so a day of
  // manual posting never blocks tomorrow's scheduled one, and vice versa.
  const sent = await sendsToday(agentId, post.timezone);
  if (source === "auto") {
    const cap = Math.min(MAX_AUTO_CAP, Math.max(1, post.auto_publish_cap ?? 1));
    if (sent.auto >= cap) {
      return { ok: false, reason: `auto_cap_reached:${sent.auto}/${cap}` };
    }
  } else if (sent.manual >= MANUAL_DAILY_CAP) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `manual_cap_reached:${sent.manual}/${MANUAL_DAILY_CAP}` };
  }

  // ---- Claim the send. This insert is the concurrency control for the whole
  // feature; nothing below runs unless it succeeds.
  const idempotencyKey = `${agentId}:${seq}`;
  const claim = await query<{ id: string }>(
    `INSERT INTO distributions (agent_id, seq, idempotency_key, status, attempts, source)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, 'in_flight', 1, $4)
     ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
     RETURNING id`,
    [agentId, seq, idempotencyKey, source],
  );
  if (claim.length === 0) {
    const existing = await query<{ status: string; external_urn: string | null; last_error: string | null }>(
      "SELECT status, external_urn, last_error FROM distributions WHERE idempotency_key = $1",
      [idempotencyKey],
    );
    const prior = existing[0];
    if (prior?.status === "sent" && prior.external_urn) {
      return { ok: true, postUrn: prior.external_urn, permalink: postPermalink(prior.external_urn) };
    }
    return {
      ok: false,
      alreadyClaimed: true,
      ambiguous: prior?.status === "in_flight",
      reason: `already_claimed:${prior?.status ?? "unknown"}${prior?.last_error ? ` (${prior.last_error})` : ""}`,
    };
  }
  const distributionId = claim[0].id;

  // 'in_flight' is a valid target here: an ambiguous outcome records the error
  // while deliberately KEEPING the claim, so nothing ever retries it.
  const settle = async (
    status: "sent" | "failed" | "in_flight",
    fields: { urn?: string; error?: string },
  ): Promise<void> => {
    await query(
      // settled_at stays NULL while in_flight — listAmbiguousSends finds these
      // by age, and stamping them as settled would hide them from that query.
      `UPDATE distributions
          SET status = $2, external_urn = $3, last_error = $4,
              settled_at = CASE WHEN $2 = 'in_flight' THEN NULL ELSE now() END
        WHERE id = $1`,
      [distributionId, status, fields.urn ?? null, fields.error?.slice(0, 500) ?? null],
    );
  };

  /** Definite rejection: release the claim so a corrected retry can run. */
  const releaseClaim = async (error: string): Promise<void> => {
    await query("DELETE FROM distributions WHERE id = $1", [distributionId]);
    await query("UPDATE posts SET status = 'failed' WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2", [agentId, seq]);
    console.warn(`[distribute] agent=${agentId} p${seq} definite failure, claim released: ${error}`);
  };

  const token = await getUsableToken(agentId);
  if (!token.ok) {
    await releaseClaim(`token_${token.reason}`);
    return {
      ok: false,
      reason: `linkedin_${token.reason}`,
      needsReauth: token.reason === "expired" || token.reason === "not_connected",
    };
  }

  const images = await loadImages(post.media_json ?? [], agentId);
  // A source link is worth including on a text post, but on an image post it
  // competes with the image for the reader's attention and looks like spam.
  const sourceUrl = images.length === 0 ? post.sources_json?.[0] : undefined;
  const text = assemblePost({
    body: post.text,
    sourceUrl,
    hashtags: post.hashtags_json ?? [],
    // Publish the reviewed post's tags, even if the voice has since changed.
    maxHashtags: MAX_HASHTAGS,
  });

  const length = checkLength(text);
  if (!length.withinLimit) {
    await releaseClaim(`too_long:${length.escapedChars}`);
    return { ok: false, reason: `post_too_long:${length.escapedChars}_escaped_chars` };
  }

  const created = await createPost({
    token: token.token,
    authorUrn: token.memberUrn,
    text,
    images,
  });

  if (created.ok) {
    await settle("sent", { urn: created.data.postUrn });
    await query(
      `UPDATE posts SET status = 'published', published_at = now(), linkedin_text = $3
        WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2`,
      [agentId, seq, text],
    );
    await recordAccountOk(agentId);
    // A published post the author edited is a new training pair. Refreshing
    // here rather than on a timer means the notes update exactly when new
    // evidence appears. Deliberately not awaited for its result and never
    // allowed to throw: this is an improvement to future posts, and it must not
    // be able to affect the outcome of a send that already succeeded.
    void refreshEditNotes(agentId);
    console.log(`[distribute] agent=${agentId} p${seq} published ${created.data.postUrn}`);
    return {
      ok: true,
      postUrn: created.data.postUrn,
      permalink: postPermalink(created.data.postUrn),
    };
  }

  await recordAccountError(agentId, created.reason);

  // AMBIGUOUS: no HTTP answer, or LinkedIn failed server-side. We cannot tell
  // whether the post went out, so the claim is kept and a human is asked.
  const ambiguous = created.status === undefined || created.status >= 500;
  if (ambiguous) {
    await settle("in_flight", { error: `AMBIGUOUS: ${created.reason}` });
    await query("UPDATE posts SET status = 'unknown' WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2", [agentId, seq]);
    console.error(
      `[distribute] agent=${agentId} p${seq} AMBIGUOUS outcome (${created.reason}) — not retrying; needs manual check`,
    );
    return { ok: false, ambiguous: true, reason: `ambiguous:${created.reason}`, needsReauth: created.needsReauth };
  }

  await releaseClaim(created.reason);
  return { ok: false, reason: created.reason, needsReauth: created.needsReauth };
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------- the send pass

interface DuePostRow {
  agent_id: string;
  seq: number;
  slot_id: string | null;
  scheduled_for: Date;
  run_date: Date | null;
  minutes_late: string;
}

export interface DuePublishResult {
  agentId: string;
  seq: number;
  outcome: "published" | "failed" | "missed" | "ambiguous";
  detail?: string;
}

/**
 * Publish everything whose time has come. The other half of the split that
 * lib/slots.ts creates — cycles write, this sends.
 *
 * A post qualifies only if ALL of these hold:
 *   - its scheduled_for has passed,
 *   - it is not held open in the composer,
 *   - and EITHER a human cleared it OR its slot is set to publish on its own.
 *
 * That last clause is the safety property the whole feature turns on. On a
 * hold-mode slot an unreviewed draft simply never qualifies: it does not fail,
 * it is not retried, it just waits — which is exactly what "nothing I have not
 * read reaches my profile" has to mean.
 *
 * Sends count against the AGENT's allowance even when a human pressed Clear,
 * because a cleared slot post is still part of the scheduled cadence. Only the
 * explicit "Send now" override counts as manual.
 */
export async function publishDuePosts(missedAfterMinutes = 45): Promise<DuePublishResult[]> {
  const due = await query<DuePostRow>(
    `SELECT p.agent_id, p.seq, p.slot_id, p.scheduled_for,
            r.run_date,
            EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - p.scheduled_for)) / 60 AS minutes_late
       FROM posts p
       JOIN agents a ON a.id = p.agent_id
       LEFT JOIN post_slots s ON s.id = p.slot_id
       LEFT JOIN slot_runs r ON r.slot_id = p.slot_id AND r.post_seq = p.seq
      WHERE p.scheduled_for IS NOT NULL
        AND p.scheduled_for <= now()
        AND p.status IN ('draft', 'approved', 'failed')
        AND (p.hold_until IS NULL OR p.hold_until <= now())
        -- Either a human cleared it, or BOTH switches say it may go on its own.
        --
        -- The agent-level flag is ANDed deliberately. Without it the master
        -- "publish without me" control was dead: the send pass consulted only
        -- the slot, so turning the global switch off changed nothing and the
        -- agent kept publishing. A global stop that does not stop anything is
        -- worse than no control at all.
        --
        -- Clearing still wins over both. Saying yes to a specific post is an
        -- explicit decision about that post, and a global default should not
        -- override it.
        AND (
          p.cleared_at IS NOT NULL
          OR (COALESCE(s.auto_publish, FALSE) AND a.auto_publish)
        )
        AND a.active AND NOT a.paused
      ORDER BY p.scheduled_for`,
  );

  const results: DuePublishResult[] = [];

  for (const row of due) {
    const runDate = row.run_date ? row.run_date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : null;

    // Too late to be worth sending. This also bounds retries: a definite
    // failure leaves the post eligible on the next tick, and this window is
    // what stops that becoming an unbounded loop.
    if (Number(row.minutes_late) > missedAfterMinutes) {
      const missed = await query("UPDATE posts SET status = 'missed' WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2 AND scheduled_for = $3 AND status IN ('draft','approved','failed') AND (hold_until IS NULL OR hold_until<=now()) RETURNING seq", [
        row.agent_id,
        row.seq,
        row.scheduled_for,
      ]);
      if (!missed.length) continue;
      if (row.slot_id && runDate) {
        await settleSlotRun(row.slot_id, runDate, "missed", {
          detail: `Not sent within ${missedAfterMinutes} minutes of its time.`,
        });
      }
      console.warn(`[distribute] agent=${row.agent_id} p${row.seq} MISSED its slot`);
      results.push({ agentId: row.agent_id, seq: row.seq, outcome: "missed" });
      continue;
    }

    const result = await publishPost(row.agent_id, row.seq, "auto");

    if (result.ok) {
      if (row.slot_id && runDate) {
        await settleSlotRun(row.slot_id, runDate, "published", { postSeq: row.seq });
      }
      results.push({ agentId: row.agent_id, seq: row.seq, outcome: "published" });
      continue;
    }

    // Ambiguous outcomes are already frozen by publishPost and must never be
    // retried, so they are reported and left exactly as it left them.
    const outcome = result.ambiguous ? "ambiguous" : "failed";
    if (row.slot_id && runDate) {
      await settleSlotRun(row.slot_id, runDate, "failed", { detail: result.reason });
    }
    results.push({ agentId: row.agent_id, seq: row.seq, outcome, detail: result.reason });
  }

  return results;
}

/** Sends stuck in_flight — surfaced in the UI because only a human can resolve them. */
export async function listAmbiguousSends(agentId: string): Promise<
  { seq: number | null; createdAt: string; lastError: string | null }[]
> {
  const rows = await query<{ seq: number | null; created_at: Date; last_error: string | null }>(
    `SELECT seq, created_at, last_error FROM distributions
      WHERE agent_id = $1 AND status = 'in_flight' AND created_at < now() - interval '5 minutes'
      ORDER BY created_at DESC`,
    [agentId],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({
    seq: r.seq,
    createdAt: r.created_at.toISOString(),
    lastError: r.last_error,
  }));
}

/**
 * Operator override for a resolved ambiguous send: the human checked LinkedIn
 * and told us what actually happened. `didPublish: false` releases the claim
 * so the post can be retried.
 */
export async function resolveAmbiguousSend(
  agentId: string,
  seq: number,
  didPublish: boolean,
): Promise<boolean> {
  await ensureSchema();
  const client = await getPool()!.connect();
  try {
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    const pending = await client.query(
      "SELECT seq FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND seq=$2 AND status='unknown' FOR UPDATE",
      [agentId, seq],
    );
    if (!pending.rowCount) {
      await client.query('ROLLBACK');
      return false;
    }
    if (didPublish) {
    await client.query(
      `UPDATE distributions SET status = 'sent', settled_at = now(),
              last_error = 'resolved manually: confirmed published'
        WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2 AND status = 'in_flight'`,
      [agentId, seq],
    );
    await client.query(
      "UPDATE posts SET status = 'published', published_at = COALESCE(published_at, now()) WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2",
      [agentId, seq],
    );
    } else {
  await client.query(
    "DELETE FROM distributions WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2 AND status = 'in_flight'",
    [agentId, seq],
  );
  // A negative confirmation permits a deliberate retry; it must not restart
  // the scheduler and send the post before the user has reviewed it again.
  await client.query("UPDATE posts SET status = 'draft', scheduled_for = NULL, cleared_at = NULL, hold_until = NULL WHERE agent_id = $1 AND seq = $2", [agentId, seq]);
    }
    await client.query('COMMIT');
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    await client.query('ROLLBACK');
    throw error;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

/**
 * HTML entity decoding, shared by discovery (ingest), the UI (render), and
 * the backfill script. Feed titles arrive with numeric (&#8217;) and named
 * (&rsquo;) entities; both must read as text everywhere.
 */
const NAMED: Record<string, string> = {
  amp: "&",
  lt: "<",
  gt: ">",
  quot: '"',
  apos: "'",
  nbsp: " ",
  mdash: "—",
  ndash: "–",
  hellip: "…",
  rsquo: "’",
  lsquo: "‘",
  rdquo: "”",
  ldquo: "“",
  trade: "™",
  copy: "©",
  reg: "®",
};

function fromCode(n: number): string {
  try {
    return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 && n <= 0x10ffff ? String.fromCodePoint(n) : "";
  } catch {
    return "";
  }
}

export function decodeEntities(s: string): string {
  return s
    .replace(/&#(\d+);/g, (_, n: string) => fromCode(Number(n)))
    .replace(/&#x([0-9a-f]+);/gi, (_, n: string) => fromCode(parseInt(n, 16)))
    .replace(/&([a-z]+);/gi, (m: string, name: string) => NAMED[name.toLowerCase()] ?? m)
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim();
}

## Source: lib/feedhealth.ts

````text
/**
 * Which feeds still work.
 *
 * Discovery is deliberately forgiving: every source is fetched in its own
 * try/catch so one dead feed can never abort a cycle. That is right, and it is
 * also why a dying feed is invisible — it costs one `console.warn` per cycle in
 * a log nobody reads, while the other twenty-six carry the day. Over a year or
 * two that is how a reading list quietly halves with no alert ever firing.
 *
 * So each fetch records its outcome here, and the watchdog reads it. Nothing in
 * this file can fail a cycle: every function swallows its own errors, because
 * bookkeeping about the quality of discovery must never stop discovery.
 */
import { query } from "./db";

/**
 * Consecutive failures before a feed is called dead.
 *
 * High enough to ride out a transient outage — a cycle runs a few times a day,
 * so this is roughly two days of continuous failure — and low enough to notice
 * within a week. A single 500 or one timeout must never raise an alarm.
 */
export const DEAD_AFTER_FAILURES = 6;

/** And it must also have gone this long without a single success. */
export const DEAD_AFTER_DAYS = 3;

/**
 * Record one fetch.
 *
 * `items` is how many entries were parsed, and zero counts as a failure even
 * when the HTTP request succeeded. A feed that answers 200 with something
 * unparseable is exactly as useless as one that times out, and it is the more
 * likely failure — a site redesign returns a beautiful HTML error page with a
 * 200 status. Note that parseFeed does not filter by date, so a merely QUIET
 * blog still returns its old entries; zero really does mean broken.
 */
export async function recordFeedResult(
  name: string,
  outcome: { ok: true; items: number } | { ok: false; error: string },
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const good = outcome.ok && outcome.items > 0;
    if (good) {
      await query(
        `INSERT INTO feed_health (name, last_ok_at, fails_in_a_row, last_error, updated_at)
         VALUES ($1, now(), 0, NULL, now())
         ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE
            SET last_ok_at = now(), fails_in_a_row = 0, last_error = NULL, updated_at = now()`,
        [name],
      );
      return;
    }
    const detail = outcome.ok ? "fetched but nothing could be parsed" : outcome.error.slice(0, 200);
    await query(
      `INSERT INTO feed_health (name, last_failed_at, fails_in_a_row, last_error, updated_at)
       VALUES ($1, now(), 1, $2, now())
       ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE
          SET last_failed_at = now(),
              fails_in_a_row = feed_health.fails_in_a_row + 1,
              last_error = $2,
              updated_at = now()`,
      [name, detail],
    );
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[feeds] could not record health:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
  }
}

export interface DeadFeed {
  name: string;
  failsInARow: number;
  lastOkAt: string | null;
  lastError: string | null;
}

/**
 * Feeds that have failed long enough to be worth mentioning.
 *
 * Both conditions must hold. Consecutive failures alone would fire during any
 * long outage at one host; "no success for days" alone would flag a feed that
 * simply has not been consulted, because the categories it serves are switched
 * off. A feed nobody fetches is not a broken feed.
 */
export async function deadFeeds(): Promise<DeadFeed[]> {
  try {
    const rows = await query<{
      name: string;
      fails_in_a_row: number;
      last_ok_at: Date | null;
      last_error: string | null;
    }>(
      `SELECT name, fails_in_a_row, last_ok_at, last_error
         FROM feed_health
        WHERE fails_in_a_row >= $1
          AND (last_ok_at IS NULL OR last_ok_at < now() - ($2 || ' days')::interval)
        ORDER BY fails_in_a_row DESC`,
      [DEAD_AFTER_FAILURES, String(DEAD_AFTER_DAYS)],
    );
    return rows.map((r) => ({
      name: r.name,
      failsInARow: r.fails_in_a_row,
      lastOkAt: r.last_ok_at?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lastError: r.last_error,
    }));
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[feeds] could not read health:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
    return [];
  }
}

## Source: lib/format.ts

````text
/**
 * Deterministic assembly of the final LinkedIn post text.
 *
 * The model writes the body and nothing else. The source line and hashtags
 * are appended here, in code, because they are the two things a language
 * model reliably mangles: URLs get "helpfully" reworded, and hashtag
 * discipline collapses into a wall of eleven tags the moment the prompt looks
 * away. Structure that must be exact does not belong in a prompt.
 */
import { MAX_COMMENTARY, toLittleText } from "./linkedin";
import { MAX_HASHTAGS } from "./style";

/** Body budget. Escaping expands the text, so this leaves room under the 3000 cap. */
export const MAX_BODY_CHARS = 2400;

/** LinkedIn truncates around here on mobile — the hook has to land before it. */
export const FOLD_CHARS = 210;

export interface AssembleArgs {
  body: string;
  sourceUrl?: string;
  hashtags?: string[];
  /** Per-agent cap from lib/style.ts. Defaults to the house style's two. */
  maxHashtags?: number;
}

function normalizeHashtag(tag: string): string | null {
  const cleaned = tag.replace(/^#/, "").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, "");
  // LinkedIn's hashtag template only accepts a single alphanumeric word; a
  // stripped tag under 3 chars is noise rather than a topic.
  return cleaned.length >= 3 && cleaned.length <= 40 ? cleaned : null;
}

/** Collapse the runaway blank lines that LLMs produce, keeping paragraph breaks. */
function tidy(body: string): string {
  return body
    .replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")
    .replace(/[ \t]+\n/g, "\n")
    .replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n")
    .trim();
}

export function assemblePost(args: AssembleArgs): string {
  const parts = [tidy(args.body)];

  if (args.sourceUrl) parts.push(`Source: ${args.sourceUrl}`);

  // Two is a topic marker and fifteen is reach-farming, but which of those the
  // author wants is their call — the cap comes from their style config. This
  // second ceiling exists only so a corrupted config cannot produce a wall of
  // tags; it must never be LOWER than the one parseStyle allows, or a setting
  // the UI accepts would be silently truncated here.
  const cap = Math.min(MAX_HASHTAGS, Math.max(0, args.maxHashtags ?? 2));
  const tags = (args.hashtags ?? [])
    .map(normalizeHashtag)
    .filter((t): t is string => t !== null)
    .filter((t, i, all) => all.indexOf(t) === i)
    .slice(0, cap);
  if (tags.length > 0) parts.push(tags.map((t) => `#${t}`).join(" "));

  return parts.join("\n\n");
}

export interface LengthCheck {
  plainChars: number;
  escapedChars: number;
  withinLimit: boolean;
}

/**
 * Measure against the limit LinkedIn actually enforces — the ESCAPED length.
 * A post of ordinary prose with parentheses and hyphens can gain over a
 * hundred characters once every reserved character grows a backslash, so
 * checking the plaintext length alone will happily hand LinkedIn a post it
 * rejects.
 */
export function checkLength(text: string): LengthCheck {
  const escapedChars = toLittleText(text).length;
  return {
    plainChars: text.length,
    escapedChars,
    withinLimit: escapedChars <= MAX_COMMENTARY,
  };
}

/** The text above the "see more" fold — what most people will actually read. */
export function hookOf(text: string): string {
  const firstLine = text.split("\n")[0];
  return firstLine.length <= FOLD_CHARS ? firstLine : firstLine.slice(0, FOLD_CHARS).trimEnd() + "…";
}

## Source: lib/http-body.ts

````text
/** Bound decoded bytes even when content-length is missing or the response is compressed. */
export async function boundedText(response: Response | Request, maxBytes: number): Promise<string> {
  if (!response.body) return '';
  const reader = response.body.getReader();
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
  let size = 0;
  let text = '';
  try {
    while (true) {
      const {value, done} = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      size += value.byteLength;
      if (size > maxBytes) {
        await reader.cancel();
        throw new Error('Response exceeds size limit');
      }
      text += decoder.decode(value, {stream:true});
    }
    return text + decoder.decode();
  } finally { reader.releaseLock(); }
}

## Source: lib/judge-core.ts

````text
/**
 * Editorial judging: ONE batched LLM call scores every candidate 0-10 on
 * five criteria and assigns it a category. Publish only the single top
 * candidate, and only above the threshold.
 *
 * A day that publishes nothing is correct behavior — there is no floor
 * forcing a post out. On a personal LinkedIn profile that matters more than
 * it did in the original feed: silence costs nothing, a weak post costs
 * credibility with people who actually know you.
 */
import type { CategoryId } from "./categories";
import { LEGACY_CATEGORY_IDS as ALL_CATEGORY_IDS, CATEGORIES, categoryBlock, isCategoryId } from "./categories";
import type { Candidate } from "./discovery";
import { parseJson, type Completion } from "./llm-contract";
import type { MemoryContext } from "./memory";
import type { PersonaRecord } from "./persona-prompt";
import { personaBlock } from "./persona-prompt";

export const PUBLISH_THRESHOLD = 6.5;

export function relevanceTotal(scores: Scores, category: unknown, active: CategoryId[]): number {
  const total=Math.round((scores.persona_fit+scores.category_fit+scores.novelty+scores.timeliness+scores.non_duplication)/5*100)/100;
  return scores.category_fit>=7 && scores.persona_fit>=6 && isCategoryId(category) && active.includes(category)
    ? total : Math.min(total,PUBLISH_THRESHOLD-0.01);
}

/**
 * Output tokens to allow for a batch of `n` candidates.
 *
 * One scored object runs about 70-90 tokens once the one-line reason is
 * included, so the budget has to track the batch or the array is cut off
 * mid-object. Ceilinged at 8192 because past that the model is being asked for
 * more than any single response should carry.
 */
export function outputBudgetFor(n: number): number {
  return Math.min(8192, Math.max(2048, 400 + n * 110));
}

export interface Scores {
  persona_fit: number;
  category_fit: number;
  novelty: number;
  timeliness: number;
  non_duplication: number;
}

export interface ScoredCandidate extends Candidate {
  scores: Scores;
  total: number;
  reason: string;
  category: CategoryId;
}

interface RawScore extends Scores {
  index: number;
  category: string;
  reason: string;
}

function inRange(n: unknown): n is number {
  return typeof n === "number" && n >= 0 && n <= 10;
}

/** One entry, judged on its own merits. */
export function isRawScore(s: unknown): s is RawScore {
  const o = s as RawScore;
  return (
    !!o &&
    typeof o.index === "number" &&
    inRange(o.persona_fit) &&
    inRange(o.category_fit) &&
    inRange(o.novelty) &&
    inRange(o.timeliness) &&
    inRange(o.non_duplication) &&
    typeof o.category === "string" &&
    typeof o.reason === "string"
  );
}

/**
 * Accept the array, then keep the entries that are actually usable.
 *
 * This used to require `v.every(...)` — every single entry valid or the whole
 * batch discarded. With 34 candidates in one response that is a bad bet: one
 * truncated tail object, one score of 11, one missing `reason`, and a day's
 * discovery is thrown away with `judge_json_invalid_after_retry` and no clue
 * which entry was at fault.
 *
 * Dropping bad entries is safe rather than lax. Nothing is published unscored:
 * a candidate that does not survive validation simply is not considered, the
 * caller still sorts by total and still refuses to publish anything below
 * PUBLISH_THRESHOLD. The failure mode this replaces was strictly worse — it
 * discarded the GOOD entries too.
 */
function isRawScores(v: unknown): v is RawScore[] {
  return Array.isArray(v) && v.some(isRawScore);
}

const SYSTEM = `You are the editorial judgment of the professional described in PERSONA, who posts on LinkedIn about their genuine interests. Use their chosen industry and categories; do not assume an engineering background. Score EVERY numbered candidate 0-10 on:
- persona_fit: would THIS person post about this, given their voice, interests and opinions?
- category_fit: does it substantively address one of the exact selected subjects, and is it substantial enough to be worth a post rather than a link? A passing mention, shared keyword, or neighbouring industry does not qualify. Score these below 5. Never force a connection to fill a slot.
- novelty: does it add something beyond what has already been covered (see PRIOR COVERAGE)?
- timeliness: is there a reason to write about it right now?
- non_duplication: 10 = nothing like it in prior coverage; 0 = already covered.

Also assign "category": the id of the single active category it best belongs to.
The active categories are the author's current scope. If older persona interests describe another field, use the current scope; never reject an otherwise suitable story just to preserve a previous industry.

Be discriminating. This publishes to a real professional profile where the author's colleagues will read it, so most candidates in a batch deserve middling or low scores. Reserve 8+ for something the author would genuinely stop and write about. Product announcements with nothing new in them, funding rounds, and press releases restating a spec sheet are 3s and 4s no matter how big the brand.

Respond with a JSON array, one object per candidate, exactly:
[{"index": number, "persona_fit": number, "category_fit": number, "novelty": number, "timeliness": number, "non_duplication": number, "category": "category-id", "reason": "one line"}]
Include every candidate index exactly once.`;

/**
 * What the profile has actually been publishing, by category.
 *
 * Scoring each candidate purely on its own merits is right for quality and
 * wrong for range: whichever category happens to produce the strongest stories
 * wins every single cycle, and a profile that watches seven interests quietly
 * becomes a profile about one. non_duplication catches a repeated STORY; it has
 * nothing to say about a repeated subject.
 *
 * This tilts the bar rather than reserving slots. Nothing here can force out a
 * post the judge does not rate — an under-covered category still has to earn
 * its score, and a silent day is still an acceptable outcome.
 */
function coverageBlock(active: CategoryId[], recent: CategoryId[]): string {
  if (recent.length === 0) return "RECENT COVERAGE BY CATEGORY: nothing published yet — score purely on merit.";
  const counts = new Map<CategoryId, number>();
  for (const c of recent) counts.set(c, (counts.get(c) ?? 0) + 1);
  const lines = active.map((id) => {
    const n = counts.get(id) ?? 0;
    return `- ${id} (${CATEGORIES[id].label}): ${n} of the last ${recent.length} posts`;
  });
  return [
    `RECENT COVERAGE BY CATEGORY (last ${recent.length} posts):`,
    ...lines,
    "This profile is meant to cover all of its active categories, not the one that writes most easily.",
    "A candidate in a category that already dominates the list above must be clearly better — higher novelty and a real reason to write now — to deserve another post. A candidate in an active category with little or no recent coverage is worth more, all else equal.",
    "Do not invent merit to fill a gap. If nothing outside the dominant category is any good, score it that way and let the day be silent.",
  ].join("\n");
}

function candidateLine(c: Candidate, i: number, summaryLen: number): string {
  return `${i}. [${c.source} · likely ${c.categoryHint} · published ${c.publishedAt || 'date unavailable'}] ${c.title}\n   ${c.summary.slice(0, summaryLen)}`;
}

function buildUser(
  persona: PersonaRecord,
  categories: CategoryId[],
  candidates: Candidate[],
  memory: MemoryContext,
  priorFingerprints: string[],
  recentCategories: CategoryId[],
  summaryLen: number,
  factCap: number,
): string {
  const priorParts = [...memory.facts.slice(0, factCap), ...priorFingerprints.slice(0, factCap)];
  return [
    personaBlock(persona),
    "",
    categoryBlock(categories),
    "",
    coverageBlock(categories, recentCategories),
    "",
    `PRIOR COVERAGE AND POSITIONS (memory source: ${memory.source}):`,
    priorParts.length > 0 ? priorParts.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n") : "- none yet",
    "",
    `CANDIDATES (${candidates.length}):`,
    `Current date: ${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}. Score timeliness using the publication dates; older material must still be useful today.`,
    ...candidates.map((c, i) => candidateLine(c, i, summaryLen)),
  ].join("\n");
}

export interface JudgeOutcome {
  scored: ScoredCandidate[]; // sorted by total desc
  callsUsed: number;
  servedBy?: string;
}

export async function judgeCandidates(
  complete: Completion,
  persona: PersonaRecord,
  categories: CategoryId[],
  candidates: Candidate[],
  memory: MemoryContext,
  priorFingerprints: string[],
  /** Categories of the most recent posts, newest first. Drives the coverage tilt. */
  recentCategories: CategoryId[] = [],
): Promise<{ ok: true; data: JudgeOutcome } | { ok: false; reason: string }> {
  if (candidates.length === 0) return { ok: false, reason: "no_candidates" };

  const active = categories.length > 0 ? categories : ALL_CATEGORY_IDS;
  const recent = recentCategories.filter((c) => active.includes(c));
  const user = buildUser(persona, active, candidates, memory, priorFingerprints, recent, 300, 10);
  // Compact variant for the 16K-TPM Gemma path: shorter summaries, fewer facts.
  const compactUser = buildUser(persona, active, candidates, memory, priorFingerprints, recent, 80, 5);

  let callsUsed = 0;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
    const res = await complete({
      system:
        attempt === 0
          ? SYSTEM
          : SYSTEM +
            "\nYour previous reply was not valid JSON of the required shape. Output ONLY the JSON array.",
      user,
      compactUser,
      jsonMode: true,
      // Scaled to the batch. A fixed 3072 was comfortable for the 12-15
      // candidates a normal cycle produces and far too tight for the 34 that
      // WIDE mode yields, so the array came back truncated mid-object — valid
      // JSON nowhere, and the whole day's discovery discarded.
      maxOutputTokens: outputBudgetFor(candidates.length),
    });
    callsUsed++;
    if (!res.ok) return { ok: false, reason: res.reason };

    const raw = parseJson(res.text, isRawScores);
    if (!raw) {
      // Say what actually came back. "invalid JSON" with no sample is the least
      // actionable log line in the system — it cannot distinguish a truncated
      // response from a refusal from a model wrapping the array in prose.
      const text = res.text.trim();
      console.warn(
        `[judge] unusable response from ${res.model} (attempt ${attempt + 1}): ` +
          `${text.length} chars, ends ${JSON.stringify(text.slice(-120))}`,
      );
      continue; // one stricter retry, then give up — never publish unscored
    }

    const scored: ScoredCandidate[] = [];
    for (const s of raw) {
      const c = candidates[s.index];
      if (!c) continue;
      const total =
        Math.round(
          ((s.persona_fit + s.category_fit + s.novelty + s.timeliness + s.non_duplication) / 5) *
            100,
        ) / 100;
      // Fall back to the source's hint if the model invents a category id.
      const category: CategoryId =
        isCategoryId(s.category) && active.includes(s.category)
          ? s.category
          : active.includes(c.categoryHint)
            ? c.categoryHint
            : active[0];
      scored.push({
        ...c,
        scores: {
          persona_fit: s.persona_fit,
          category_fit: s.category_fit,
          novelty: s.novelty,
          timeliness: s.timeliness,
          non_duplication: s.non_duplication,
        },
        // Relevance is a gate, not an average that novelty can compensate for.
        total: relevanceTotal(s,s.category,active),
        category,
        reason: s.reason.slice(0, 300),
      });
    }
    if (scored.length === 0) continue;
    if (scored.length < candidates.length) {
      // Not fatal, but worth seeing: a model that drops candidates every cycle
      // is quietly shrinking the pool the winner is chosen from.
      console.warn(
        `[judge] scored ${scored.length} of ${candidates.length} candidates — ${candidates.length - scored.length} entries were unusable`,
      );
    }

    scored.sort((a, b) => b.total - a.total);
    return { ok: true, data: { scored, callsUsed, servedBy: res.model } };
  }
  return { ok: false, reason: "judge_json_invalid_after_retry" };
}

/**
 * Typed LinkedIn API client. Modeled on the Breeth client in this codebase:
 * every function returns { ok: true, data } | { ok: false, reason } and NEVER
 * throws, so a LinkedIn outage degrades the product instead of crashing a
 * cycle.
 *
 * Scope: personal-profile posting via the versioned APIs.
 *   POST /rest/posts                      create a post as urn:li:person:{id}
 *   POST /rest/images?action=initializeUpload   register an image upload
 *   GET  /v2/userinfo                     OIDC identity -> person URN
 *   POST /oauth/v2/accessToken            authorization-code exchange
 *
 * Both versioned endpoints require Linkedin-Version (YYYYMM) and
 * X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0. LinkedIn sunsets versions about a year
 * out, so the version lives in an env var — bumping it must never require a
 * code change.
 *
 * RETRY POLICY, deliberately asymmetric:
 *   - Reads and upload registration retry once on 5xx/network.
 *   - createPost NEVER retries. A timeout does not mean LinkedIn rejected the
 *     post; retrying is how you publish the same thing twice to a real human's
 *     profile. Ambiguity is escalated to a person (see lib/distribute.ts).
 */

export type LinkedInResult<T> =
  | { ok: true; data: T }
  | { ok: false; reason: string; status?: number; needsReauth?: boolean; retryable?: boolean };

const AUTH_BASE = "https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2";
const API_BASE = "https://api.linkedin.com";

const TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000;
const UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;

/** Scopes for the two self-serve products: Sign In with LinkedIn (OIDC) + Share on LinkedIn. */
export const SCOPES = ["openid", "profile", "email", "w_member_social"] as const;

/** LinkedIn sunsets versioned APIs ~12 months out; override without a redeploy. */
export function apiVersion(): string {
  return process.env.LINKEDIN_API_VERSION ?? "202607";
}

/** Warn once the pinned version is this old. Sunset is ~12 months. */
const VERSION_WARN_MONTHS = 10;

/**
 * How old the pinned API version is, in months, and whether that is a problem.
 *
 * This is the one guaranteed breakage with no natural warning. The version is a
 * YYYYMM string frozen in an environment variable, LinkedIn retires versions
 * about a year after release, and the day it happens every publish starts
 * failing with a version error — an alert that arrives strictly AFTER a post
 * did not go out.
 *
 * Ten months gives two months to bump one variable, which is the entire fix.
 * Returns null if the pin is unparseable, which is not worth an alarm: a
 * malformed version fails loudly on the very next request anyway.
 */
export function apiVersionAge(): { version: string; months: number; stale: boolean } | null {
  const version = apiVersion();
  const match = /^(\d{4})(\d{2})$/.exec(version);
  if (!match) return null;
  const year = Number(match[1]);
  const month = Number(match[2]);
  if (month < 1 || month > 12) return null;

  const now = new Date();
  const months =
    (now.getUTCFullYear() - year) * 12 + (now.getUTCMonth() + 1 - month);
  return { version, months, stale: months >= VERSION_WARN_MONTHS };
}

function versionedHeaders(token: string): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
    "LinkedIn-Version": apiVersion(),
    "X-Restli-Protocol-Version": "2.0.0",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  };
}

async function withTimeout<T>(
  ms: number,
  run: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ms);
  try {
    return await run(controller.signal);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

/** Map a failed response to a structured reason. 401 is the re-auth signal. */
async function toFailure(res: Response): Promise<Extract<LinkedInResult<never>, { ok: false }>> {
  let detail = "";
  try {
    detail = (await res.text()).slice(0, 400);
  } catch {
    /* body already consumed or unreadable — status alone is enough */
  }
  return {
    ok: false,
    status: res.status,
    reason: `http_${res.status}${detail ? `: ${detail}` : ""}`,
    // 401 means the 60-day token expired or was revoked: a human must reconnect.
    needsReauth: res.status === 401,
    retryable: res.status >= 500 || res.status === 429,
  };
}

function toNetworkFailure(err: unknown): Extract<LinkedInResult<never>, { ok: false }> {
  const message = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err);
  return {
    ok: false,
    reason: message === "The operation was aborted." ? "timeout" : `network: ${message}`,
    retryable: true,
  };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ little text

/**
 * Reserved characters in LinkedIn's "little" text format. EVERY one of these
 * must be backslash-escaped in commentary even when it is not being used as
 * markup — an unescaped parenthesis in ordinary prose is enough to corrupt or
 * reject a post, which is why no caller is trusted to remember this.
 */
const RESERVED = ["\\", "|", "{", "}", "@", "[", "]", "(", ")", "<", ">", "#", "*", "_", "~"];

function escapeLittle(text: string): string {
  let out = text;
  // Backslash FIRST — escaping it after the others would double-escape them.
  for (const ch of RESERVED) {
    out = out.split(ch).join(`\\${ch}`);
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Convert plain post text into little format, preserving intended hashtags.
 *
 * A literal "#tag" escaped to "\#tag" renders as inert text — to get a real
 * clickable hashtag LinkedIn requires the {hashtag|\#|tag} template. So
 * hashtag tokens are lifted out before escaping and re-inserted as templates.
 * Only [A-Za-z0-9] tags qualify; anything else stays plain text.
 */
export function toLittleText(text: string): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  const pattern = /(^|\s)#([A-Za-z0-9]+)\b/g;
  let last = 0;
  let match: RegExpExecArray | null;

  while ((match = pattern.exec(text)) !== null) {
    parts.push(escapeLittle(text.slice(last, match.index + match[1].length)));
    parts.push(`{hashtag|\\#|${match[2]}}`);
    last = match.index + match[0].length;
  }
  parts.push(escapeLittle(text.slice(last)));
  return parts.join("");
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------ oauth

export function authorizeUrl(state: string, redirectUri: string): string | null {
  const clientId = process.env.LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID;
  if (!clientId) return null;
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    response_type: "code",
    client_id: clientId,
    redirect_uri: redirectUri,
    state,
    scope: SCOPES.join(" "),
  });
  return `${AUTH_BASE}/authorization?${params.toString()}`;
}

export interface TokenGrant {
  accessToken: string;
  expiresInSeconds: number;
  refreshToken?: string;
  scope?: string;
}

async function tokenRequest(body: URLSearchParams): Promise<LinkedInResult<TokenGrant>> {
  const clientId = process.env.LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID;
  const clientSecret = process.env.LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET;
  if (!clientId || !clientSecret) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "missing_linkedin_client_credentials" };
  }
  body.set("client_id", clientId);
  body.set("client_secret", clientSecret);

  try {
    const res = await withTimeout(TIMEOUT_MS, (signal) =>
      fetch(`${AUTH_BASE}/accessToken`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
        body,
        signal,
      }),
    );
    if (!res.ok) return await toFailure(res);
    const json = (await res.json()) as {
      access_token?: string;
      expires_in?: number;
      refresh_token?: string;
      scope?: string;
    };
    if (!json.access_token || typeof json.expires_in !== "number") {
      return { ok: false, reason: "token_response_malformed" };
    }
    return {
      ok: true,
      data: {
        accessToken: json.access_token,
        expiresInSeconds: json.expires_in,
        refreshToken: json.refresh_token,
        scope: json.scope,
      },
    };
  } catch (err) {
    return toNetworkFailure(err);
  }
}

export function exchangeCode(code: string, redirectUri: string): Promise<LinkedInResult<TokenGrant>> {
  return tokenRequest(
    new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "authorization_code", code, redirect_uri: redirectUri }),
  );
}

/**
 * Only usable by apps approved for programmatic refresh tokens (Marketing
 * Developer Platform partners). A standard self-serve app never receives a
 * refresh_token, so this exists for the day the app is approved — callers must
 * treat "no refresh token stored" as the normal case, not an error.
 */
export function refreshAccessToken(refreshToken: string): Promise<LinkedInResult<TokenGrant>> {
  return tokenRequest(
    new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token: refreshToken }),
  );
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------- identity

export interface MemberIdentity {
  personUrn: string;
  name?: string;
  picture?: string;
  email?: string;
}

/** OIDC userinfo. `sub` is the member id; the Posts author URN is urn:li:person:{sub}. */
export async function getMemberIdentity(token: string): Promise<LinkedInResult<MemberIdentity>> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await withTimeout(TIMEOUT_MS, (signal) =>
        fetch(`${API_BASE}/v2/userinfo`, {
          headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
          signal,
        }),
      );
      if (!res.ok) {
        const failure = await toFailure(res);
        if (failure.retryable && attempt === 0) continue;
        return failure;
      }
      const json = (await res.json()) as {
        sub?: string;
        name?: string;
        picture?: string;
        email?: string;
      };
      if (!json.sub) return { ok: false, reason: "userinfo_missing_sub" };
      return {
        ok: true,
        data: {
          personUrn: `urn:li:person:${json.sub}`,
          name: json.name,
          picture: json.picture,
          email: json.email,
        },
      };
    } catch (err) {
      if (attempt === 0) continue;
      return toNetworkFailure(err);
    }
  }
  return { ok: false, reason: "userinfo_failed" };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------ media

export interface RegisteredImage {
  imageUrn: string;
  uploadUrl: string;
}

/** Step 1 of an image upload: register it and get a signed upload URL back. */
export async function initializeImageUpload(
  token: string,
  ownerUrn: string,
): Promise<LinkedInResult<RegisteredImage>> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await withTimeout(TIMEOUT_MS, (signal) =>
        fetch(`${API_BASE}/rest/images?action=initializeUpload`, {
          method: "POST",
          headers: versionedHeaders(token),
          body: JSON.stringify({ initializeUploadRequest: { owner: ownerUrn } }),
          signal,
        }),
      );
      if (!res.ok) {
        const failure = await toFailure(res);
        if (failure.retryable && attempt === 0) continue;
        return failure;
      }
      const json = (await res.json()) as { value?: { uploadUrl?: string; image?: string } };
      if (!json.value?.uploadUrl || !json.value.image) {
        return { ok: false, reason: "initialize_upload_malformed" };
      }
      return { ok: true, data: { imageUrn: json.value.image, uploadUrl: json.value.uploadUrl } };
    } catch (err) {
      if (attempt === 0) continue;
      return toNetworkFailure(err);
    }
  }
  return { ok: false, reason: "initialize_upload_failed" };
}

/**
 * Step 2: PUT the bytes to the signed URL.
 *
 * This runs server-side on purpose. Letting the browser upload directly would
 * mean handing it the access token — that token can post as the member for 60
 * days. Instead the client downsizes images before sending them here, which
 * also keeps requests under the ~4.5MB serverless body cap.
 */
export async function uploadImageBytes(
  token: string,
  uploadUrl: string,
  bytes: ArrayBuffer,
  contentType: string,
): Promise<LinkedInResult<null>> {
  try {
    const res = await withTimeout(UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, (signal) =>
      fetch(uploadUrl, {
        method: "PUT",
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": contentType },
        body: bytes,
        signal,
      }),
    );
    if (!res.ok) return await toFailure(res);
    return { ok: true, data: null };
  } catch (err) {
    return toNetworkFailure(err);
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------ posts

export interface PostImage {
  imageUrn: string;
  altText?: string;
}

export interface CreatePostArgs {
  token: string;
  authorUrn: string;
  /** Plain text. Escaped into little format here so no call site can forget. */
  text: string;
  images?: PostImage[];
  visibility?: "PUBLIC" | "CONNECTIONS";
}

/** LinkedIn's own limit on commentary length. */
export const MAX_COMMENTARY = 3000;
const MAX_MULTI_IMAGE = 20;

function buildContent(images: PostImage[]): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
  if (images.length === 0) return undefined;
  if (images.length === 1) {
    return { media: { id: images[0].imageUrn, altText: images[0].altText ?? "" } };
  }
  return {
    multiImage: {
      images: images.slice(0, MAX_MULTI_IMAGE).map((i) => ({
        id: i.imageUrn,
        altText: i.altText ?? "",
      })),
    },
  };
}

/**
 * Create the post. NO RETRIES — see the file header. A caller that receives a
 * network failure here must treat the outcome as UNKNOWN, not as "failed".
 */
export async function createPost(
  args: CreatePostArgs,
): Promise<LinkedInResult<{ postUrn: string }>> {
  const commentary = toLittleText(args.text);
  if (commentary.length > MAX_COMMENTARY) {
    // Escaping expands the text, so the check has to happen on the escaped
    // form — the caller's 3000-char plaintext can still overflow here.
    return { ok: false, reason: `commentary_too_long_after_escaping:${commentary.length}` };
  }

  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {
    author: args.authorUrn,
    commentary,
    visibility: args.visibility ?? "PUBLIC",
    distribution: {
      feedDistribution: "MAIN_FEED",
      targetEntities: [],
      thirdPartyDistributionChannels: [],
    },
    lifecycleState: "PUBLISHED",
    isReshareDisabledByAuthor: false,
  };
  const content = buildContent(args.images ?? []);
  if (content) body.content = content;

  try {
    const res = await withTimeout(TIMEOUT_MS, (signal) =>
      fetch(`${API_BASE}/rest/posts`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: versionedHeaders(args.token),
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
        signal,
      }),
    );
    if (!res.ok) return await toFailure(res);
    // The post URN comes back in a header, not the body.
    const postUrn = res.headers.get("x-restli-id") ?? res.headers.get("X-RestLi-Id");
    if (!postUrn) return { ok: false, reason: "created_but_no_urn_header" };
    return { ok: true, data: { postUrn } };
  } catch (err) {
    return toNetworkFailure(err);
  }
}

/** Public permalink for a created post URN. */
export function postPermalink(postUrn: string): string {
  return `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/${postUrn}/`;
}

````text
export interface CompleteArgs {
  system: string;
  user: string;
  /** Smaller prompt variant for low-TPM models (Gemma). Optional. */
  compactUser?: string;
  jsonMode?: boolean;
  maxOutputTokens?: number;
}

export type CompleteResult =
  | { ok: true; text: string; model: string }
  | { ok: false; reason: string };


export type Completion = (args: CompleteArgs) => Promise<CompleteResult>;

export function parseJson<T>(text: string, guard: (v: unknown) => v is T): T | null {
  const cleaned = text
    .trim()
    .replace(/^```(?:json)?\s*/i, "")
    .replace(/\s*```$/, "");
  try {
    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(cleaned);
    return guard(parsed) ? parsed : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

````text
/**
 * Provider-agnostic LLM adapter. Everything above this file (persona.ts,
 * judge.ts, writer.ts) calls complete() and never knows the provider.
 *
 * Provider is chosen by LLM_PROVIDER (default "gemini"). An "anthropic"
 * branch is stubbed behind the same interface so switching is one env var.
 *
 * Free-tier design (see DEPLOY.md for the measured dashboard limits):
 * - CASCADE: primary GEMINI_MODEL -> GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODEL ->
 *   GEMINI_LAST_RESORT_MODEL. On 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED the SAME request is
 *   retried on the next model; quotas are per model, so they stack.
 * - RPM: all calls are serialized with a minimum 4s gap (15 RPM ceiling on
 *   the Flash Lites; the spacing alone mathematically caps us at 15/min).
 * - RPD: per-model daily counters persisted in Postgres (llm_calls), keyed
 *   by Pacific-time day because Google resets free-tier quotas at midnight
 *   Pacific. A model at >=90% of its cap is skipped in the cascade.
 * - Gemma has a 16K TPM ceiling (vs 250K): callers may pass compactUser,
 *   used instead of user when a gemma model serves the call. Gemma also
 *   lacks systemInstruction and native JSON mode, so the adapter merges the
 *   system prompt into the content and instructs JSON in text.
 * - Never put secrets or env values into prompts; free-tier inputs may be
 *   used for model training.
 */
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";
import { query } from "./db";
import { usageOwner, reserveUserCall, reserveProviderCall, recordAiUsage } from './ai-usage';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';

import type { CompleteArgs, CompleteResult } from "./llm-contract";
export type { CompleteArgs, CompleteResult } from "./llm-contract";
const MIN_GAP_MS = 4_000;
const DEFAULT_RPD: Record<string, number> = {}; // filled per call from env

function cascade(): string[] {
  return [
    process.env.GEMINI_MODEL,
    process.env.GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODEL,
    process.env.GEMINI_LAST_RESORT_MODEL,
  ].filter((m): m is string => Boolean(m));
}

function rpdCap(model: string): number {
  if (model === process.env.GEMINI_MODEL) {
    return Number(process.env.GEMINI_RPD_LIMIT) || 500;
  }
  if (model.startsWith("gemma")) return 14_400;
  return 500;
}

function isGemma(model: string): boolean {
  return model.startsWith("gemma");
}

// ---- pacing: serialize every call, >=4s apart, across the whole instance
let chain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
let lastCallAt = 0;

function paced<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const run = chain.then(async () => {
    const wait = lastCallAt + MIN_GAP_MS - Date.now();
    if (wait > 0) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, wait));
    lastCallAt = Date.now();
    return fn();
  });
  chain = run.then(
    () => undefined,
    () => undefined,
  );
  return run;
}

// ---- per-model daily counters (Pacific day, matching Google's quota reset)
export function pacificToday(): string {
  return new Date().toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/Los_Angeles" });
}

async function todayCount(model: string): Promise<number> {
  const rows = await query<{ call_count: number }>(
    "SELECT call_count FROM llm_calls WHERE day = $1 AND model = $2",
    [pacificToday(), model],
  );
  return rows[0]?.call_count ?? 0;
}

async function bumpCount(model: string): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO llm_calls (day, model, call_count) VALUES ($1, $2, 1)
     ON CONFLICT (day, model) DO UPDATE SET call_count = llm_calls.call_count + 1`,
    [pacificToday(), model],
  );
}

/** Today's per-model call counts, for the UI and checkpoint reporting. */
export async function getTodayCalls(): Promise<{ model: string; calls: number; cap: number }[]> {
  const rows = await query<{ model: string; call_count: number }>(
    "SELECT model, call_count FROM llm_calls WHERE day = $1 ORDER BY model",
    [pacificToday()],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({ model: r.model, calls: r.call_count, cap: rpdCap(r.model) }));
}

// ---- gemini call
let genai: GoogleGenAI | null = null;
function client(): GoogleGenAI {
  if (!genai) genai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY });
  return genai;
}

function is429(err: unknown): boolean {
  const s = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err);
  return /429|RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED|quota/i.test(s);
}

async function callGemini(model: string, args: CompleteArgs): Promise<string> {
  if(!await reserveProviderCall(model,pacificToday(),rpdCap(model)))throw new Error('provider_allowance_or_pacing_limit');
  const userText = isGemma(model) && args.compactUser ? args.compactUser : args.user;
  const jsonNudge = args.jsonMode
    ? "\n\nRespond with ONLY valid JSON. No markdown fences, no commentary."
    : "";

  const request = isGemma(model)
    ? {
        // Gemma: no systemInstruction, no native JSON mode — inline both.
        model,
        contents: `${args.system}\n\n---\n\n${userText}${jsonNudge}`,
        config: { maxOutputTokens: args.maxOutputTokens ?? 2048 },
      }
    : {
        model,
        contents: userText,
        config: {
          systemInstruction: args.system,
          maxOutputTokens: args.maxOutputTokens ?? 2048,
          ...(args.jsonMode ? { responseMimeType: "application/json" } : {}),
        },
      };

  const owner=await usageOwner();
  let res;
  try {res=await client().models.generateContent(request);}
  catch(e){await recordAiUsage(owner,model,false).catch(()=>{});throw e;}
  await recordAiUsage(owner,model,true,res.usageMetadata?.promptTokenCount,res.usageMetadata?.candidatesTokenCount).catch(()=>{});
  const text = res.text;
  if (!text || !text.trim()) throw new Error("empty completion");
  return text;
}

async function completeGemini(args: CompleteArgs): Promise<CompleteResult> {
  for (const model of cascade()) {
    // Skip models at >=90% of their daily cap rather than erroring into 429s.
    try {
      const used = await todayCount(model);
      if (used >= rpdCap(model) * 0.9) {
        console.warn(`[llm] ${model} at ${used}/${rpdCap(model)} daily calls — skipping`);
        continue;
      }
    } catch {
      // counter unavailable (db hiccup) — proceed; the API enforces anyway
    }

    // One retry on transient (non-429) errors, then cascade onward.
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
      try {
        const text = await paced(() => callGemini(model, args));
        await bumpCount(model).catch(() => {});
        console.log(`[llm] served by ${model}`);
        return { ok: true, text, model };
      } catch (err) {
        if (is429(err)) {
          console.warn(`[llm] ${model} rate-limited — cascading to next model`);
          break; // next model in cascade
        }
        console.warn(`[llm] ${model} attempt ${attempt + 1} failed:`, String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
        if (attempt === 0) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1_000));
      }
    }
  }
  return { ok: false, reason: "all_models_failed_or_exhausted" };
}

/** The single entry point. Never throws. */
export async function complete(args: CompleteArgs): Promise<CompleteResult> {
  if(process.env.BYLINE_TEST_MODE === "true") return {ok:false, reason:"local_test_ai_disabled"};
  if(process.env.BYLINE_ZERO_BUDGET_STATE_FILE) {
    try {
      const guard=JSON.parse(await readFile(process.env.BYLINE_ZERO_BUDGET_STATE_FILE,'utf8'));
      if(guard.billingEnabled!==false||!Number.isFinite(guard.verifiedUntil)||guard.verifiedUntil<=Date.now()||guard.keyHash!==createHash('sha256').update(process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY??'').digest('hex'))return {ok:false,reason:'free_tier_verification_required'};
    }catch{return {ok:false,reason:'free_tier_verification_required'};}
  }
  const provider = process.env.LLM_PROVIDER ?? "gemini";
  if (provider === "anthropic") {
    // Stub kept behind the same interface: switching providers is one env
    // var (LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) plus filling this in.
    return { ok: false, reason: "anthropic_provider_not_implemented" };
  }
  if (!process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY) return { ok: false, reason: "missing_gemini_api_key" };
  try {
    if(!await reserveUserCall(await usageOwner(),pacificToday()))return {ok:false,reason:'daily_ai_allowance_reached'};
    return await completeGemini(args);
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, reason: String((err as Error)?.message ?? err) };
  }
}

/**
 * Strict JSON helper: strips accidental fences, parses, and validates with
 * the caller's guard. Used by judge/writer so a malformed response can never
 * publish unscored content.
 */
export { parseJson } from "./llm-contract";

import { query } from './db';
export async function ownsMedia(agentId:string,ids:string[]) {
  if(!ids.length)return true;
  if(ids.some(id=>!/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i.test(id)))return false;
  const owned=await query('SELECT id FROM media_assets WHERE agent_id=$1 AND id=ANY($2::uuid[])',[agentId,ids]);
  return owned.length===new Set(ids).size;
}

## Source: lib/memory.ts

/**
 * Memory layer: Breeth (intent-aware graph memory) with Postgres fallback.
 *
 * Breeth is an ENHANCEMENT, never a hard dependency. When it is unreachable,
 * quota-exceeded, or slow, recall degrades to the last 20 post fingerprints
 * from Postgres and the agent keeps publishing on schedule. Degradation is
 * surfaced honestly (source/degraded fields), never hidden.
 *
 * Episode formatting rule (learned from the smoke test): episodes must be
 * natural prose with the agent NAMED as subject and real predicates —
 * "Ada published an analysis of X because Y". Terse fragments produce zero
 * graph edges, and search returns only edges, so bad prose makes the memory
 * silently write-only.
 */
import { isDegraded, search, writeEpisode } from "./breeth";
import { query } from "./db";

export interface MemoryContext {
  facts: string[];
  source: "breeth" | "postgres" | "none";
  degraded: boolean;
}

/** Persist Breeth health so the UI (any lambda) can report it honestly. */
async function recordBreethStatus(healthy: boolean, note: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await query(
      `INSERT INTO system_status (key, value, updated_at) VALUES ('breeth', $1, now())
       ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = $1, updated_at = now()`,
      [JSON.stringify({ healthy, note })],
    );
  } catch {
    // status is best-effort; never let it affect a cycle
  }
}

async function fingerprintFallback(agentId: string): Promise<string[]> {
  try {
    const rows = await query<{ fingerprint: string }>(
      "SELECT fingerprint FROM posts WHERE agent_id = $1 ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 20",
      [agentId],
    );
    return rows.map((r) => r.fingerprint);
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

/** Recall prior coverage and editorial positions relevant to `topics`. */
export async function recall(agentId: string, topics: string): Promise<MemoryContext> {
  const res = await search({
    agentId,
    query: `previous coverage and editorial position on ${topics}`,
    limit: 10,
  });
  await recordBreethStatus(res.ok, res.ok ? `search ok (${res.data.length} facts)` : `search failed: ${res.reason}`);
  if (res.ok && res.data.length > 0) {
    return { facts: res.data.map((e) => e.fact), source: "breeth", degraded: false };
  }
  const fallback = await fingerprintFallback(agentId);
  if (fallback.length > 0) {
    return { facts: fallback, source: "postgres", degraded: !res.ok };
  }
  return { facts: [], source: "none", degraded: !res.ok };
}

/**
 * Record a publish decision as an intent-carrying episode. Processing is
 * async server-side (returns a task_id) — we do not block on it, only on the
 * write itself (~16s, acceptable inside the awaited background cycle).
 */
export async function rememberPublish(
  agentId: string,
  agentName: string,
  post: { title: string; rationale: string; runnersUp: string[] },
): Promise<void> {
  const runnerText =
    post.runnersUp.length > 0
      ? ` ${agentName} chose it over ${post.runnersUp.map((t) => `"${t}"`).join(" and ")}.`
      : "";
  const content =
    `${agentName} published a post about "${post.title}".` +
    ` ${agentName} selected this topic because ${post.rationale}` +
    runnerText;
  const res = await writeEpisode({ agentId, content, extractIntent: true });
  await recordBreethStatus(res.ok, res.ok ? "episode write ok" : `episode write failed: ${res.reason}`);
  if (!res.ok) console.warn(`[memory] publish episode failed: ${res.reason}`);
}

/** Record what was passed over and why, so standards accumulate across cycles. */
export async function rememberRejections(
  agentId: string,
  agentName: string,
  rejects: { title: string; reason: string }[],
): Promise<void> {
  if (rejects.length === 0) return;
  const content = rejects
    .slice(0, 3)
    .map((r) => `${agentName} passed over the story "${r.title}" because ${r.reason}`)
    .join(" ");
  const res = await writeEpisode({ agentId, content, extractIntent: false });
  if (!res.ok) console.warn(`[memory] rejection episode failed: ${res.reason}`);
}

/** Current memory health, for the UI. */
export function memoryDegraded(): boolean {
  return isDegraded();
}

````

import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { createUserSession } from './auth';
import { query, getPool, ensureSchema } from './db';
import { exchangeCode, getMemberIdentity } from './linkedin';
import { saveAccount } from './accounts';

export const localTestMode = () => process.env.BYLINE_TEST_MODE === 'true' && process.env.BYLINE_LOCAL_ONLY === 'true';
export const digest = (s: string) => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');

export async function provisionUser(provider: string, subject: string, name: string) {
  await ensureSchema();
  const c = await getPool()!.connect();
  try {
    await c.query('BEGIN');
    const { rows: [user] } = await c.query<{ id: string }>(
      `INSERT INTO byline_users(provider,subject,name) VALUES($1,$2,$3)
       ON CONFLICT(provider,subject) DO UPDATE SET name=EXCLUDED.name RETURNING id`, [provider,subject,name.slice(0,100)]);
    const persona = {input:{name,domain:'Your selected topics'}, identity:{voice:'Clear and thoughtful. Do not invent personal experiences or opinions.',interests:[],opinions:[],skeptical_of:[]},generator:'fallback'};
    await c.query(`INSERT INTO agents(name,domain,persona_json,persona_hash,owner_id,paused,timezone,post_time_local,style_json,categories_json)
      VALUES($1,'Your selected topics',$2,$3,$4,true,'UTC','09:00',$5,'["emerging-tech"]')
      ON CONFLICT(owner_id) WHERE owner_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING`,
      [name,JSON.stringify(persona),digest(`byline:${user.id}`),user.id,JSON.stringify({signature:null})]);
    await c.query('INSERT INTO onboarding(user_id) VALUES($1) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING',[user.id]);
    await c.query('COMMIT');
    return user.id;
  } catch(e) { await c.query('ROLLBACK'); throw e; } finally { c.release(); }
}

export async function issueSession(userId: string) {
  const id = randomUUID();
  const session = await createUserSession(userId,id);
  await query('INSERT INTO byline_sessions(id,user_id,expires_at) VALUES($1,$2,now()+interval \'30 days\')',[id,userId]);
  return session.value;
}

export async function completeNativeAuth(state: string, code: string | null, denied: boolean) {
  const [flow] = await query<{provider:string;redirect_uri:string;return_uri:string|null}>(
    `UPDATE native_auth SET claimed_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND claimed_at IS NULL
     AND created_at>now()-interval '10 minutes' RETURNING provider,redirect_uri,return_uri`,[state]);
  if (!flow) return null;
  let ok = true;
  try {
    if (denied || !code) throw new Error('Sign-in was cancelled. Please try again.');
    let userId: string;
    if (flow.provider === 'linkedin') {
      const grant = await exchangeCode(code,flow.redirect_uri);
      if (!grant.ok) throw new Error('LinkedIn sign-in could not be completed. Please try again.');
      const identity = await getMemberIdentity(grant.data.accessToken);
      if (!identity.ok) throw new Error('Could not verify your LinkedIn identity.');
      userId = await provisionUser('linkedin',identity.data.personUrn,identity.data.name ?? 'ByLine author');
      const [agent] = await query<{id:string}>('SELECT id FROM agents WHERE owner_id=$1',[userId]);
      await saveAccount(agent.id,grant.data,identity.data);
    } else if (flow.provider === 'google') {
      const r = await fetch('https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token',{method:'POST',signal:AbortSignal.timeout(15000),
        body:new URLSearchParams({code,client_id:process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID!,client_secret:process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET!,redirect_uri:flow.redirect_uri,grant_type:'authorization_code'})});
      if (!r.ok) throw new Error('Google sign-in could not be completed. Please try again.');
      const token = await r.json();
      const u = await fetch('https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo',{headers:{Authorization:`Bearer ${token.access_token}`},signal:AbortSignal.timeout(15000)});
      if (!u.ok) throw new Error('Could not verify your Google identity.');
      const identity = await u.json();
      if (typeof identity.sub !== 'string') throw new Error('Could not verify your Google identity.');
      userId = await provisionUser('google',identity.sub,identity.name ?? 'ByLine author');
    } else throw new Error('Unsupported sign-in provider.');
    await query('UPDATE native_auth SET user_id=$2 WHERE id=$1',[state,userId]);
  } catch(e) {
    ok = false;
    await query('UPDATE native_auth SET error=$2 WHERE id=$1',[state,(e as Error).message.slice(0,200)]);
  }
  return {ok, returnUri:flow.return_uri};
}

/** Browser-to-desktop signal only. Never forward codes or tokens to this URL. */
export function nativeReturnUri(value: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return null;
  // Exact loopback literal, unprivileged port and a random, app-owned path.
  // Reject URL normalization tricks, credentials, queries and fragments.
  const match = /^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:([0-9]{4,5})\/byline-return\/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.exec(value);
  if (!match) return null;
  const port = Number(match[1]);
  return port >= 1024 && port <= 65535 ? value : null;
}
