````text
import { query } from './db';
import { getAccountStatus } from './accounts';
import { CATEGORIES, ALL_CATEGORY_IDS, isCategoryId, MAX_SELECTED_CATEGORIES, describeCategories, type CategoryId } from './categories';
import { SUBJECT_GROUPS, subjectId } from './category-catalogue';
import { discover } from './discovery';
import { judgeCandidates, PUBLISH_THRESHOLD } from './judge';
import { writePost } from './writer';
import { critique } from './critique';
import type { PersonaRecord } from './persona';
import { localTestMode } from './native-auth';
import { isValidTimeZone, normalizeHhMm, nextDailyRun, localClock } from './schedule';
import { parseStyle, type StyleConfig } from './style';

export * from './setup-config';
import { INDUSTRIES, VOICES, defaultSetup, setupCategories, setupPersona, setupStyle, type SetupConfig } from './setup-config';
export interface Sample {text:string;sources:string[];title:string;testMode:boolean}
export async function generateSetupSample(c:SetupConfig, name = 'The author'):Promise<Sample> {
  if(localTestMode()) return {text:`${c.voice==='punchy'?'Start small. Measure what changes.':`A useful question about ${c.topics[0]}: what would make this better for the people using it?`}\n\nAcross ${c.topics.slice(1).join(' and ')}, a clear goal matters more than adding another tool. Define one outcome, try a small change, and ask the people affected what improved.\n\nKeep the evidence. Change what did not work. That makes the next decision easier.`,sources:['https://www.oecd.org/en/topics/digital-transformation.html'],title:'Local demonstration — not a live article-based Gemini draft',testMode:true};
  const categories=setupCategories(c);
  const candidates=(await discover({categories})).filter(s=>s.summary.length>80&&/^https?:\/\//.test(s.url));
  const persona=setupPersona(c,name);
  const memory={facts:[],source:'none' as const,degraded:false};
  const judged=await judgeCandidates(persona,categories,candidates,memory,[]);
  if (!judged.ok) throw new Error('We could not prepare a relevant sample right now. Your preferences are saved; please try again.');
  const source=judged.data.scored.find(s=>s.total>=PUBLISH_THRESHOLD);
  if (!source) throw new Error('No source closely matches your subjects yet. Your preferences are saved; try again later or adjust your subjects.');
  const style=setupStyle(c);
  const r=await writePost({persona,style,winner:source,runnersUp:[],memory,priorPosts:[],samples:c.samples.map(text=>({text,origin:'corpus'}))});
  if(!r.ok) throw new Error('The writer is temporarily unavailable. Your settings are saved; please try again.');
  const text=r.data.text.trim();
  if(critique(text,style,{hashtags:r.data.hashtags,usedQuote:r.data.used_quote}).length) throw new Error('The sample needs another pass to match your writing preferences. Please try again.');
  return {text: text + (r.data.hashtags.length ? '\n\n' + r.data.hashtags.map(tag=>'#'+tag).join(' ') : ''),sources:[source.url],title:source.title,testMode:false};
}
export async function setupStatus(userId:string) {
  const [row]=await query<{config:Partial<SetupConfig>;revision:number;preview:Sample|null;preview_revision:number|null;accepted_revision:number|null;completed_at:Date|null;next_delivery_at:Date|null}>(`SELECT * FROM onboarding WHERE user_id=$1`,[userId]);
  if(!row) throw new Error('Setup is unavailable. Sign in again.');
  const [agent]=await query<{id:string}>('SELECT id FROM agents WHERE owner_id=$1',[userId]);
  if(row.completed_at) {
    const [next]=await query<{at:Date|null}>('SELECT min(next_run_at) AS at FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id=$1 AND enabled',[agent.id]);
    row.next_delivery_at=next?.at??null;
  }
  const config={...defaultSetup,...row.config};
  return {...row,config,nextDeliveryLabel:row.next_delivery_at?`${localClock(config.timezone,row.next_delivery_at).date} at ${config.time} (${config.timezone})`:null,account:await getAccountStatus(agent.id),industries:INDUSTRIES,voices:VOICES,categories:ALL_CATEGORY_IDS.map(id=>CATEGORIES[id]),testMode:localTestMode()};
}
````

````text
import type { CategoryId } from "./categories";

export interface PersonaIdentity {
  voice: string; // voice and register, 1-3 sentences
  interests: string[]; // 3-5 stable technical interests
  opinions: string[]; // 3-5 specific opinions the persona holds
  skeptical_of: string[]; // things it is skeptical of
}

export interface PersonaRecord {
  input: { name: string; domain: string };
  identity: PersonaIdentity;
  generator: "llm" | "fallback";
  /**
   * The categories this identity was grown from. Compared against the agent's
   * live categories to decide whether it is stale. Absent on records written
   * before this field existed — treated as stale, which rebuilds them once.
   */
  builtFor?: CategoryId[];
}

/** Stable prompt block rendered from the persisted record — used by judge and writer. */
export function personaBlock(p: PersonaRecord): string {
  const i = p.identity;
  return [
    `PERSONA: ${p.input.name} — domain: ${p.input.domain}`,
    `Voice: ${i.voice}`,
    `Stable interests: ${i.interests.join("; ")}`,
    `Held opinions: ${i.opinions.join("; ")}`,
    `Skeptical of: ${i.skeptical_of.join("; ")}`,
  ].join("\n");
}
````

## Source: lib/persona.ts

````text
/**
 * Persona construction. One LLM call expands { name, domain } plus the chosen
 * categories into a full editorial identity, persisted to agents.persona_json.
 * Every later prompt reads that stored record so the voice cannot drift across
 * months of daily posting.
 *
 * Stable is not the same as frozen. The identity is derived FROM the agent's
 * categories, so it has to be rebuilt when those change — `builtFor` records
 * which set it was grown from, and lib/agents.ts rebuilds it when that no
 * longer matches. Without this the interests and opinions stayed pinned to
 * whatever was selected at setup, and the judge went on scoring persona_fit
 * against categories the author had since switched off.
 *
 * Nothing here is hardcoded to a particular persona — name, domain and
 * categories all arrive from the agent's own settings.
 */
import type { CategoryId } from "./categories";
import { CATEGORIES } from "./categories";
import { complete, parseJson } from "./llm";

import type { PersonaIdentity, PersonaRecord } from "./persona-prompt";
export type { PersonaIdentity, PersonaRecord } from "./persona-prompt";
function isIdentity(v: unknown): v is PersonaIdentity {
  const o = v as PersonaIdentity;
  return (
    !!o &&
    typeof o.voice === "string" &&
    o.voice.length > 10 &&
    Array.isArray(o.interests) &&
    o.interests.length >= 3 &&
    Array.isArray(o.opinions) &&
    o.opinions.length >= 3 &&
    Array.isArray(o.skeptical_of) &&
    o.skeptical_of.length >= 2 &&
    [...o.interests, ...o.opinions, ...o.skeptical_of].every((s) => typeof s === "string")
  );
}

const SYSTEM = `You construct stable editorial identities for people who publish regularly under their own name. Respond with JSON matching exactly:
{"voice": string, "interests": string[], "opinions": string[], "skeptical_of": string[]}
- voice: 2-3 sentences describing how this person writes — register, sentence rhythm, what they refuse to do stylistically. A practitioner with an opinion, never a growth account. This is a real professional profile, not a brand channel.
- interests: 4-6 stable, specific technical interests, spread across their stated categories — at least one per category, and none of them naming a field the categories do not cover.
- opinions: 4-6 concrete, defensible opinions they actually hold (specific claims someone could argue with, not platitudes).
- skeptical_of: 2-5 things in their fields they distrust, briefly and specifically.`;

/**
 * Expand a raw persona into a full identity. If the LLM is unavailable at
 * init (quota, outage), fall back to a mechanical identity so init NEVER
 * fails — the record is marked generator:"fallback" and surfaced honestly.
 */
export async function expandPersona(
  name: string,
  domain: string,
  categories: CategoryId[] = [],
): Promise<PersonaRecord> {
  const categoryLines = categories
    .map((id) => `- ${CATEGORIES[id].label}: ${CATEGORIES[id].blurb}`)
    .join("\n");
  const user = [
    `Construct the editorial identity for a person named "${name}" whose stated domain is "${domain}".`,
    categories.length > 0 ? `They publish across these categories:\n${categoryLines}` : "",
    "The category list above is the complete and authoritative account of what this person writes about.",
    "Their interests and opinions must span these categories, not collapse into whichever one is easiest to write about.",
    // Named explicitly because it is the failure this whole record exists to
    // prevent: an identity that keeps one retired speciality alive skews every
    // persona_fit score afterwards towards it.
    "Do NOT introduce a speciality that is absent from the list, however natural it seems for someone with this name or domain.",
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join("\n");

  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
    const res = await complete({
      system: SYSTEM,
      user:
        attempt === 0
          ? user
          : `${user}\nYour previous reply was not valid JSON of the required shape. Reply with ONLY the JSON object.`,
      jsonMode: true,
      maxOutputTokens: 1024,
    });
    if (!res.ok) break;
    const identity = parseJson(res.text, isIdentity);
    if (identity) {
      return { input: { name, domain }, identity, generator: "llm", builtFor: categories };
    }
  }

  console.warn(`[persona] LLM expansion unavailable — using mechanical fallback for "${name}"`);
  return {
    input: { name, domain },
    identity: {
      voice: `${name} writes plainly and concretely about ${domain}: short declarative sentences, evidence before opinion, no hype vocabulary and no engagement-bait formatting.`,
      interests: [
        `practical, deployed ${domain}`,
        `measurement and evaluation in ${domain}`,
        `failure modes and incidents in ${domain}`,
      ],
      opinions: [
        `most headline claims in ${domain} understate their tradeoffs`,
        `reproducible evidence beats vendor benchmarks in ${domain}`,
        `boring, well-understood tools are underrated in ${domain}`,
      ],
      skeptical_of: [
        `press releases framed as research in ${domain}`,
        `benchmarks without published methodology`,
      ],
    },
    generator: "fallback",
    builtFor: categories,
  };
}

export { personaBlock } from "./persona-prompt";

````

````text
import { hookOf } from "./format";
export interface PostRow {
  id: string;
  seq: number;
  text: string;
  rationale: string;
  status: string;
  kind: string;
  category: string | null;
  scores_json: Record<string, number> | null;
  sources_json: string[];
  media_json: string[];
  hashtags_json: string[];
  continuity: string | null;
  used_quote: boolean;
  created_at: Date;
  published_at: Date | null;
  scheduled_for: Date | null;
  slot_id: string | null;
  cleared_at: Date | null;
  hold_until: Date | null;
}

export function serializePost(r: PostRow) {
  return {
    id: r.id,
    seq: r.seq,
    text: r.text,
    hook: hookOf(r.text),
    rationale: r.rationale,
    status: r.status,
    kind: r.kind,
    category: r.category,
    scores: r.scores_json,
    sources: r.sources_json ?? [],
    media: r.media_json ?? [],
    hashtags: r.hashtags_json ?? [],
    continuity: r.continuity,
    usedQuote: r.used_quote,
    createdAt: r.created_at.toISOString(),
    publishedAt: r.published_at?.toISOString() ?? null,
    // Scheduling. `scheduledFor` null means the post is not on the timetable
    // and will only ever go out if a human sends it by hand.
    scheduledFor: r.scheduled_for?.toISOString() ?? null,
    slotId: r.slot_id,
    clearedAt: r.cleared_at?.toISOString() ?? null,
    // Only reported while genuinely in effect, so the client never has to work
    // out whether an expired hold still counts.
    heldUntil:
      r.hold_until && r.hold_until.getTime() > Date.now() ? r.hold_until.toISOString() : null,
  };
}

export const POST_COLUMNS = `id, seq, text, rationale, status, kind, category, scores_json,
                      sources_json, media_json, hashtags_json, continuity, used_quote,
                      created_at, published_at, scheduled_for, slot_id, cleared_at, hold_until`;
````

````text
/**
 * Push notifications to the phone, via Firebase Cloud Messaging.
 *
 * FCM is free at any volume this app will ever reach, and it is the only way to
 * reach an Android app that is not currently running. The alternative — the app
 * polling — cannot work, because the whole point is to hear about a failure on
 * a day you never opened it.
 *
 * No SDK. The HTTP v1 API wants a Google OAuth2 access token, and that is a
 * signed JWT exchanged for a bearer token: about forty lines with Web Crypto,
 * against a dependency tree that has to keep building for years. The private
 * key is a service-account key from the Firebase console, held in env vars.
 *
 * Everything here fails SOFT. A notification that cannot be sent is logged and
 * forgotten — it must never fail a cycle, block a publish, or throw into a
 * route. The post going out matters; being told about it does not.
 */
import { query } from "./db";
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token";
const SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/firebase.messaging";

export function pushConfigured(): boolean {
  return !!(process.env.FCM_PROJECT_ID && ((process.env.FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL && process.env.FCM_PRIVATE_KEY)||process.env.FCM_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE));
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ access tokens

interface CachedToken {
  value: string;
  expiresAt: number;
}

/**
 * Cached on globalThis for the same reason the pg Pool is: `next dev`
 * re-evaluates modules constantly, and a lambda that re-mints a token on every
 * message pays an extra round trip to Google for nothing. Tokens last an hour.
 */
const g = globalThis as unknown as { __linkdinPushToken?: CachedToken | null };

/**
 * PEM (PKCS#8) to the raw DER bytes crypto.subtle wants.
 *
 * Exported for the selftest. The service-account key is pasted by hand into an
 * environment variable, and every way of getting that wrong fails with the same
 * unhelpful "invalid key" from crypto.subtle — so which formats are tolerated
 * is worth pinning down in a test rather than discovering in production.
 */
export function pemToBytes(pem: string): ArrayBuffer {
  const body = pem
    .replace(/-----BEGIN [^-]+-----/, "")
    .replace(/-----END [^-]+-----/, "")
    .replace(/\s+/g, "");
  const binary = atob(body);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(new ArrayBuffer(binary.length));
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes.buffer;
}

function base64url(input: string | Uint8Array): string {
  const binary =
    typeof input === "string" ? input : String.fromCharCode(...Array.from(input));
  return btoa(binary).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
}

async function mintAccessToken(): Promise<string | null> {
  if(process.env.FCM_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE) {
    const saved=JSON.parse(await readFile(process.env.FCM_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE,'utf8'));
    return typeof saved.accessToken==='string'&&saved.expiresAt>Date.now()+60_000?saved.accessToken:null;
  }
  const clientEmail = process.env.FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL;
  // Env vars cannot carry real newlines, so the key is stored with them escaped
  // and restored here. Getting this wrong produces an opaque "invalid key"
  // from crypto.subtle, which is why it is a single obvious line.
  const privateKey = process.env.FCM_PRIVATE_KEY?.replace(/\\n/g, "\n");
  if (!clientEmail || !privateKey) return null;

  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const header = base64url(JSON.stringify({ alg: "RS256", typ: "JWT" }));
  const claims = base64url(
    JSON.stringify({
      iss: clientEmail,
      scope: SCOPE,
      aud: TOKEN_URL,
      iat: now,
      exp: now + 3600,
    }),
  );

  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    "pkcs8",
    pemToBytes(privateKey),
    { name: "RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5", hash: "SHA-256" },
    false,
    ["sign"],
  );
  const signature = new Uint8Array(
    await crypto.subtle.sign(
      "RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5",
      key,
      new TextEncoder().encode(`${header}.${claims}`),
    ),
  );

  const res = await fetch(TOKEN_URL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
    body: new URLSearchParams({
      grant_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer",
      assertion: `${header}.${claims}.${base64url(signature)}`,
    }),
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    console.warn(`[push] token exchange failed: ${res.status} ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 200)}`);
    return null;
  }
  const data = (await res.json()) as { access_token?: string; expires_in?: number };
  if (!data.access_token) return null;

  g.__linkdinPushToken = {
    value: data.access_token,
    // Sixty seconds of headroom, so a token cannot expire mid-flight.
    expiresAt: Date.now() + (data.expires_in ?? 3600) * 1000 - 60_000,
  };
  return data.access_token;
}

/**
 * Do the stored credentials actually work?
 *
 * Distinct from pushConfigured(), which only says the three variables exist. A
 * private key pasted with the JSON's quotes still round-trips through env vars
 * perfectly and fails at crypto.subtle — and because notify() is deliberately
 * silent, the first sign would be a notification that never arrived on a day
 * something was wrong. This exchanges a real token and sends nothing.
 */
export async function checkCredentials(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; detail: string }> {
  if (!pushConfigured()) {
    return { ok: false, detail: "FCM_PROJECT_ID, FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL or FCM_PRIVATE_KEY is not set" };
  }
  try {
    // Deliberately bypasses the cache: the point is to prove the KEY works now,
    // not that a token minted an hour ago is still valid.
    const token = await mintAccessToken();
    return token
      ? { ok: true, detail: process.env.FCM_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE ? "Operator access token is available; send a test notification to verify delivery." : "credentials accepted by Google" }
      : { ok: false, detail: "Google refused the credentials — see the logs for the exchange error" };
  } catch (err) {
    const message = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err);
    // The signature of a mis-pasted key, called out by name because it is the
    // one mistake the setup notes warn about.
    const hint = /invalid character|asn|decode/i.test(message)
      ? " — FCM_PRIVATE_KEY looks malformed; the likeliest cause is copying it with the JSON's surrounding double quotes"
      : "";
    return { ok: false, detail: message.slice(0, 160) + hint };
  }
}

async function accessToken(): Promise<string | null> {
  const cached = g.__linkdinPushToken;
  if (cached && cached.expiresAt > Date.now()) return cached.value;
  return mintAccessToken();
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ device registry

export async function registerDevice(
  agentId: string,
  token: string,
  platform: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO device_tokens (token, agent_id, platform, last_seen_at)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, now())
     ON CONFLICT (token) DO UPDATE
        SET agent_id = $2, platform = $3, last_seen_at = now()`,
    [token, agentId, platform.slice(0, 20)],
  );
}

export async function forgetDevice(token: string): Promise<void> {
  await query("DELETE FROM device_tokens WHERE token = $1", [token]);
}

async function devicesFor(agentId: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const rows = await query<{ token: string }>(
    "SELECT token FROM device_tokens WHERE agent_id = $1",
    [agentId],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => r.token);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ events

/**
 * What the app is allowed to tell you about.
 *
 * A closed set rather than free-form strings, so every notification the app can
 * produce is visible in one place and can be read as a list of "things worth
 * interrupting someone for". Anything that does not deserve that is a log line.
 */
export type PushEvent =
  | { kind: "draft_ready"; seq: number; hook: string; at: string | null }
  | { kind: "published"; seq: number }
  | { kind: "publish_failed"; seq: number; detail: string }
  | { kind: "cycle_failed"; detail: string }
  | { kind: "token_expiring"; days: number }
  | { kind: "scheduler_stalled"; minutes: number }
  // Only ever sent on request. Exists because the last link in the chain —
  // server to Google to a specific handset — cannot be proved any other way,
  // and the first real alert is a bad time to discover it was never wired up.
  | { kind: "feed_dead"; names: string[] }
  | { kind: "api_version_stale"; version: string; months: number }
  | { kind: "test" };

interface Rendered {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  /** Which tab to open. The app reads this from the data payload. */
  tab: string;
  /** Quiet events post silently; problems do not. */
  urgent: boolean;
}

function render(event: PushEvent): Rendered {
  switch (event.kind) {
    case "draft_ready":
      return {
        title: "A draft is ready to read",
        body: event.at ? `${event.hook} — goes out at ${event.at}.` : event.hook,
        tab: "queue",
        urgent: false,
      };
    case "published":
      return {
        title: "Posted to LinkedIn",
        body: `Post #${event.seq} went out.`,
        tab: "queue",
        urgent: false,
      };
    case "publish_failed":
      return {
        title: "A post did not go out",
        body: `Post #${event.seq} failed: ${event.detail}`,
        tab: "queue",
        urgent: true,
      };
    case "cycle_failed":
      return {
        title: "The agent could not write today",
        body: event.detail,
        tab: "status",
        urgent: true,
      };
    case "token_expiring":
      return {
        title: "Reconnect LinkedIn",
        body:
          event.days <= 0
            ? "The LinkedIn connection has expired. Nothing can publish until you reconnect."
            : `LinkedIn access expires in ${event.days} day${event.days === 1 ? "" : "s"}. It cannot renew itself.`,
        tab: "status",
        urgent: true,
      };
    case "scheduler_stalled":
      return {
        title: "The scheduler has stopped",
        body: `No tick for ${event.minutes} minutes. Nothing is being written or sent.`,
        tab: "status",
        urgent: true,
      };
    case "feed_dead": {
      const [first, ...rest] = event.names;
      return {
        title: rest.length > 0 ? `${event.names.length} feeds have stopped working` : "A feed has stopped working",
        body:
          rest.length > 0
            ? `${event.names.join(", ")} — discovery is running on fewer sources than you think.`
            : `${first} has returned nothing for days. Discovery is running on fewer sources than you think.`,
        tab: "status",
        // Not urgent: nothing is broken and nothing is waiting on you. It is a
        // slow leak in the quality of what the agent reads, and it deserves to
        // be noticed rather than to interrupt.
        urgent: false,
      };
    }
    case "api_version_stale":
      return {
        title: "LinkedIn's API version needs bumping",
        body: `Version ${event.version} is ${event.months} months old and LinkedIn retires them at about twelve. Set LINKEDIN_API_VERSION before it stops publishing.`,
        tab: "status",
        urgent: false,
      };
    case "test":
      return {
        title: "Notifications are working",
        body: "This is the only message the agent will ever send that means nothing.",
        tab: "status",
        // Sent on the alerts channel deliberately: this is the channel the
        // messages that matter use, so a test that arrives proves the one you
        // actually need will arrive too.
        urgent: true,
      };
  }
}

/**
 * How long the same KIND of event stays quiet after being sent.
 *
 * Without this the standing problems are the loud ones: a stalled scheduler is
 * re-detected on every tick and an expiring token on every status read, so the
 * two alerts that most need to be believed would arrive dozens of times a day
 * and be muted within a week. Things that happen once per post have no cooldown
 * at all — each one is genuinely new.
 */
const COOLDOWN_MINUTES: Record<PushEvent["kind"], number> = {
  draft_ready: 0,
  published: 0,
  publish_failed: 0,
  cycle_failed: 180,
  token_expiring: 1440, // once a day is plenty for a 60-day clock
  scheduler_stalled: 360,
  // Weekly. A dead feed stays dead until someone edits lib/discovery.ts, and
  // an alert repeating before then is pure nagging about a known problem.
  feed_dead: 10080,
  // Weekly too. The fix is one environment variable and it is not urgent for
  // months, so this is a standing reminder rather than an alarm.
  api_version_stale: 10080,
  // Asked for explicitly, so throttling it would only ever be confusing.
  test: 0,
};

async function withinCooldown(agentId: string, kind: PushEvent["kind"]): Promise<boolean> {
  const minutes = COOLDOWN_MINUTES[kind];
  if (minutes <= 0) return false;
  const rows = await query<{ recent: string }>(
    `SELECT count(*) AS recent FROM push_log
      WHERE agent_id = $1 AND kind = $2 AND sent_at > now() - ($3 || ' minutes')::interval`,
    [agentId, kind, String(minutes)],
  );
  return Number(rows[0]?.recent ?? 0) > 0;
}

/**
 * Send one notification, to every device this agent has registered.
 *
 * Returns how many devices it reached, which is only useful for tests and logs
 * — no caller should branch on it. Never throws.
 */
export async function notify(agentId: string, event: PushEvent, deviceToken?: string): Promise<number> {
  try {
    if (!pushConfigured()) return 0;
    if (await withinCooldown(agentId, event.kind)) {
      console.log(`[push] ${event.kind} suppressed by cooldown`);
      return 0;
    }

    const registered = await devicesFor(agentId);
    const tokens = deviceToken ? registered.filter(token => token === deviceToken) : registered;
    if (tokens.length === 0) return 0;

    const bearer = await accessToken();
    if (!bearer) return 0;

    const { title, body, tab, urgent } = render(event);
    const projectId = process.env.FCM_PROJECT_ID;
    let delivered = 0;

    // Sent one at a time: the v1 API has no batch endpoint, and this app has
    // one or two devices. Sequential also means one dead token cannot stop the
    // others from being tried.
    for (const token of tokens) {
      const res = await fetch(`https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${projectId}/messages:send`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${bearer}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          message: {
            token,
            notification: { title, body },
            // Strings only — FCM rejects a data payload with non-string values.
            data: { kind: event.kind, tab, ...('seq' in event ? {seq:String(event.seq)} : {}) },
            android: {
              priority: urgent ? "HIGH" : "NORMAL",
              notification: {
                channel_id: urgent ? "linkdin_alerts" : "linkdin_updates",
                // Grouped by kind, so five failures collapse into one line
                // rather than five identical rows in the shade.
                tag: event.kind,
              },
            },
          },
        }),
      });

      if (res.ok) {
        delivered++;
        continue;
      }
      const detail = (await res.text()).slice(0, 300);
      // 404 UNREGISTERED and 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT on the token mean the app was
      // uninstalled or the token rotated. Keeping it would mean retrying a dead
      // address forever, so it is dropped.
      if (res.status === 404 || detail.includes("UNREGISTERED") || detail.includes("INVALID_ARGUMENT")) {
        console.warn(`[push] dropping dead device token: ${res.status}`);
        await forgetDevice(token);
      } else {
        console.warn(`[push] send failed: ${res.status} ${detail}`);
      }
    }

    if (delivered > 0) {
      await query("INSERT INTO push_log (agent_id, kind) VALUES ($1, $2)", [agentId, event.kind]);
    }
    return delivered;
  } catch (err) {
    // A cycle must never fail because a notification did.
    console.warn("[push] notify failed:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
    return 0;
  }
}

````

## Source: lib/ratelimit.ts

````text
/**
 * Rate limiting for the login gate.
 *
 * The gate already delayed 800ms on a wrong password, which is a real brake on
 * a sequential guesser and almost none on a parallel one: serverless runs
 * requests concurrently, so twenty simultaneous guesses all wait 800ms at the
 * same time and cost the attacker 800ms in total. Behind that gate is an
 * endpoint that publishes to a real LinkedIn profile.
 *
 * So attempts are counted in Postgres rather than in memory. A per-process
 * counter would be reset by every cold start and sidestepped by requests
 * landing on different instances — the exact shape of the attack.
 *
 * Deliberately counts FAILURES only, and only for the login route. A correct
 * password clears the record, so ordinary use never approaches the limit and
 * nobody can lock the real user out by guessing from another address: the
 * window is keyed by client.
 */
import { query } from "./db";

/** Failures allowed from one client before it is refused. */
export const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8;

/** How far back failures are counted, and how long a block therefore lasts. */
export const WINDOW_MINUTES = 15;

/**
 * The client, as far as we can tell.
 *
 * Vercel sets x-forwarded-for and x-real-ip; nothing else is trustworthy. A
 * request with neither is bucketed under "unknown", which means every such
 * request shares one allowance — the conservative direction, since a client
 * that hides its address should not get a fresh quota by doing so.
 *
 * Only the first address is used: x-forwarded-for is a chain, and the entries
 * after the first are supplied by the caller.
 */
export function clientKey(request: Request): string {
  const forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")?.split(",")[0]?.trim();
  const real = request.headers.get("x-real-ip")?.trim();
  return (forwarded || real || "unknown").slice(0, 100);
}

export interface RateVerdict {
  allowed: boolean;
  /** Failures already recorded in the window. */
  recent: number;
  /** Whole minutes until the oldest failure ages out. Only meaningful when blocked. */
  retryAfterMinutes: number;
}

/**
 * Whether this client may attempt a login right now.
 *
 * Fails OPEN on a database error. A login gate that refuses everyone because
 * the counter table is unreachable turns a degraded database into a total
 * lockout, and the password check itself is unaffected either way.
 */
export async function checkLoginAllowed(client: string): Promise<RateVerdict> {
  try {
    const rows = await query<{ recent: string; oldest: Date | null }>(
      `SELECT count(*) AS recent, min(at) AS oldest
         FROM login_attempts
        WHERE client = $1 AND at > now() - ($2 || ' minutes')::interval`,
      [client, String(WINDOW_MINUTES)],
    );
    const recent = Number(rows[0]?.recent ?? 0);
    const oldest = rows[0]?.oldest;
    const retryAfterMinutes = oldest
      ? Math.max(1, WINDOW_MINUTES - Math.floor((Date.now() - oldest.getTime()) / 60_000))
      : WINDOW_MINUTES;
    return { allowed: recent < MAX_ATTEMPTS, recent, retryAfterMinutes };
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[ratelimit] check failed, allowing:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
    return { allowed: true, recent: 0, retryAfterMinutes: 0 };
  }
}

/** Record one failed attempt, and opportunistically sweep expired rows. */
export async function recordLoginFailure(client: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await query("INSERT INTO login_attempts (client) VALUES ($1)", [client]);
    // Swept here rather than on a schedule: this table only grows when someone
    // is failing to log in, so the moment of failure is exactly when it is
    // worth tidying, and it keeps the app free of a second cron.
    await query(
      `DELETE FROM login_attempts WHERE at < now() - ($1 || ' minutes')::interval`,
      [String(WINDOW_MINUTES)],
    );
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[ratelimit] could not record failure:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
  }
}

/** Forget this client's failures. Called on a successful login. */
export async function clearLoginFailures(client: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await query("DELETE FROM login_attempts WHERE client = $1", [client]);
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[ratelimit] could not clear failures:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
  }
}
````

````text
import { headers } from 'next/headers';
import { sessionIdentity, verifySession } from './auth';
import { query } from './db';
import { getAgentSettings, getPrimaryAgent } from './agents';

export function credential(h: Headers): string | undefined {
  const bearer = h.get('authorization');
  if (bearer?.startsWith('Bearer ')) return bearer.slice(7);
  return h.get('cookie')?.split(';').map(v => v.trim()).find(v => v.startsWith('lc_session='))?.slice(11);
}

export async function requestIdentity() {
  const token = credential(await headers());
  const identity = await sessionIdentity(token);
  if (!identity) return null;
  const rows = await query<{ id: string; name: string }>(
    `SELECT u.id, u.name FROM byline_users u JOIN byline_sessions s ON s.user_id=u.id
      WHERE u.id=$1 AND s.id=$2 AND s.expires_at>now() AND s.revoked_at IS NULL`,
    [identity.userId, identity.sessionId]);
  return rows[0] ? { ...identity, name: rows[0].name } : null;
}

/** Legacy password sessions retain the old installation. Native sessions never fall back to it. */
export async function getRequestAgent() {
  const token = credential(await headers());
  if (token?.startsWith('v2.')) {
    const identity = await requestIdentity();
    if (!identity) return null;
    const rows = await query<{ id: string }>('SELECT id FROM agents WHERE owner_id=$1 AND active', [identity.userId]);
    return rows[0] ? getAgentSettings(rows[0].id) : null;
  }
  return await verifySession(token) ? getPrimaryAgent() : null;
}
````

````text
/**
 * Delete rows that have stopped being worth keeping.
 *
 * Most tables here are bounded by their own shape — llm_calls holds one row per
 * model per day, slot_runs one per slot per day — and would take decades to
 * matter. `rejections` is the exception and the reason this file exists: a
 * cycle judges twenty to forty candidates and writes a row for every one it
 * turns down, several times a day, forever. That is the fastest-growing table
 * in the system by two orders of magnitude, and nothing was removing any of it.
 *
 * None of this is urgent in gigabytes. It matters because the alternative is a
 * free-tier database that fills up in some year nobody is thinking about, and
 * the failure that produces — writes refused — looks like the whole app broken.
 *
 * What is NOT swept, deliberately:
 *   - posts: the archive is the point, and the writer reads it for voice.
 *   - distributions: the publish idempotency record. Deleting one could let a
 *     post be sent twice, which is the single worst outcome this app has.
 *   - agents, post_slots, linkedin_accounts: configuration, not history.
 */
import { query } from "./db";

/**
 * What is swept, by which column, and how long is kept.
 *
 * The timestamp column is named per table rather than guessed: slot_runs keys
 * on run_date and llm_calls on day, and a rule that assumed created_at would
 * produce SQL that is perfectly valid TypeScript and fails at runtime — the
 * exact class of bug scripts/dbtest.ts exists to catch.
 *
 * login_attempts and oauth_states are absent on purpose: both are already swept
 * where they are written, which is the better place for something with a
 * fifteen-minute and one-hour lifetime respectively.
 *
 * The rejection log is read in the app as "what did it turn down lately" —
 * fifteen rows, always recent. Ninety days is far more than that needs and
 * still answers "why did it ignore this back in March".
 */
export const RETENTION: { table: string; column: string; days: number }[] = [
  { table: "rejections", column: "created_at", days: 90 },
  { table: "push_log", column: "sent_at", days: 30 },
  { table: "llm_calls", column: "day", days: 90 },
  { table: "slot_runs", column: "run_date", days: 180 },
];

/** Run the sweep at most this often. */
const SWEEP_EVERY_HOURS = 20;

export interface SweepResult {
  ran: boolean;
  deleted: Record<string, number>;
}

/**
 * Sweep, but no more than once a day.
 *
 * Called from the cron tick, which fires every few minutes — so the throttle is
 * load-bearing rather than tidiness. The marker is claimed with a conditional
 * UPDATE so two ticks racing cannot both decide it is their turn.
 */
export async function sweepIfDue(): Promise<SweepResult> {
  const empty: SweepResult = { ran: false, deleted: {} };
  try {
    const claimed = await query<{ key: string }>(
      `INSERT INTO system_status (key, value, updated_at)
       VALUES ('last_sweep', '{}'::jsonb, now())
       ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET updated_at = now()
        WHERE system_status.updated_at < now() - ($1 || ' hours')::interval
       RETURNING key`,
      [String(SWEEP_EVERY_HOURS)],
    );
    if (claimed.length === 0) return empty;

    const deleted: Record<string, number> = {};
    for (const { table, column, days } of RETENTION) {
      // Table and column are literals from the list above, never from input —
      // that is what makes interpolating them safe. The cutoff is still bound.
      //
      // Counted in the database rather than by returning the rows: the first
      // sweep on an old database could delete tens of thousands, and there is
      // no reason to carry all of them back over the wire to call .length on.
      const rows = await query<{ n: number }>(
        `WITH removed AS (
           DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE ${column} < now() - ($1 || ' days')::interval RETURNING 1
         )
         SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM removed`,
        [String(days)],
      );
      const n = rows[0]?.n ?? 0;
      if (n > 0) deleted[table] = n;
    }

    const total = Object.values(deleted).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
    console.log(
      total > 0
        ? `[retention] swept ${total} row(s): ${JSON.stringify(deleted)}`
        : "[retention] nothing old enough to remove",
    );
    return { ran: true, deleted };
  } catch (err) {
    // Housekeeping must never take the scheduler down with it.
    console.warn("[retention] sweep failed:", String((err as Error)?.message ?? err));
    return empty;
  }
}
````

````text
/** Client-safe preparation feedback: never expose raw provider/SQL errors. */
export interface ReviewAttempt {
  attempts: number;
  lease_until: Date | null;
  retry_at: Date;
  last_error: string | null;
}

export function reviewFeedback(attempt: ReviewAttempt | undefined, now = Date.now()) {
  if (attempt?.lease_until && attempt.lease_until.getTime() > now) {
    return {status: 409, body: {error: 'Your post is still being prepared. Refresh shortly to see it.', code: 'preparing'}};
  }
  const reason = attempt?.last_error ?? '';
  const code = reason === 'below_threshold' ? 'no_suitable_story'
    : reason === 'No suitable draft yet. The worker will retry.' ? 'previous_attempt'
    : reason === 'no_candidates' ? 'no_new_sources'
    : reason.includes('free_tier_verification_required') ? 'service_verification_required'
    : reason.includes('daily_ai_allowance_reached') ? 'daily_ai_limit'
    : reason.includes('all_models_failed_or_exhausted') ? 'writer_unavailable'
    : reason.startsWith('writer:') ? 'writing_failed'
    : reason.startsWith('judge:') ? 'source_review_failed'
    : reason === 'locked' ? 'preparation_busy' : 'preparation_unavailable';
  const descriptions: Record<string, string> = {
    previous_attempt: 'The previous attempt did not produce a draft. A new attempt has not started yet.',
    no_suitable_story: 'The available articles did not meet the quality bar for your topics.',
    no_new_sources: 'There are no new usable articles for your topics yet.',
    service_verification_required: 'ByLine’s free-tier service verification needs to be renewed by the operator.',
    daily_ai_limit: 'Your daily AI allowance has been reached. It resets with the provider’s next day.',
    writer_unavailable: 'The AI service is unavailable or its free allowance is temporarily exhausted.',
    writing_failed: 'The writer could not finish a usable draft.',
    source_review_failed: 'The AI service could not finish reviewing the source articles.',
    preparation_busy: 'Another preparation is already running.',
    preparation_unavailable: 'Preparation has not produced a draft yet.',
  };
  const waiting = !!attempt && attempt.retry_at.getTime() > now;
  const retry = attempt && attempt.attempts < 3
    ? waiting ? 'ByLine will retry in about ' + Math.max(1, Math.ceil((attempt.retry_at.getTime() - now) / 60000)) + ' minutes while the server is running.'
      : 'ByLine is due to retry while the server is running.'
    : waiting ? 'Automatic retries for today have ended. You can try again in about ' + Math.max(1, Math.ceil((attempt!.retry_at.getTime() - now) / 60000)) + ' minutes, or use Start a post.'
      : 'You can try again, or use Start a post to write your own.';
  return {status: waiting ? 429 : 503, body: {
    error: `${descriptions[code]} ${retry} Your settings are saved.`, code,
    retryAt: waiting ? attempt!.retry_at.toISOString() : null,
  }};
}
````

## Source: lib/review-progress.ts

````text
import { query } from './db';
import { reviewFeedback, type ReviewAttempt } from './review-feedback';

/** Milestones completed, not a prediction of elapsed time or generated tokens. */
export async function reviewProgress(agentId: string, day: string) {
  const [post] = await query<{seq:number}>('SELECT seq FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND review_date=$2',[agentId,day]);
  if (post) return {state:'ready',stage:'ready',completed:4,total:4,seq:post.seq,
    message:'Your post is ready to review.'};
  const [attempt] = await query<ReviewAttempt & {stage:string|null}>(
    'SELECT attempts,lease_until,retry_at,last_error,stage FROM review_deliveries WHERE agent_id=$1 AND delivery_date=$2',[agentId,day]);
  if (!attempt) return {state:'idle',stage:null,completed:0,total:4};
  const stages = ['discovering','judging','writing','saving'];
  const completed = Math.max(0,stages.indexOf(attempt.stage??''));
  const active = (attempt.lease_until?.getTime()??0)>Date.now();
  if (active) return {state:'working',stage:attempt.stage??'discovering',completed,total:4};
  const retrying = attempt.attempts<3;
  return {state:retrying?'waiting':'paused',stage:attempt.stage,completed,total:4,
    retryAt:retrying?attempt.retry_at.toISOString():null,
    message:reviewFeedback(attempt).body.error};
}
````

````text
/** Durable daily review delivery; advanced fixed-time posting still uses slots. */
import { query } from './db';
import { runCycleWithLock } from './cycle';
import { localTestMode } from './native-auth';
import { generateSetupSample, type SetupConfig } from './onboarding';
import { localClock, nextDailyRun } from './schedule';
import { notify, type PushEvent } from './push';

export async function runDueReviews(agentId?:string) {
  const due=await query<{id:string;owner_id:string;config:SetupConfig;next_delivery_at:string}>(
    `SELECT a.id,a.owner_id,o.config,o.next_delivery_at::text AS next_delivery_at FROM agents a JOIN onboarding o ON o.user_id=a.owner_id
      WHERE a.active AND NOT a.paused AND o.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND NOT o.timetable_migrated AND o.next_delivery_at<=now()+interval '15 minutes'
      AND ($1::uuid IS NULL OR a.id=$1)
      ORDER BY o.next_delivery_at LIMIT 5`,[agentId??null]);
  for(const d of due) {
    const day=localClock(d.config.timezone,new Date(d.next_delivery_at)).date;
    await query(`INSERT INTO review_deliveries(agent_id,delivery_date) VALUES($1,$2) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`,[d.id,day]);
    const lease=await query(`UPDATE review_deliveries SET lease_until=now()+interval '10 minutes',attempts=attempts+1,stage='discovering',last_error=NULL
      WHERE agent_id=$1 AND delivery_date=$2 AND seq IS NULL AND attempts<3 AND retry_at<=now()
      AND (lease_until IS NULL OR lease_until<now()) RETURNING agent_id`,[d.id,day]);
    if(!lease.length)continue;
    try {
      let [post]=await query<{seq:number;text:string}>('SELECT seq,text FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND review_date=$2',[d.id,day]);
      if(!post) {
        if(localTestMode()) {
          const sample=await generateSetupSample(d.config);
          [post]=await query<{seq:number;text:string}>(`INSERT INTO posts(agent_id,seq,text,rationale,sources_json,fingerprint,status,kind,review_date)
            VALUES($1,byline_next_seq($1),$2,'Local demonstration; no AI call',$3,$4,'draft','auto',$5)
            ON CONFLICT(agent_id,review_date) WHERE review_date IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET review_date=EXCLUDED.review_date RETURNING seq,text`,
            [d.id,sample.text,JSON.stringify(sample.sources),`local-review:${day}`,day]);
        } else {
          const result=await runCycleWithLock(d.id,true,{reviewDate:day,suppressNotification:true,
            onProgress: async stage => {
              await query('UPDATE review_deliveries SET stage=$3 WHERE agent_id=$1 AND delivery_date=$2 AND seq IS NULL',[d.id,day,stage]);
            }});
          [post]=await query<{seq:number;text:string}>('SELECT seq,text FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND review_date=$2',[d.id,day]);
          // Preserve the cause instead of turning every quiet day, provider
          // failure and competing worker into the same misleading error.
          if(!post)throw new Error(result.skippedReason ?? 'preparation_failed');
        }
      }
      const event:PushEvent={kind:'draft_ready',seq:post.seq,hook:post.text.slice(0,160),at:null};
      await query(`INSERT INTO notification_outbox(agent_id,payload,dedupe_key,retry_at) VALUES($1,$2,$3,$4) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`,[d.id,JSON.stringify(event),`${d.id}:${day}`,d.next_delivery_at]);
      await query(`UPDATE review_deliveries SET seq=$3,lease_until=NULL,last_error=NULL,stage='ready' WHERE agent_id=$1 AND delivery_date=$2`,[d.id,day,post.seq]);
      await advance(d.owner_id,d.config,d.next_delivery_at);
    }catch(e) {
      await query(`UPDATE review_deliveries SET lease_until=NULL,retry_at=now()+interval '10 minutes',last_error=$3 WHERE agent_id=$1 AND delivery_date=$2`,[d.id,day,(e as Error).message.slice(0,250)]);
    }
  }
  // A completed row or exhausted retry survives a crash between settling and advancing.
  const settled=await query<{owner_id:string;config:SetupConfig;next_delivery_at:string}>(
    `SELECT a.owner_id,o.config,o.next_delivery_at::text AS next_delivery_at FROM onboarding o JOIN agents a ON a.owner_id=o.user_id
      JOIN review_deliveries r ON r.agent_id=a.id AND r.delivery_date=to_char(o.next_delivery_at AT TIME ZONE a.timezone,'YYYY-MM-DD')
      WHERE (r.seq IS NOT NULL OR r.attempts>=3) AND (r.lease_until IS NULL OR r.lease_until<now()) AND o.next_delivery_at<=now()+interval '15 minutes'
      AND ($1::uuid IS NULL OR a.id=$1)`,[agentId??null]);
  for(const s of settled)await advance(s.owner_id,s.config,s.next_delivery_at);
}
// Keep the database timestamp text: JS Date drops PostgreSQL microseconds,
// making an exact compare-and-swap silently match zero rows.
async function advance(userId:string,config:SetupConfig,previous:string) {
  const next=nextDailyRun(config.timezone,config.time,new Date(Math.max(Date.now(),new Date(previous).getTime())));
  await query(`UPDATE onboarding SET next_delivery_at=$2 WHERE user_id=$1 AND next_delivery_at=$3`,[userId,next,previous]);
}
export async function flushNotifications() {
  const pending=await query<{id:string;agent_id:string;payload:PushEvent}>(
    `UPDATE notification_outbox SET retry_at=now()+interval '5 minutes',attempts=attempts+1
      WHERE id IN(SELECT id FROM notification_outbox WHERE delivered_at IS NULL AND retry_at<=now() AND attempts<12 ORDER BY id LIMIT 10 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
      RETURNING id,agent_id,payload`);
  for(const p of pending)if(await notify(p.agent_id,p.payload)>0)
    await query('UPDATE notification_outbox SET delivered_at=now() WHERE id=$1',[p.id]);
}
````

## Source: lib/schedule.ts

````text
/**
 * Daily cadence maths, done with Intl rather than a date library.
 *
 * The agent posts once a day at a local wall-clock time. The cron ticks every
 * 15 minutes in UTC, so the only question this module answers is "when, in
 * UTC, is the next occurrence of HH:MM in the operator's timezone?".
 *
 * Known limitation, stated rather than hidden: this computes the offset from
 * the CURRENT local time, so on the two DST-transition days per year the post
 * can land an hour early or late. Asia/Kolkata — the default — has no DST at
 * all, and for a once-daily post an hour of drift twice a year is not worth a
 * dependency.
 */

export interface LocalClock {
  hour: number;
  minute: number;
  date: string; // YYYY-MM-DD in the given zone
  /** 0 = Sunday, matching JS getDay() and Postgres EXTRACT(DOW). */
  weekday: number;
}

/**
 * Whether Intl recognises this timezone name.
 *
 * Exists because Postgres is far less forgiving than the rest of this codebase:
 * `now() AT TIME ZONE $1` THROWS on an unknown zone rather than falling back,
 * so a nonsense value stored in agents.timezone would turn a cap check into a
 * 500 and block publishing entirely. Everything that hands a zone to SQL runs
 * it through safeTimeZone first.
 */
export function isValidTimeZone(timezone: string): boolean {
  if (!timezone) return false;
  try {
    new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone: timezone });
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** The zone if usable, otherwise UTC. Never throws, always safe for SQL. */
export function safeTimeZone(timezone: string | null | undefined): string {
  return timezone && isValidTimeZone(timezone) ? timezone : "UTC";
}

export function localClock(timezone: string, at: Date = new Date()): LocalClock {
  try {
    const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", {
      timeZone: timezone,
      hour12: false,
      year: "numeric",
      month: "2-digit",
      day: "2-digit",
      hour: "2-digit",
      minute: "2-digit",
    }).formatToParts(at);
    const get = (type: string) => parts.find((p) => p.type === type)?.value ?? "0";
    const date = `${get("year")}-${get("month")}-${get("day")}`;
    return {
      // Intl renders midnight as "24" in some ICU versions; normalise it.
      hour: Number(get("hour")) % 24,
      minute: Number(get("minute")),
      date,
      // Read the weekday off the LOCAL calendar date rather than asking Intl for
      // it separately: parsing "YYYY-MM-DD" as UTC and taking getUTCDay() is
      // locale-independent, where a formatted weekday name would need mapping
      // and would break under a non-English default locale.
      weekday: new Date(`${date}T00:00:00Z`).getUTCDay(),
    };
  } catch {
    // An invalid timezone string must not break the scheduler.
    console.warn(`[schedule] unknown timezone "${timezone}" — falling back to UTC`);
    return {
      hour: at.getUTCHours(),
      minute: at.getUTCMinutes(),
      date: at.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
      weekday: at.getUTCDay(),
    };
  }
}

/**
 * Normalize a user-supplied time to exactly "HH:MM", or null if it is not a
 * usable time at all.
 *
 * Browsers are not consistent about what `<input type="time">` yields: a bare
 * "9:30", a seconds-bearing "18:00:00", and an empty string for a half-entered
 * value are all possible. Storing the raw string means the scheduler later
 * silently falls back to 09:30, and rejecting it without saying so means the
 * UI reports a save that never happened. So: coerce what is meaningful, and
 * return null for what is not, so the caller can answer honestly.
 */
export function normalizeHhMm(value: string): string | null {
  const match = /^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})(?::\d{2})?$/.exec(value.trim());
  if (!match) return null;
  const hour = Number(match[1]);
  const minute = Number(match[2]);
  if (hour > 23 || minute > 59) return null;
  return `${String(hour).padStart(2, "0")}:${String(minute).padStart(2, "0")}`;
}

export function parseHhMm(hhmm: string): { hour: number; minute: number } {
  const match = /^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(hhmm.trim());
  if (!match) return { hour: 9, minute: 30 };
  return {
    hour: Math.min(23, Number(match[1])),
    minute: Math.min(59, Number(match[2])),
  };
}

/**
 * The next occurrence of `hhmm` local time, as a UTC Date. Always strictly in
 * the future: asking at exactly the post time returns tomorrow, which is what
 * stops a just-completed cycle from immediately re-qualifying as due.
 */
export function nextDailyRun(timezone: string, hhmm: string, from: Date = new Date()): Date {
  return nextSlotRun(timezone, hhmm, 127, from)!;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ weekdays

/** Every day. */
export const MASK_DAILY = 0b1111111;
/** Monday to Friday — the default, because 3 posts × 7 days is 21 a week. */
export const MASK_WEEKDAYS = 0b0111110;
/** Saturday and Sunday. */
export const MASK_WEEKENDS = 0b1000001;

export function isDayEnabled(daysMask: number, weekday: number): boolean {
  return (daysMask & (1 << weekday)) !== 0;
}

/** Coerce anything into a usable mask. An empty mask would never fire, so it becomes daily. */
export function parseDaysMask(v: unknown): number {
  const n = typeof v === "number" ? Math.round(v) : Number(v);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return MASK_WEEKDAYS;
  const masked = n & MASK_DAILY;
  return masked === 0 ? MASK_DAILY : masked;
}

const DAY_NAMES = ["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"];

/** "Mon-Fri", "Every day", "Mon, Wed, Fri" — for the UI and for logs. */
export function describeDays(daysMask: number): string {
  const mask = parseDaysMask(daysMask);
  if (mask === MASK_DAILY) return "Every day";
  if (mask === MASK_WEEKDAYS) return "Mon-Fri";
  if (mask === MASK_WEEKENDS) return "Weekends";
  return DAY_NAMES.filter((_, i) => isDayEnabled(mask, i)).join(", ");
}

/**
 * The next occurrence of `hhmm` local time on a weekday the mask allows, as a
 * UTC Date. Always strictly in the future.
 *
 * Generalises nextDailyRun. The loop re-derives the local clock for each
 * candidate day rather than assuming 24-hour days, so a DST transition shifts
 * the answer by an hour instead of landing on the wrong weekday — the same
 * tolerance the rest of this module documents.
 *
 * Returns null only if the mask is empty, which parseDaysMask makes impossible.
 */
export function nextSlotRun(
  timezone: string,
  hhmm: string,
  daysMask: number,
  from: Date = new Date(),
): Date | null {
  const mask = parseDaysMask(daysMask);
  const zone = safeTimeZone(timezone);
  const now = localClock(zone, from);
  const target = parseHhMm(hhmm);

  const midnight = Date.parse(`${now.date}T00:00:00Z`);
  for (let day = 0; day < 9; day++) {
    const calendar = new Date(midnight + day * 86400000);
    if (!isDayEnabled(mask, calendar.getUTCDay())) continue;
    const date = calendar.toISOString().slice(0,10);
    const desired = calendar.getTime() + (target.hour * 60 + target.minute) * 60000;
    const offsets = new Set<number>();
    for (const delta of [-86400000,0,86400000]) {
      const instant = new Date(desired + delta);
      const l = localClock(zone,instant);
      offsets.add(Date.parse(`${l.date}T00:00:00Z`) + (l.hour*60+l.minute)*60000 - instant.getTime());
    }
    const possible = [...offsets].map(o=>new Date(desired-o)).sort((a,b)=>a.getTime()-b.getTime());
    const exact = possible.filter(t=> {const l=localClock(zone,t);return l.date===date&&l.hour===target.hour&&l.minute===target.minute;});
    // Repeated times run once at the earlier instant; missing times move forward by the DST gap.
    const candidate = exact[0] ?? possible.find(t=> {const l=localClock(zone,t);return l.date===date&&l.hour*60+l.minute>target.hour*60+target.minute;});
    if (candidate && candidate.getTime()>from.getTime()) return candidate;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Human-readable local time, for the dashboard. */
export function formatInZone(date: Date, timezone: string): string {
  try {
    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {
      timeZone: timezone,
      weekday: "short",
      hour: "2-digit",
      minute: "2-digit",
      hour12: false,
    }).format(date);
  } catch {
    return date.toISOString().slice(0, 16).replace("T", " ") + " UTC";
  }
}

````

````text
/**
 * Postgres schema, applied idempotently on first DB access (see lib/db.ts).
 * Embedded as a string rather than a .sql file so Next's output tracing can
 * never drop it — the only durable state is Neon Postgres.
 *
 * Inherited from the autonomous-creator base: agents, posts, rejections,
 * scheduler_state, llm_calls, system_status.
 * Added here: the LinkedIn distribution layer — connected accounts, an
 * append-only send ledger keyed by an idempotency key, media assets, and the
 * OAuth state table.
 *
 * Rule: never edit a CREATE TABLE in place once a database exists. Add an
 * ALTER ... IF NOT EXISTS line below it — existing databases only run those.
 */
export const SCHEMA_SQL = `
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agents (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name          TEXT NOT NULL,
  domain        TEXT NOT NULL,
  persona_json  JSONB NOT NULL,
  persona_hash  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  is_demo       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  active        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE;
-- The categories chosen at init; drives discovery weighting and judging.
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS categories_json JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';
-- Daily cadence: one post attempt per day at post_time_local in timezone.
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS timezone TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Asia/Kolkata';
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS post_time_local TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '09:30';
-- FALSE = drafts wait in the approval queue. The whole safety posture is here.
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS auto_publish BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
-- Kill switch: paused agents still cycle nothing and distribute nothing.
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS paused BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
-- How many posts the AGENT may publish by itself per rolling 24h. Only ever
-- consulted on the auto-publish path; a human pressing Publish is bounded by
-- LinkedIn's own limits instead, not by this.
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS auto_publish_cap INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
-- Voice configuration (lib/style.ts): structure, emoji, hook, CTA, length,
-- hashtag cap, signature line, custom rules. An empty object means "house
-- style", so existing agents keep writing exactly what they wrote before.
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS style_json JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}';
/*
 * Writing samples the author supplied — posts of their own they are happy with,
 * or ones whose voice they want to borrow. Used as few-shot examples in the
 * writer prompt.
 *
 * This is the largest single lever on how the output sounds, and until it
 * existed the writer had never read one thing the author actually wrote: the
 * persona was invented by an LLM at init from a name and a one-line domain, and
 * every post for months afterwards was written against that invention. Style
 * RULES describe a voice from the outside; examples are the voice.
 */
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS corpus_json JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';
/*
 * A standing summary of how this author rewrites the agent, distilled from
 * (original_text, text) pairs on posts they edited before publishing. Null
 * until enough pairs exist to say anything honest.
 */
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS edit_notes TEXT;
/* How many edit pairs the current edit_notes was derived from, so the summary
 * is only recomputed when genuinely new evidence has accumulated. */
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS edit_notes_from INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS posts (
  agent_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  seq           INT  NOT NULL,
  id            TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS ('p' || seq) STORED,
  text          TEXT NOT NULL,
  rationale     TEXT NOT NULL,
  sources_json  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  fingerprint   TEXT NOT NULL,
  scores_json   JSONB,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (agent_id, seq)
);

ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scores_json JSONB;
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS continuity TEXT;
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cycle_id INT;
-- draft -> approved -> published, or rejected / failed. Drafts are what the
-- approval queue renders; nothing reaches LinkedIn from 'draft'.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'published';
-- 'auto' = the daily agent cycle wrote it; 'custom' = the user composed it.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'auto';
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS category TEXT;
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS client_request_id TEXT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS posts_client_request_idx ON posts(agent_id,client_request_id) WHERE client_request_id IS NOT NULL;
-- Ordered media_assets.id values attached to this post.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS media_json JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';
-- When this post is due to reach LinkedIn. NULL means "not on a schedule" —
-- an old-style draft, or one the author will send by hand.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scheduled_for TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS published_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
-- Which slot produced this, if any. Deliberately NOT a foreign key: deleting a
-- slot must not cascade into published history, and a post that outlives its
-- slot is normal rather than an error.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS slot_id UUID;
-- When a human said yes. The publisher requires either this or the slot's own
-- auto_publish — an unreviewed draft never goes out on hold-mode slots.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cleared_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
-- Set while the composer has this post open, so the scheduled send cannot fire
-- mid-edit and publish half a sentence. Carries an expiry rather than a flag:
-- a crashed app must not be able to silence a slot forever.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS hold_until TIMESTAMPTZ;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS posts_due_idx ON posts (agent_id, status, scheduled_for);
-- Hashtags chosen by the writer; appended deterministically at assembly time.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS hashtags_json JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';
-- Whether this post used a Marvel line, so the writer can ration the signature.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS used_quote BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
-- Text as actually sent to LinkedIn (after formatting), kept for the record.
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS linkedin_text TEXT;
/*
 * What the agent wrote, before the author touched it. Captured on the FIRST
 * edit only, so it always holds the machine's version rather than the previous
 * human revision.
 *
 * Every time someone rewrites a draft before publishing they produce a labelled
 * training pair — the AI version, and the version a human was willing to sign.
 * That is the highest-quality signal this system will ever have about the
 * author's voice, and until this column existed the edit overwrote posts.text
 * in place and the original was gone forever.
 */
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS original_text TEXT;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS posts_status_idx ON posts (agent_id, status, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rejections (
  id           BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  agent_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  cycle_id     INT  NOT NULL,
  title        TEXT NOT NULL,
  url          TEXT NOT NULL,
  scores_json  JSONB NOT NULL,
  reason       TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scheduler_state (
  agent_id     UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES agents(id),
  last_run_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  next_run_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  cycle_count  INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

/*
 * The daily timetable. One row per recurring posting time.
 *
 * This replaces agents.post_time_local, which held a single HH:MM and could
 * therefore only ever describe one post a day. That column is left in place and
 * still populated — it is the migration source (see lib/slots.ts) and the value
 * the web dashboard reads — but the scheduler no longer consults it.
 *
 * next_run_at stores the next OCCURRENCE (when the post should go out), not the
 * next generation time. Generation is derived as next_run_at - lead_minutes in
 * the due query, so the two can never drift apart the way two stored timestamps
 * eventually would.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS post_slots (
  id               UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  agent_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  local_time       TEXT NOT NULL,
  -- Bit per weekday, 0 = Sunday, matching both JS getDay() and Postgres DOW.
  -- 127 = every day, 62 = Mon-Fri (the default: three posts every single day
  -- is 21 a week, which almost nobody actually wants).
  days_mask        INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 62,
  -- The review window, in minutes. Treated as a MINIMUM, never a target — see
  -- lib/slots.ts for why a drifting cron must only ever give you more warning.
  lead_minutes     INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 15,
  -- Per slot, not per agent: the morning slot can be trusted to publish itself
  -- while an evening one still waits for a human.
  auto_publish     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  -- Empty array = whatever the agent as a whole is watching.
  categories_json  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  enabled          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  position         INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  next_run_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS post_slots_due_idx ON post_slots (agent_id, enabled, next_run_at);

/*
 * One row per slot per local day — the INSTANCE of a recurring rule.
 *
 * Three jobs. It is the idempotency guard that stops a slot generating twice in
 * a day however often the cron fires. It is the timeline the UI renders,
 * including the days when nothing cleared the threshold, so silence is visible
 * as a judgment rather than looking like a broken cron. And because today's row
 * is separate from the recurring rule, a one-off change — skip tonight, move
 * this morning to 11:00 — is an update here and never a edit to the schedule.
 *
 * outcome: pending | drafted | silent | missed | failed | published
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS slot_runs (
  slot_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES post_slots(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  run_date      DATE NOT NULL,
  scheduled_for TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  generated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  post_seq      INT,
  outcome       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  detail        TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (slot_id, run_date)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS slot_runs_date_idx ON slot_runs (run_date DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_calls (
  day          DATE NOT NULL,
  model        TEXT NOT NULL,
  call_count   INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (day, model)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS system_status (
  key         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value       JSONB NOT NULL,
  updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- LinkedIn

/*
 * One connected LinkedIn member per agent. Tokens are AES-256-GCM encrypted
 * with TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (lib/crypto.ts) — a Postgres dump must not be a
 * posting credential.
 *
 * refresh_token_enc is almost always NULL: LinkedIn issues programmatic
 * refresh tokens only to approved Marketing Developer Platform partners. A
 * standard app gets a 60-day access token, so expires_at drives the re-auth
 * banner and the automatic pause.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS linkedin_accounts (
  agent_id          UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES agents(id),
  member_urn        TEXT NOT NULL,
  member_name       TEXT,
  member_picture    TEXT,
  access_token_enc  TEXT NOT NULL,
  refresh_token_enc TEXT,
  scopes            TEXT,
  expires_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  connected_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_ok_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_error        TEXT
);

/*
 * The send ledger. THE most important table for not embarrassing yourself:
 * idempotency_key is UNIQUE, so a duplicate cron tick, a retried request, or
 * a double-clicked Publish button can insert at most one row per post — and
 * only the transaction that wins the insert may call the LinkedIn API.
 *
 * status lifecycle: in_flight -> sent | failed.
 * 'in_flight' rows are NEVER auto-retried. If the process dies between the
 * API call and the status update we cannot tell whether LinkedIn accepted it,
 * and r_member_social (which would let us read our own posts back) is a
 * restricted scope we do not have. An orphaned in_flight row is surfaced in
 * the UI for a human to check rather than silently retried into a double post.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS distributions (
  id               BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  agent_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  seq              INT,
  idempotency_key  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  target           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'linkedin_member',
  status           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in_flight',
  external_urn     TEXT,
  attempts         INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error       TEXT,
  created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  settled_at       TIMESTAMPTZ
);

/*
 * 'auto'   — the daily cycle published this without a human.
 * 'manual' — a person pressed Publish.
 * The two are capped separately: the agent gets a deliberately small allowance
 * so a logic error cannot spam a real profile, while a human is limited only
 * by what LinkedIn itself permits. Defaulting to 'manual' is the safe choice
 * for pre-existing rows: it never makes the agent's allowance look emptier
 * than it is.
 */
ALTER TABLE distributions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS distributions_agent_idx ON distributions (agent_id, created_at DESC);

/*
 * Media registered with LinkedIn. The browser PUTs bytes straight to
 * upload_url (Vercel caps request bodies near 4.5MB, so proxying images
 * through the function would break on ordinary phone photos).
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS media_assets (
  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  agent_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  kind         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'image',
  linkedin_urn TEXT NOT NULL,
  upload_url   TEXT NOT NULL,
  alt_text     TEXT,
  filename     TEXT,
  status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'initialized',
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

/*
 * One row per feed, recording whether it still works.
 *
 * Feeds die quietly. A blog moves host, an RSS path changes, a site adds
 * Cloudflare — and discovery logs one warning per cycle and carries on with the
 * other twenty-six, which is the correct behaviour and also why nobody ever
 * notices. Over a couple of years that is how a reading list of 27 sources
 * becomes a reading list of 12 without a single alert.
 *
 * Keyed by feed NAME rather than URL so a feed whose URL is corrected keeps its
 * history instead of appearing to be a brand new source that has always worked.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS feed_health (
  name            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  last_ok_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_failed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  /* Reset to zero by any successful fetch. */
  fails_in_a_row  INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error      TEXT,
  updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

/*
 * Devices that may receive push notifications, and what has been sent.
 *
 * The token is the primary key rather than an id: FCM issues one per app
 * install and rotates it, so the same phone reappearing with a new token is a
 * new row and the old one is deleted when FCM reports it dead.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS device_tokens (
  token        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  agent_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  platform     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'android',
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS device_tokens_agent ON device_tokens (agent_id);

/*
 * What has been sent, so a standing problem is not reported on every tick.
 * A stalled scheduler is re-detected every minute; without this the two alerts
 * that most need to be believed would be the two that get muted first.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS push_log (
  id       BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  agent_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  kind     TEXT NOT NULL,
  sent_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS push_log_agent_kind_at ON push_log (agent_id, kind, sent_at DESC);

/*
 * Failed login attempts, for rate limiting.
 *
 * In a table rather than in memory because the gate runs on serverless
 * instances that do not share memory: a per-process counter is reset by every
 * cold start and bypassed entirely by concurrent requests landing on different
 * instances, which is exactly the shape a guessing attack has.
 */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS login_attempts (
  id         BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  /* Truncated client address. Kept only long enough to rate limit. */
  client     TEXT NOT NULL,
  at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS login_attempts_client_at ON login_attempts (client, at DESC);

/* Short-lived CSRF state for the OAuth round trip; swept on use and by age. */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oauth_states (
  state       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  agent_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS byline_users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  provider TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE(provider, subject)
);
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS owner_id UUID REFERENCES byline_users(id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS agents_owner_unique ON agents(owner_id) WHERE owner_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS byline_sessions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES byline_users(id),
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS native_auth (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, provider TEXT NOT NULL, verifier_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  redirect_uri TEXT NOT NULL, user_id UUID REFERENCES byline_users(id),
  error TEXT, claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS onboarding (
  user_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES byline_users(id),
  config JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', revision INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  preview JSONB, preview_revision INT, accepted_revision INT,
  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, next_delivery_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  preview_attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, attempts_day DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
  generating_until TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS review_deliveries (
  agent_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id), delivery_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  seq INT, attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, retry_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  lease_until TIMESTAMPTZ, last_error TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id, delivery_date)
);
ALTER TABLE review_deliveries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS stage TEXT;
ALTER TABLE onboarding ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS timetable_migrated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
ALTER TABLE slot_runs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS stage TEXT;
ALTER TABLE slot_runs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
ALTER TABLE slot_runs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS retry_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now();
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS slot_date DATE;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS posts_slot_day ON posts(agent_id,slot_id,slot_date) WHERE slot_date IS NOT NULL;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notification_outbox (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, agent_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  payload JSONB NOT NULL, dedupe_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, retry_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  delivered_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);
ALTER TABLE oauth_states ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS native BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
ALTER TABLE oauth_states ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS return_uri TEXT;
ALTER TABLE native_auth ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS return_uri TEXT;
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS review_date TEXT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS posts_review_day ON posts(agent_id,review_date) WHERE review_date IS NOT NULL;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS post_counters(agent_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES agents(id), value INT NOT NULL);
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION byline_next_seq(a UUID) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE n INT;
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO post_counters(agent_id,value) SELECT a, COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1 FROM posts WHERE agent_id=a
  ON CONFLICT(agent_id) DO UPDATE SET value=GREATEST(post_counters.value+1,EXCLUDED.value) RETURNING value INTO n;
  RETURN n;
END $$;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ai_user_days(owner TEXT NOT NULL,day DATE NOT NULL,requests INT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(owner,day));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ai_provider_days(model TEXT NOT NULL,day DATE NOT NULL,attempts INT NOT NULL,next_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(model,day));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ai_usage(id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,owner TEXT NOT NULL,model TEXT NOT NULL,success BOOLEAN NOT NULL,input_tokens INT,output_tokens INT,created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now());
`;

````
