````text
import { isCategoryId, MAX_SELECTED_CATEGORIES, describeCategories, type CategoryId } from './categories';
import { SUBJECT_GROUPS, subjectId } from './category-catalogue';
import type { PersonaRecord } from './persona-prompt';
import { isValidTimeZone, normalizeHhMm, nextDailyRun, localClock } from './schedule';
import { parseStyle, type StyleConfig } from './style';

export const INDUSTRIES = [
  {id:'tech',label:'Technology',categories:['emerging-tech','ai-ml','dev-tooling'],topics:['AI','Software development','Emerging technology','Product building','Open source']},
  {id:'marketing',label:'Marketing',categories:['marketing'],topics:['Content strategy','Brand building','Customer experience','Growth','Research']},
  {id:'hr',label:'People & HR',categories:['hr'],topics:['Hiring','Leadership','Workplace culture','Learning','Employee experience']},
  {id:'finance',label:'Finance',categories:['finance'],topics:['Economic trends','Financial technology','Banking','Business finance','Financial literacy']},
  {id:'healthcare',label:'Healthcare',categories:['healthcare'],topics:['Public health','Health technology','Care delivery','Research','Prevention']},
  {id:'business',label:'Business',categories:['business'],topics:['Entrepreneurship','Strategy','Leadership','Customers','Operations']},
  ...SUBJECT_GROUPS.map(([id, label, subjects]) => ({id, label,
    categories: subjects.split('|').slice(0, 3).map(subject => subjectId(id, subject)),
    topics: subjects.split('|')})),
] as const;
export const VOICES = ['professional','conversational','storyteller','punchy','analytical','educational','reflective','warm','witty','inspirational'] as const;
export interface SetupConfig {industry:string;topics:string[];categories?:CategoryId[];voice:string;voiceNotes?:string;style?:Partial<StyleConfig>;samples:string[];timezone:string;time:string;notifications:string}
export const defaultSetup:SetupConfig={industry:'tech',topics:['AI','Software development','Emerging technology'],voice:'professional',samples:[],timezone:'UTC',time:'09:00',notifications:'not_requested'};
export function parseSetup(v:unknown):SetupConfig {
  const b=v as Partial<SetupConfig>;
  if (!b || typeof b!=='object' || !INDUSTRIES.some(i=>i.id===b.industry)) throw new Error('Choose an industry.');
  if (!Array.isArray(b.topics)||b.topics.length<1||b.topics.length>12||b.topics.some(t=>typeof t!=='string'||t.trim().length<2||t.length>80)) throw new Error('Choose 1–12 topics.');
  if (new Set(b.topics.map(t=>t.trim().toLowerCase())).size!==b.topics.length) throw new Error('Choose distinct topics.');
  if (b.voice !== undefined && !VOICES.some(v=>v===b.voice)) throw new Error('Choose a voice.');
  if (b.categories !== undefined && (!Array.isArray(b.categories) || b.categories.length < 1 || b.categories.length > MAX_SELECTED_CATEGORIES || b.categories.some(id => !isCategoryId(id)) || new Set(b.categories).size !== b.categories.length)) throw new Error('Choose 1–12 distinct subjects from the catalogue.');
  if (b.style !== undefined && (!b.style || typeof b.style !== 'object' || Array.isArray(b.style))) throw new Error('Check your writing preferences.');
  if (b.style) {
    const normalized=parseStyle(b.style);
    for (const key of ['structure','emoji','hook','cta','register','minWords','maxWords','hashtagCount'] as const) {
      if (b.style[key] !== undefined && b.style[key] !== normalized[key]) throw new Error('Check your writing preferences and word range.');
    }
    if (b.style.bannedPhrases !== undefined && (!Array.isArray(b.style.bannedPhrases) || b.style.bannedPhrases.length>40 || b.style.bannedPhrases.some(v=>typeof v!=='string'||v.trim().length>80))) throw new Error('Use up to 40 phrases to avoid, each up to 80 characters.');
  }
  if (b.voiceNotes !== undefined && (typeof b.voiceNotes !== 'string' || b.voiceNotes.length > 1200)) throw new Error('Describe your voice in up to 1200 characters.');
  if (!Array.isArray(b.samples)||b.samples.length>3||b.samples.some(s=>typeof s!=='string'||s.trim().length<80||s.length>2400)) throw new Error('Use up to three post samples, each 80–2400 characters.');
  if (typeof b.timezone!=='string'||!isValidTimeZone(b.timezone)) throw new Error('Choose a valid timezone.');
  const time=typeof b.time==='string'?normalizeHhMm(b.time):null;
  if (!time) throw new Error('Choose a delivery time.');
  return {...defaultSetup,...b,voice:b.voice??defaultSetup.voice,topics:b.topics.map(t=>t.trim()),samples:b.samples.map(s=>s.trim()),time,
    notifications:['enabled','denied','unavailable','later'].includes(b.notifications??'')?b.notifications!:'not_requested'} as SetupConfig;
}
export function setupStyle(c:SetupConfig) {
  return parseStyle({signature:null,register:c.voice==='professional'?'practitioner':'peer',
    structure:c.voice==='punchy'?'short-lines':'prose',minWords:c.voice==='punchy'?60:100,maxWords:c.voice==='punchy'?140:200,
    ...c.style,
    customRules:[`Use a ${c.voice} tone.`, 'Never invent personal experiences, credentials, results or opinions.',
      ...(c.voiceNotes?.match(/[\s\S]{1,240}/g) ?? [])]});
}
export function setupCategories(c: SetupConfig): CategoryId[] {
  return c.categories?.length ? c.categories : [...INDUSTRIES.find(i=>i.id===c.industry)!.categories];
}
export function setupPersona(c:SetupConfig,name:string): PersonaRecord & {managed:true} {
  return {input:{name,domain:describeCategories(setupCategories(c))},managed:true,builtFor:setupCategories(c),identity:{voice:`${c.voice}. ${c.voiceNotes ?? ''} Never invent the author's experiences or opinions.`,interests:c.topics,opinions:[],skeptical_of:['Unsubstantiated claims']},generator:'fallback'};
}
export function firstDelivery(c:SetupConfig, now=new Date()) {
  // Tomorrow in the author's calendar, even if today's time has not passed.
  const today=localClock(c.timezone,now).date;
  let next=nextDailyRun(c.timezone,c.time,now);
  if(localClock(c.timezone,next).date===today) next=nextDailyRun(c.timezone,c.time,next);
  return next;
}
````

````text
/**
 * The daily timetable: what a "slot" is, when it is due, and what happened to
 * it today.
 *
 * The whole point of this module is a split that did not exist before it: the
 * moment a post is WRITTEN stops being the moment it is SENT. A slot fires its
 * generation `lead_minutes` early, the draft lands with a `scheduled_for`, and
 * a separate pass in lib/distribute.ts does the sending. The gap between the
 * two is the review window.
 *
 * LEAD TIME IS A MINIMUM, NEVER A TARGET. A cron driver is not a real-time
 * system — GitHub Actions floors at 5 minutes and routinely runs 15+ late, and
 * even a good driver drifts. So the due test asks "has the window opened yet",
 * which means a late tick gives MORE warning than promised and never less. The
 * one thing a review window must never do is quietly shrink to nothing.
 *
 * Two guards stop a wobbly cron from doing damage:
 *   - `slot_runs` has a (slot_id, run_date) primary key, so however many times
 *     the tick fires, a slot generates at most once per local day.
 *   - A slot noticed more than MISSED_AFTER_MINUTES past its time is marked
 *     `missed` rather than generated. A scheduled post published hours late is
 *     worse than no post: it is a post you did not choose to send at that hour.
 */
import { type CategoryId, parseCategories } from "./categories";
import { getPool, query } from "./db";
import { migrateTimetable } from './unified-timetable';
import {
  MASK_WEEKDAYS,
  localClock,
  nextSlotRun,
  normalizeHhMm,
  parseDaysMask,
  safeTimeZone,
} from "./schedule";

/** Hard ceiling on slots per agent. Five posts a day is already a lot. */
export const MAX_SLOTS = 5;
/** Anything shorter is not a review window, it is a notification. */
export const MIN_LEAD_MINUTES = 10;
/** Half a day. Beyond this the "news" the post was written from is stale. */
export const MAX_LEAD_MINUTES = 720;
/** Past this much lateness a slot is missed rather than published late. */
export const MISSED_AFTER_MINUTES = 45;

/**
 * Head start given to generation, on top of the review window.
 *
 * The review window is a promise about when the draft is READY TO READ, not
 * about when the machine starts thinking. Firing generation exactly at
 * `T - lead` keeps the wrong half of that promise: the cycle then takes 30-90
 * seconds of feed fetching and two or three LLM calls, so a 15-minute window
 * hands you the draft with 13 minutes left.
 *
 * Worse, a cron does not tick continuously. At a 5-minute interval the tick
 * that should fire at T-15 may not arrive until T-11, and the draft lands with
 * nine minutes left on a fifteen-minute promise.
 *
 * So generation starts at `T - lead - GENERATION_BUFFER`, sized to cover the
 * slowest realistic cycle plus one missed tick. The draft is then in the queue
 * BEFORE the window opens, every time, and the window you were promised is the
 * window you actually get.
 *
 * Costs nothing but eight minutes of extra notice, and it is deliberately not
 * folded into lead_minutes: lead is the author's promise, this is the slack
 * needed to keep it.
 */
export const GENERATION_BUFFER_MINUTES = 8;
/** How long a composer's edit lock survives without being refreshed. */
export const HOLD_MINUTES = 30;

export type SlotOutcome =
  | "pending"
  | "drafted"
  | "silent"
  | "missed"
  | "failed"
  | "published";

export interface PostSlot {
  id: string;
  agentId: string;
  localTime: string;
  daysMask: number;
  leadMinutes: number;
  autoPublish: boolean;
  categories: CategoryId[];
  enabled: boolean;
  position: number;
  nextRunAt: string | null;
}

interface SlotRow {
  id: string;
  agent_id: string;
  local_time: string;
  days_mask: number;
  lead_minutes: number;
  auto_publish: boolean;
  categories_json: unknown;
  enabled: boolean;
  position: number;
  next_run_at: Date | null;
}

/** Every column [toSlot] needs, in one place. */
export const SLOT_COLUMN_NAMES = [
  "id",
  "agent_id",
  "local_time",
  "days_mask",
  "lead_minutes",
  "auto_publish",
  "categories_json",
  "enabled",
  "position",
  "next_run_at",
] as const;

/** Unqualified — for the single-table queries, where there is nothing to clash with. */
const SLOT_COLUMNS = SLOT_COLUMN_NAMES.join(", ");

/**
 * Qualified with the `s` alias, for the JOIN against agents.
 *
 * Written out from the same array rather than derived by string surgery on the
 * unqualified list. The previous version did `SLOT_COLUMNS.split(", ")`, which
 * silently failed to split where the constant wrapped across a line — so
 * `categories_json` came through with no alias, and since BOTH post_slots and
 * agents have a column of that name, every tick died with
 * `column reference "categories_json" is ambiguous`. The scheduler never ran.
 *
 * The selftests could not catch it: they exercise pure logic and never open a
 * connection, so a query that is valid TypeScript and invalid SQL runs clean
 * through the whole suite.
 */
export const SLOT_COLUMNS_QUALIFIED = SLOT_COLUMN_NAMES.map((c) => `s.${c}`).join(", ");

function toSlot(r: SlotRow): PostSlot {
  return {
    id: r.id,
    agentId: r.agent_id,
    localTime: r.local_time,
    daysMask: parseDaysMask(r.days_mask),
    leadMinutes: clampLead(r.lead_minutes),
    autoPublish: r.auto_publish,
    categories: parseCategories(r.categories_json),
    enabled: r.enabled,
    position: r.position,
    nextRunAt: r.next_run_at?.toISOString() ?? null,
  };
}

export function clampLead(v: unknown): number {
  const n = typeof v === "number" ? Math.round(v) : Number(v);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return 15;
  return Math.min(MAX_LEAD_MINUTES, Math.max(MIN_LEAD_MINUTES, n));
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ reading

export async function listSlots(agentId: string): Promise<PostSlot[]> {
  const rows = await query<SlotRow>(
    `SELECT ${SLOT_COLUMNS} FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id = $1
      ORDER BY position, local_time`,
    [agentId],
  );
  return rows.map(toSlot);
}

export async function getSlot(agentId: string, slotId: string): Promise<PostSlot | null> {
  const rows = await query<SlotRow>(
    `SELECT ${SLOT_COLUMNS} FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id = $1 AND id = $2`,
    [agentId, slotId],
  );
  return rows[0] ? toSlot(rows[0]) : null;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ writing

/**
 * Keep agents.auto_publish_cap in step with the timetable.
 *
 * The cap exists so a logic error cannot spam a real profile, and its right
 * value is simply "how many posts did the author actually schedule". Deriving
 * it removes an entire class of confusing failure: configure a fourth slot,
 * forget the cap is 3, and the fourth post fails at send time with
 * `auto_cap_reached` — which reads as a bug rather than a limit.
 */
async function syncAutoCap(agentId: string): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `UPDATE agents SET auto_publish_cap = GREATEST(1, LEAST($2, (
       SELECT count(*) FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id = $1 AND enabled
     ))) WHERE id = $1`,
    [agentId, MAX_SLOTS],
  );
}

/** Recompute when this slot next fires. Called after any change that moves it. */
export async function rescheduleSlot(slot: PostSlot, timezone: string, after: Date = new Date()): Promise<void> {
  if (!slot.enabled) {
    await query("UPDATE post_slots SET next_run_at = NULL WHERE id = $1", [slot.id]);
    return;
  }
  const next = nextSlotRun(safeTimeZone(timezone), slot.localTime, slot.daysMask, after);
  await query("UPDATE post_slots SET next_run_at = $2 WHERE id = $1", [
    slot.id,
    next?.toISOString() ?? null,
  ]);
}

export async function rescheduleAllSlots(agentId: string, timezone: string): Promise<void> {
  for (const slot of await listSlots(agentId)) await rescheduleSlot(slot, timezone);
}

export interface SlotInput {
  localTime?: string;
  daysMask?: number;
  leadMinutes?: number;
  autoPublish?: boolean;
  categories?: CategoryId[];
  enabled?: boolean;
  position?: number;
}

export type SlotWriteResult =
  | { ok: true; slot: PostSlot }
  | { ok: false; error: "too_many_slots" | "bad_time" | "not_found" };

export async function createSlot(
  agentId: string,
  timezone: string,
  input: SlotInput,
): Promise<SlotWriteResult> {
  const existing = await listSlots(agentId);
  // Refused at creation rather than at send time. A limit you discover by
  // having a post silently not go out is not a limit, it is a trap.
  if (existing.length >= MAX_SLOTS) return { ok: false, error: "too_many_slots" };

  const localTime = normalizeHhMm(input.localTime ?? "");
  if (!localTime) return { ok: false, error: "bad_time" };

  const rows = await query<SlotRow>(
    `INSERT INTO post_slots (agent_id, local_time, days_mask, lead_minutes, auto_publish,
                             categories_json, enabled, position)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
     RETURNING ${SLOT_COLUMNS}`,
    [
      agentId,
      localTime,
      parseDaysMask(input.daysMask ?? MASK_WEEKDAYS),
      clampLead(input.leadMinutes ?? 15),
      input.autoPublish ?? false,
      JSON.stringify(parseCategories(input.categories ?? [])),
      input.enabled ?? true,
      input.position ?? existing.length,
    ],
  );

  const slot = toSlot(rows[0]);
  await rescheduleSlot(slot, timezone);
  await syncAutoCap(agentId);
  return { ok: true, slot: (await getSlot(agentId, slot.id)) ?? slot };
}

export async function updateSlot(
  agentId: string,
  slotId: string,
  timezone: string,
  patch: SlotInput,
): Promise<SlotWriteResult> {
  const current = await getSlot(agentId, slotId);
  if (!current) return { ok: false, error: "not_found" };

  const sets: string[] = [];
  const params: unknown[] = [slotId];
  const push = (fragment: string, value: unknown) => {
    params.push(value);
    sets.push(`${fragment} = $${params.length}`);
  };

  if (patch.localTime !== undefined) {
    const normalized = normalizeHhMm(patch.localTime);
    if (!normalized) return { ok: false, error: "bad_time" };
    push("local_time", normalized);
  }
  if (patch.daysMask !== undefined) push("days_mask", parseDaysMask(patch.daysMask));
  if (patch.leadMinutes !== undefined) push("lead_minutes", clampLead(patch.leadMinutes));
  if (typeof patch.autoPublish === "boolean") push("auto_publish", patch.autoPublish);
  if (patch.categories !== undefined) {
    push("categories_json", JSON.stringify(parseCategories(patch.categories)));
  }
  if (typeof patch.enabled === "boolean") push("enabled", patch.enabled);
  if (patch.position !== undefined) push("position", patch.position);

  if (sets.length > 0) {
    await query(`UPDATE post_slots SET ${sets.join(", ")} WHERE id = $1`, params);
  }

  const updated = (await getSlot(agentId, slotId))!;
  await rescheduleSlot(updated, timezone);
  await syncAutoCap(agentId);
  return { ok: true, slot: (await getSlot(agentId, slotId))! };
}

export async function deleteSlot(agentId: string, slotId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await query<{ id: string }>(
    "DELETE FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id = $1 AND id = $2 RETURNING id",
    [agentId, slotId],
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) return false;
  await syncAutoCap(agentId);
  return true;
}

/** Resize the timetable itself, rather than changing an unrelated send cap. */
export async function setSlotCount(agentId:string,timezone:string,count:number) {
  if(!Number.isInteger(count)||count<1||count>MAX_SLOTS)throw new Error('Choose 1–5 posting times.');
  await migrateTimetable(agentId);
  const c=await getPool()!.connect();
  try {
    await c.query('BEGIN');
    const agent=await c.query('SELECT id FROM agents WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE',[agentId]);
    if(!agent.rowCount)throw new Error('Account unavailable.');
    const saved=await c.query('SELECT * FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id=$1 ORDER BY position,local_time FOR UPDATE',[agentId]);
    const keep=saved.rows.slice(0,count);
    for(const removed of saved.rows.slice(count))await c.query('DELETE FROM post_slots WHERE id=$1',[removed.id]);
    const used=new Set<string>(keep.map(s=>s.local_time));
    const firstTime=(keep[0]?.local_time??'09:00').split(':').map(Number);
    const firstMinutes=firstTime[0]*60+firstTime[1];
    for(let i=keep.length;i<count;i++) {
      let minutes=(firstMinutes+i*150)%(24*60);
      let time='';
      do {time=`${Math.floor(minutes/60).toString().padStart(2,'0')}:${(minutes%60).toString().padStart(2,'0')}`;minutes=(minutes+30)%(24*60);}while(used.has(time));
      used.add(time);
      const mask=keep[0]?.days_mask??127;
      await c.query(`INSERT INTO post_slots(agent_id,local_time,days_mask,lead_minutes,auto_publish,position,next_run_at)
        VALUES($1,$2,$3,15,false,$4,$5)`,[agentId,time,mask,i,nextSlotRun(timezone,time,mask)]);
    }
    await c.query(`UPDATE agents SET auto_publish_cap=GREATEST(1,(SELECT count(*) FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id=$1 AND enabled)) WHERE id=$1`,[agentId]);
    await c.query('COMMIT');
  }catch(e){await c.query('ROLLBACK');throw e;}finally{c.release();}
}

/**
 * Give an agent its first slot from the legacy single post time.
 *
 * Runs once, guarded by "does this agent have any slot at all", so it is safe
 * to call on every status read. Behaviour is deliberately unchanged by the
 * migration: one slot, at the same time, carrying the agent's existing
 * auto_publish setting — a user who never opens the new screen keeps exactly
 * the cadence they had. Days default to daily rather than weekdays here for
 * the same reason: the old scheduler ran every day.
 */
export async function ensureSlotsMigrated(
  agentId: string,
  postTimeLocal: string,
  timezone: string,
  autoPublish: boolean,
): Promise<PostSlot[]> {
  await migrateTimetable(agentId);
  const existing = await listSlots(agentId);
  const native = await query('SELECT 1 FROM agents WHERE id=$1 AND owner_id IS NOT NULL', [agentId]);
  if (native.length) return existing;
  // Returned, not discarded: /api/status used to call this and then call
  // listSlots again for the same rows — a second network round trip for data
  // it already had in hand.
  if (existing.length > 0) return existing;

  const created = await createSlot(agentId, timezone, {
    localTime: normalizeHhMm(postTimeLocal) ?? "09:30",
    daysMask: 0b1111111,
    leadMinutes: 15,
    autoPublish,
    enabled: true,
    position: 0,
  });
  if (!created.ok) {
    console.warn(`[slots] migration failed for agent=${agentId}: ${created.error}`);
    return [];
  }
  console.log(`[slots] agent=${agentId} migrated post_time_local=${postTimeLocal} to a slot`);
  return listSlots(agentId);
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------- due

export interface DueSlot {
  slot: PostSlot;
  timezone: string;
  /** When this instance should reach LinkedIn. */
  scheduledFor: Date;
  /** Local calendar date of the occurrence — the slot_runs key. */
  runDate: string;
  /** True when we noticed too late to be worth publishing. */
  missed: boolean;
}

interface DueRow extends SlotRow {
  timezone: string;
}

/**
 * Every slot whose generation window has opened, across all active agents.
 *
 * The window test is `next_run_at - lead <= now()`, computed in SQL from one
 * stored timestamp so the occurrence and the generation time cannot drift.
 */
export async function listDueSlots(): Promise<DueSlot[]> {
  const rows = await query<DueRow>(
    `SELECT ${SLOT_COLUMNS_QUALIFIED}, a.timezone
       FROM post_slots s
       JOIN agents a ON a.id = s.agent_id
      WHERE s.enabled AND a.active AND NOT a.paused
        AND s.next_run_at IS NOT NULL
        AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM slot_runs r WHERE r.slot_id=s.id
          AND r.run_date=(s.next_run_at AT TIME ZONE a.timezone)::date
          AND (r.post_seq IS NOT NULL OR r.retry_at>now()))
        -- lead + buffer, so the draft is READY when the review window opens
        -- rather than only starting to be written then. See
        -- GENERATION_BUFFER_MINUTES.
        AND s.next_run_at - make_interval(mins => s.lead_minutes + $1::int) <= now()
      ORDER BY s.next_run_at`,
    [GENERATION_BUFFER_MINUTES],
  );

  const now = Date.now();
  return rows.map((r) => {
    const slot = toSlot(r);
    const timezone = safeTimeZone(r.timezone);
    const scheduledFor = r.next_run_at!;
    return {
      slot,
      timezone,
      scheduledFor,
      runDate: localClock(timezone, scheduledFor).date,
      missed: now > scheduledFor.getTime() + MISSED_AFTER_MINUTES * 60_000,
    };
  });
}

/**
 * Claim this slot's run for today. Returns false if another tick already has it.
 *
 * Same shape as the idempotency claim in lib/distribute.ts, and for the same
 * reason: the primary key does the concurrency control, so overlapping cron
 * ticks collapse into one generation rather than racing.
 */
export async function claimSlotRun(due: DueSlot, manual=false): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await query<{ slot_id: string }>(
    // DO UPDATE rather than DO NOTHING, but only for a run that FAILED and
    // whose send time has not yet passed.
    //
    // A plain DO NOTHING made any transient failure fatal for the day: one bad
    // judge response, one 429, one feed timeout, and the row sat at 'failed'
    // while every later tick reported `already_ran_today` and refused to try
    // again. That is not what a review window is for — there is nothing to
    // review, and hours of remaining time were being thrown away.
    //
    // Still exactly-once for the outcomes that matter. A run that DRAFTED,
    // PUBLISHED, went SILENT or was MISSED is never re-claimed, so a slot
    // cannot produce two posts in a day however often the cron fires.
    `INSERT INTO slot_runs (slot_id, run_date, scheduled_for, outcome)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, 'pending')
     ON CONFLICT (slot_id, run_date) DO UPDATE
        SET outcome = 'pending', detail = NULL,stage='discovering',generated_at=NULL,
          attempts=slot_runs.attempts+1,retry_at=now()+interval '10 minutes'
      WHERE slot_runs.post_seq IS NULL
        AND slot_runs.outcome IN ('failed','silent','missed','pending')
        AND slot_runs.retry_at<=now()
        AND (slot_runs.outcome<>'pending' OR slot_runs.retry_at<now()-interval '10 minutes')
        AND ($4 OR (slot_runs.attempts<3 AND slot_runs.scheduled_for > now()))
     RETURNING slot_id`,
    [due.slot.id, due.runDate, due.scheduledFor.toISOString(),manual],
  );
  return rows.length > 0;
}

export async function settleSlotRun(
  slotId: string,
  runDate: string,
  outcome: SlotOutcome,
  fields: { postSeq?: number; detail?: string } = {},
): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `UPDATE slot_runs
        SET outcome = $3, generated_at = COALESCE(generated_at, now()),
            post_seq = COALESCE($4, post_seq), detail = $5,retry_at=now()+interval '10 minutes',
            stage=CASE WHEN $4::int IS NOT NULL THEN 'ready' ELSE stage END
      WHERE slot_id = $1 AND run_date = $2`,
    [slotId, runDate, outcome, fields.postSeq ?? null, fields.detail?.slice(0, 300) ?? null],
  );
}

/**
 * Run `fn` holding an advisory lock on this SLOT.
 *
 * Keyed on the slot rather than the agent, which is what makes two slots at the
 * same time work. The agent-wide lock the old single cycle used would let one
 * of them take the lock and silently drop the other as `locked` — a lost post
 * with no error anywhere.
 */
export async function withSlotLock<T>(
  slotId: string,
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  onBusy: T,
): Promise<T> {
  const pool = getPool();
  if (!pool) return onBusy;
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query("BEGIN");
    const lock = await client.query<{ locked: boolean }>(
      "SELECT pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(43, hashtext($1)) AS locked",
      [slotId],
    );
    if (!lock.rows[0].locked) {
      await client.query("ROLLBACK");
      return onBusy;
    }
    const result = await fn();
    await client.query("COMMIT"); // releases the lock
    return result;
  } catch (err) {
    await client.query("ROLLBACK").catch(() => {});
    console.error(`[slots] lock wrapper failed for slot=${slotId}:`, err);
    return onBusy;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------- heartbeat

/**
 * How long without a tick before the scheduler is presumed dead.
 *
 * Three missed ticks at the recommended 5-minute interval. Long enough to ride
 * out one slow run or a provider hiccup, short enough that a stopped cron is
 * noticed within the quarter hour.
 */
export const TICK_STALE_MINUTES = 16;

/**
 * Record that the scheduler checked in.
 *
 * Exists because "nothing happened today" has two completely different causes
 * that looked identical from the app: the agent judged everything below the bar
 * and stayed quiet, or NOTHING IS RUNNING AT ALL. The first is the system
 * working; the second is a cron that stopped hours ago, and the only visible
 * difference was an empty timeline in both cases.
 *
 * Never throws. A heartbeat that could break a tick would be worse than no
 * heartbeat.
 */
export async function recordTick(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await query(
      `INSERT INTO system_status (key, value, updated_at)
       VALUES ('last_tick', '{}'::jsonb, now())
       ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET updated_at = now()`,
    );
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[slots] could not record the tick heartbeat:", err);
  }
}

/**
 * The watchdog reporting that IT is alive.
 *
 * The watchdog is what notices the scheduler dying. Nothing noticed the
 * watchdog dying — and it runs on GitHub Actions, which disables scheduled
 * workflows in a repository with no commits for 60 days. So the safety net
 * could be switched off by a quiet couple of months and nothing anywhere would
 * say so. This heartbeat is read by /api/status and shown in the app, which
 * turns a silent disappearance into a stale timestamp somebody can see.
 */
export async function recordWatchdog(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await query(
      `INSERT INTO system_status (key, value, updated_at)
       VALUES ('last_watchdog', '{}'::jsonb, now())
       ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET updated_at = now()`,
    );
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("[slots] could not record the watchdog heartbeat:", err);
  }
}

/** When the watchdog last checked in, and whether that was recently enough. */
export async function watchdogHealth(): Promise<{ lastAt: string | null; minutesSince: number | null }> {
  try {
    const rows = await query<{ updated_at: Date }>(
      "SELECT updated_at FROM system_status WHERE key = 'last_watchdog'",
    );
    const last = rows[0]?.updated_at ?? null;
    return {
      lastAt: last?.toISOString() ?? null,
      minutesSince: last ? Math.floor((Date.now() - last.getTime()) / 60_000) : null,
    };
  } catch {
    return { lastAt: null, minutesSince: null };
  }
}

export interface SchedulerHealth {
  lastTickAt: string | null;
  minutesSince: number | null;
  /** False when the cron has stopped, or has never run at all. */
  healthy: boolean;
  staleAfterMinutes: number;
}

export async function schedulerHealth(): Promise<SchedulerHealth> {
  try {
    const rows = await query<{ updated_at: Date }>(
      "SELECT updated_at FROM system_status WHERE key = 'last_tick'",
    );
    const last = rows[0]?.updated_at ?? null;
    if (!last) {
      // Never ticked. Not a stale heartbeat — an absent one, which usually
      // means the cron was never pointed at this deployment.
      return { lastTickAt: null, minutesSince: null, healthy: false, staleAfterMinutes: TICK_STALE_MINUTES };
    }
    const minutesSince = Math.floor((Date.now() - last.getTime()) / 60_000);
    return {
      lastTickAt: last.toISOString(),
      minutesSince,
      healthy: minutesSince <= TICK_STALE_MINUTES,
      staleAfterMinutes: TICK_STALE_MINUTES,
    };
  } catch {
    // A database hiccup is not evidence the scheduler is down, so this reports
    // unknown-but-healthy rather than crying wolf.
    return { lastTickAt: null, minutesSince: null, healthy: true, staleAfterMinutes: TICK_STALE_MINUTES };
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- timeline

export interface TimelineEntry {
  slotId: string;
  localTime: string;
  runDate: string;
  scheduledFor: string;
  outcome: SlotOutcome;
  postSeq: number | null;
  detail: string | null;
}

/**
 * What each slot did over the last `days` local days, newest first.
 *
 * This is what makes a silent day legible. A slot that found nothing worth
 * writing appears with outcome `silent` and the reason attached, so the app can
 * say "nothing cleared 6.5 — best was 5.8" instead of showing a gap that looks
 * indistinguishable from a broken cron.
 */
export async function slotTimeline(agentId: string, days = 7): Promise<TimelineEntry[]> {
  const rows = await query<{
    slot_id: string;
    local_time: string;
    run_date: Date;
    scheduled_for: Date;
    outcome: string;
    post_seq: number | null;
    detail: string | null;
  }>(
    `SELECT r.slot_id, s.local_time, r.run_date, r.scheduled_for, r.outcome, r.post_seq, r.detail
       FROM slot_runs r JOIN post_slots s ON s.id = r.slot_id
      WHERE s.agent_id = $1 AND r.run_date > (now() - make_interval(days => $2))::date
      ORDER BY r.scheduled_for DESC`,
    [agentId, days],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({
    slotId: r.slot_id,
    localTime: r.local_time,
    runDate: r.run_date.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    scheduledFor: r.scheduled_for.toISOString(),
    outcome: r.outcome as SlotOutcome,
    postSeq: r.post_seq,
    detail: r.detail,
  }));
}
````

````text
/**
 * Post style configuration — the voice rules, lifted out of the writer prompt
 * and made per-agent data.
 *
 * Every constraint here used to be a hardcoded line in writer.ts's SYSTEM
 * string: no emojis, no bullets, no CTA, 120-220 words, two hashtags, the
 * rationed Marvel line. Those rules are a real editorial opinion and a good
 * one for a working engineer's own profile — but they are ONE opinion, and a
 * second user of this app will want a different one. So they become settings
 * with DEFAULT_STYLE reproducing the previous behaviour exactly: an existing
 * install that never touches these controls writes what it wrote yesterday.
 *
 * Two rules are NOT configurable, because they are facts about LinkedIn rather
 * than matters of taste:
 *   - No markdown. LinkedIn renders none of it; asterisks appear literally.
 *   - The first line carries the post, because everything past ~210 characters
 *     is behind "see more".
 * Bullets therefore mean literal unicode marks (see BULLET_MARK) and hard line
 * breaks, which lib/format.ts's tidy() preserves — not "- " markdown, which
 * would publish as a stray hyphen.
 */

/** The bullet character used when structure is "bullets". Renders everywhere LinkedIn does. */
/**
 * Ceiling on hashtags per post.
 *
 * Raised from 5 at the author's request. The house style still defaults to two
 * — beyond a handful they stop marking a topic and start looking like reach
 * farming — but that is a matter of taste and belongs to whoever is posting,
 * not to this file.
 */
export const MAX_HASHTAGS = 15;

export const BULLET_MARK = "→";

export type Structure = "prose" | "bullets" | "short-lines" | "mixed";
export type EmojiPolicy = "none" | "sparing" | "expressive";
export type HookIntensity = "plain" | "sharp" | "bold";
export type CtaPolicy = "none" | "soft" | "direct";
export type Register = "practitioner" | "peer" | "accessible";

/**
 * A rationed catchphrase — generalized from the original Marvel-quote rule.
 * The rationing is the whole point: a well-chosen quote is a voice, the same
 * quote every day is a tic, so the writer is told how heavily it has leaned on
 * this lately and expected to back off.
 */
export interface SignatureConfig {
  /** Where the lines come from, in the user's words: "Marvel films", "F1", "jazz records". */
  source: string;
  /** Hard word cap on the quoted line. */
  maxWords: number;
  /** At most this many of the last five posts may carry one. 0 disables it. */
  budgetPerFive: number;
  /** Overexposed lines banned outright as generic inspiration. */
  banned: string[];
}

export interface StyleConfig {
  /** Paragraphs, a unicode bullet list, punchy one-liners, or a lead plus bullets. */
  structure: Structure;
  emoji: EmojiPolicy;
  /** How hard the first line pushes. It is always the hook; this is about volume. */
  hook: HookIntensity;
  /** Whether the post closes by asking for engagement. */
  cta: CtaPolicy;
  /** Target body length, in words. */
  minWords: number;
  maxWords: number;
  /** How many hashtags lib/format.ts appends. 0-5. */
  hashtagCount: number;
  register: Register;
  /** Rationed catchphrase, or null for none. */
  signature: SignatureConfig | null;
  /** Free-text rules appended verbatim to the prompt. The escape hatch. */
  customRules: string[];
  /** Phrases the writer must never emit. */
  bannedPhrases: string[];
}

/**
 * The house style: exactly the rules that were hardcoded in writer.ts before
 * this file existed. Do not "improve" these defaults — changing them silently
 * changes the voice of every existing install.
 */
export const DEFAULT_STYLE: StyleConfig = {
  structure: "prose",
  emoji: "none",
  hook: "sharp",
  cta: "none",
  minWords: 120,
  maxWords: 220,
  hashtagCount: 2,
  register: "practitioner",
  signature: {
    source: "Marvel films",
    maxWords: 12,
    budgetPerFive: 1,
    banned: [
      "With great power comes great responsibility",
      "I am Iron Man",
      "Avengers, assemble",
      "I can do this all day",
    ],
  },
  customRules: [],
  bannedPhrases: [
    "Here's the thing",
    "Let that sink in",
    "Read that again",
    "Thoughts?",
    "Agree?",
    "game-changer",
    "This is huge",
    "I'm excited to announce",
  ],
};

/**
 * Named starting points. These only fill in a StyleConfig — every field stays
 * individually editable afterwards, so a preset is a shortcut, never a mode.
 */
export const PRESETS: Record<string, { label: string; blurb: string; style: StyleConfig }> = {
  practitioner: {
    label: "Practitioner",
    blurb: "Restrained prose, no emojis, no call to action. Written for colleagues who would mute a growth account.",
    style: DEFAULT_STYLE,
  },
  builder: {
    label: "Builder",
    blurb: "A lead paragraph then scannable bullets, occasional emoji, a light question at the end.",
    style: {
      ...DEFAULT_STYLE,
      structure: "mixed",
      emoji: "sparing",
      cta: "soft",
      minWords: 100,
      maxWords: 180,
      hashtagCount: 3,
    },
  },
  operator: {
    label: "Operator",
    blurb: "Short punchy lines, a bold opening claim, direct ask at the close. Highest-reach register.",
    style: {
      ...DEFAULT_STYLE,
      structure: "short-lines",
      emoji: "expressive",
      hook: "bold",
      cta: "direct",
      minWords: 80,
      maxWords: 150,
      hashtagCount: 4,
      register: "accessible",
      signature: null,
      bannedPhrases: [],
    },
  },
  explainer: {
    label: "Explainer",
    blurb: "Teaching voice for a mixed audience: full bullets, plain language, no jargon left unexplained.",
    style: {
      ...DEFAULT_STYLE,
      structure: "bullets",
      emoji: "sparing",
      hook: "plain",
      cta: "soft",
      minWords: 130,
      maxWords: 240,
      hashtagCount: 3,
      register: "accessible",
      signature: null,
    },
  },
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing

function oneOf<T extends string>(v: unknown, allowed: readonly T[], fallback: T): T {
  return typeof v === "string" && (allowed as readonly string[]).includes(v) ? (v as T) : fallback;
}

function clamp(v: unknown, min: number, max: number, fallback: number): number {
  const n = typeof v === "number" ? v : Number(v);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return fallback;
  return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, Math.round(n)));
}

function stringList(v: unknown, maxItems: number, maxLen: number): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(v)) return [];
  return v
    .filter((s): s is string => typeof s === "string")
    .map((s) => s.trim())
    .filter((s) => s.length > 0 && s.length <= maxLen)
    .slice(0, maxItems);
}

function parseSignature(v: unknown): SignatureConfig | null {
  if (!v || typeof v !== "object") return null;
  const o = v as Partial<SignatureConfig>;
  const source = typeof o.source === "string" ? o.source.trim() : "";
  if (!source) return null;
  const budgetPerFive = clamp(o.budgetPerFive, 0, 5, 1);
  // A budget of zero is how the UI turns the signature off; normalize it to
  // null so every downstream reader has exactly one "no signature" case.
  if (budgetPerFive === 0) return null;
  return {
    source: source.slice(0, 80),
    maxWords: clamp(o.maxWords, 3, 30, 12),
    budgetPerFive,
    banned: stringList(o.banned, 20, 120),
  };
}

/**
 * Parse whatever is in agents.style_json into a complete, valid StyleConfig.
 * Never throws and never returns partial data: an empty object, a null, or a
 * hand-edited row full of nonsense all resolve to DEFAULT_STYLE fields, so the
 * writer prompt is always well-formed.
 */
export function parseStyle(v: unknown): StyleConfig {
  if (!v || typeof v !== "object" || Array.isArray(v)) return { ...DEFAULT_STYLE };
  const o = v as Partial<StyleConfig>;

  const minWords = clamp(o.minWords, 40, 400, DEFAULT_STYLE.minWords);
  // Keep the window sane whatever arrives: a max below the min would produce an
  // impossible instruction ("write 200-80 words") that the model resolves at random.
  const maxWords = clamp(o.maxWords, minWords + 20, 500, Math.max(minWords + 20, DEFAULT_STYLE.maxWords));

  return {
    structure: oneOf(o.structure, ["prose", "bullets", "short-lines", "mixed"], DEFAULT_STYLE.structure),
    emoji: oneOf(o.emoji, ["none", "sparing", "expressive"], DEFAULT_STYLE.emoji),
    hook: oneOf(o.hook, ["plain", "sharp", "bold"], DEFAULT_STYLE.hook),
    cta: oneOf(o.cta, ["none", "soft", "direct"], DEFAULT_STYLE.cta),
    minWords,
    maxWords,
    hashtagCount: clamp(o.hashtagCount, 0, MAX_HASHTAGS, DEFAULT_STYLE.hashtagCount),
    register: oneOf(o.register, ["practitioner", "peer", "accessible"], DEFAULT_STYLE.register),
    // These three use presence rather than truthiness: an ABSENT key means
    // "unset, use the house default", while an explicitly supplied empty array
    // means "I want none of these". Reading a missing key as an empty list
    // would silently strip the default banned phrases from every agent whose
    // style_json predates this column.
    signature: "signature" in o ? parseSignature(o.signature) : DEFAULT_STYLE.signature,
    customRules: "customRules" in o ? stringList(o.customRules, 12, 240) : DEFAULT_STYLE.customRules,
    bannedPhrases:
      "bannedPhrases" in o ? stringList(o.bannedPhrases, 40, 80) : DEFAULT_STYLE.bannedPhrases,
  };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ prompting

const STRUCTURE_RULES: Record<Structure, string> = {
  prose:
    "STRUCTURE: paragraphs of 2-4 sentences, two or three paragraphs total. No lists. No one-sentence-per-line drama stacking.",
  bullets: `STRUCTURE: one short lead sentence, then 3-5 bullet lines, then one closing sentence. Start each bullet with "${BULLET_MARK} " on its own line — that exact character, never "-", "*" or "1." (LinkedIn renders no markdown, so those publish literally). Each bullet is one line, under 20 words, and carries a real point rather than a fragment.`,
  "short-lines":
    "STRUCTURE: short punchy lines, most of them one sentence, separated by single line breaks. Group into two or three clusters with a blank line between. This is the highest-energy register — every line must still say something concrete.",
  mixed: `STRUCTURE: a 2-3 sentence lead paragraph that carries the argument, then 3-4 scannable bullet lines each beginning with "${BULLET_MARK} " on its own line (that exact character — LinkedIn renders no markdown), then a one-sentence close. Never "-", "*" or "1.".`,
};

const EMOJI_RULES: Record<EmojiPolicy, string> = {
  none: "EMOJI: none at all. Not in the body, not as bullets, not as decoration.",
  sparing:
    "EMOJI: at most two in the whole post, and only where one genuinely replaces a word or marks a section. Never as bullet points, never in the first line, never decorative. If none fit, use none.",
  expressive:
    "EMOJI: use them naturally to punctuate and to mark sections, roughly one every two or three lines. Never more than one in a row, and never in place of an actual point.",
};

const HOOK_RULES: Record<HookIntensity, string> = {
  plain:
    "HOOK: open by plainly stating the subject and why it matters. Calm and informative, not a pitch.",
  sharp:
    "HOOK: open with the concrete, specific thing — a fact, a number, or a claim someone could disagree with. Never a tease, never throat-clearing, never \"I've been thinking about...\".",
  bold: "HOOK: open with your strongest, most surprising claim, stated flatly in under 12 words. It must be something the post actually goes on to support — a bold opening you then walk back is the worst outcome here.",
};

const CTA_RULES: Record<CtaPolicy, string> = {
  none: "CLOSE: end on your last real point. No call to engage, no question to the reader, no invitation to comment.",
  soft: "CLOSE: you may end with ONE short, genuine question that a knowledgeable reader would actually want to answer — a real open problem, not \"Thoughts?\" or \"Agree?\".",
  direct:
    "CLOSE: end with one clear, specific ask — comment with your own experience, share it, or try the thing. One line, and specific about what you want.",
};

const REGISTER_RULES: Record<Register, string> = {
  practitioner:
    "REGISTER: a working practitioner with an opinion, writing for peers. Assume domain knowledge; never explain the basics.",
  peer: "REGISTER: a knowledgeable colleague explaining something to a broad professional audience. Define jargon in passing, without condescending.",
  accessible:
    "REGISTER: plain language for a mixed audience, most of whom are not specialists. Every technical term gets a short plain-English gloss the first time.",
};

/**
 * Render the style as the prompt's constraint block. Shared by the daily writer
 * and the composer's polish action so a user's manual drafts get edited toward
 * the same voice their automated posts are written in.
 */
export function styleBlock(style: StyleConfig): string {
  const lines: string[] = [
    "HARD VOICE CONSTRAINTS — violating any of these is a failure:",
    style.structure==='bullets'&&style.minWords>180
      ?`STRUCTURE: a short lead, then 4-6 bullet sections beginning with "${BULLET_MARK} ", then a short close. Each section may contain several short sentences to reach the requested word count. Use short words and concise phrasing; the full post including its link and tags must fit LinkedIn's 3000-character limit.`
      :STRUCTURE_RULES[style.structure],
    EMOJI_RULES[style.emoji],
    HOOK_RULES[style.hook],
    CTA_RULES[style.cta],
    REGISTER_RULES[style.register],
    // A target and a warning, not a bare range. A range reads as guidance and
    // models drift out of a narrow one constantly; naming the midpoint and
    // saying the count is checked afterwards lands inside it far more often.
    `LENGTH: ${style.minWords}-${style.maxWords} words — aim for about ${style.minWords>300?style.minWords:Math.round((style.minWords + style.maxWords) / 2)}. Also keep the body under 2400 characters so the appended source and hashtags fit. For a long word count use short, plain words, rather than long technical phrases. Both limits are checked programmatically.`,
    "NO markdown of any kind. LinkedIn renders none of it — asterisks, backticks and brackets appear literally on screen.",
    "The FIRST LINE is the whole hook: everything past ~210 characters is hidden behind \"see more\".",
    "Be concrete about the selected subject. Name the relevant development and its implications using only facts present in the source. Do not force technical jargon into nontechnical subjects or invent numbers for specificity.",
  ];

  if (style.bannedPhrases.length > 0) {
    lines.push(
      `BANNED PHRASES — never write any of these, in any casing: ${style.bannedPhrases
        .map((p) => `"${p}"`)
        .join(", ")}.`,
    );
  }

  if (style.signature) {
    const s = style.signature;
    lines.push(
      "",
      `THE SIGNATURE LINE — this person's trademark, drawn from ${s.source}, used with discipline:`,
      `- At most ONE short quote (under ${s.maxWords} words), attributed inline after an em dash.`,
      "- It must illuminate the actual point of this story and be accurately attributed. If no verifiable quote fits, omit it.",
      s.banned.length > 0
        ? `- BANNED as generic inspiration: ${s.banned.map((b) => `"${b}"`).join(", ")} — unless the story gives you a genuinely specific reason to reach for exactly that line.`
        : "",
      "- If no line fits this story, USE NONE. A forced quote is far worse than none, and reads as a bot with a gimmick. Most posts should have none.",
      '- Set "used_quote" to whether you actually included one.',
    );
  } else {
    lines.push("", 'NO catchphrase or signature quote. Always set "used_quote" to false.');
  }

  if (style.customRules.length > 0) {
    lines.push("", "ADDITIONAL RULES FROM THE AUTHOR — these override anything above that conflicts:");
    for (const rule of style.customRules) lines.push(`- ${rule}`);
  }

  return lines.filter((l) => l !== "").join("\n");
}

/**
 * How heavily the signature has been used lately, rendered as budget guidance.
 * Kept here beside the config it enforces rather than in the writer, so the
 * ration and the rule that defines it cannot drift apart.
 */
export function signatureBudget(style: StyleConfig, quotesInLastFive: number): string {
  if (!style.signature) return "";
  const budget = style.signature.budgetPerFive;
  if (quotesInLastFive === 0) {
    return `You have used no signature line in your recent posts. If one genuinely fits today's story, this is a good moment for it.`;
  }
  if (quotesInLastFive < budget) {
    return `You used a signature line ${quotesInLastFive} time(s) in your last 5 posts, against a budget of ${budget}. Another is fine only if it clearly earns its place.`;
  }
  return `You used a signature line in ${quotesInLastFive} of your last 5 posts, at or over your budget of ${budget}. Do NOT use one today unless it is undeniable.`;
}
````

````text
import { query } from './db';
import { localClock } from './schedule';
import { listSlots, type DueSlot } from './slots';
import { migrateTimetable } from './unified-timetable';
import { POST_COLUMNS, serializePost, type PostRow } from './post-view';
import { reviewFeedback } from './review-feedback';

export async function timetableDay(agentId:string, timezone:string, paused:boolean) {
  await migrateTimetable(agentId);
  const clock=localClock(timezone);
  const slots=(await listSlots(agentId)).filter(s=>s.enabled && (s.daysMask & (1<<clock.weekday))!==0)
    .sort((a,b)=>a.localTime.localeCompare(b.localTime));
  const runs=await query<{slot_id:string;post_seq:number|null;outcome:string;stage:string|null;detail:string|null;attempts:number;retry_at:Date;occurrence:Date}>(
    `SELECT s.id AS slot_id,COALESCE(r.post_seq,(SELECT p.seq FROM posts p
       WHERE p.agent_id=s.agent_id AND p.slot_id=s.id AND p.slot_date=$2::date LIMIT 1)) AS post_seq,
      r.outcome,r.stage,r.detail,r.attempts,r.retry_at,
      ($2::date+s.local_time::time) AT TIME ZONE $3 AS occurrence
      FROM post_slots s LEFT JOIN slot_runs r ON r.slot_id=s.id AND r.run_date=$2::date
      WHERE s.agent_id=$1`,[agentId,clock.date,timezone]);
  const seqs=runs.flatMap(r=>r.post_seq===null?[]:[r.post_seq]);
  const posts=await query<PostRow>(`SELECT ${POST_COLUMNS} FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND
    (seq=ANY($2::int[]) OR to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE $3,'YYYY-MM-DD')=$4
      OR to_char(scheduled_for AT TIME ZONE $3,'YYYY-MM-DD')=$4) ORDER BY seq`,[agentId,seqs,timezone,clock.date]);
  const entries=slots.map(slot=>{
    const run=runs.find(r=>r.slot_id===slot.id)!;
    const post=posts.find(p=>p.seq===run.post_seq);
    const completed=Math.max(0,['discovering','judging','writing','saving'].indexOf(run.stage??''));
    const active=run.outcome==='pending' && run.retry_at?.getTime()>Date.now()-10*60_000;
    const waiting=!paused && ['failed','silent'].includes(run.outcome) && run.attempts<3 && run.occurrence.getTime()>Date.now();
    const feedback=run.outcome ? reviewFeedback({attempts:waiting?1:3,lease_until:null,retry_at:run.retry_at,
      last_error:run.outcome==='silent'?'below_threshold':run.detail}).body.error : null;
    const progress=post ? {state:'ready',stage:'ready',completed:4,total:4}
      : active ? {state:'working',stage:run.stage??'discovering',completed,total:4}
      : paused ? {state:'paused',completed,total:4,message:'ByLine is paused. Resume it in Timetable to prepare posts.'}
      : run.outcome ? {state:waiting?'waiting':'paused',stage:run.stage,completed,total:4,
          message:run.outcome==='missed'?'This time has passed. Prepare a draft to publish manually, or wait for the next scheduled day.':feedback}
      : {state:'idle',completed:0,total:4};
    return {slotId:slot.id,time:slot.localTime,scheduledFor:run.occurrence.toISOString(),
      post:post?serializePost(post):null,progress,
      canPrepare:!paused && !post && !active && (!run.outcome || run.retry_at.getTime()<=Date.now())};
  });
  const assigned=new Set(entries.flatMap(e=>e.post?[e.post.seq]:[]));
  return {date:clock.date,timezone,paused,entries,posts:posts.filter(p=>!assigned.has(p.seq)).map(serializePost),
    total:entries.length,ready:entries.filter(e=>e.post).length};
}

export async function manualOccurrences(agentId:string,timezone:string,slotIds:string[]):Promise<DueSlot[]> {
  const day=await timetableDay(agentId,timezone,false);
  const slots=await listSlots(agentId);
  return day.entries.filter(e=>e.canPrepare && (!slotIds.length||slotIds.includes(e.slotId))).map(e=>({
    slot:slots.find(s=>s.id===e.slotId)!,timezone,scheduledFor:new Date(e.scheduledFor),runDate:day.date,missed:false,
  }));
}
````

````text
import { getPool, query } from './db';
import { nextSlotRun } from './schedule';

/** A one-time, transactional handover. Never recreate a user's deleted slots. */
export async function migrateTimetable(agentId?:string) {
  const rows=await query<{id:string}>(`SELECT a.id FROM agents a JOIN onboarding o ON o.user_id=a.owner_id
    WHERE o.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND NOT o.timetable_migrated AND ($1::uuid IS NULL OR a.id=$1)`,[agentId??null]);
  for(const row of rows) {
    const c=await getPool()!.connect();
    try {
      await c.query('BEGIN');
      const locked=await c.query(`SELECT a.id,a.owner_id,a.timezone,a.post_time_local,o.next_delivery_at,o.timetable_migrated
        FROM agents a JOIN onboarding o ON o.user_id=a.owner_id WHERE a.id=$1 FOR UPDATE OF a,o`,[row.id]);
      const a=locked.rows[0];
      if(!a || a.timetable_migrated) {await c.query('COMMIT');continue;}
      let slots=await c.query('SELECT id FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id=$1 ORDER BY position,local_time',[a.id]);
      if(!slots.rowCount) {
        const next=a.next_delivery_at && a.next_delivery_at>new Date() ? a.next_delivery_at
          : nextSlotRun(a.timezone,a.post_time_local,127);
        slots=await c.query(`INSERT INTO post_slots(agent_id,local_time,days_mask,lead_minutes,auto_publish,next_run_at)
          VALUES($1,$2,127,15,false,$3) RETURNING id`,[a.id,a.post_time_local,next]);
      }
      // The existing daily draft occupies the first slot for that day; do not
      // generate a duplicate during migration or change its publish permission.
      const first=slots.rows[0].id;
      await c.query(`INSERT INTO slot_runs(slot_id,run_date,scheduled_for,post_seq,outcome,stage)
        SELECT $2,review_date::date,COALESCE(scheduled_for,created_at),seq,
          CASE WHEN status='published' THEN 'published' ELSE 'drafted' END,'ready'
        FROM posts WHERE agent_id=$1 AND review_date IS NOT NULL
        ON CONFLICT(slot_id,run_date) DO NOTHING`,[a.id,first]);
      await c.query(`UPDATE posts p SET slot_id=$2,slot_date=p.review_date::date FROM slot_runs r
        WHERE p.agent_id=$1 AND p.review_date IS NOT NULL AND p.slot_id IS NULL
          AND r.slot_id=$2 AND r.post_seq=p.seq AND r.run_date=p.review_date::date`,[a.id,first]);
      const covered=await c.query(`SELECT s.* FROM post_slots s JOIN slot_runs r ON r.slot_id=s.id
        AND r.run_date=(s.next_run_at AT TIME ZONE $2)::date WHERE s.agent_id=$1 AND r.post_seq IS NOT NULL`,[a.id,a.timezone]);
      for(const slot of covered.rows)await c.query('UPDATE post_slots SET next_run_at=$2 WHERE id=$1',
        [slot.id,nextSlotRun(a.timezone,slot.local_time,slot.days_mask,new Date(Math.max(Date.now(),slot.next_run_at.getTime())))]);
      await c.query('UPDATE onboarding SET timetable_migrated=true,next_delivery_at=NULL WHERE user_id=$1',[a.owner_id]);
      await c.query(`UPDATE agents SET auto_publish_cap=GREATEST(1,LEAST(5,
        (SELECT count(*) FROM post_slots WHERE agent_id=$1 AND enabled))) WHERE id=$1`,[a.id]);
      await c.query('COMMIT');
    } catch(e) {await c.query('ROLLBACK');throw e;} finally {c.release();}
  }
}
````

````text
/** Hard cap per sample. Long enough for a real post, short enough for the budget. */
const MAX_SAMPLE_CHARS = 2400;
/** How many samples the author may store. */
const MAX_CORPUS = 10;
/** How many reach any single prompt. More crowds out the actual assignment. */
export const SAMPLES_IN_PROMPT = 3;
/** Edit pairs needed before a summary is worth deriving. */
export const MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES = 3;

export interface VoiceSample {
  text: string;
  /** Where it came from, which changes how the model is told to read it. */
  origin: "corpus" | "published";
}

/**
 * Parse whatever is in agents.corpus_json into usable samples.
 *
 * Never throws and never returns junk: a hand-edited row, a null, or an array
 * of numbers all resolve to an empty list, which simply means no samples reach
 * the prompt.
 */
export function parseCorpus(v: unknown): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(v)) return [];
  return v
    .filter((s): s is string => typeof s === "string")
    .map((s) => s.trim())
    .filter((s) => s.length >= 80)
    .map((s) => s.slice(0, MAX_SAMPLE_CHARS))
    .slice(0, MAX_CORPUS);
}

/**
 * Choose which samples to show, preferring the author's own pasted corpus.
 *
 * Corpus first because it is an explicit statement of intent — "this is how I
 * want to sound" — whereas a published post may simply be one the author let
 * through rather than one they admired. Published posts fill the remainder, so
 * an install with no corpus still gets few-shot examples once it has an
 * archive.
 */
export function pickSamples(
  corpus: string[],
  published: string[],
  limit = SAMPLES_IN_PROMPT,
): VoiceSample[] {
  // Both sides are trimmed before comparison. parseCorpus already trims what it
  // stores, but this function must not depend on its caller having done so —
  // otherwise a single trailing space defeats the duplicate check below and the
  // model is handed the same post twice under two different labels.
  const out: VoiceSample[] = corpus
    .slice(0, limit)
    .map((text) => ({ text: text.trim().slice(0, MAX_SAMPLE_CHARS), origin: "corpus" as const }));

  for (const text of published) {
    if (out.length >= limit) break;
    const trimmed = text.trim().slice(0, MAX_SAMPLE_CHARS);
    if (trimmed.length < 80) continue;
    // Never show the model a sample it is about to be asked to avoid repeating.
    if (out.some((s) => s.text === trimmed)) continue;
    out.push({ text: trimmed, origin: "published" });
  }

  return out;
}

/**
 * Render samples and edit notes as a prompt block, or "" when there is nothing
 * to say.
 *
 * The framing matters as much as the content. Samples are labelled as voice
 * references and explicitly NOT as subject matter, because a model given three
 * posts about synthesisers will happily write a fourth about synthesisers
 * regardless of what story it was actually handed.
 */
export function voiceBlock(samples: VoiceSample[], editNotes?: string | null): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];

  if (samples.length > 0) {
    parts.push(
      "HOW THIS PERSON ACTUALLY WRITES — study these before writing:",
      "These are voice references, NOT subject matter. Do not write about what they are about, and do not reuse their sentences. Take the rhythm, the sentence length, the vocabulary, how much they hedge, how they open and how they end.",
    );
    samples.forEach((s, i) => {
      parts.push(
        "",
        `--- SAMPLE ${i + 1} (${s.origin === "corpus" ? "chosen by the author as a model of their voice" : "one of their own published posts"}) ---`,
        s.text,
      );
    });
    parts.push("--- END SAMPLES ---");
  }

  if (editNotes && editNotes.trim().length > 0) {
    parts.push(
      "",
      "HOW THIS AUTHOR EDITS YOU — learned from drafts they rewrote before publishing. Pre-empt these corrections rather than making them necessary again:",
      editNotes.trim(),
    );
  }

  return parts.join("\n");
}

````

````text
/**
 * Teaching the writer what this person actually sounds like.
 *
 * lib/style.ts describes a voice from the OUTSIDE — structure, emoji policy,
 * word counts, banned phrases. Those are real constraints and worth having, but
 * they are a description of a voice rather than the voice itself, which is why
 * output written only against them reads as competent and generic.
 *
 * This module supplies the inside view, from two sources:
 *
 *   SAMPLES  Real posts. Either ones the author pasted in as "this is how I
 *            want to sound", or their own published posts from the archive.
 *            Few-shot examples move a model's register further than any amount
 *            of instruction, because they carry rhythm, hedging, vocabulary and
 *            the shape of an argument — none of which survive being described.
 *
 *   EDITS    What the author changed when they rewrote the agent. Every edited
 *            draft is a labelled pair: the machine's attempt, and the version a
 *            human was willing to put their name on. Distilled into a standing
 *            note, that is the sharpest correction signal available.
 *
 * Both are optional. With neither, the prompt is exactly what it was before this
 * file existed, so an install that never supplies a sample is unaffected.
 */
import { query } from "./db";
import { complete } from "./llm";

export { parseCorpus, pickSamples, voiceBlock, SAMPLES_IN_PROMPT, MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES } from "./voice-prompt";
export type { VoiceSample } from "./voice-prompt";
import { MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES } from "./voice-prompt";

// ------------------------------------------------------------ edit learning

export interface EditPair {
  original: string;
  final: string;
}

const NOTES_SYSTEM = `You analyse how a specific person edits AI-written LinkedIn posts, so a writing model can pre-empt their corrections.

You will see pairs: the draft a model produced, and the version the person actually published after editing it.

Report ONLY patterns that appear in more than one pair. A single edit is a preference about that post; a repeated edit is a rule about their voice.

Write 3-6 short imperative lines, each a specific instruction a writer could follow. Name concrete things — words they cut, structures they collapse, hedges they remove, openings they rewrite. "Be more concise" is useless; "cut the scene-setting first sentence and open on the number" is useful.

If the pairs show no repeated pattern, reply with exactly: NONE

Reply with the lines only. No preamble, no numbering, no JSON.`;

/**
 * Distil edit pairs into a standing instruction block.
 *
 * Returns null when there is nothing honest to say — too few pairs, an
 * unavailable model, or a genuine absence of repeated patterns. Null is a
 * perfectly good outcome: an invented "pattern" derived from one edit would
 * push the voice in a direction the author never asked for, which is worse than
 * leaving the prompt as it was.
 */
export async function deriveEditNotes(pairs: EditPair[]): Promise<string | null> {
  if (pairs.length < MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES) return null;

  const user = pairs
    .slice(0, 12)
    .map(
      (p, i) =>
        `PAIR ${i + 1}\n[model wrote]\n${p.original.slice(0, 1200)}\n\n[they published]\n${p.final.slice(0, 1200)}`,
    )
    .join("\n\n----\n\n");

  const res = await complete({
    system: NOTES_SYSTEM,
    user,
    maxOutputTokens: 512,
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    console.warn(`[voice] could not derive edit notes: ${res.reason}`);
    return null;
  }

  const text = res.text.trim();
  if (!text || /^NONE$/im.test(text)) return null;
  return text.slice(0, 1500);
}

/**
 * Refresh an agent's edit notes if enough NEW evidence has accumulated.
 *
 * Guarded on a count rather than a timer, and only ever recomputed when the
 * number of pairs has grown by at least MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES since the last
 * derivation. Two reasons: an LLM call per publish would be pure waste when the
 * evidence has not changed, and a summary that churns on every edit would make
 * the voice wander instead of settle.
 *
 * Only PUBLISHED posts count. A draft the author edited and then discarded is
 * not evidence of how they want to sound — it is evidence of a post they did
 * not want at all.
 *
 * Never throws. This is a background improvement; failing it must never affect
 * a publish.
 */
export async function refreshEditNotes(agentId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const pairs = await query<{ original_text: string; text: string }>(
      `SELECT original_text, text FROM posts
        WHERE agent_id = $1 AND status = 'published'
          AND original_text IS NOT NULL AND original_text <> text
        ORDER BY published_at DESC NULLS LAST, seq DESC
        LIMIT 12`,
      [agentId],
    );

    if (pairs.length < MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES) return false;

    const state = await query<{ edit_notes_from: number }>(
      "SELECT edit_notes_from FROM agents WHERE id = $1",
      [agentId],
    );
    const derivedFrom = state[0]?.edit_notes_from ?? 0;
    if (pairs.length < derivedFrom + MIN_PAIRS_FOR_NOTES) return false;

    const notes = await deriveEditNotes(
      pairs.map((p) => ({ original: p.original_text, final: p.text })),
    );
    if (!notes) {
      // Record the attempt anyway, so a set of pairs with no repeated pattern
      // is not re-analysed on every publish forever.
      await query("UPDATE agents SET edit_notes_from = $2 WHERE id = $1", [agentId, pairs.length]);
      return false;
    }

    await query("UPDATE agents SET edit_notes = $2, edit_notes_from = $3 WHERE id = $1", [
      agentId,
      notes,
      pairs.length,
    ]);
    console.log(`[voice] agent=${agentId} edit notes refreshed from ${pairs.length} pairs`);
    return true;
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`[voice] refreshEditNotes failed for agent=${agentId}:`, err);
    return false;
  }
}

````
