````text
/// The shared vocabulary. Every screen is built from these; no screen reaches
/// for a raw Color, EdgeInsets or TextStyle.
///
/// THE LAYOUT RULE, which is the whole difference from what came before:
///
///   > Copy sits on the page. A box means an object you act on.
///
/// The old system put every screen inside a stack of identical bordered
/// panels, so nothing had hierarchy and the post — the one thing on screen
/// worth reading — was a third of the box it sat in. Sections here are
/// separated by rhythm and a [SectionRule]; [ObjectCard] is reserved for the
/// three things that are genuinely objects: a draft awaiting a decision, a
/// posting slot, and a sheet.
///
/// And an ObjectCard is a FILL, not an outline. Separation comes from the
/// raised ground and the space around it; a border on top of that is the same
/// statement made twice, and a page of outlined rectangles is what reads as
/// cramped no matter how much padding is inside them.
library;

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import '../theme.dart';
import 'form_select.dart';
import 'editorial.dart';

/// What a piece of state MEANS. Never "what colour is it".
enum Tone {
  /// On the desk. Still yours to change.
  desk,

  /// Out in the world. Published, cleared, connected, settled.
  out,

  /// Broken. Missed, failed, expired.
  broken,

  /// Deliberate silence, or plain information. Gets no colour on purpose.
  quiet,
}

extension ToneColour on Tone {
  Color get ink => switch (this) {
    Tone.desk => C.filament,
    Tone.out => C.daylight,
    Tone.broken => C.flare,
    Tone.quiet => C.paperFaint,
  };

  Color get wash => switch (this) {
    Tone.desk => C.filamentWash,
    Tone.out => C.daylightWash,
    Tone.broken => C.flareWash,
    Tone.quiet => C.ink3,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- structure

/// A section heading: condensed uppercase slug on a hairline that runs to the
/// edge. This is what replaced the panel title — it separates without boxing.
class SectionRule extends StatelessWidget {
  const SectionRule(
    this.label, {
    super.key,
    this.trailing,
    this.tone = Tone.quiet,
  });

  final String label;

  /// A count, a control, a status word.
  final Widget? trailing;
  final Tone tone;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: S.x3),
      child: Row(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
        children: [
          Flexible(
            child: Text(
              label,
              style: T.sectionRule.copyWith(
                color: tone == Tone.quiet ? C.paperDim : tone.ink,
              ),
            ),
          ),
          const SizedBox(width: S.x3),
          const Expanded(
            child: Divider(color: C.rule, height: 1, thickness: 1),
          ),
          if (trailing != null) ...[const SizedBox(width: S.x3), trailing!],
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// A raised surface. Reserved for something you act on — a draft, a slot.
class ObjectCard extends StatelessWidget {
  const ObjectCard({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.tone,
    this.padding = const EdgeInsets.all(S.x4),
    this.emphasis = false,
  });

  final Widget child;

  /// Tints the edge. Null leaves it neutral, which is the common case — a card
  /// that shouts about its own state before you have read it is noise.
  final Tone? tone;

  /// A brighter edge and a wash behind it, for the one object on a screen that
  /// has a deadline.
  final bool emphasis;

  final EdgeInsets padding;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // A light boundary keeps actionable objects distinct on a white workspace.
    // Sections and navigation remain flat; only drafts and slots use this edge.
    final edge = Border.all(
      color: tone == null
          ? C.rule
          : tone!.ink.withValues(alpha: emphasis ? 0.55 : 0.28),
    );

    return AnimatedContainer(
      duration: motionAllowed(context) ? kStateChange : Duration.zero,
      curve: Curves.easeOut,
      width: double.infinity,
      padding: padding,
      decoration: BoxDecoration(
        color: emphasis ? C.ink3 : C.ink2,
        border: edge,
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.md),
      ),
      child: child,
    );
  }
}

/// A labelled form row.
class Field extends StatelessWidget {
  const Field({super.key, required this.label, required this.child, this.hint});

  final String label;
  final String? hint;
  final Widget child;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: S.x4),
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text(label, style: T.slug),
          if (hint != null) ...[
            const SizedBox(height: S.x1),
            Text(hint!, style: T.micro),
          ],
          const SizedBox(height: S.x2),
          child,
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ markers

/// A short state word. Carries an icon whenever the state matters, because
/// colour is never allowed to be the only signal.
class Slug extends StatelessWidget {
  const Slug(this.label, {super.key, this.tone = Tone.quiet, this.icon});

  final String label;
  final Tone tone;
  final IconData? icon;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final colour = tone.ink;
    return Container(
      padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(icon == null ? S.x2 : 6, 3, S.x2, 4),
      decoration: BoxDecoration(
        color: tone == Tone.quiet ? C.ink3 : tone.wash,
        // Coloured markers keep a faint edge because the wash behind them is
        // subtle; a neutral one is carried by its fill alone. Outlining every
        // small thing on screen is a large part of what reads as busy.
        border: tone == Tone.quiet
            ? null
            : Border.all(color: colour.withValues(alpha: 0.28)),
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.sm),
      ),
      child: Row(
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        children: [
          if (icon != null) ...[
            Icon(icon, size: 12, color: colour),
            const SizedBox(width: S.x1),
          ],
          Text(label.toUpperCase(), style: T.slug.copyWith(color: colour)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// A thin proportion bar. Used for scores and budgets.
class Meter extends StatelessWidget {
  const Meter({super.key, required this.value, this.tone = Tone.out});

  /// 0..1.
  final double value;
  final Tone tone;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => ClipRRect(
    borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(999),
    child: LinearProgressIndicator(
      value: value.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
      minHeight: 3,
      backgroundColor: C.ink3,
      valueColor: AlwaysStoppedAnimation(tone.ink),
    ),
  );
}

/// Something the user should know before reading the rest of the screen: a dry
/// run, an expiring token, a stopped scheduler.
///
/// Not a card. It is a condition of the page, so it spans the page and carries
/// the tone on a left bar rather than a full border.
class Notice extends StatelessWidget {
  const Notice({
    super.key,
    required this.tone,
    required this.icon,
    required this.title,
    required this.body,
    this.actionLabel,
    this.onAction,
  });

  final Tone tone;
  final IconData icon;
  final String title;
  final String body;
  final String? actionLabel;
  final VoidCallback? onAction;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final colour = tone.ink;
    return Container(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(S.x3, S.x3, S.x3, S.x3),
      decoration: BoxDecoration(
        color: tone.wash,
        border: Border(left: BorderSide(color: colour, width: 2)),
        borderRadius: const BorderRadius.horizontal(
          right: Radius.circular(R.sm),
        ),
      ),
      child: Row(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Icon(icon, size: 17, color: colour),
          const SizedBox(width: S.x3),
          Expanded(
            child: Column(
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
              children: [
                Text(
                  title,
                  style: T.bodyStrong.copyWith(color: colour, fontSize: 14),
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 2),
                Text(body, style: T.micro.copyWith(color: C.paperDim)),
                if (actionLabel != null) ...[
                  const SizedBox(height: S.x2),
                  SizedBox(
                    height: 36,
                    child: OutlinedButton(
                      onPressed: onAction,
                      style: OutlinedButton.styleFrom(
                        minimumSize: const Size(0, 36),
                        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: S.x3),
                        foregroundColor: colour,
                        side: BorderSide(color: colour.withValues(alpha: 0.5)),
                      ),
                      child: Text(actionLabel!),
                    ),
                  ),
                ],
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// A condition, on ONE line, that leads somewhere it can be fixed.
///
/// The multi-line [Notice] is right where the explanation is the point — on the
/// settings page that owns the problem. It is wrong at the top of the Desk,
/// where two of them stacked pushed the deadline off the screen. Anything
/// standing between the reader and the thing with a countdown has to earn its
/// height, and three lines of prose about a token does not.
class ConditionStrip extends StatelessWidget {
  const ConditionStrip({
    super.key,
    required this.tone,
    required this.icon,
    required this.text,
    this.onTap,
  });

  final Tone tone;
  final IconData icon;
  final String text;
  final VoidCallback? onTap;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final colour = tone.ink;
    return InkWell(
      onTap: onTap,
      borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.sm),
      child: Container(
        constraints: const BoxConstraints(minHeight: 40),
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: S.x3, vertical: S.x2),
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: tone.wash,
          border: Border(left: BorderSide(color: colour, width: 2)),
          borderRadius: const BorderRadius.horizontal(
            right: Radius.circular(R.sm),
          ),
        ),
        child: Row(
          children: [
            Icon(icon, size: 15, color: colour),
            const SizedBox(width: S.x2),
            Expanded(
              child: Text(
                text,
                style: T.small.copyWith(color: colour, height: 1.3),
              ),
            ),
            if (onTap != null)
              Icon(
                Icons.chevron_right,
                size: 17,
                color: colour.withValues(alpha: 0.7),
              ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// Inline failure, next to the thing that failed. Says what happened; never
/// apologises, never vague.
class ErrorNote extends StatelessWidget {
  const ErrorNote(this.message, {super.key});

  final String message;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: S.x2),
    child: Row(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
      children: [
        const Icon(Icons.error_outline, size: 16, color: C.flare),
        const SizedBox(width: S.x2),
        Expanded(
          child: Text(message, style: T.small.copyWith(color: C.flare)),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  );
}

/// An empty screen is an invitation to act, not a shrug.
class Empty extends StatelessWidget {
  const Empty({
    super.key,
    required this.icon,
    required this.title,
    required this.blurb,
    this.actionLabel,
    this.onAction,
  });

  final IconData icon;
  final String title;
  final String blurb;
  final String? actionLabel;
  final VoidCallback? onAction;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: S.x7, horizontal: S.x4),
    child: Column(
      children: [
        const StudioArt(scene: StudioScene.ideas, height: 112),
        Icon(icon, size: 22, color: C.filament),
        const SizedBox(height: S.x4),
        Text(
          title.toUpperCase(),
          style: T.sectionRule,
          textAlign: TextAlign.center,
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: S.x2),
        ConstrainedBox(
          constraints: const BoxConstraints(maxWidth: 320),
          child: Text(blurb, style: T.small, textAlign: TextAlign.center),
        ),
        if (actionLabel != null) ...[
          const SizedBox(height: S.x4),
          OutlinedButton(onPressed: onAction, child: Text(actionLabel!)),
        ],
      ],
    ),
  );
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ controls

/// Single-choice form dropdowns preserve the existing value contracts.
class Choice<V> extends StatelessWidget {
  const Choice({
    super.key,
    required this.value,
    required this.options,
    required this.onChanged,
    this.enabled = true,
  });
  final V value;
  final Map<V, String> options;
  final ValueChanged<V> onChanged;
  final bool enabled;
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => FormSelect<V>(
    value: value,
    options: options,
    onChanged: enabled ? onChanged : null,
  );
}

/// One selectable chip. 48 high because these are primary controls.
class PickChip extends StatelessWidget {
  const PickChip({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    required this.selected,
    required this.onTap,
    this.enabled = true,
  });

  final String label;
  final bool selected;
  final bool enabled;
  final VoidCallback onTap;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Semantics(
      selected: selected,
      button: true,
      child: InkWell(
        onTap: enabled ? onTap : null,
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.sm),
        child: AnimatedContainer(
          duration: motionAllowed(context) ? kStateChange : Duration.zero,
          constraints: const BoxConstraints(minHeight: kMinTouch),
          padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: S.x4),
          decoration: BoxDecoration(
            color: selected ? C.filamentWash : C.ink2,
            border: Border.all(color: selected ? C.filament : C.ruleStrong),
            borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.sm),
          ),
          // Center with both factors at 1, NOT Container(alignment:) — a
          // Container given an alignment expands to whatever width the parent
          // offers, which turns a row of chips into a stack of full-width bars.
          child: Center(
            widthFactor: 1,
            heightFactor: 1,
            child: Text(
              label,
              style: T.body.copyWith(
                color: !enabled
                    ? C.paperFaint
                    : selected
                    ? C.paper
                    : C.paperDim,
                fontVariations: selected
                    ? const [FontVariation('wght', 600)]
                    : const [FontVariation('wght', 400)],
              ),
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// A title, an explanation, and a switch.
class SwitchRow extends StatefulWidget {
  const SwitchRow({
    super.key,
    required this.title,
    required this.blurb,
    required this.value,
    required this.onChanged,
  });

  final String title;
  final String blurb;
  final bool value;
  final ValueChanged<bool>? onChanged;

  @override
  State<SwitchRow> createState() => _SwitchRowState();
}

class _SwitchRowState extends State<SwitchRow> {
  /// What this switch shows while the server catches up.
  ///
  /// THE FIX for toggles that felt broken. Every one of these calls the API,
  /// and the API sets a global `loading` flag that disabled the switch — so the
  /// thumb did not move until a round trip to Vercel came back, which on a
  /// phone is hundreds of milliseconds of a control that visibly ignored you.
  ///
  /// The thumb moves NOW and the request follows. If the server disagrees or
  /// fails, [didUpdateWidget] drops the guess and the switch snaps back to the
  /// truth — which is the correct behaviour for an optimistic control, and is
  /// visible rather than silent because the failure also raises a snackbar.
  bool? _optimistic;

  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(SwitchRow old) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(old);
    // The moment real state agrees with the guess — or contradicts it — the
    // guess has done its job.
    if (_optimistic != null && widget.value != old.value) {
      setState(() => _optimistic = null);
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final shown = _optimistic ?? widget.value;
    final onChanged = widget.onChanged;

    return Semantics(
      toggled: shown,
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: S.x2),
        child: Row(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Expanded(
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text(widget.title, style: T.bodyStrong),
                  const SizedBox(height: 2),
                  Text(widget.blurb, style: T.micro),
                ],
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: S.x3),
            Switch(
              value: shown,
              // Deliberately still live while a request is in flight. Disabling
              // it was the bug; guarding against a second tap of the SAME value
              // is all that was actually needed.
              onChanged: onChanged == null
                  ? null
                  : (v) {
                      if (v == shown) return;
                      setState(() => _optimistic = v);
                      onChanged(v);
                    },
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// A label and a value, read-only.
class Readout extends StatelessWidget {
  const Readout(this.label, this.value, {super.key, this.tone = Tone.quiet});

  final String label;
  final String value;
  final Tone tone;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: S.x2),
    child: Row(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
      children: [
        Expanded(child: Text(label, style: T.small)),
        const SizedBox(width: S.x3),
        Text(
          value,
          style: T.data.copyWith(
            color: tone == Tone.quiet ? C.paper : tone.ink,
          ),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  );
}

/// A row that opens something. Full-width target, chevron to say so.
class NavRow extends StatelessWidget {
  const NavRow({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    required this.value,
    required this.onTap,
    this.icon,
    this.tone,
  });

  final String label;
  final String value;
  final IconData? icon;
  final Tone? tone;
  final VoidCallback? onTap;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return InkWell(
      onTap: onTap,
      child: Container(
        constraints: const BoxConstraints(minHeight: 64),
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: S.x3),
        child: Row(
          children: [
            if (icon != null) ...[
              Icon(icon, size: 20, color: tone?.ink ?? C.paperFaint),
              const SizedBox(width: S.x3),
            ],
            Expanded(
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.center,
                children: [
                  Text(
                    label,
                    style: T.bodyStrong.copyWith(
                      color: onTap == null ? C.paperFaint : C.paper,
                    ),
                  ),
                  if (value.isNotEmpty) ...[
                    const SizedBox(height: 2),
                    Text(
                      value,
                      style: T.micro.copyWith(color: tone?.ink ?? C.paperFaint),
                      maxLines: 2,
                      overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
                    ),
                  ],
                ],
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: S.x2),
            const Icon(Icons.chevron_right, size: 20, color: C.paperFaint),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// A row that folds something away. Used for the judge's reasoning, which is
/// the answer to a question asked occasionally — not five meters competing
/// with the copy on every draft.
class Disclosure extends StatefulWidget {
  const Disclosure({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    required this.child,
    this.trailing,
  });

  final String label;
  final String? trailing;
  final Widget child;

  @override
  State<Disclosure> createState() => _DisclosureState();
}

class _DisclosureState extends State<Disclosure> {
  bool _open = false;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
      children: [
        Semantics(
          button: true,
          expanded: _open,
          child: InkWell(
            onTap: () => setState(() => _open = !_open),
            child: Container(
              constraints: const BoxConstraints(minHeight: kMinTouch),
              alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
              child: Row(
                children: [
                  AnimatedRotation(
                    turns: _open ? 0.25 : 0,
                    duration: motionAllowed(context)
                        ? kStateChange
                        : Duration.zero,
                    child: const Icon(
                      Icons.chevron_right,
                      size: 18,
                      color: C.paperFaint,
                    ),
                  ),
                  const SizedBox(width: S.x2),
                  Expanded(child: Text(widget.label, style: T.slug)),
                  if (widget.trailing != null)
                    Text(widget.trailing!, style: T.data),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
        ),
        if (_open)
          Padding(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: S.x2, bottom: S.x2),
            child: widget.child,
          ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

/// The write button, as a header action rather than a floating one.
///
/// Compact and outlined: writing your own post is a real thing you do, but it
/// is not the recurring job — deciding on what the agent wrote is — so it sits
/// beside the refresh control instead of claiming the corner of the screen.
class WriteButton extends StatelessWidget {
  const WriteButton({super.key, required this.onTap});

  final VoidCallback onTap;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Semantics(
    button: true,
    label: 'Write a post',
    child: InkWell(
      onTap: onTap,
      borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.sm),
      child: Container(
        height: 34,
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: S.x3),
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: C.filamentWash,
          border: Border.all(color: C.filament.withValues(alpha: 0.55)),
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(R.sm),
        ),
        child: Row(
          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
          children: [
            const Icon(Icons.edit_outlined, size: 15, color: C.filament),
            const SizedBox(width: S.x2),
            Text('WRITE', style: T.slug.copyWith(color: C.filament)),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    ),
  );
}
````

````text
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

/// Keeps staged settings from disappearing when the user goes back.
class UnsavedChangesGuard extends StatefulWidget {
  const UnsavedChangesGuard({
    super.key,
    required this.dirty,
    required this.child,
  });
  final bool dirty;
  final Widget child;

  @override
  State<UnsavedChangesGuard> createState() => _UnsavedChangesGuardState();
}

class _UnsavedChangesGuardState extends State<UnsavedChangesGuard> {
  bool _allowLeave = false, _asking = false;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => PopScope(
    canPop: !widget.dirty || _allowLeave,
    onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, result) async {
      if (didPop || _asking) return;
      _asking = true;
      final leave = await showDialog<bool>(
        context: context,
        builder: (ctx) => AlertDialog(
          title: const Text('Leave without saving?'),
          content: const Text(
            'Your unsaved changes on this page will be lost.',
          ),
          actions: [
            TextButton(
              onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(ctx, false),
              child: const Text('Keep editing'),
            ),
            TextButton(
              onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(ctx, true),
              child: const Text('Discard changes'),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      );
      _asking = false;
      if (!mounted || leave != true) return;
      setState(() => _allowLeave = true);
      WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
        if (mounted) Navigator.of(context).pop(result);
      });
    },
    child: widget.child,
  );
}
````

````text
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import '../api/models.dart';
import 'form_select.dart';

/// The same controls are available during setup and in the saved voice editor.
class WritingPreferences extends StatelessWidget {
  const WritingPreferences({
    super.key,
    required this.value,
    required this.onChanged,
  });
  final StyleConfig value;
  final ValueChanged<StyleConfig>? onChanged;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    Widget choice(
      String label,
      String selected,
      Map<String, String> options,
      StyleConfig Function(String) update,
    ) => Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: 20),
      child: FormSelect<String>(
        label: label,
        value: selected,
        options: options,
        onChanged: onChanged == null ? null : (v) => onChanged!(update(v)),
      ),
    );
    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
      children: [
        choice('Structure', value.structure, const {
          'prose': 'Paragraphs',
          'bullets': 'Bullets',
          'short-lines': 'Short lines',
          'mixed': 'Lead + bullets',
        }, (v) => value.copyWith(structure: v)),
        choice('Written for', value.register, const {
          'practitioner': 'Specialists',
          'peer': 'Professionals',
          'accessible': 'A broad audience',
        }, (v) => value.copyWith(register: v)),
        choice('Opening line', value.hook, const {
          'plain': 'Calm and clear',
          'sharp': 'Specific and direct',
          'bold': 'Bold and evidence based',
        }, (v) => value.copyWith(hook: v)),
        choice('Closing', value.cta, const {
          'none': 'End on the main point',
          'soft': 'A thoughtful question',
          'direct': 'A clear invitation',
        }, (v) => value.copyWith(cta: v)),
        choice('Emoji', value.emoji, const {
          'none': 'None',
          'sparing': 'Occasional',
          'expressive': 'Expressive',
        }, (v) => value.copyWith(emoji: v)),
        Text('Post length: ${value.minWords}–${value.maxWords} words'),
        RangeSlider(
          values: RangeValues(
            value.minWords.toDouble(),
            value.maxWords.toDouble(),
          ),
          min: 40,
          max: 500,
          divisions: 46,
          labels: RangeLabels(
            '${value.minWords} words',
            '${value.maxWords} words',
          ),
          semanticFormatterCallback: (v) => '${v.round()} words',
          onChanged: onChanged == null
              ? null
              : (v) {
                  final low = v.start.round().clamp(40, 400);
                  final high = v.end.round().clamp(low + 20, 500);
                  onChanged!(value.copyWith(minWords: low, maxWords: high));
                },
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: 12),
        FormSelect<int>(
          label: 'Hashtags',
          value: value.hashtagCount,
          options: {for (var i = 0; i <= 15; i++) i: i == 0 ? 'None' : '$i'},
          onChanged: onChanged == null
              ? null
              : (v) => onChanged!(value.copyWith(hashtagCount: v)),
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: 20),
      ],
    );
  }
}
````

````text
name: linkdin_mobile
description: "ByLine: your LinkedIn writing workspace."
# The following line prevents the package from being accidentally published to
# pub.dev using `flutter pub publish`. This is preferred for private packages.
publish_to: 'none' # Remove this line if you wish to publish to pub.dev

# The following defines the version and build number for your application.
# A version number is three numbers separated by dots, like 1.2.43
# followed by an optional build number separated by a +.
# Both the version and the builder number may be overridden in flutter
# build by specifying --build-name and --build-number, respectively.
# In Android, build-name is used as versionName while build-number used as versionCode.
# Read more about Android versioning at https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/versioning
# In iOS, build-name is used as CFBundleShortVersionString while build-number is used as CFBundleVersion.
# Read more about iOS versioning at
# https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Articles/CoreFoundationKeys.html
# In Windows, build-name is used as the major, minor, and patch parts
# of the product and file versions while build-number is used as the build suffix.
version: 1.0.2+3

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.1

# Dependencies specify other packages that your package needs in order to work.
# To automatically upgrade your package dependencies to the latest versions
# consider running `flutter pub upgrade --major-versions`. Alternatively,
# dependencies can be manually updated by changing the version numbers below to
# the latest version available on pub.dev. To see which dependencies have newer
# versions available, run `flutter pub outdated`.
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The following adds the Cupertino Icons font to your application.
  # Use with the CupertinoIcons class for iOS style icons.
  cupertino_icons: ^1.0.8

  # Kept small on purpose. Every package here is a thing that can break a build
  # months from now, and this app's whole job is rendering one JSON document and
  # PATCHing bits of it back — so each one below earns its place by doing
  # something the app genuinely cannot do without.
  http: ^1.2.2 # API calls
  provider: ^6.1.2 # app-wide state
  shared_preferences: ^2.3.2 # session cookie + server address
  image_picker: ^1.1.2 # attach photos; also does the downscale (see media upload)
  http_parser: ^4.0.2 # MediaType for multipart uploads — see _imageSubtype
  # Opens LinkedIn's consent page in the SYSTEM browser. OAuth cannot happen
  # inside the app's own HTTP client: the consent screen needs a real browser,
  # and a token minted anywhere else would not be the one the session carries.
  url_launcher: ^6.3.0
  # Push notifications. Comfortably the largest thing in this file, and taken
  # deliberately: there is no way to reach an Android app that is not currently
  # running without FCM, and the whole point of the alerts is hearing that the
  # agent has stopped on a day you never opened it. The alternative was routing
  # them through a second app, which trades this weight for a notification that
  # is not ours and cannot open the right tab.
  firebase_core: ^3.8.0
  firebase_messaging: ^15.1.5
  flutter_secure_storage: 10.0.0
  flutter_timezone: ^5.1.0
  flutter_local_notifications_windows: ^3.1.1

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter

  # The "flutter_lints" package below contains a set of recommended lints to
  # encourage good coding practices. The lint set provided by the package is
  # activated in the `analysis_options.yaml` file located at the root of your
  # package. See that file for information about deactivating specific lint
  # rules and activating additional ones.
  flutter_lints: ^6.0.0

# For information on the generic Dart part of this file, see the
# following page: https://dart.dev/tools/pub/pubspec

# The following section is specific to Flutter packages.
flutter:

  # The following line ensures that the Material Icons font is
  # included with your application, so that you can use the icons in
  # the material Icons class.
  uses-material-design: true

  assets:
    - assets/fonts/OFL.txt

  # Three faces, three jobs — see DESIGN.md §3. All bundled rather than
  # fetched: a CDN font is a silent single point of failure, and a family that
  # does not resolve falls back without an error.
  #
  # Plex Sans is the VARIABLE cut — google/fonts no longer publishes static
  # instances of it. Flutter does not map TextStyle.fontWeight onto a variable
  # axis, so weight comes from fontVariations in theme.dart rather than from
  # extra `weight:` entries here, which would silently do nothing.
  #
  # Barlow Condensed is deliberately the STATIC cut for the opposite reason: a
  # fontVariations list makes a TextStyle non-const, and these styles sit in
  # const widget trees across every screen.
  fonts:
    - family: BarlowCondensed
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/BarlowCondensed-Medium.ttf
          weight: 500
        - asset: assets/fonts/BarlowCondensed-SemiBold.ttf
          weight: 600
        - asset: assets/fonts/BarlowCondensed-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700
    - family: PlexSans
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/IBMPlexSans.ttf
    - family: PlexMono
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf
          weight: 400
        - asset: assets/fonts/IBMPlexMono-SemiBold.ttf
          weight: 600
        - asset: assets/fonts/IBMPlexMono-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700

  # To add assets to your application, add an assets section, like this:
  # assets:
  #   - images/a_dot_burr.jpeg
  #   - images/a_dot_ham.jpeg

  # An image asset can refer to one or more resolution-specific "variants", see
  # https://flutter.dev/to/resolution-aware-images

  # For details regarding adding assets from package dependencies, see
  # https://flutter.dev/to/asset-from-package

  # To add custom fonts to your application, add a fonts section here,
  # in this "flutter" section. Each entry in this list should have a
  # "family" key with the font family name, and a "fonts" key with a
  # list giving the asset and other descriptors for the font. For
  # example:
  # fonts:
  #   - family: Schyler
  #     fonts:
  #       - asset: fonts/Schyler-Regular.ttf
  #       - asset: fonts/Schyler-Italic.ttf
  #         style: italic

  #     fonts:

  #       - asset: fonts/TrajanPro_Bold.ttf
  #         weight: 700
  #
  # For details regarding fonts from package dependencies,
````

## Source: mobile/test/android_notifications_test.dart

````text
import 'package:firebase_messaging/firebase_messaging.dart';
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/android_notifications.dart';

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  const channel = MethodChannel('byline/notifications');
  final messenger =
      TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger;
  final calls = <MethodCall>[];
  setUp(() {
    debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = TargetPlatform.android;
    calls.clear();
    messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(channel, (call) async {
      calls.add(call);
      return call.method == 'show' ? true : null;
    });
  });
  tearDown(() {
    stopAndroidNotificationTaps();
    messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(channel, null);
    debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = null;
  });

  const message = RemoteMessage(
    data: {'kind': 'test', 'tab': 'status'},
    notification: RemoteNotification(
      title: 'Notifications are working',
      body: 'Test message',
      android: AndroidNotification(channelId: 'linkdin_alerts', tag: 'test'),
    ),
  );
  test(
    'received foreground push keeps its channel, grouping and destination',
    () async {
      expect(await showAndroidNotification(message), isTrue);
      expect(calls.single.arguments, {
        'title': 'Notifications are working',
        'body': 'Test message',
        'channel': 'linkdin_alerts',
        'tag': 'test',
        'tab': 'status',
      });
    },
  );
  test(
    'data-only and non-Android messages do not create duplicate notifications',
    () async {
      expect(
        await showAndroidNotification(
          const RemoteMessage(data: {'tab': 'queue'}),
        ),
        isFalse,
      );
      debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = TargetPlatform.windows;
      expect(await showAndroidNotification(message), isFalse);
      expect(calls, isEmpty);
    },
  );
  test(
    'blocked or unavailable platform notifications allow the banner fallback',
    () async {
      messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(channel, (_) async => false);
      expect(await showAndroidNotification(message), isFalse);
      messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(
        channel,
        (_) async => throw PlatformException(code: 'denied'),
      );
      expect(await showAndroidNotification(message), isFalse);
    },
  );
  test('cold notification tap is consumed when listener starts', () async {
    messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(
      channel,
      (call) async => call.method == 'takePendingTab' ? 'queue' : null,
    );
    final tabs = <String>[];
    await listenAndroidNotificationTaps(tabs.add);
    expect(tabs, ['queue']);
    await clearAndroidNotifications();
  });
}
````

## Source: mobile/test/api_test.dart

````text
/// Transport-layer tests: the HTTP method, path and body of every call.
///
/// These exist because of a real bug. `/api/posts/[seq]` exports PATCH; the
/// client called POST; every publish, discard and edit from the phone returned
/// 405. Twenty-four passing widget tests said nothing about it, because none of
/// them touched the network.
///
/// A route's verb is a contract with the backend, and the only place it can be
/// checked is here.
library;

import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:http/testing.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/client.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/models.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/state/app_state.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

/// One recorded request.
class _Call {
  _Call(this.method, this.path, this.body, this.headers, this.rawBody);
  final String method;
  final String path;
  final Map<String, dynamic> body;
  final Map<String, String> headers;

  /// The unparsed body — the only way to inspect multipart part headers.
  final String rawBody;
}

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  late List<_Call> calls;

  /// Builds a state wired to a fake transport that records everything and
  /// answers with [response].
  Future<AppState> buildState({
    Map<String, dynamic> response = const {'ok': true},
    int status = 200,
    bool signedIn = true,
  }) async {
    SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues(
      signedIn
          ? {
              'session_cookie': 'lc_session=abc',
              'base_url': 'http://test.local',
            }
          : {},
    );
    calls = [];

    final mock = MockClient((request) async {
      // latin1, not request.body: that getter decodes as UTF-8 and a multipart
      // body carrying real image bytes is not valid UTF-8, so it throws.
      final raw = latin1.decode(request.bodyBytes, allowInvalid: true);

      Map<String, dynamic> parsed = {};
      if (raw.isNotEmpty && !raw.startsWith('--')) {
        try {
          final decoded = jsonDecode(raw);
          if (decoded is Map<String, dynamic>) parsed = decoded;
        } on FormatException {
          // Not JSON — rawBody still carries it.
        }
      }
      calls.add(
        _Call(request.method, request.url.path, parsed, request.headers, raw),
      );
      return http.Response(
        jsonEncode(response),
        status,
        headers: {'content-type': 'application/json'},
      );
    });

    return AppState(await ApiClient.create(httpClient: mock));
  }

  test('sign-out unregisters the device with an authenticated JSON body', () async {
    final state = await buildState(response: {'ok': true, 'configured': true});
    state.phase = AuthPhase.signedIn;
    expect(await state.registerDevice('test-notification-device-12345'), true);
    await state.signOut();
    final removal = calls.firstWhere((c) => c.method == 'DELETE' && c.path == '/api/devices');
    expect(removal.body, {'token': 'test-notification-device-12345'});
    expect(calls.indexOf(removal), lessThan(calls.indexWhere((c) => c.path == '/api/auth')));
  });

  group('post actions use the verb the route actually exports', () {
    // Clearing and sending are DIFFERENT verbs, and conflating them is the
    // regression these two tests exist to catch. Clearing says "let it go at
    // its scheduled time"; sending says "go now". If clear ever starts emitting
    // action:publish again, every cleared draft publishes the instant it is
    // reviewed and the whole review window silently disappears.
    test('clear sends PATCH /api/posts/<seq> with action clear', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.clear(7);

      final call = calls.first;
      expect(
        call.method,
        'PATCH',
        reason: 'the route exports PATCH; POST returns 405',
      );
      expect(call.path, '/api/posts/7');
      expect(
        call.body['action'],
        'clear',
        reason: 'clearing must not publish — it authorises the scheduled send',
      );
    });

    test('sendNow sends PATCH with action publish', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.sendNow(7);

      final call = calls.first;
      expect(call.method, 'PATCH');
      expect(call.path, '/api/posts/7');
      expect(call.body['action'], 'publish');
    });

    test('unclear withdraws the clearance', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.unclear(2);
      expect(calls.first.body['action'], 'unclear');
    });

    test('holdForEditing takes the edit lock', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.holdForEditing(5);
      expect(calls.first.path, '/api/posts/5');
      expect(calls.first.body['action'], 'hold');
    });

    test('reschedule sends an ISO instant in UTC', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      final when = DateTime.utc(2026, 8, 20, 9, 30);
      await state.reschedule(6, when);

      expect(calls.first.body['action'], 'reschedule');
      expect(calls.first.body['scheduledFor'], when.toIso8601String());
    });

    test('reschedule with null lifts a post off the timetable', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.reschedule(6, null);
      expect(calls.first.body['action'], 'reschedule');
      expect(calls.first.body['scheduledFor'], isNull);
    });

    test('discard sends PATCH with action discard', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.discard(3);
      expect(calls.first.method, 'PATCH');
      expect(calls.first.path, '/api/posts/3');
      expect(calls.first.body['action'], 'discard');
    });

    test('editPost sends PATCH with the text', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.editPost(4, 'New body text', ['DSP']);

      final call = calls.first;
      expect(call.method, 'PATCH');
      expect(call.path, '/api/posts/4');
      expect(call.body['action'], 'edit');
      expect(call.body['text'], 'New body text');
      expect(call.body['hashtags'], ['DSP']);
    });

    test('editPost omits mediaIds entirely when not given', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.editPost(4, 'Body text here', const []);
      // Absent means "leave existing images alone"; sending an empty array
      // would silently detach every image on the post.
      expect(calls.first.body.containsKey('mediaIds'), isFalse);
    });

    test(
      'editPost sends mediaIds when given, including an explicit empty list',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState();
        await state.editPost(4, 'Body text here', const [], mediaIds: const []);
        expect(calls.first.body['mediaIds'], isEmpty);
        expect(calls.first.body.containsKey('mediaIds'), isTrue);
      },
    );

    test(
      'compose sends POST /api/posts — the collection route IS a POST',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState(
          response: {'ok': true, 'id': 'p9', 'seq': 9},
        );
        await state.compose(
          text: 'A new post body',
          polish: true,
          publishNow: false,
        );

        expect(calls.first.method, 'POST');
        expect(calls.first.path, '/api/posts');
        expect(calls.first.body['polish'], isTrue);
      },
    );

    test(
      'rewrite sends PATCH with the variant index and returns the text',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState(
          response: {'ok': true, 'text': 'A different version.'},
        );
        final text = await state.rewriteDraft(5, variant: 2);

        expect(calls.first.method, 'PATCH');
        expect(calls.first.path, '/api/posts/5');
        expect(calls.first.body['action'], 'rewrite');
        expect(calls.first.body['variant'], 2);
        expect(text, 'A different version.');
      },
    );

    test(
      'rewrite rejects an empty result rather than blanking the draft',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState(response: {'ok': true, 'text': '   '});
        expect(() => state.rewriteDraft(5), throwsA(isA<ApiException>()));
      },
    );

    test(
      'rewriting UNSAVED text posts the body, since there is no seq yet',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState(
          response: {'ok': true, 'text': 'Another angle entirely.'},
        );
        final text = await state.rewriteText(
          'Some text the user just typed out.',
          variant: 1,
        );

        expect(calls.first.method, 'POST');
        expect(calls.first.path, '/api/compose/rewrite');
        expect(calls.first.body['text'], 'Some text the user just typed out.');
        expect(calls.first.body['variant'], 1);
        expect(text, 'Another angle entirely.');
      },
    );

    test('an unsaved rewrite also refuses an empty result', () async {
      final state = await buildState(response: {'ok': true, 'text': ''});
      expect(
        () => state.rewriteText('Some text the user just typed out.'),
        throwsA(isA<ApiException>()),
      );
    });
  });

  group('image upload', () {
    test('declares a real image content type, not octet-stream', () async {
      final state = await buildState(response: {'ok': true, 'id': 'media-1'});
      final file = File('${Directory.systemTemp.path}/linkdin_test_upload.jpg')
        ..writeAsBytesSync([0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xE0, 0x00]);
      addTearDown(() => file.existsSync() ? file.deleteSync() : null);

      final ids = await state.uploadImages([file.path]);

      expect(ids, ['media-1']);
      expect(calls.first.method, 'POST');
      expect(calls.first.path, '/api/media');
      // /api/media checks the DECLARED type against {jpeg, png, gif}.
      // MultipartFile defaults to application/octet-stream, which made every
      // valid photo fail with 400 unsupported_type.
      expect(calls.first.rawBody, contains('image/jpeg'));
      expect(calls.first.rawBody, isNot(contains('application/octet-stream')));
    });

    test('png keeps its own type rather than being called a jpeg', () async {
      final state = await buildState(response: {'ok': true, 'id': 'media-2'});
      final file = File('${Directory.systemTemp.path}/linkdin_test_upload.png')
        ..writeAsBytesSync([0x89, 0x50, 0x4E, 0x47]);
      addTearDown(() => file.existsSync() ? file.deleteSync() : null);

      await state.uploadImages([file.path]);
      expect(calls.first.rawBody, contains('image/png'));
    });
  });

  group('settings', () {
    test(
      'style save sends PATCH /api/settings with the whole config',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState();
        await state.setStyle(StyleConfig.houseStyle.copyWith(emoji: 'sparing'));

        expect(calls.first.method, 'PATCH');
        expect(calls.first.path, '/api/settings');
        expect((calls.first.body['style'] as Map)['emoji'], 'sparing');
      },
    );

    test('preset save sends the preset id, not a style blob', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.applyPreset('builder');
      expect(calls.first.body['preset'], 'builder');
    });
  });

  group('session handling', () {
    test('the session cookie is attached to authenticated calls', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      await state.clear(1);
      expect(calls.first.headers['cookie'], 'lc_session=abc');
    });

    test('a 401 clears the session and drops back to the gate', () async {
      final state = await buildState(
        response: {'error': 'unauthorized'},
        status: 401,
      );
      state.phase = AuthPhase.signedIn;

      await state.refresh();

      expect(
        state.phase,
        AuthPhase.signedOut,
        reason:
            'a dead cookie must not leave a signed-in shell that 401s on every tap',
      );
      expect(state.status, isNull);
    });

    test(
      'a server error surfaces its detail instead of a generic message',
      () async {
        final state = await buildState(
          response: {
            'error': 'bad_post_time',
            'detail': 'Expected HH:MM, got "18:00:00"',
          },
          status: 400,
        );
        final error = await state.setStyle(StyleConfig.houseStyle);
        expect(error, contains('Expected HH:MM'));
      },
    );
  });

  group('editing target', () {
    test('startEditing sets the target and raises a compose request', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p2',
        'seq': 2,
        'text': 'Body',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      final before = state.composeRequest;
      state.startEditing(post);

      expect(state.editing?.seq, 2);
      expect(
        state.composeRequest,
        greaterThan(before),
        reason: 'the shell watches this counter to bring the composer forward',
      );
    });

    test('editing the same post twice still raises a fresh request', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p2',
        'seq': 2,
        'text': 'Body',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      state.startEditing(post);
      final first = state.composeRequest;
      state.startEditing(post);

      // Otherwise "edit" does nothing when you are already on that draft but
      // have since navigated to another tab.
      expect(state.composeRequest, greaterThan(first));
    });

    test('stopEditing clears the target', () async {
      final state = await buildState();
      state.startEditing(
        Post.fromJson({
          'id': 'p2',
          'seq': 2,
          'text': 'Body',
          'status': 'draft',
        }),
      );
      state.stopEditing();
      expect(state.editing, isNull);
    });
  });

  group('scheduling state on a post', () {
    Post post(Map<String, dynamic> extra) => Post.fromJson({
      'id': 'p1',
      'seq': 1,
      'text': 'Body text long enough to be a post.',
      'status': 'draft',
      ...extra,
    });

    final future = DateTime.now().toUtc().add(const Duration(minutes: 12));
    final past = DateTime.now().toUtc().subtract(const Duration(minutes: 5));

    test('an unscheduled draft is not scheduled and never overdue', () {
      final p = post({});
      expect(p.isScheduled, isFalse);
      expect(p.isOverdue, isFalse);
      expect(p.timeUntilSend, isNull);
    });

    test('a scheduled draft reports the time remaining', () {
      final p = post({'scheduledFor': future.toIso8601String()});
      expect(p.isScheduled, isTrue);
      expect(p.isCleared, isFalse);
      expect(p.timeUntilSend!.inMinutes, inInclusiveRange(10, 12));
      expect(p.isOverdue, isFalse);
    });

    test('past its time and not cleared is overdue', () {
      final p = post({'scheduledFor': past.toIso8601String()});
      expect(
        p.isOverdue,
        isTrue,
        reason:
            'this is the state worth shouting about — it usually means it was never cleared',
      );
    });

    // A published post is never overdue however long ago its time was: it went
    // out. Getting this wrong would leave every historical post flagged red.
    test('a published post is never overdue', () {
      final p = post({
        'scheduledFor': past.toIso8601String(),
        'status': 'published',
        'publishedAt': past.toIso8601String(),
      });
      expect(p.isOverdue, isFalse);
    });

    test('a missed post is never overdue either', () {
      final p = post({
        'scheduledFor': past.toIso8601String(),
        'status': 'missed',
      });
      expect(p.isMissed, isTrue);
      expect(p.isOverdue, isFalse);
    });

    test('clearedAt and heldUntil are read back', () {
      final p = post({
        'scheduledFor': future.toIso8601String(),
        'clearedAt': past.toIso8601String(),
        'heldUntil': future.toIso8601String(),
      });
      expect(p.isCleared, isTrue);
      expect(p.isHeld, isTrue);
    });

    test('a slot parses its display fields', () {
      final s = PostSlot.fromJson({
        'id': 's1',
        'localTime': '09:30',
        'daysMask': 62,
        'daysLabel': 'Mon-Fri',
        'leadMinutes': 15,
        'autoPublish': false,
        'categories': ['emerging-tech'],
        'enabled': true,
      });
      expect(s.localTime, '09:30');
      expect(s.daysLabel, 'Mon-Fri');
      expect(s.leadMinutes, 15);
      expect(s.autoPublish, isFalse);
      expect(s.categories, ['emerging-tech']);
      // Absent `enabled` must read as true, not false — a slot that silently
      // defaults to disabled is a schedule that never runs.
      expect(
        PostSlot.fromJson({'id': 's2', 'localTime': '18:00'}).enabled,
        isTrue,
      );
    });

    test('nextDue picks the soonest pending post, not the newest', () {
      final status = AppStatus.fromJson({
        'initialized': true,
        'queue': [
          {
            'id': 'p9',
            'seq': 9,
            'text': 'Later today.',
            'status': 'draft',
            'scheduledFor': DateTime.now()
                .toUtc()
                .add(const Duration(hours: 8))
                .toIso8601String(),
          },
          {
            'id': 'p8',
            'seq': 8,
            'text': 'Very soon.',
            'status': 'draft',
            'scheduledFor': future.toIso8601String(),
          },
        ],
      });
      expect(
        status.nextDue!.seq,
        8,
        reason:
            'the one with the nearest deadline is the one that needs reading',
      );
      expect(status.needingReview, 2);
    });
  });

  // Every settings change used to cost two sequential round trips to a database
  // on another continent — the PATCH, then a full /api/status rebuild of the
  // queue, history, rejections, slot timeline and LLM budget, none of which a
  // settings change can alter. At roughly half a second each, with the whole UI
  // disabled in between, that was most of what "the app feels slow" meant.
  group('settings changes cost one round trip, not two', () {
    Map<String, dynamic> agentJson({
      List<String> categories = const ['ai-ml'],
    }) => {
      'agentId': 'a1',
      'name': 'A Working Engineer',
      'domain': 'AI and ML engineering',
      'categories': categories,
      'timezone': 'Asia/Kolkata',
      'postTimeLocal': '09:30',
      'autoPublish': false,
      'paused': false,
      'autoPublishCap': 1,
      'style': {'structure': 'prose', 'hashtagCount': 2},
    };

    Future<AppState> seeded({
      Map<String, dynamic>? response,
      int status = 200,
    }) async {
      final state = await buildState(
        response: response ?? {'ok': true, 'agent': agentJson()},
        status: status,
      );
      state.status = AppStatus.fromJson({
        'initialized': true,
        'agent': agentJson(categories: ['ai-ml', 'dev-tooling']),
        'account': {'connected': true},
        'config': {'liveMode': false},
      });
      return state;
    }

    test('a style change does not refetch the whole dashboard', () async {
      final state = await seeded();
      await state.setStyle(StyleConfig.houseStyle.copyWith(register: 'blunt'));

      expect(
        calls.map((c) => c.path),
        ['/api/settings'],
        reason: 'the PATCH already answers with the updated agent',
      );
    });

    test('the updated agent is taken from the PATCH response', () async {
      final state = await seeded(
        response: {
          'ok': true,
          'agent': agentJson(categories: ['compute-silicon']),
        },
      );
      await state.setPaused(true);
      expect(state.agent!.categories, ['compute-silicon']);
    });

    test(
      'a response without an agent still falls back to a full refresh',
      () async {
        // An older backend, or a shape this build does not recognise. Showing
        // possibly-stale settings would be worse than paying for the round trip.
        final state = await seeded(response: {'ok': true});
        await state.setPaused(true);
        expect(calls.map((c) => c.path), ['/api/settings', '/api/status']);
      },
    );

    test('the schedule fields still take the full refresh', () async {
      // Changing the timezone reschedules every slot, and slots are not part of
      // the agent object — so this one genuinely has to re-read everything.
      final state = await seeded();
      await state.setTimezone('Europe/Berlin');
      expect(calls.map((c) => c.path), ['/api/settings', '/api/status']);
    });

    test(
      'a category tap shows immediately, before the server answers',
      () async {
        final state = await seeded();
        final pending = state.setCategories(['ai-ml']);
        expect(
          state.agent!.categories,
          ['ai-ml'],
          reason: 'the chip must not wait half a second to look pressed',
        );
        expect(
          state.loading,
          isFalse,
          reason: 'setting loading would disable every control on the screen',
        );
        await pending;
      },
    );

    test('a rejected category change is rolled back', () async {
      final state = await seeded(
        response: {'error': 'update_failed'},
        status: 500,
      );
      final error = await state.setCategories(['ai-ml']);

      expect(error, isNotNull);
      expect(
        state.agent!.categories,
        ['ai-ml', 'dev-tooling'],
        reason: 'a refused change must never be left looking accepted',
      );
    });
  });

  // A follow-up is two database reads, a model call, and usually a SECOND model
  // call repairing the draft to the author's word range — with every model call
  // paced four seconds behind the last. Half a minute is normal. The client used
  // to give up at thirty seconds flat, so the post was written and thrown away.
  group('calls that wait on a model get a longer ceiling', () {
    test(
      'the writer ceiling outlasts the server, so the server error wins',
      () {
        // If the client gave up first, the user would see a stopwatch message
        // instead of whatever actually went wrong.
        expect(
          kWriterTimeout.inSeconds,
          greaterThan(120),
          reason: 'the routes behind these calls allow 120s',
        );
      },
    );

    test('a follow-up survives longer than a status refresh would', () async {
      // Answers after 40s: past the old 30s default, inside the writer ceiling.
      SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({
        'session_cookie': 'lc_session=abc',
        'base_url': 'http://test.local',
      });
      final slow = MockClient((_) async {
        await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 60));
        return http.Response(
          jsonEncode({
            'ok': true,
            'text': 'A follow-up long enough to be a real post body.',
          }),
          200,
          headers: {'content-type': 'application/json'},
        );
      });
      final state = AppState(await ApiClient.create(httpClient: slow));
      final error = await state.followUp(7);

      expect(error, isNull);
      expect(state.composeSeed, contains('A follow-up'));
      // A follow-up is a NEW post; arriving bound to the original would
      // overwrite the post being followed up.
      expect(state.editing, isNull);
    });
  });

  // The composer watches this to decide whether to offer a re-run. It used to
  // watch StyleConfig.summary, which names three fields out of a prompt built
  // from every style rule plus the author's samples and edit notes.
  group('the voice fingerprint notices every part of the voice', () {
    Map<String, dynamic> withAgent(Map<String, dynamic> agent) => {
      'initialized': true,
      'agent': agent,
      'account': {'connected': true},
      'config': {'liveMode': false},
    };

    Map<String, dynamic> base({
      Map<String, dynamic> style = const {
        'structure': 'prose',
        'hashtagCount': 2,
      },
      List<String> corpus = const [],
      String? editNotes,
    }) => {
      'agentId': 'a1',
      'name': 'N',
      'domain': 'd',
      'categories': ['ai-ml'],
      'timezone': 'UTC',
      'postTimeLocal': '09:30',
      'autoPublish': false,
      'paused': false,
      'autoPublishCap': 1,
      'style': style,
      'corpus': corpus,
      'editNotes': editNotes,
    };

    Future<String> fingerprintOf(Map<String, dynamic> agent) async {
      final state = await buildState();
      state.status = AppStatus.fromJson(withAgent(agent));
      return state.styleFingerprint;
    }

    test('a register change moves it', () async {
      expect(
        await fingerprintOf(
          base(style: {'structure': 'prose', 'register': 'blunt'}),
        ),
        isNot(
          await fingerprintOf(
            base(style: {'structure': 'prose', 'register': 'practitioner'}),
          ),
        ),
        reason:
            'style.summary never mentioned the register, so the banner stayed silent',
      );
    });

    test('adding a writing sample moves it', () async {
      // The single largest lever on how the output sounds, and previously
      // invisible to the composer entirely.
      expect(
        await fingerprintOf(
          base(corpus: ['A sample of how this person writes.']),
        ),
        isNot(await fingerprintOf(base())),
      );
    });

    test('edit notes move it', () async {
      expect(
        await fingerprintOf(base(editNotes: 'Open on the number.')),
        isNot(await fingerprintOf(base())),
      );
    });

    test('an unchanged voice keeps the same fingerprint', () async {
      expect(
        await fingerprintOf(base(corpus: ['x'])),
        await fingerprintOf(base(corpus: ['x'])),
      );
    });
  });
}
````

````text
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/auth_return.dart';

void main() {
  test(
    'loopback return rejects unrelated requests and signals only once',
    () async {
      var returned = 0;
      final listener = await LoopbackAuthReturn.start(
        onReturn: () async {
          returned++;
        },
      );
      final client = HttpClient();
      Future<int> get(Uri uri, {String? host}) async {
        final req = await client.getUrl(uri);
        if (host != null) req.headers.set(HttpHeaders.hostHeader, host);
        final res = await req.close();
        await res.drain<void>();
        return res.statusCode;
      }

      try {
        expect(listener.uri.host, '127.0.0.1');
        expect(listener.uri.pathSegments.last.length, 43);
        expect(await get(listener.uri.replace(path: '/unrelated')), 404);
        expect(await get(listener.uri, host: 'external.example'), 404);
        expect(
          await get(listener.uri.replace(query: 'token=not-accepted')),
          404,
        );
        expect(returned, 0);
        expect(await get(listener.uri), 200);
        await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 20));
        expect(returned, 1);
        expect(await get(listener.uri), 200);
        expect(returned, 1);
      } finally {
        client.close(force: true);
        await listener.close();
      }
    },
  );
}
````

````text
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:ui' as ui;
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:http/testing.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/client.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/onboarding_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/state/app_state.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/theme.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/form_select.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/writing_preferences.dart';
import 'onboarding_test.dart' show setupFixture;

void main() {
  test('errors explain recovery without exposing service internals', () {
    expect(
      ApiException(
        0,
        'timeout',
        detail: 'http://10.0.2.2 adb reverse',
      ).toString(),
      isNot(contains('adb')),
    );
    expect(
      ApiException(
        500,
        'gemini_missing_key',
        detail: 'GEMINI_API_KEY',
      ).toString(),
      contains('temporarily unavailable'),
    );
    expect(
      ApiException(
        400,
        'setup_failed',
        detail: 'Choose a valid timezone.',
      ).toString(),
      'Choose a valid timezone.',
    );
  });

  testWidgets('large catalogue search retains choices and cancels safely', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    var selected = ['subject-1'];
    final options = {
      for (var i = 0; i < 1100; i++) 'subject-$i': 'Specialist subject $i',
      'solar': 'Solar energy · Energy & utilities',
    };
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      MaterialApp(
        theme: buildTheme(),
        home: Scaffold(
          body: StatefulBuilder(
            builder: (context, set) => MultiSelectField(
              label: 'Subjects',
              options: options,
              values: selected,
              max: 12,
              onChanged: (v) => set(() => selected = v),
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
    await tester.tap(find.byType(MultiSelectField));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(
      find.byType(CheckboxListTile).evaluate().length,
      lessThan(30),
      reason: 'the catalogue is rendered lazily',
    );
    await tester.enterText(find.byType(TextField), 'energy solar');
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.tap(find.text('Solar energy · Energy & utilities'));
    await tester.tap(find.text('Apply'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(selected, ['subject-1', 'solar']);
    await tester.tap(find.byType(MultiSelectField));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.enterText(find.byType(TextField), 'zzzz');
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(find.textContaining('No matching options'), findsOneWidget);
    await tester.tap(find.text('Cancel'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(selected, ['subject-1', 'solar']);
  });

  for (final defaults in [false, true]) {
    testWidgets(
      defaults
          ? 'voice setup can be skipped with defaults'
          : 'setup sends the selected subjects and fine-tuned voice',
      (tester) async {
        SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({});
        tester.view.physicalSize = const Size(390, 844);
        tester.view.devicePixelRatio = 1;
        addTearDown(tester.view.resetPhysicalSize);
        addTearDown(tester.view.resetDevicePixelRatio);
        final initial = setupFixture()
          ..['preview'] = null
          ..['account'] = {'connected': true};
        (initial['config'] as Map)['categories'] = ['solar'];
        (initial['config'] as Map)['topics'] = ['Solar energy'];
        initial['categories'] = [
          {
            'id': 'solar',
            'label': 'Solar energy',
            'groupLabel': 'Energy & utilities',
          },
          ...List.generate(
            1100,
            (i) => {'id': 's$i', 'label': 'Specialist subject $i'},
          ),
        ];
        final calls = <Map<String, dynamic>>[];
        final api = await ApiClient.create(
          httpClient: MockClient((r) async {
            final body = jsonDecode(r.body) as Map<String, dynamic>;
            calls.add(body);
            return http.Response(
              jsonEncode({
                ...initial,
                'revision': 2,
                'preview': body['action'] == 'preview'
                    ? {
                        'text': 'A reviewed sample about solar energy.',
                        'sources': [],
                      }
                    : null,
              }),
              200,
              headers: {'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8'},
            );
          }),
        );
        await tester.runAsync(() async {
          await (FontLoader(
            'PlexSans',
          )..addFont(rootBundle.load('assets/fonts/IBMPlexSans.ttf'))).load();
          await (FontLoader('MaterialIcons')
                ..addFont(rootBundle.load('fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf')))
              .load();
        });
        final boundary = GlobalKey();
        await tester.pumpWidget(
          ChangeNotifierProvider.value(
            value: AppState(api),
            child: MaterialApp(
              theme: buildTheme(),
              home: RepaintBoundary(
                key: boundary,
                child: OnboardingScreen(initial: initial, onComplete: () {}),
              ),
            ),
          ),
        );
        Future<void> reveal(Finder f) async {
          await tester.scrollUntilVisible(
            f,
            180,
            scrollable: find.byType(Scrollable).first,
          );
          await tester.pumpAndSettle();
        }

        await reveal(find.text('Continue'));
        await tester.tap(find.text('Continue'));
        await tester.pumpAndSettle();
        expect(find.text('Make it sound like you'), findsOneWidget);
        if (!defaults) {
          await reveal(find.text('Fine-tune your writing'));
          await tester.tap(find.text('Fine-tune your writing'));
          await tester.pumpAndSettle();
          await reveal(find.byType(WritingPreferences));
          final prefs = tester.widget<WritingPreferences>(
            find.byType(WritingPreferences),
          );
          prefs.onChanged!(
            prefs.value.copyWith(
              structure: 'bullets',
              minWords: 80,
              maxWords: 160,
              hashtagCount: 0,
              register: 'accessible',
            ),
          );
          await tester.pumpAndSettle();
          expect(tester.takeException(), isNull);
          // Reviewable rendering from the real setup screen at phone width.
          await tester.runAsync(() async {
            final image =
                await (boundary.currentContext!.findRenderObject()
                        as RenderRepaintBoundary)
                    .toImage();
            final bytes = await image.toByteData(
              format: ui.ImageByteFormat.png,
            );
            final file = File('../.byline-local/voice-setup-390.png');
            await file.writeAsBytes(bytes!.buffer.asUint8List());
            image.dispose();
          });
        }
        final button = find.text(
          defaults ? 'Use default voice' : 'Show my sample',
        );
        await reveal(button);
        await tester.tap(button);
        await tester.pumpAndSettle();
        final saved =
            calls.firstWhere((c) => c['action'] == 'save')['config'] as Map;
        expect(saved['categories'], ['solar']);
        expect(saved['topics'], ['Solar energy']);
        if (defaults) {
          expect(saved['voice'], 'professional');
          expect(saved['style'], isNull);
          expect(saved['samples'], isEmpty);
        } else {
          expect(saved['style']['structure'], 'bullets');
          expect(saved['style']['minWords'], 80);
          expect(saved['style']['maxWords'], 160);
          expect(saved['style']['hashtagCount'], 0);
        }
        expect(calls.last['action'], 'preview');
        expect(tester.takeException(), isNull);
      },
    );
  }
}
````

````text
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:http/testing.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/client.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/models.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/state/app_state.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/theme.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/today_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/home_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/form_select.dart';
import 'screens_test.dart' show statusFixture;

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  setUp(() {
    TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger
        .setMockMethodCallHandler(
          const MethodChannel('plugins.it_nomads.com/flutter_secure_storage'),
          (_) async => null,
        );
  });
  for (final outcome in [
    'draft',
    'published',
    'rejected',
    'approved',
    'failure',
  ]) {
    testWidgets('preparation handles $outcome through the timetable API', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({});
      final fixture = statusFixture();
      final post = {
        ...(fixture['queue'] as List).first as Map<String, dynamic>,
        'status': outcome,
        'scheduledFor': null,
      };
      fixture['queue'] = [];
      var prepares = 0;
      final api = await ApiClient.create(
        httpClient: MockClient((r) async {
          if (r.method == 'POST') {
            expect(r.url.path, '/api/review-delivery');
            expect(jsonDecode(r.body)['action'], 'generate');
            prepares++;
            return http.Response(
              jsonEncode(
                outcome == 'failure' ? {'error': 'unavailable'} : {'ok': true},
              ),
              outcome == 'failure' ? 503 : 200,
            );
          }
          final ready = prepares > 0 && outcome != 'failure';
          return http.Response(
            jsonEncode(
              r.url.path == '/api/review-delivery'
                  ? {
                      'timezone': 'UTC',
                      'entries': [
                        {
                          'slotId': 's1',
                          'time': '09:00',
                          'canPrepare': !ready,
                          'progress': {'state': 'idle'},
                          'post': ready ? post : null,
                        },
                      ],
                    }
                  : fixture,
            ),
            200,
            headers: {'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8'},
          );
        }),
      );
      await api.saveNativeSession('test-session');
      final state = AppState(api)..status = AppStatus.fromJson(fixture);
      await tester.pumpWidget(
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(
          value: state,
          child: MaterialApp(
            theme: buildTheme(),
            home: const Scaffold(body: TodayScreen()),
          ),
        ),
      );
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
      await tester.tap(find.text('Prepare today’s posts'));
````

````text
            if (call.method == 'read') return secure[args['key']];

            if (interruption == 'server') {

            }

          final dynamic value = r.url.path == '/api/native-auth'

              : r.url.path == '/api/onboarding'

              : fixture;
          return http.Response(

          );
        });
        final before = await ApiClient.create(httpClient: transport);
        await before.savePendingSignIn({
````
