## Source: mobile/test/reconnect_test.dart

````text
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:http/testing.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/client.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/state/app_state.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/home_screen.dart';
import 'screens_test.dart' show statusFixture;

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  test(
    'a suspended connection retries reads but never repeats a mutation',
    () async {
      SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({});
      var gets = 0, posts = 0;
      final api = await ApiClient.create(
        httpClient: MockClient((r) async {
          if (r.method == 'POST') {
            posts++;
            throw http.ClientException('connection closed');
          }
          if (++gets == 1) throw http.ClientException('stale pooled socket');
          return http.Response('{"ok":true}', 200);
        }),
      );
      expect(await api.get('/api/status'), {'ok': true});
      expect(gets, 2);
      await expectLater(
        api.post('/api/posts/1', {'action': 'publish'}),
        throwsA(isA<ApiException>()),
      );
      expect(posts, 1);
    },
  );

  test('an unauthorized read is not retried', () async {
    SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({});
    var calls = 0;
    final api = await ApiClient.create(
      httpClient: MockClient((r) async {
        calls++;
        return http.Response('{"error":"unauthorized"}', 401);
      }),
    );
    await expectLater(api.get('/api/status'), throwsA(isA<ApiException>()));
    expect(calls, 1);
  });

  testWidgets(
    'returning to My posts clears stale connection errors and shows job failure',
    (tester) async {
      SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({
        'session_cookie': 'lc_session=test',
      });
      final fixture = statusFixture()..['queue'] = [];
      fixture['generation'] = {
        'id': 'job',
        'state': 'working',
        'stage': 'writing',
      };
      var reads = 0;
      final api = await ApiClient.create(
        httpClient: MockClient((r) async {
          reads++;
          return http.Response(
            jsonEncode(fixture),
            200,
            headers: {'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8'},
          );
        }),
      );
      final state = AppState(api);
      await state.bootstrap();
      await tester.pumpWidget(
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(
          value: state,
          child: const MaterialApp(home: HomeScreen(initialIndex: 1)),
        ),
      );
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
      await tester.scrollUntilVisible(find.text('Writing in your voice'), 180,
          scrollable: find.byType(Scrollable).first);
      expect(find.text('Writing in your voice'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.text('Ask it to write one now'), findsNothing);
      final before = reads;
      tester.binding.handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(
        AppLifecycleState.paused,
      );
      state.error = 'We could not connect to ByLine.';
      fixture['generation'] = {
        'id': 'job',
        'state': 'failed',
        'error': 'The draft needs another pass.',
      };
      tester.binding.handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(
        AppLifecycleState.resumed,
      );
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
      expect(reads, greaterThan(before));
      expect(state.error, isNull);
      expect(find.text('Draft preparation could not finish'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.text('The draft needs another pass.'), findsOneWidget);
      await tester.pumpWidget(const SizedBox.shrink());
    },
  );
}
````

````text
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:http/testing.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/client.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/models.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/state/app_state.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/theme.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/home_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/voice_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/welcome_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/onboarding_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/delivery_settings_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/settings_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/timetable_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/experience.dart';
import 'screens_test.dart' show statusFixture;
import 'onboarding_test.dart' show setupFixture;

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  test('light palette maintains readable text and control boundaries', () {
    double contrast(Color a, Color b) {
      final x = a.computeLuminance(), y = b.computeLuminance();
      return ((x > y ? x : y) + .05) / ((x > y ? y : x) + .05);
    }

    for (final bg in [C.ink, C.ink2, C.ink3]) {
      for (final fg in [
        C.paper,
        C.paperDim,
        C.paperFaint,
        C.filament,
        C.daylight,
        C.flare,
      ]) {
        expect(contrast(fg, bg), greaterThanOrEqualTo(4.5));
      }
    }
    expect(contrast(C.onFilament, C.filament), greaterThanOrEqualTo(4.5));
    expect(contrast(C.ruleStrong, C.ink2), greaterThanOrEqualTo(3));
  });

  Future<AppState> fixtureState() async {
    SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({});
    TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger
        .setMockMethodCallHandler(
          const MethodChannel('plugins.it_nomads.com/flutter_secure_storage'),
          (_) async => null,
        );
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    final api = await ApiClient.create(
      httpClient: MockClient((r) async {
        final body = switch (r.url.path) {
          '/api/native-auth' => {
            'linkedin': true,
            'google': false,
            'localTest': false,
          },
          '/api/interests' => {
            'topics': ['AI in everyday work', 'Product design', 'Leadership'],
          },
          '/api/onboarding' => setupFixture(),
          _ => fixture,
        };
        return http.Response(
          jsonEncode(body),
          200,
          headers: {'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8'},
        );
      }),
    );
    await api.saveNativeSession('design-fixture');
    return AppState(api)
      ..status = AppStatus.fromJson(fixture)
      ..phase = AuthPhase.signedIn;
  }

  final pages = <String, Widget Function()>{
    'welcome': () => const WelcomeScreen(),
    'interests-onboarding': () => OnboardingScreen(
      initial: {
        ...setupFixture(),
        'preview': null,
        'account': {'connected': true, 'memberName': 'Alex Morgan'},
      },
      onComplete: () {},
    ),
    'sample': () =>
        OnboardingScreen(initial: setupFixture(), onComplete: () {}),
    'daily': () => const HomeScreen(),
    'voice': () => const VoiceScreen(),
    'topics': () => const TopicsScreen(),
    'delivery': () => const DeliverySettingsScreen(),
    'timetable': () => const TimetableScreen(),
  };
  for (final size in [
    const Size(390, 844),
    const Size(900, 900),
    const Size(1280, 900),
  ]) {
    for (final page in pages.entries) {
      testWidgets('${page.key} adapts at ${size.width.toInt()}', (
        tester,
      ) async {
        tester.view.physicalSize = size;
        tester.view.devicePixelRatio = 1;
        addTearDown(tester.view.reset);
        final loader = FontLoader('PlexSans')
          ..addFont(rootBundle.load('assets/fonts/IBMPlexSans.ttf'));
        await loader.load();
        await (FontLoader(
          'MaterialIcons',
        )..addFont(rootBundle.load('fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf'))).load();
        await (FontLoader(
              'PlexMono',
            )..addFont(rootBundle.load('assets/fonts/IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf')))
            .load();
        final state = await fixtureState();
        final boundary = GlobalKey();
        await tester.pumpWidget(
          ChangeNotifierProvider.value(
            value: state,
            child: MaterialApp(
              theme: buildTheme(),
              home: RepaintBoundary(key: boundary, child: page.value()),
            ),
          ),
        );
        await tester.pumpAndSettle();
        expect(tester.takeException(), isNull);
        if (Platform.environment['BYLINE_CAPTURE_UI'] == 'true') {
          final renderer =
              boundary.currentContext!.findRenderObject()
                  as RenderRepaintBoundary;
          await tester.runAsync(() async {
            final image = await renderer.toImage();
            final bytes = await image.toByteData(
              format: ui.ImageByteFormat.png,
            );
            final dir = Directory('../reports/ui-preview')
              ..createSync(recursive: true);
            File(
              '${dir.path}/${page.key}-${size.width.toInt()}.png',
            ).writeAsBytesSync(bytes!.buffer.asUint8List());
            image.dispose();
          });
        }
        await tester.pumpWidget(const SizedBox());
        state.dispose();
      });
    }
  }
  for (final page in pages.entries) {
    testWidgets('${page.key} supports larger text on a small phone', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      tester.view.physicalSize = const Size(360, 800);
      tester.view.devicePixelRatio = 1;
      addTearDown(tester.view.reset);
      final state = await fixtureState();
      await tester.pumpWidget(
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(
          value: state,
          child: MaterialApp(
            theme: buildTheme(),
            builder: (context, child) => MediaQuery(
              data: MediaQuery.of(
                context,
              ).copyWith(textScaler: const TextScaler.linear(1.6)),
              child: child!,
            ),
            home: page.value(),
          ),
        ),
      );
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
      expect(tester.takeException(), isNull);
      await tester.pumpWidget(const SizedBox());
      state.dispose();
    });
  }
  testWidgets('delivery allows a time outside quarter-hour presets', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    String? selected;
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      MaterialApp(
        theme: buildTheme(),
        home: Scaffold(
          body: TimeChoice(value: '09:07', onChanged: (v) => selected = v),
        ),
      ),
    );
    await tester.tap(
      find
          .descendant(
            of: find.byType(TimeChoice),
            matching: find.byType(InkWell),
          )
          .first,
    );
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.tap(find.text('OK'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(selected, '09:07');
  });
  testWidgets('voice instructions are directly editable and enable Save', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final state = await fixtureState();
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      ChangeNotifierProvider.value(
        value: state,
        child: MaterialApp(theme: buildTheme(), home: const VoiceScreen()),
      ),
    );
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.enterText(
      find.widgetWithText(TextField, 'Your own rules'),
      'Write warmly. Avoid jargon.',
    );
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(
      tester
          .widget<FilledButton>(find.widgetWithText(FilledButton, 'Save'))
          .onPressed,
      isNotNull,
    );
  });
}
````

````text
/// Render tests for every screen, at real phone sizes.
///
/// These exist because Flutter's most common UI defect — a RenderFlex overflow
/// — is not a crash and not a compile error. It is a yellow stripe you only
/// see if you happen to look at that screen at that width. Pumping each screen
/// at 360x640 (a small-but-common Android viewport) turns that into a test
/// failure, since the test binding reports overflows as exceptions.
library;

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:http/testing.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/client.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/models.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/archive_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/composer_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/desk_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/gate_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/settings_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/timetable_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/screens/voice_screen.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/state/app_state.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/theme.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/day_rail.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/form_select.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

/// A populated status payload — the busy case, where overflows actually happen.

    'missedAfterMinutes': 45,
  },

/// The Desk filters today's rail by local date, so the fixture has to be
/// stamped with the machine's today rather than a frozen date.
String _todayLocal() {
  final now = DateTime.now();
  return '${now.year.toString().padLeft(4, '0')}-'
      '${now.month.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}-'
      '${now.day.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}';
}

Future<AppState> buildState(Map<String, dynamic>? status) async {
  if (status != null) return buildStateWithApi(status, status);
  SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({});
  return AppState(await ApiClient.create());
}

/// Same, wired to a transport that answers every call with [response].
/// Needed by anything that presses a button which actually talks to the server.
Future<AppState> buildStateWithApi(
  Map<String, dynamic>? status,
  Map<String, dynamic> response,
) async {
  SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({
    'session_cookie': 'lc_session=abc',
    'base_url': 'http://test.local',
  });
  final client = MockClient(
    (_) async => http.Response(
      jsonEncode(response),
      200,
      headers: {'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8'},
    ),
  );
  final state = AppState(await ApiClient.create(httpClient: client));
  if (status != null) {
    state.status = AppStatus.fromJson(status);
    state.phase = AuthPhase.signedIn;
  }
  return state;
}

void main() {
  // A small-but-common Android viewport. Anything that overflows will overflow
  // here first.
  const phone = Size(360, 640);

  Future<void> pumpScreen(
    WidgetTester tester,
    Widget screen,
    AppState state,
  ) async {
    tester.view.physicalSize = phone;
    tester.view.devicePixelRatio = 1.0;
    addTearDown(tester.view.reset);

    await tester.pumpWidget(
      ChangeNotifierProvider<AppState>.value(
        value: state,
        child: MaterialApp(
          theme: buildTheme(),
          home: Scaffold(body: SafeArea(child: screen)),
        ),
      ),
    );
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
  }

  /// Scroll a lazily-built ListView until [finder] is mounted.
  ///
  /// Needed because these screens are taller than a phone: a widget below the
  /// fold does not exist yet, so asserting on it without scrolling tests the
  /// viewport height rather than the screen.
  Future<void> scrollTo(WidgetTester tester, Finder finder) async {
    await tester.scrollUntilVisible(
      finder,
      120,
      scrollable: find.byType(Scrollable).first,
    );
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ gate

  testWidgets('GateScreen renders without overflow', (tester) async {
    final state = await buildState(null);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const GateScreen(), state);
    expect(find.text('Sign in'), findsOneWidget);
    // The emulator hint is load-bearing: without it the first run fails on a
    // connection error nobody can diagnose.
    expect(find.textContaining('10.0.2.2'), findsWidgets);
  });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ desk

  testWidgets('DeskScreen renders a populated desk without overflow', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);
    // Only the real draft is publishable; the failed one is stranded below.
    await scrollTo(tester, find.textContaining('Ableton 12.2'));
    expect(find.textContaining('Ableton 12.2'), findsWidgets);
    expect(
      find.text('see more'),
      findsOneWidget,
    ); // the long post crosses the fold
  });

  // Dry run is deliberately a masthead chip rather than a banner: it is a
  // standing condition, and as a banner it was permanently the first thing on
  // the screen, above the thing with a deadline.
  testWidgets(
    'DeskScreen states dry run and a dead token without burying the desk',
    (tester) async {
      final state = await buildState(
        statusFixture(liveMode: false, needsReauth: true),
      );
      await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);
      expect(find.text('DRY RUN'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.textContaining('LinkedIn access expired'), findsOneWidget);
    },
  );

  // The regression this guards: the countdown used to live on a different tab
  // from the draft it applied to, so the same post was rendered twice in two
  // shapes. The next post due IS the first card here, wearing its own clock.
  testWidgets(
    'DeskScreen leads with the next post due, wearing its countdown',
    (tester) async {
      final fixture = statusFixture();
      (fixture['queue'] as List)[0] = {
        ...(fixture['queue'] as List)[0] as Map<String, dynamic>,
        'scheduledFor': DateTime.now()
            .add(const Duration(hours: 2, minutes: 14))
            .toUtc()
            .toIso8601String(),
        'slotId': 's2',
      };
      final state = await buildState(fixture);
      await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);

      expect(find.text('NEXT OUT'), findsOneWidget);
      // Two formats, so 2 hours 13 minutes cannot be read as 2 minutes 13
      // seconds. The colon form only ever means minutes and seconds.
      expect(find.textContaining('2h13m'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.textContaining('TO REVIEW'), findsOneWidget);
      // And the post it belongs to is right underneath it, not a tab away.
      await scrollTo(tester, find.textContaining('Ableton 12.2'));
      expect(find.textContaining('Ableton 12.2'), findsWidgets);
    },
  );

  testWidgets('a cleared post cools to the send clock', (tester) async {
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    (fixture['queue'] as List)[0] = {
      ...(fixture['queue'] as List)[0] as Map<String, dynamic>,
      'status': 'approved',
      'scheduledFor': DateTime.now()
          .add(const Duration(minutes: 40))
          .toUtc()
          .toIso8601String(),
      'clearedAt': DateTime.now().toUtc().toIso8601String(),
    };
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);

    expect(find.text('SCHEDULED'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.textContaining('TO SEND'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('NEXT OUT'), findsNothing);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen shows the day rail, silence included', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);
    await scrollTo(tester, find.byType(DayRail));

    // The state the rail exists for: a slot that judged its candidates and
    // chose silence. Rendered as a gap it is indistinguishable from a dead cron.
    expect(find.text('Stayed quiet'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.textContaining('best was 5.8'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('Published'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen makes a stranded approved post actionable again', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    // A publish that fails on the daily cap leaves the post 'approved'. If that
    // card renders read-only it can never be retried or dropped.
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    (fixture['queue'] as List)[1] = {
      'id': 'p11',
      'seq': 11,
      'text': 'A post that was approved but never actually sent anywhere.',
      'status': 'approved',
      'kind': 'custom',
      'hashtags': <String>[],
    };
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);

    await scrollTo(
      tester,
      find.textContaining('approved but never actually sent'),
    );
    expect(
      find.textContaining('approved but never actually sent'),
      findsOneWidget,
    );
    // The stranded card carries a Publish of its own. Asserting a COUNT here
    // would be counting the viewport rather than the screen: the draft above
    // has already been unmounted by the scroll that got us here.
    expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsWidgets);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen leaves an ambiguous send inert', (tester) async {
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    (fixture['queue'] as List)[1] = {
      'id': 'p11',
      'seq': 11,
      'text': 'A send that LinkedIn never confirmed one way or the other.',
      'status': 'unknown',
      'hashtags': <String>[],
    };
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);

    // 'never confirmed' appears in BOTH the post body and the explanation above
    // it, and scrollUntilVisible needs exactly one match. The heading is unique.
    await scrollTo(tester, find.text('Needs a hand'));
    // Republishing a send LinkedIn never confirmed is how you post twice to a
    // real audience, so this card offers nothing at all. Asserted here rather
    // than by counting: the draft above has been unmounted by the scroll.
    expect(find.widgetWithText(FilledButton, 'Publish'), findsNothing);
    expect(find.textContaining('LinkedIn never confirmed'), findsWidgets);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen invites action rather than showing a blank page', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final fixture = statusFixture()..['queue'] = <Map<String, dynamic>>[];
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);
    expect(find.text('NOTHING ON THE DESK'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('Ask it to write one now'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen shouts when the scheduler has stopped', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    fixture['scheduler'] = {
      'lastTickAt': '2026-08-20T02:00:00.000Z',
      'minutesSince': 680,
      'healthy': false,
      'staleAfterMinutes': 16,
    };
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);

    await scrollTo(tester, find.textContaining('The scheduler stopped'));
    expect(find.textContaining('The scheduler stopped'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen distinguishes never-started from stopped', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    fixture['scheduler'] = {
      'minutesSince': null,
      'healthy': false,
      'staleAfterMinutes': 16,
    };
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);

    expect(find.textContaining('The scheduler never started'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('DeskScreen says nothing when the scheduler is healthy', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);
    expect(find.textContaining('scheduler'), findsNothing);
  });

  // --------------------------------------------------------------- archive

  testWidgets('Archive reaches published history and what was passed over', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final fixture = statusFixture();
    fixture['history'] = [
      {
        'id': 'p1',
        'seq': 1,
        'text': 'A post that already went out to LinkedIn some time ago.',
        'status': 'published',
        'hashtags': ['DSP'],
        'publishedAt': '2026-08-10T09:30:00.000Z',
      },
    ];
    fixture['rejections'] = [
      {
        'title': 'Google Play adds Venmo as a payment option',
        'url': 'https://example.com/venmo',
        'reason':
            'Consumer payment integration news, zero engineering substance.',
      },
    ];
    final state = await buildState(fixture);
    await pumpScreen(tester, const ArchiveScreen(), state);

    // Defaults to what went out.
    expect(find.textContaining('already went out to LinkedIn'), findsOneWidget);
    // The only thing still worth doing with a post that is out.
    expect(find.text('Write a follow-up'), findsOneWidget);

    await tester.tap(find.byIcon(Icons.keyboard_arrow_down).first);
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.tap(find.textContaining('Passed over (').last);
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await scrollTo(
      tester,
      find.text('Google Play adds Venmo as a payment option'),
    );
    expect(
      find.text('Google Play adds Venmo as a payment option'),
      findsOneWidget,
    );
    expect(find.textContaining('zero engineering substance'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('Archive shelves have their own empty states', (tester) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    await pumpScreen(tester, const ArchiveScreen(), state);

    expect(find.text('NOTHING PUBLISHED YET'), findsOneWidget);

    await tester.tap(find.byIcon(Icons.keyboard_arrow_down).first);
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    await tester.tap(find.textContaining('Passed over (').last);
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(find.text('NOTHING PASSED OVER'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  // A follow-up to something unpublished is a rewrite, and the composer
  // already does that.
  testWidgets('a draft is never offered a follow-up', (tester) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    await pumpScreen(tester, const DeskScreen(), state);
    expect(find.text('Write a follow-up'), findsNothing);
  });

  // -------------------------------------------------------------- composer

  testWidgets('ComposerScreen renders without overflow', (tester) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    await pumpScreen(tester, const ComposerScreen(), state);
    expect(find.text('Save draft'), findsOneWidget);
    expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('the composer picks up a follow-up and consumes it', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    // What AppState.followUp leaves behind once the writer answers.
    state.composeSeed =
        'The follow-up the writer produced, long enough to be a real post.';
    state.composeSeedHashtags = ['DSP'];

    await pumpScreen(tester, const ComposerScreen(), state);
    expect(
      find.textContaining('The follow-up the writer produced'),
      findsOneWidget,
    );
    await scrollTo(tester, find.text('#DSP'));
    expect(find.text('#DSP'), findsOneWidget);

    // Consumed on the way in. Otherwise leaving and coming back would resurrect
    // it over whatever had been typed since.
    expect(state.composeSeed, isNull);
    expect(state.takeComposeSeed(), isNull);
  });

  testWidgets('a follow-up is a NEW post, not an edit of the original', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
    // Edit mode is left behind by followUp() deliberately: arriving in a
    // composer still bound to the original would overwrite the post being
    // followed up the moment it was saved.
    state.startEditing(state.status!.queue.first);
    state.editing = null;
    state.composeSeed =
        'A follow-up that must not be bound to the post it follows.';

    await pumpScreen(tester, const ComposerScreen(), state);
    expect(find.textContaining('must not be bound'), findsOneWidget);
    // "Editing p12" is the title shown when a real post is loaded.
    expect(find.textContaining('Editing'), findsNothing);
  });

  testWidgets(
    'ComposerScreen offers rewrite on a NEW post, gated on enough text',
    (tester) async {
      final state = await buildState(statusFixture());
      await pumpScreen(tester, const ComposerScreen(), state);

      final rewrite = find.widgetWithText(
        OutlinedButton,
        'Rewrite in my voice',
````

````text
/// Tests for the parts that fail SILENTLY.
///
/// The model layer is deliberately total — every field falls back rather than
/// throwing — which means a decoding mistake does not crash, it just quietly
/// shows the wrong thing. That is exactly the failure mode worth testing.
library;

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/api/models.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/theme.dart';
import 'package:linkdin_mobile/widgets/draft_card.dart';

void main() {
  group('StyleConfig', () {
    test('a null payload is the house style', () {
      final s = StyleConfig.fromJson(null);
      expect(s.structure, 'prose');
      expect(s.emoji, 'none');
      expect(s.hashtagCount, 2);
    });

    test('missing fields fall back rather than throwing', () {
      final s = StyleConfig.fromJson({'structure': 'bullets'});
      expect(s.structure, 'bullets');
      expect(s.emoji, 'none');
      expect(s.minWords, 120);
    });

    test('wrong-typed fields fall back', () {
      final s = StyleConfig.fromJson({
        'hashtagCount': 'three',
        'minWords': null,
      });
      expect(s.hashtagCount, 2);
      expect(s.minWords, 120);
    });

    test('a round trip through JSON preserves every field', () {
      const original = StyleConfig(
        structure: 'mixed',
        emoji: 'sparing',
        hook: 'bold',
        cta: 'soft',
        minWords: 90,
        maxWords: 160,
        hashtagCount: 4,
        register: 'accessible',
        signature: SignatureConfig(
          source: 'F1 radio',
          maxWords: 10,
          budgetPerFive: 2,
          banned: ['x'],
        ),
        customRules: ['never name the client'],
        bannedPhrases: ['synergy'],
      );
      final back = StyleConfig.fromJson(original.toJson());
      expect(back.toJson().toString(), original.toJson().toString());
    });

    test(
      'clearSignature removes the signature, and a plain copyWith keeps it',
      () {
        const withSig = StyleConfig(
          structure: 'prose',
          emoji: 'none',
          hook: 'sharp',
          cta: 'none',
          minWords: 120,
          maxWords: 220,
          hashtagCount: 2,
          register: 'practitioner',
          signature: SignatureConfig(
            source: 'Marvel films',
            maxWords: 12,
            budgetPerFive: 1,
            banned: [],
          ),
          customRules: [],
          bannedPhrases: [],
        );
        // Without the explicit flag, copyWith must not silently drop a nullable
        // field — that would turn "change the emoji setting" into "delete the
        // signature", which is unrecoverable from the UI.
        expect(withSig.copyWith(emoji: 'sparing').signature, isNotNull);
        expect(withSig.copyWith(clearSignature: true).signature, isNull);
      },
    );

    test('the summary reflects the settings a user just changed', () {
      final s = StyleConfig.fromJson(
        null,
      ).copyWith(hashtagCount: 0, emoji: 'expressive');
      expect(s.summary, contains('no tags'));
      expect(s.summary, contains('expressive emoji'));
    });
  });

  group('AppStatus', () {
    test('an uninitialised backend decodes without an agent', () {
      final s = AppStatus.fromJson({
        'initialized': false,
        'config': {'liveMode': false},
      });
      expect(s.initialized, isFalse);
      expect(s.agent, isNull);
      expect(s.account.connected, isFalse);
      expect(s.queue, isEmpty);
    });

    test('a full payload decodes agent, queue and presets', () {
      final s = AppStatus.fromJson({
        'initialized': true,
        'agent': {
          'agentId': 'a1',
          'name': 'Test Agent',
          'domain': 'audio',
          'categories': ['emerging-tech'],
          'timezone': 'Asia/Kolkata',
          'postTimeLocal': '09:30',
          'autoPublish': false,
          'paused': false,
          'style': {'structure': 'bullets'},
        },
        'account': {
          'connected': true,
          'memberName': 'Someone',
          'daysRemaining': 42,
        },
        'config': {
          'liveMode': true,
          'presets': [
            {
              'id': 'builder',
              'label': 'Builder',
              'blurb': 'b',
              'style': {'emoji': 'sparing'},
            },
          ],
        },
        'schedule': {'nextRunLocal': 'tomorrow 09:30', 'cycleCount': 7},
        'queue': [
          {
            'id': 'p1',
            'seq': 1,
            'text': 'Body',
            'status': 'draft',
            'hashtags': ['DSP'],
          },
        ],
        'history': [],
      });

      expect(s.agent!.name, 'Test Agent');
      expect(s.agent!.style.structure, 'bullets');
      expect(s.account.usable, isTrue);
      expect(s.presets.single.label, 'Builder');
      expect(s.queue.single.isDraft, isTrue);
      expect(s.queue.single.hashtags, ['DSP']);
      expect(s.cycleCount, 7);
    });

    test('needsReauth makes an otherwise connected account unusable', () {
      final s = AppStatus.fromJson({
        'initialized': true,
        'account': {'connected': true, 'needsReauth': true},
        'config': {},
      });
      expect(s.account.connected, isTrue);
      expect(s.account.usable, isFalse);
    });

    test('a garbage queue entry list does not crash decoding', () {
      final s = AppStatus.fromJson({
        'initialized': true,
        'config': {},
        'queue': ['not a post', 42, null],
      });
      expect(s.queue, isEmpty);
    });
  });

  group('DraftCard', () {
    Widget wrap(Widget child) => MaterialApp(
      theme: buildTheme(),
      home: Scaffold(body: SingleChildScrollView(child: child)),
    );

    testWidgets('a short post shows no fold marker', (tester) async {
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p1',
        'seq': 1,
        'text': 'Short one.',
        'status': 'draft',
      });
      await tester.pumpWidget(wrap(DraftCard(post: post)));
      expect(find.text('see more'), findsNothing);
    });

    testWidgets('a long post shows the fold where LinkedIn cuts it', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p2',
        'seq': 2,
        'text': 'A' * (kFoldChars + 120),
        'status': 'draft',
      });
      await tester.pumpWidget(wrap(DraftCard(post: post)));
      expect(find.text('see more'), findsOneWidget);
    });

    // "see more" used to be a caption between two rules, with the rest of the
    // text already visible underneath — it looked like a button, sat where a
    // button belongs, and did nothing.
    testWidgets('see more actually expands and collapses', (tester) async {
      final tail = 'TAIL_MARKER ' * 6;
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p30',
        'seq': 30,
        'text': 'A' * (kFoldChars + 5) + ' $tail',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(wrap(DraftCard(post: post)));

      // Collapsed first: what a reader scrolling their feed sees.
      expect(find.text('see more'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.textContaining('TAIL_MARKER'), findsNothing);

      await tester.tap(find.text('see more'));
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();

      expect(find.text('see less'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.textContaining('TAIL_MARKER'), findsOneWidget);

      await tester.tap(find.text('see less'));
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();

      expect(find.text('see more'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.textContaining('TAIL_MARKER'), findsNothing);
    });

    // A post that fits above the fold has nothing to expand, so offering the
    // control would be offering to reveal nothing.
    testWidgets('a short post gets no toggle at all', (tester) async {
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p31',
        'seq': 31,
        'text': 'Short enough to survive the fold intact.',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(wrap(DraftCard(post: post)));

      expect(find.text('see more'), findsNothing);
      expect(find.text('see less'), findsNothing);
    });

    testWidgets('draft actions appear only when handlers are given', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p3',
        'seq': 3,
        'text': 'Body text.',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(wrap(DraftCard(post: post)));
      expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsNothing);

      await tester.pumpWidget(
        wrap(
          DraftCard(
            post: post,
            actions: DraftActions(onSendNow: () {}),
          ),
        ),
      );
      expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsOneWidget);
    });

    // An unscheduled post has no time to be cleared FOR, so the only thing
    // approving it can mean is sending it. Offering "Clear" here would promise
    // a scheduled send that nothing would ever perform.
    testWidgets('an unscheduled post offers Publish, never Clear', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p4',
        'seq': 4,
        'text': 'Body text.',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(
        wrap(
          DraftCard(
            post: post,
            actions: DraftActions(onSendNow: () {}),
          ),
        ),
      );

      expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.textContaining('Schedule post'), findsNothing);
    });

    // The regression that would quietly destroy the review window: if the
    // primary button on a scheduled draft ever publishes instead of clearing,
    // reviewing a post at 08:48 sends it at 08:48.
    testWidgets('a scheduled post leads with Clear, not Publish', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      final at = DateTime.now().add(const Duration(minutes: 20));
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p5',
        'seq': 5,
        'text': 'Body text.',
        'status': 'draft',
        'scheduledFor': at.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(
        wrap(
          DraftCard(
            post: post,
            actions: DraftActions(onClear: () {}, onSendNow: () {}),
          ),
        ),
      );

      final hhmm =
          '${at.hour.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}:${at.minute.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}';
      expect(find.text('Schedule post'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsOneWidget);
      // And the countdown must be on screen — a review window you cannot see
      // the end of is not a review window.
      expect(find.textContaining('Sends $hhmm'), findsOneWidget);
    });

    // A draft with no time is a perfectly normal thing you will publish when
    // you get to it, so the control has to read as an OFFER rather than an
    // empty field waiting to be filled.
    testWidgets('an unscheduled draft is offered a send time', (tester) async {
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p7',
        'seq': 7,
        'text': 'A draft with no send time of its own.',
        'status': 'draft',
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(
        wrap(
          DraftCard(
            post: post,
            actions: DraftActions(onSendNow: () {}, onSchedule: () {}),
          ),
        ),
      );

      await tester.tap(find.byTooltip('More actions'));
      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
      expect(find.text('Choose publish time'), findsOneWidget);
    });

    // Once it has a time the countdown replaces the offer — showing both would
    // suggest there are two different times in play.
    testWidgets('a scheduled draft shows the countdown, not the offer', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      final at = DateTime.now().add(const Duration(minutes: 30));
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p8',
        'seq': 8,
        'text': 'A draft that already has a send time.',
        'status': 'draft',
        'scheduledFor': at.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(
        wrap(
          DraftCard(
            post: post,
            actions: DraftActions(
              onSendNow: () {},
              onSchedule: () {},
              onUnschedule: () {},
            ),
          ),
        ),
      );

      expect(find.text('Choose publish time'), findsNothing);
      expect(find.textContaining('Sends '), findsOneWidget);
    });

    testWidgets('a cleared post says so and stops offering Clear', (
      tester,
    ) async {
      final at = DateTime.now().add(const Duration(minutes: 20));
      final post = Post.fromJson({
        'id': 'p6',
        'seq': 6,
        'text': 'Body text.',
        'status': 'approved',
        'scheduledFor': at.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
        'clearedAt': DateTime.now().toUtc().toIso8601String(),
      });

      await tester.pumpWidget(
        wrap(
          DraftCard(
            post: post,
            actions: DraftActions(onSendNow: () {}),
          ),
        ),
      );

      expect(find.textContaining('Scheduled'), findsOneWidget);
      expect(find.text('Publish now'), findsOneWidget);
    });
  });
}
````

````text
# Project-level configuration.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.14)
set(CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM 3.5)
project(linkdin_mobile LANGUAGES CXX)

# The name of the executable created for the application. Change this to change
# the on-disk name of your application.
set(BINARY_NAME "ByLine")
# Keep bundles in the build tree even after a failed first configuration has
# cached CMake's Program Files default. No system-wide installation is needed.
set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/runner/$<CONFIG>" CACHE PATH "ByLine application bundle" FORCE)

# Explicitly opt in to modern CMake behaviors to avoid warnings with recent
# versions of CMake.
cmake_policy(VERSION 3.14...3.25)

# Define build configuration option.
get_property(IS_MULTICONFIG GLOBAL PROPERTY GENERATOR_IS_MULTI_CONFIG)
if(IS_MULTICONFIG)
  set(CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES "Debug;Profile;Release"
    CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
else()
  if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE "Debug" CACHE
      STRING "Flutter build mode" FORCE)
    set_property(CACHE CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE PROPERTY STRINGS
      "Debug" "Profile" "Release")
  endif()
endif()
# Define settings for the Profile build mode.
set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE}")
set(CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE}")
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE}")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE}")

# Use Unicode for all projects.
add_definitions(-DUNICODE -D_UNICODE)

# Compilation settings that should be applied to most targets.
#
# Be cautious about adding new options here, as plugins use this function by
# default. In most cases, you should add new options to specific targets instead
# of modifying this function.
function(APPLY_STANDARD_SETTINGS TARGET)
  target_compile_features(${TARGET} PUBLIC cxx_std_17)
  target_compile_options(${TARGET} PRIVATE /W4 /WX /wd"4100")
  target_compile_options(${TARGET} PRIVATE /EHsc)
  target_compile_definitions(${TARGET} PRIVATE "_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0")
  target_compile_definitions(${TARGET} PRIVATE "$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:_DEBUG>")
endfunction()

# Flutter library and tool build rules.
set(FLUTTER_MANAGED_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/flutter")
add_subdirectory(${FLUTTER_MANAGED_DIR})

# Application build; see runner/CMakeLists.txt.
add_subdirectory("runner")


# Generated plugin build rules, which manage building the plugins and adding
# them to the application.
include(flutter/generated_plugins.cmake)


# === Installation ===
# Support files are copied into place next to the executable, so that it can
# run in place. This is done instead of making a separate bundle (as on Linux)
# so that building and running from within Visual Studio will work.
set(BUILD_BUNDLE_DIR "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:${BINARY_NAME}>")
# Make the "install" step default, as it's required to run.
set(CMAKE_VS_INCLUDE_INSTALL_TO_DEFAULT_BUILD 1)
if(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX_INITIALIZED_TO_DEFAULT)
  set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX "${BUILD_BUNDLE_DIR}" CACHE PATH "..." FORCE)
endif()

set(INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/data")
set(INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}")

install(TARGETS ${BINARY_NAME} RUNTIME DESTINATION "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}"
  COMPONENT Runtime)

install(FILES "${FLUTTER_ICU_DATA_FILE}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}"
  COMPONENT Runtime)

install(FILES "${FLUTTER_LIBRARY}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
  COMPONENT Runtime)

if(PLUGIN_BUNDLED_LIBRARIES)
  install(FILES "${PLUGIN_BUNDLED_LIBRARIES}"
    DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
    COMPONENT Runtime)
endif()

# Copy the native assets provided by the build.dart from all packages.
set(NATIVE_ASSETS_DIR "${PROJECT_BUILD_DIR}native_assets/windows/")
install(DIRECTORY "${NATIVE_ASSETS_DIR}"
   DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
   COMPONENT Runtime)

# Fully re-copy the assets directory on each build to avoid having stale files
# from a previous install.
set(FLUTTER_ASSET_DIR_NAME "flutter_assets")
install(CODE "
  file(REMOVE_RECURSE \"${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}/${FLUTTER_ASSET_DIR_NAME}\")
  " COMPONENT Runtime)
install(DIRECTORY "${PROJECT_BUILD_DIR}/${FLUTTER_ASSET_DIR_NAME}"
  DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}" COMPONENT Runtime)

# Install the AOT library on non-Debug builds only.
install(FILES "${AOT_LIBRARY}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}"
  CONFIGURATIONS Profile;Release
  COMPONENT Runtime)
````

````text
# This file controls Flutter-level build steps. It should not be edited.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.14)

set(EPHEMERAL_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ephemeral")

# Configuration provided via flutter tool.
include(${EPHEMERAL_DIR}/generated_config.cmake)

# TODO: Move the rest of this into files in ephemeral. See
# https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/57146.
set(WRAPPER_ROOT "${EPHEMERAL_DIR}/cpp_client_wrapper")

# Set fallback configurations for older versions of the flutter tool.
if (NOT DEFINED FLUTTER_TARGET_PLATFORM)
  set(FLUTTER_TARGET_PLATFORM "windows-x64")
endif()

# === Flutter Library ===
set(FLUTTER_LIBRARY "${EPHEMERAL_DIR}/flutter_windows.dll")

# Published to parent scope for install step.
set(FLUTTER_LIBRARY ${FLUTTER_LIBRARY} PARENT_SCOPE)
set(FLUTTER_ICU_DATA_FILE "${EPHEMERAL_DIR}/icudtl.dat" PARENT_SCOPE)
set(PROJECT_BUILD_DIR "${PROJECT_DIR}/build/" PARENT_SCOPE)
set(AOT_LIBRARY "${PROJECT_DIR}/build/windows/app.so" PARENT_SCOPE)

list(APPEND FLUTTER_LIBRARY_HEADERS
  "flutter_export.h"
  "flutter_windows.h"
  "flutter_messenger.h"
  "flutter_plugin_registrar.h"
  "flutter_texture_registrar.h"
)
list(TRANSFORM FLUTTER_LIBRARY_HEADERS PREPEND "${EPHEMERAL_DIR}/")
add_library(flutter INTERFACE)
target_include_directories(flutter INTERFACE
  "${EPHEMERAL_DIR}"
)
target_link_libraries(flutter INTERFACE "${FLUTTER_LIBRARY}.lib")
add_dependencies(flutter flutter_assemble)

# === Wrapper ===
list(APPEND CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE
  "core_implementations.cc"
  "standard_codec.cc"
)
list(TRANSFORM CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE PREPEND "${WRAPPER_ROOT}/")
list(APPEND CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_PLUGIN
  "plugin_registrar.cc"
)
list(TRANSFORM CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_PLUGIN PREPEND "${WRAPPER_ROOT}/")
list(APPEND CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_APP
  "flutter_engine.cc"
  "flutter_view_controller.cc"
)
list(TRANSFORM CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_APP PREPEND "${WRAPPER_ROOT}/")

# Wrapper sources needed for a plugin.
add_library(flutter_wrapper_plugin STATIC
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE}
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_PLUGIN}
)
apply_standard_settings(flutter_wrapper_plugin)
set_target_properties(flutter_wrapper_plugin PROPERTIES
  POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
set_target_properties(flutter_wrapper_plugin PROPERTIES
  CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden)
target_link_libraries(flutter_wrapper_plugin PUBLIC flutter)
target_include_directories(flutter_wrapper_plugin PUBLIC
  "${WRAPPER_ROOT}/include"
)
add_dependencies(flutter_wrapper_plugin flutter_assemble)

# Wrapper sources needed for the runner.
add_library(flutter_wrapper_app STATIC
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE}
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_APP}
)
apply_standard_settings(flutter_wrapper_app)
target_link_libraries(flutter_wrapper_app PUBLIC flutter)
target_include_directories(flutter_wrapper_app PUBLIC
  "${WRAPPER_ROOT}/include"
)
add_dependencies(flutter_wrapper_app flutter_assemble)

# === Flutter tool backend ===
# _phony_ is a non-existent file to force this command to run every time,
# since currently there's no way to get a full input/output list from the
# flutter tool.
set(PHONY_OUTPUT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/_phony_")
set_source_files_properties("${PHONY_OUTPUT}" PROPERTIES SYMBOLIC TRUE)
add_custom_command(
  OUTPUT ${FLUTTER_LIBRARY} ${FLUTTER_LIBRARY_HEADERS}
    ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE} ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_PLUGIN}
    ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_APP}
    ${PHONY_OUTPUT}
  COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
    ${FLUTTER_TOOL_ENVIRONMENT}
    "${FLUTTER_ROOT}/packages/flutter_tools/bin/tool_backend.bat"
      ${FLUTTER_TARGET_PLATFORM} $<CONFIG>
  VERBATIM
)
add_custom_target(flutter_assemble DEPENDS
  "${FLUTTER_LIBRARY}"
  ${FLUTTER_LIBRARY_HEADERS}
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE}
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_PLUGIN}
  ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_APP}
)
````

````text
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.14)
project(runner LANGUAGES CXX)

# Define the application target. To change its name, change BINARY_NAME in the
# top-level CMakeLists.txt, not the value here, or `flutter run` will no longer
# work.
#
# Any new source files that you add to the application should be added here.
add_executable(${BINARY_NAME} WIN32
  "flutter_window.cpp"
  "main.cpp"
  "utils.cpp"
  "win32_window.cpp"
  "${FLUTTER_MANAGED_DIR}/generated_plugin_registrant.cc"
  "Runner.rc"
  "runner.exe.manifest"
)

# Apply the standard set of build settings. This can be removed for applications
# that need different build settings.
apply_standard_settings(${BINARY_NAME})

# Add preprocessor definitions for the build version.
target_compile_definitions(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "FLUTTER_VERSION=\"${FLUTTER_VERSION}\"")
target_compile_definitions(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "FLUTTER_VERSION_MAJOR=${FLUTTER_VERSION_MAJOR}")
target_compile_definitions(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "FLUTTER_VERSION_MINOR=${FLUTTER_VERSION_MINOR}")
target_compile_definitions(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "FLUTTER_VERSION_PATCH=${FLUTTER_VERSION_PATCH}")
target_compile_definitions(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "FLUTTER_VERSION_BUILD=${FLUTTER_VERSION_BUILD}")

# Disable Windows macros that collide with C++ standard library functions.
target_compile_definitions(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "NOMINMAX")

# Add dependency libraries and include directories. Add any application-specific
# dependencies here.
target_link_libraries(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE flutter flutter_wrapper_app)
target_link_libraries(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "dwmapi.lib")
target_include_directories(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")

# Run the Flutter tool portions of the build. This must not be removed.
add_dependencies(${BINARY_NAME} flutter_assemble)
````

## Source: mobile/windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp

````text
#include "flutter_window.h"

#include <optional>
#include <dwmapi.h>
#include <flutter/standard_method_codec.h>

#include "flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.h"

FlutterWindow::FlutterWindow(const flutter::DartProject& project)
    : project_(project) {}

FlutterWindow::~FlutterWindow() {}

bool FlutterWindow::OnCreate() {
  if (!Win32Window::OnCreate()) {
    return false;
  }

  // Keep the native frame in the same light palette as the writing workspace.
  // Older Windows versions ignore unsupported DWM attributes.
  const COLORREF caption_color = RGB(243, 246, 249);
  const COLORREF caption_text = RGB(25, 25, 25);
  DwmSetWindowAttribute(GetHandle(), DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR,
                       &caption_color, sizeof(caption_color));
  DwmSetWindowAttribute(GetHandle(), DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR,
                       &caption_text, sizeof(caption_text));

  RECT frame = GetClientArea();

  // The size here must match the window dimensions to avoid unnecessary surface
  // creation / destruction in the startup path.
  flutter_controller_ = std::make_unique<flutter::FlutterViewController>(
      frame.right - frame.left, frame.bottom - frame.top, project_);
  // Ensure that basic setup of the controller was successful.
  if (!flutter_controller_->engine() || !flutter_controller_->view()) {
    return false;
  }
  RegisterPlugins(flutter_controller_->engine());
  SetChildContent(flutter_controller_->view()->GetNativeWindow());
  window_channel_ = std::make_unique<flutter::MethodChannel<flutter::EncodableValue>>(
      flutter_controller_->engine()->messenger(), "byline/window",
      &flutter::StandardMethodCodec::GetInstance());
  window_channel_->SetMethodCallHandler([this](const auto& call, auto result) {
    if (call.method_name() != "show") {
      result->NotImplemented();
      return;
    }
    HWND hwnd = GetHandle();
    ::ShowWindow(hwnd, ::IsIconic(hwnd) ? SW_RESTORE : SW_SHOW);
    if (!::SetForegroundWindow(hwnd)) {
      FLASHWINFO info = {sizeof(FLASHWINFO), hwnd, FLASHW_TRAY, 3, 0};
      ::FlashWindowEx(&info);
    }
    result->Success();
  });

  flutter_controller_->engine()->SetNextFrameCallback([&]() {
    this->Show();
  });

  // Flutter can complete the first frame before the "show window" callback is
  // registered. The following call ensures a frame is pending to ensure the
  // window is shown. It is a no-op if the first frame hasn't completed yet.
  flutter_controller_->ForceRedraw();

  return true;
}

void FlutterWindow::OnDestroy() {
  window_channel_ = nullptr;
  if (flutter_controller_) {
    flutter_controller_ = nullptr;
  }

  Win32Window::OnDestroy();
}

LRESULT
FlutterWindow::MessageHandler(HWND hwnd, UINT const message,
                              WPARAM const wparam,
                              LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  // Give Flutter, including plugins, an opportunity to handle window messages.
  if (flutter_controller_) {
    std::optional<LRESULT> result =
        flutter_controller_->HandleTopLevelWindowProc(hwnd, message, wparam,
                                                      lparam);
    if (result) {
      return *result;
    }
  }

  switch (message) {
    case WM_FONTCHANGE:
      flutter_controller_->engine()->ReloadSystemFonts();
      break;
  }

  return Win32Window::MessageHandler(hwnd, message, wparam, lparam);
}
````

````text
#include <flutter/dart_project.h>
#include <flutter/flutter_view_controller.h>
#include <windows.h>

#include "flutter_window.h"
#include "utils.h"

int APIENTRY wWinMain(_In_ HINSTANCE instance, _In_opt_ HINSTANCE prev,
                      _In_ wchar_t *command_line, _In_ int show_command) {
  // Attach to console when present (e.g., 'flutter run') or create a
  // new console when running with a debugger.
  if (!::AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) && ::IsDebuggerPresent()) {
    CreateAndAttachConsole();
  }

  // Initialize COM, so that it is available for use in the library and/or
  // plugins.
  ::CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);

  flutter::DartProject project(L"data");

  std::vector<std::string> command_line_arguments =
      GetCommandLineArguments();

  project.set_dart_entrypoint_arguments(std::move(command_line_arguments));

  FlutterWindow window(project);
  Win32Window::Point origin(10, 10);
  Win32Window::Size size(1280, 720);
  if (!window.Create(L"ByLine", origin, size)) {
    return EXIT_FAILURE;
  }
  window.SetQuitOnClose(true);

  ::MSG msg;
  while (::GetMessage(&msg, nullptr, 0, 0)) {
    ::TranslateMessage(&msg);
    ::DispatchMessage(&msg);
  }

  ::CoUninitialize();
  return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}
````

````text
#include "utils.h"

#include <flutter_windows.h>
#include <io.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <windows.h>

#include <iostream>

void CreateAndAttachConsole() {
  if (::AllocConsole()) {
    FILE *unused;
    if (freopen_s(&unused, "CONOUT$", "w", stdout)) {
      _dup2(_fileno(stdout), 1);
    }
    if (freopen_s(&unused, "CONOUT$", "w", stderr)) {
      _dup2(_fileno(stdout), 2);
    }
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio();
    FlutterDesktopResyncOutputStreams();
  }
}

std::vector<std::string> GetCommandLineArguments() {
  // Convert the UTF-16 command line arguments to UTF-8 for the Engine to use.
  int argc;
  wchar_t** argv = ::CommandLineToArgvW(::GetCommandLineW(), &argc);
  if (argv == nullptr) {
    return std::vector<std::string>();
  }

  std::vector<std::string> command_line_arguments;

  // Skip the first argument as it's the binary name.
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
    command_line_arguments.push_back(Utf8FromUtf16(argv[i]));
  }

  ::LocalFree(argv);

  return command_line_arguments;
}

std::string Utf8FromUtf16(const wchar_t* utf16_string) {
  if (utf16_string == nullptr) {
    return std::string();
  }
  // First, find the length of the string with a safe upper bound (CWE-126).
  // UNICODE_STRING_MAX_CHARS (32767) is the maximum length of a UNICODE_STRING.
  int input_length = static_cast<int>(wcsnlen(utf16_string, UNICODE_STRING_MAX_CHARS));
  // Now use that bounded length to determine the required buffer size.
  // When an explicit length is passed, WideCharToMultiByte does not include
  // the null terminator in its returned size.
  int target_length = ::WideCharToMultiByte(
      CP_UTF8, WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf16_string,
      input_length, nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr);
  std::string utf8_string;
  if (target_length == 0 || static_cast<size_t>(target_length) > utf8_string.max_size()) {
    return utf8_string;
  }
  utf8_string.resize(target_length);
  int converted_length = ::WideCharToMultiByte(
      CP_UTF8, WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf16_string,
      input_length, utf8_string.data(), target_length, nullptr, nullptr);
  if (converted_length == 0) {
    return std::string();
  }
  return utf8_string;
}
````

````text
#include "win32_window.h"

#include <dwmapi.h>
#include <flutter_windows.h>

#include "resource.h"

namespace {

/// Window attribute that enables dark mode window decorations.
///
/// Redefined in case the developer's machine has a Windows SDK older than
/// version 10.0.22000.0.
/// See: https://docs.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/dwmapi/ne-dwmapi-dwmwindowattribute
#ifndef DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE
#define DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE 20
#endif

constexpr const wchar_t kWindowClassName[] = L"FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW";

/// Registry key for app theme preference.
///
/// A value of 0 indicates apps should use dark mode. A non-zero or missing
/// value indicates apps should use light mode.
constexpr const wchar_t kGetPreferredBrightnessRegKey[] =
  L"Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Themes\\Personalize";
constexpr const wchar_t kGetPreferredBrightnessRegValue[] = L"AppsUseLightTheme";

// The number of Win32Window objects that currently exist.
static int g_active_window_count = 0;

using EnableNonClientDpiScaling = BOOL __stdcall(HWND hwnd);

// Scale helper to convert logical scaler values to physical using passed in
// scale factor
int Scale(int source, double scale_factor) {
  return static_cast<int>(source * scale_factor);
}

// Dynamically loads the |EnableNonClientDpiScaling| from the User32 module.
// This API is only needed for PerMonitor V1 awareness mode.
void EnableFullDpiSupportIfAvailable(HWND hwnd) {
  HMODULE user32_module = LoadLibraryA("User32.dll");
  if (!user32_module) {
    return;
  }
  auto enable_non_client_dpi_scaling =
      reinterpret_cast<EnableNonClientDpiScaling*>(
          GetProcAddress(user32_module, "EnableNonClientDpiScaling"));
  if (enable_non_client_dpi_scaling != nullptr) {
    enable_non_client_dpi_scaling(hwnd);
  }
  FreeLibrary(user32_module);
}

}  // namespace

// Manages the Win32Window's window class registration.
class WindowClassRegistrar {
 public:
  ~WindowClassRegistrar() = default;

  // Returns the singleton registrar instance.
  static WindowClassRegistrar* GetInstance() {
    if (!instance_) {
      instance_ = new WindowClassRegistrar();
    }
    return instance_;
  }

  // Returns the name of the window class, registering the class if it hasn't
  // previously been registered.
  const wchar_t* GetWindowClass();

  // Unregisters the window class. Should only be called if there are no
  // instances of the window.
  void UnregisterWindowClass();

 private:
  WindowClassRegistrar() = default;

  static WindowClassRegistrar* instance_;

  bool class_registered_ = false;
};

WindowClassRegistrar* WindowClassRegistrar::instance_ = nullptr;

const wchar_t* WindowClassRegistrar::GetWindowClass() {
  if (!class_registered_) {
    WNDCLASS window_class{};
    window_class.hCursor = LoadCursor(nullptr, IDC_ARROW);
    window_class.lpszClassName = kWindowClassName;
    window_class.style = CS_HREDRAW | CS_VREDRAW;
    window_class.cbClsExtra = 0;
    window_class.cbWndExtra = 0;
    window_class.hInstance = GetModuleHandle(nullptr);
    window_class.hIcon =
        LoadIcon(window_class.hInstance, MAKEINTRESOURCE(IDI_APP_ICON));
    window_class.hbrBackground = 0;
    window_class.lpszMenuName = nullptr;
    window_class.lpfnWndProc = Win32Window::WndProc;
    RegisterClass(&window_class);
    class_registered_ = true;
  }
  return kWindowClassName;
}

void WindowClassRegistrar::UnregisterWindowClass() {
  UnregisterClass(kWindowClassName, nullptr);
  class_registered_ = false;
}

Win32Window::Win32Window() {
  ++g_active_window_count;
}

Win32Window::~Win32Window() {
  --g_active_window_count;
  Destroy();
}

bool Win32Window::Create(const std::wstring& title,
                         const Point& origin,
                         const Size& size) {
  Destroy();

  const wchar_t* window_class =
      WindowClassRegistrar::GetInstance()->GetWindowClass();

  const POINT target_point = {static_cast<LONG>(origin.x),
                              static_cast<LONG>(origin.y)};
  HMONITOR monitor = MonitorFromPoint(target_point, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST);
  UINT dpi = FlutterDesktopGetDpiForMonitor(monitor);
  double scale_factor = dpi / 96.0;

  HWND window = CreateWindow(
      window_class, title.c_str(), WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW,
      Scale(origin.x, scale_factor), Scale(origin.y, scale_factor),
      Scale(size.width, scale_factor), Scale(size.height, scale_factor),
      nullptr, nullptr, GetModuleHandle(nullptr), this);

  if (!window) {
    return false;
  }

  UpdateTheme(window);

  return OnCreate();
}

bool Win32Window::Show() {
  return ShowWindow(window_handle_, SW_SHOWNORMAL);
}

// static
LRESULT CALLBACK Win32Window::WndProc(HWND const window,
                                      UINT const message,
                                      WPARAM const wparam,
                                      LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  if (message == WM_NCCREATE) {
    auto window_struct = reinterpret_cast<CREATESTRUCT*>(lparam);
    SetWindowLongPtr(window, GWLP_USERDATA,
                     reinterpret_cast<LONG_PTR>(window_struct->lpCreateParams));

    auto that = static_cast<Win32Window*>(window_struct->lpCreateParams);
    EnableFullDpiSupportIfAvailable(window);
    that->window_handle_ = window;
  } else if (Win32Window* that = GetThisFromHandle(window)) {
    return that->MessageHandler(window, message, wparam, lparam);
  }

  return DefWindowProc(window, message, wparam, lparam);
}

LRESULT
Win32Window::MessageHandler(HWND hwnd,
                            UINT const message,
                            WPARAM const wparam,
                            LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  switch (message) {
    case WM_DESTROY:
      window_handle_ = nullptr;
      Destroy();
      if (quit_on_close_) {
        PostQuitMessage(0);
      }
      return 0;

    case WM_DPICHANGED: {
      auto newRectSize = reinterpret_cast<RECT*>(lparam);
      LONG newWidth = newRectSize->right - newRectSize->left;
      LONG newHeight = newRectSize->bottom - newRectSize->top;

      SetWindowPos(hwnd, nullptr, newRectSize->left, newRectSize->top, newWidth,
                   newHeight, SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE);

      return 0;
    }
    case WM_SIZE: {
      RECT rect = GetClientArea();
      if (child_content_ != nullptr) {
        // Size and position the child window.
        MoveWindow(child_content_, rect.left, rect.top, rect.right - rect.left,
                   rect.bottom - rect.top, TRUE);
      }
      return 0;
    }

    case WM_ACTIVATE:
      if (child_content_ != nullptr) {
        SetFocus(child_content_);
      }
      return 0;

    case WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED:
      UpdateTheme(hwnd);
      return 0;
  }

  return DefWindowProc(window_handle_, message, wparam, lparam);
}

void Win32Window::Destroy() {
  OnDestroy();

  if (window_handle_) {
    DestroyWindow(window_handle_);
    window_handle_ = nullptr;
  }
  if (g_active_window_count == 0) {
    WindowClassRegistrar::GetInstance()->UnregisterWindowClass();
  }
}

Win32Window* Win32Window::GetThisFromHandle(HWND const window) noexcept {
  return reinterpret_cast<Win32Window*>(
      GetWindowLongPtr(window, GWLP_USERDATA));
}

void Win32Window::SetChildContent(HWND content) {
  child_content_ = content;
  SetParent(content, window_handle_);
  RECT frame = GetClientArea();

  MoveWindow(content, frame.left, frame.top, frame.right - frame.left,
             frame.bottom - frame.top, true);

  SetFocus(child_content_);
}

RECT Win32Window::GetClientArea() {
  RECT frame;
  GetClientRect(window_handle_, &frame);
  return frame;
}

HWND Win32Window::GetHandle() {
  return window_handle_;
}

void Win32Window::SetQuitOnClose(bool quit_on_close) {
  quit_on_close_ = quit_on_close;
}

bool Win32Window::OnCreate() {
  // No-op; provided for subclasses.
  return true;
}

void Win32Window::OnDestroy() {
  // No-op; provided for subclasses.
}

void Win32Window::UpdateTheme(HWND const window) {
  DWORD light_mode;
  DWORD light_mode_size = sizeof(light_mode);
  LSTATUS result = RegGetValue(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, kGetPreferredBrightnessRegKey,
                               kGetPreferredBrightnessRegValue,
                               RRF_RT_REG_DWORD, nullptr, &light_mode,
                               &light_mode_size);

  if (result == ERROR_SUCCESS) {
    BOOL enable_dark_mode = light_mode == 0;
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(window, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE,
                          &enable_dark_mode, sizeof(enable_dark_mode));
  }
}
````

````text
#ifndef RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW_H_
#define RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW_H_

#include <windows.h>

#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

// A class abstraction for a high DPI-aware Win32 Window. Intended to be
// inherited from by classes that wish to specialize with custom
// rendering and input handling
class Win32Window {
 public:
  struct Point {
    unsigned int x;
    unsigned int y;
    Point(unsigned int x, unsigned int y) : x(x), y(y) {}
  };

  struct Size {
    unsigned int width;
    unsigned int height;
    Size(unsigned int width, unsigned int height)
        : width(width), height(height) {}
  };

  Win32Window();
  virtual ~Win32Window();

  // Creates a win32 window with |title| that is positioned and sized using
  // |origin| and |size|. New windows are created on the default monitor. Window
  // sizes are specified to the OS in physical pixels, hence to ensure a
  // consistent size this function will scale the inputted width and height as
  // as appropriate for the default monitor. The window is invisible until
  // |Show| is called. Returns true if the window was created successfully.
  bool Create(const std::wstring& title, const Point& origin, const Size& size);

  // Show the current window. Returns true if the window was successfully shown.
  bool Show();

  // Release OS resources associated with window.
  void Destroy();

  // Inserts |content| into the window tree.
  void SetChildContent(HWND content);

  // Returns the backing Window handle to enable clients to set icon and other
  // window properties. Returns nullptr if the window has been destroyed.
  HWND GetHandle();

  // If true, closing this window will quit the application.
  void SetQuitOnClose(bool quit_on_close);

  // Return a RECT representing the bounds of the current client area.
  RECT GetClientArea();

 protected:
  // Processes and route salient window messages for mouse handling,
  // size change and DPI. Delegates handling of these to member overloads that
  // inheriting classes can handle.
  virtual LRESULT MessageHandler(HWND window,
                                 UINT const message,
                                 WPARAM const wparam,
                                 LPARAM const lparam) noexcept;

  // Called when CreateAndShow is called, allowing subclass window-related
  // setup. Subclasses should return false if setup fails.
  virtual bool OnCreate();

  // Called when Destroy is called.
  virtual void OnDestroy();

 private:
  friend class WindowClassRegistrar;

  // OS callback called by message pump. Handles the WM_NCCREATE message which
  // is passed when the non-client area is being created and enables automatic
  // non-client DPI scaling so that the non-client area automatically
  // responds to changes in DPI. All other messages are handled by
  // MessageHandler.
  static LRESULT CALLBACK WndProc(HWND const window,
                                  UINT const message,
                                  WPARAM const wparam,
                                  LPARAM const lparam) noexcept;

  // Retrieves a class instance pointer for |window|
  static Win32Window* GetThisFromHandle(HWND const window) noexcept;

  // Update the window frame's theme to match the system theme.
  static void UpdateTheme(HWND const window);

  bool quit_on_close_ = false;

  // window handle for top level window.
  HWND window_handle_ = nullptr;

  // window handle for hosted content.
  HWND child_content_ = nullptr;
};

#endif  // RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW_H_

````

## Source: next.config.ts

````text
import type { NextConfig } from "next";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // Deployed on Vercel (Hobby, serverless functions). No standalone output;
  // the cycle driver is /api/cron/tick with maxDuration 300.
  //
  // The build directory is overridable so a verification build can be run
  // WITHOUT clobbering a dev server that is already running.
  //
  // `next dev` and `next build` both own .next/. Run a build while the dev
  // server is live and the build replaces the chunks the running server still
  // holds references to — after which every request dies with
  // `Cannot find module './331.js'` or a missing vendor-chunk. It looks like a
  // catastrophic code failure and is purely a clobbered cache; the only cure is
  // deleting .next and restarting.
  //
  // `npm run build:check` sets NEXT_DIST_DIR so the two never share a directory.
  distDir: process.env.NEXT_DIST_DIR || ".next",

  /**
   * Response headers. This dashboard can publish to a real LinkedIn profile
   * from a URL that is guessable and crawlable, so the cheap browser-side
   * protections are worth having even with one user.
   *
   * Deliberately NOT a full Content-Security-Policy: Next injects inline
   * scripts for hydration, a script-src that forbids them breaks the app, and
   * the nonce plumbing that fixes it properly is a real project. frame-ancestors
   * is the one directive that cannot be set any other way and costs nothing.
   */
  async headers() {
    return [
      {
        source: "/:path*",
        headers: [
          // Two years, and only meaningful over HTTPS — which on Vercel is all
          // there is. Stops a first request over http:// being downgradeable.
          { key: "Strict-Transport-Security", value: "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains" },
          // An uploaded GIF must never be sniffed into something executable.
          { key: "X-Content-Type-Options", value: "nosniff" },
          // Clickjacking: nothing here should ever be framed. X-Frame-Options
          // for older browsers, frame-ancestors for the ones that matter.
          { key: "X-Frame-Options", value: "DENY" },
          { key: "Content-Security-Policy", value: "frame-ancestors 'none'" },
          // Do not leak the path of an authenticated page to third parties.
          { key: "Referrer-Policy", value: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" },
          // Nothing here needs hardware. Saying so removes the prompt entirely.
          { key: "Permissions-Policy", value: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), interest-cohort=()" },
        ],
      },
    ];
  },
};

export default nextConfig;

````

````text
# Install ByLine on Android

[Download the latest APK](https://github.com/Don-Gabriel/link_agent/raw/refs/heads/main/releases/android/byline-latest.apk)

The APK is the signed **ByLine cloud release**, connected to
`https://byline-api.byline-b79.workers.dev`. It does not require your computer to run.
GitHub repository access is required if the repository is private.

1. Download the APK on your Android phone. In GitHub's file view, select **Download raw file**.
2. Open it from Downloads/Files. If prompted, allow that browser or file manager to
   **install unknown apps**, then tap **Install** and **Open**. Device policies and
   Android verification requirements may add prompts or restrictions.
3. Sign in with an available provider in the system browser and return to ByLine.
4. Choose subjects and optional voice preferences, generate and accept a sample,
   connect LinkedIn, and choose your posting time and timezone.
5. Allow notifications if wanted. Review drafts in **Home** and **My posts**.
   Automatic publishing starts off; the first recurring slot is tomorrow in your timezone.

Customers do not enter Gemini keys or database credentials. This is an Android APK;
there is no iPhone IPA/TestFlight build in this repository.

See [release.json](release.json) for the exact version, SDK/architecture requirements,
signing certificate and SHA-256. [SHA256SUMS](SHA256SUMS) verifies the download:

```powershell
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\byline-latest.apk
```

An existing release signed with the same key can update in place. If Android reports
a signature conflict, do not uninstall without preserving account access and planning
the migration. A previous debug/live build may use the same package ID with a different
certificate. ByLine Preview uses a separate package and can coexist.

## Rebuild

Restore the owner's private signing key/configuration and matching Firebase client
configuration into the ignored locations described in [cloud/README.md](../../cloud/README.md).
Then run from the repository root:

```powershell
node scripts/prepare-cloud-android.mjs https://byline-api.byline-b79.workers.dev
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/build-cloud-android.ps1
```

Verify the APK with Android SDK `apksigner` and `aapt`, copy the exact build to
`releases/android/byline-latest.apk`, and regenerate its checksum/metadata. Never
commit private keys, key.properties, server API keys or service-account credentials.
Neither of the above build commands installs anything on a phone.

[Complete project handbook](../../output/pdf/ByLine-Complete-Project-Handbook.pdf)

Platform references: [Android distribution](https://developer.android.com/distribute/marketing-tools/alternative-distribution),
[APK signature verification](https://developer.android.com/tools/apksigner).

````
