## Source: reports/ByLine-UX-redesign-plan.md

````text
# ByLine: complete Android and Windows experience

Prepared before UI implementation, 6 September 2026. Scope: first launch, OAuth, onboarding, daily approval, editor, history, voice, interests, delivery, advanced timetable, connection and diagnostics. The working local backend remains the test environment. Budget: zero; no paid assets, generation, hosting or external design service required.

## Research and diagnosis

This is a heuristic review of the code and the owner's hands-on feedback, not a claim that interviews or a usability study have occurred. Professional users do not universally prefer one theme. Here the owner explicitly wants a lighter reading experience and more control, so light is the chosen default.

- [W3C contrast guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html): body text needs at least 4.5:1 contrast. Use deep blue text on white; pale blue is a surface color. Test actual token pairs rather than assuming all blues are accessible.
- [Flutter adaptive guidance](https://docs.flutter.dev/ui/adaptive-responsive/best-practices): adapt to available width, preserve state across layout changes, and constrain long content instead of stretching phone forms across a monitor.
- [Microsoft layout guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/design/layout/): desktop windows need responsive navigation and a coherent hierarchy at varied sizes.
- [NN/g progressive disclosure](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/): emphasize the few controls needed for the current task while retaining specialist controls in clearly named expandable sections.
- Applied installed Claude skills: UI Visual Design System, Mobile UX Design, Desktop App Design, Accessibility & Inclusive Design under the owner's `.claude/skills` directory. Their general guidance is adapted to Flutter; no Claude API calls or paid agents are involved.

Current issues: black/gold tokens are global; condensed all-cap labels make ordinary settings look technical; large desktop windows stretch controls; onboarding hides examples; voice opens with presets and many chips before reaching free-text rules; custom interests cannot be edited naturally after setup; delivery uses a coarse slider; advanced timetable language incorrectly implies no daily draft exists without slots; next-delivery text displays raw timestamps. Loading, success and error states need more consistent presentation.

## Design system

Soft blue-gray canvas (#F5F7FB), white content surfaces, dark slate body text (#17243B), slate secondary text (#506078), deep blue primary (#2457C5), pale blue selected surfaces (#EAF0FF). Green confirmations and red errors have icons/text as well as color. White text only on sufficiently dark filled buttons. Inputs use visible slate outlines and blue keyboard focus. Rounded 12–20px surfaces, limited borders, generous space between sections; avoid nesting everything in cards. Use bundled Plex Sans for reading and headings and tabular numbers only where useful. Touch targets at least 48 logical pixels; no clipped labels at larger text sizes. Motion is brief and respects system reduced-motion settings.

## Journey and screen specification

| Stage | Experience | Preserved contract |
|---|---|---|
| First launch | Clear ByLine identity, short promise, focused sign-in panel; connection error has Retry; browser handoff shows waiting/cancel | Existing provider flags, secure verifier, interrupted login recovery, legacy installation access |
| LinkedIn | Immediate connected-name confirmation; no developer setup for clients | OAuth, separate member account, encrypted credentials |
| Interests | Industry helps choose sources; suggested chips plus editable personal topics and clear limits | Source-backed discovery, 3–5 onboarding topics; custom interests feed writer persona |
| Voice | Describe how you write in plain language; pasted examples prominent; four presets optional | Existing corpus, style rules, preview, banned phrases, signature and granular style controls |
| Sample | Readable post surface, source link, regenerate/edit voice, explicit acceptance | Revision-bound acceptance; no publish during setup |
| Delivery | Exact time picker with keyboard entry, quick morning choices, timezone field with suggestions | Server time validation, timezone rescheduling, one daily approval default |
| Notifications | Plain explanation, allow/later, test control with delivery feedback | FCM foreground and background, Windows toast polling, notification tap routing |
| Ready | Specific first delivery and next action | Activation only after accepted sample |
| Daily use | One readable draft with clear source and Approve/Edit/Skip; helpful next-delivery empty state | Reviewed snapshot protection, one-tap publish, skip, manual generation and advanced draft access |
| Editor/history | Light reading/editing surfaces; keep attachments, rewrites, scheduling and archive actions | Existing endpoints and state mutations |
| Preferences | Voice and topics easy to find; everyday delivery distinguished from advanced publishing slots | Pause, auto-publish, caps, connection, diagnostics and all legacy controls retained |

Desktop: navigation rail at wider sizes, content limited to readable width, keyboard focus and resizable layouts. Phone: labelled bottom navigation, single-column forms and touch-sized controls. Controls change position only when the layout requires it; state survives width changes.

## Implementation order and safeguards

1. Save this plan; leave credentials, account data, published posts and schedule unchanged.
2. Replace global tokens and shared components; adapt navigation and content bounds.
3. Redesign welcome, onboarding, daily reading and delivery controls.
4. Surface voice rules and examples; add persistent custom interests without changing broad feed choices. Additive server validation only where necessary. Preserve advanced controls behind clear disclosure.
5. Test contrast, phone and desktop layouts, text scaling, custom-input persistence, existing onboarding and publishing request semantics. Run existing Flutter tests and relevant backend checks. Generate previews from real widgets; inspect phone screenshots.
6. Build/install Android in place (preserve session); build Windows release and provide the complete executable folder. Do not send LinkedIn posts during verification. Avoid paid AI calls; use fixtures for generation tests.

## Moving beyond localhost, after the redesign

The desktop and Android clients ultimately connect to one public HTTPS backend, which owns OAuth callback handling, Gemini credentials, PostgreSQL, scheduling and FCM. Customers install the app and sign in; no web dashboard or customer API keys are needed.

At zero budget, a controlled remote pilot can use an HTTPS tunnel to the existing computer while it stays awake. [Cloudflare Quick Tunnels](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/) are for testing, use a generated hostname and are not a durable production endpoint. A stable endpoint and callback registration are required before reliable client distribution. This is not a promise of free always-on production hosting. The next hosting decision must verify current provider limits, commercial terms, background scheduling, database persistence, backups and billing-disabled guarantees before provisioning. No public deployment is part of this UI change.

## Acceptance and limits

No deleted capabilities; no new onboarding API-key fields; custom voice and interests are saved and used, not decorative controls; exact delivery time is supported; minimum text contrast checks pass; navigation works at phone and desktop widths; tests and both native builds pass. Human TalkBack/Narrator testing and a broader client usability study remain separate validation—automated tests cannot certify complete accessibility.

## Implementation and verification — 6 September 2026

Implemented the light palette and typography across native screens, responsive desktop navigation, readable content widths, welcoming sign-in and matching browser-return page, custom onboarding voice instructions, prominent writing examples, optional voice presets and expandable advanced controls, persisted personal interests, exact delivery-time input, clearer timetable language and a readable daily approval surface. Existing APIs and actions were preserved; custom interests use an additive authenticated endpoint that updates only the current account's interests while retaining its voice and source categories.

Validation completed:

- **148 Flutter tests passed**, including existing onboarding/sample-acceptance, approval-request, editing, scheduling and notification tests. New coverage includes contrast token pairs, eight screens at 390/900/1280 widths, small-phone layouts with 160% text, custom voice editing and exact-minute input.
- **47 local backend integration checks passed**: custom voice persistence and writer style, custom interests persistence, account isolation, invalid-input rejection, preservation of voice/source categories, exact-minute rescheduling, reviewed-snapshot approval and the existing daily loop. All generation/publishing in this suite uses the isolated fixture database. It confirmed zero Gemini calls and zero LinkedIn distributions.
- `flutter analyze`, TypeScript checking and the existing backend self-check suite passed.
- Android debug APK and Windows release build succeeded. The complete Windows release folder was packaged as `.byline-local/ByLine-Windows.zip`; the Android APK is `.byline-local/byline-live.apk`.
- Inspected widget-rendered previews using synthetic data, including daily desktop, phone topics and onboarding sample screens. These render the actual Flutter widgets and bundled fonts.

The phone was disconnected during final build verification, so installation and a fresh physical-device UI check remain pending. The Windows executable passed a process-launch smoke check; a complete interactive desktop sign-in/notification check remains pending. These limits do not replace the owner's earlier successful live phone publishing test, and that earlier test is not represented as validation of this new interface.

No public host, paid service or new billable AI call was introduced. The APK is a development build, not a signed store release. Google provider configuration, production credentials/hosting, account deletion/export, provider linking, release distribution and overnight real-device delivery remain release work described in `BYLINE-LIVE.md`.

````

## Source: reports/ByLine-UX-v2-plan.md

````text
# ByLine UX v2 — planned before implementation

6 September 2026. The owner rejected the previous refresh because it retained the button-heavy structure. This revision changes navigation, forms, page composition and daily-post states, while retaining the working backend and zero-budget safeguards.

## Reference analysis

LinkedIn's [published design examples](https://design.linkedin.com/) include desktop feed and mobile profile/network screens. Its [design principles](https://design.linkedin.com/design-principles) emphasize useful, simple and trustworthy experiences. Its [desktop redesign explanation](https://www.linkedin.com/blog/member/product/linkedin-desktop-redesign-puts-conversations-and-content-at-the-center) describes top-level navigation and content as the main focus; it is historical evidence, not a claim that every current account has that exact layout. Current public app/store and image-search references reinforce the profile summary, central post card, author metadata, source preview and mobile bottom-navigation patterns.

Use the familiar LinkedIn blue (#0A66C2), warm neutral canvas (#F3F2EF), white cards, charcoal text, restrained gray borders and pill-shaped primary actions. Keep ByLine's name and own iconography. Do not add LinkedIn's logo or imply that ByLine is LinkedIn. Form controls use visible labels, clear focus outlines and accessible dark text. Contrast is measured against the actual backgrounds.

Applied installed Claude skills: UI Visual Design System, Mobile UX Design, Desktop App Design, Accessibility & Inclusive Design. This is a reference/heuristic review with the owner's feedback, not a formal user study.

## New structure

- **Home:** author/profile summary, a compact 'Start a post' entry, today's suggestion or an explicit daily outcome, and next-delivery information. Desktop uses a top navigation bar with profile/context columns around a narrow feed. Mobile puts the feed first with a compact account header and bottom navigation.
- **My posts:** retained draft management and published/source history, with dropdown navigation/filtering instead of segmented button rows. Existing editing, attachments, rewrite, schedule, hold and publish controls remain available.
- **Me:** profile/connection card followed by grouped preference rows. Writing preferences, interests and delivery are ordinary editable forms; technical diagnostics stay separate.
- **Voice:** free-text instructions and examples, a preset dropdown, and labelled dropdowns for structure, emoji, opening, closing and audience. Advanced length, signature and banned-phrase controls remain.
- **Topics:** searchable multi-select picker with a checked list and Apply/Cancel; selected topics appear as a summary, not a wall of buttons. Custom topics remain editable. Source categories retain the at-least-one rule.
- **Delivery and timetable:** exact time entry, searchable timezone selection with custom IANA input, and a weekday picker rather than seven small selector buttons. Preserve individual minutes, lead times, caps and automatic publishing safeguards.
- **First launch and setup:** a focused sign-in card, labelled progress/navigation, white form surfaces, industry/voice dropdowns, topic picker, readable sample card and specific completion message. Existing OAuth and sample acceptance rules remain.

## Daily preparation state contract

Currently `/api/review-delivery` returns `alreadyPrepared` and a sequence, which the client drops. Published or discarded posts disappear from the draft queue. Fix this by returning a complete, account-scoped daily-post summary and exposing today's state on reload. Distinguish not prepared, preparing/retrying, draft, approved/scheduled, published, skipped, failed and uncertain publishing. Existing posts never trigger another AI generation or another publish.

The button must show progress and a visible result. A repeated prepare opens the existing post. Published and skipped posts get a clear explanation, a read-only view of that exact post and next-delivery information; failures get a useful recovery route. Do not reset the daily cap or silently create duplicates.

## Verification and delivery

Use fixture data for AI and publishing tests. Add repeat-prepare tests for draft/published/skipped states and tenant isolation, dropdown/multi-select keyboard and selection tests, phone/desktop rendering and enlarged text. Retain existing behavior tests, adapting only the intended new control interactions. Inspect actual widget previews, then build Android and Windows, install on the connected phone in place and replace the Downloads Windows archive with a verified updated copy. Do not publish a LinkedIn post during testing.

````

## Source: reports/ByLine-build-status-2026-09-06.md

````text
# ByLine implementation and verification — 6 September 2026

## Live integration follow-up

The follow-up build now uses real services in a separate local environment; see [BYLINE-LIVE.md](../BYLINE-LIVE.md). Google billing was verified disabled for both the existing Gemini project and Firebase project. Four real Gemini requests succeeded: one onboarding sample and a complete source-discovery/scoring/writing run including a repair. The latter scored 34 candidates and saved an unscheduled draft above the existing quality threshold. No LinkedIn send was attempted.

Registered the separate Android package `com.linkdin.byline` in the existing Firebase project and installed it as **ByLine Live**. Firebase resources are included for background initialization. The FCM API is enabled and the local server can refresh operator access tokens without storing a new service-account private key. Added an in-app notification test, real immediate daily preparation with deduplication, recovery for interrupted sign-in, a native callback return link, reviewed-content checks on daily approval, and native Windows notifications while the desktop client is open/minimized. Added a private local database-backup command and created an archive.

Verification: the existing 108 Flutter tests passed, plus the new sign-in recovery test; 32 HTTP integration checks, four zero-budget failure checks, backend self-tests, TypeScript validation, and the backend production build passed. Android and Windows native builds succeeded. At the latest integration check, the user's LinkedIn sign-in had started but had not returned consent: there were no real signed-in accounts or registered phone tokens in this environment. Physical notification delivery and real publishing therefore remain unverified until the user completes that handoff. Google OAuth client configuration and the public-release items below are still outstanding.

The original preview findings below describe the first build and its deliberately disabled external integrations.

The Android local preview and Windows desktop client now use the existing backend and publishing engine. Customers can complete the new guided setup entirely in the native app. The existing web interface remains in the repository for compatibility with the original installation; it is not required for the new onboarding or daily loop.

## Implemented

| Area | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Account setup | Google and LinkedIn browser consent flows, verifier-protected completion exchange, individual account provisioning and revocable sessions in platform secure storage. Provider buttons appear when the service is configured. |
| LinkedIn connection | Server-owned credentials, automatic connection polling, account-name confirmation and expiry handling. Native customers never create their own developer app or enter API keys. |
| Interests | Six industries, 3–5 editable topics and automatic source selection. Added populated feeds for marketing, HR, finance, healthcare and business. |
| Voice and sample | Four presets or up to three writing examples; saved progress; sample generation, regeneration and revision-bound acceptance before activation. Real mode uses Gemini and source material. Local mode visibly uses demonstrations. |
| Daily delivery | Default 09:00 in the device timezone, adjustable time, next-day activation, durable daily records, retries, deduplication and notification outbox. Delivery time can be changed in Settings. |
| Daily interaction | Source link, hashtags, Approve/Edit/Skip and the existing composer. Scheduled advanced posts retain their scheduled approval behavior. |
| Existing features | Advanced slots, pause, publishing controls, custom writing styles, categories, manual composition, media, archive, rewrites, follow-ups, diagnostics and legacy owner login remain available. |
| Service controls | Account-scoped API access, media ownership checks, atomic post numbering, shared AI pacing and daily allowances, token-usage recording, additive migration ledger and deployment migration gate. |
| Free local testing | Separate local PostgreSQL cluster and server, fixtures without Gemini calls, simulated approval without LinkedIn sends, separate Android package alongside the original app. |

## Checks performed

- Backend self-tests and additional session, setup-validation and daylight-saving checks passed.
- 91 database checks passed against the isolated local database.
- 29 HTTP integration checks passed, including account isolation, acceptance, activation, daily deduplication, concurrent composer saves, local approval, delivery changes and session revocation.
- 108 Flutter tests passed, including a regression test covering setup completion without restarting the app.
- Flutter analysis reported no issues; TypeScript and the Next.js production build passed.
- Android debug APK and Windows release executable built successfully.
- Installed the preview on the connected Android phone. Exercised guided setup, session restoration, draft delivery, source display, editing and the settings entry. A phone-discovered setup transition bug was reproduced in a test and fixed.
- New feed URLs returned populated RSS. Replaced the initially selected broken business feed with Entrepreneur.

The tests made no Gemini calls and no LinkedIn sends. Original credentials, the original application's phone data, and the original hosted database were not replaced. The local preview server must remain running and the phone must retain its USB connection/ADB forwarding.

## Remaining work before customers

This build is a local preview, not a completed public production rollout. Real Google/LinkedIn consent and account reconnect need integration testing with the service-owned provider registrations and approved callback URLs. Gemini output quality, quota behavior and free-service data terms need validation with appropriate test content. Physical FCM delivery is not tested in the credential-free preview; native Windows notifications still need an implementation. LinkedIn recent-post import is not implemented because ordinary sign-in grants do not establish access to member post history; pasted examples work instead.

Release signing and update delivery, operational backup/restore validation, public privacy/support material, account export/deletion, provider linking across Google and LinkedIn identities, and verified migration of the original owner's history remain release work. Signing in through a different provider currently creates a separate account. Source failures or the existing quality threshold can still result in a quiet day after retries; the service cannot guarantee one suitable post or an exact push arrival time every day.

No billing or paid services were enabled. Local commands and integration boundaries are documented in [BYLINE-LOCAL.md](../BYLINE-LOCAL.md).

````

## Source: reports/ByLine-finance-preparation-fix-2026-09-06.md

````text
# Finance daily preparation

## Observed cause

Read-only inspection of the new finance account showed completed onboarding,
an unpaused agent, and a successful Gemini judging call. Its first daily
preparation on 2026-09-06 scored one Federal Reserve enforcement-action update
at 5.2, below the unchanged 6.5 threshold. No post was inserted. Finance had only
one configured feed and discovery excluded material older than 72 hours.

The daily review worker discarded the cycle's `below_threshold` result and
stored a generic failure. The endpoint also returned the same generic failure
when a retry was cooling down, already running, or exhausted for the day.

## Changes

- Add Banking Dive, ECB Blog and ECB Publications to finance discovery.
- Supplement categories with fewer than five recent candidates using articles
  no older than seven days. Keep candidate caps, deduplication, rejection
  cooldown, per-user/provider AI limits and the 6.5 quality threshold.
- Give judging and writing the publication date and current date. Remove the
  judge's universal assumption that every client is an engineer.
- Persist the actual cycle failure reason; map it to safe, specific client
  messages without exposing raw provider or database errors.
- Report active preparation, retry cooldown and exhausted automatic retries.
  An explicit Prepare request may reopen one attempt after cooldown; background
  retries remain capped. Do not require a database edit to recover.
- Scope review settlement to the requested account during manual preparation.

The existing Android and Windows API clients display these server messages, so
no client rebuild or reinstall is needed. The Next.js development server loads
these changes on subsequent requests.

## Sources and validation limits

Publisher endpoints: https://www.bankingdive.com/feeds/news/,
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/rss/blog.html and
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/rss/pub.html. ECB documents its feeds at
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/home/html/rss.en.html. The browser fetcher recognized
RSS content but cannot render that content type; the new feeds are marked
unverified until observed by runtime feed health.

TypeScript compilation: `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` passed.
No test suite, app launch, live generation, notification or publication was
triggered. No live account data was edited. User acceptance testing remains
with the user. Broader discovery improves the candidate pool; it cannot
guarantee a suitable article or a successful provider response on every run.

````

## Source: reports/ByLine-functional-gap-audit-2026-09-06.md

````text
# ByLine functional gap audit — 6 September 2026

This was a code and workflow audit of the Android and Windows app, its API contracts, stored post states, and background jobs. It was not a hands-on acceptance test. No test suites, AI generations, test notifications, or LinkedIn publications were run during this audit. No account, draft, published post, credentials, or user preferences were reset.

## Changes made

| Area | Gap found | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Write → rewrite | Editing a saved draft then rewriting sent the old database text to the writer. | Rewriting always uses the current composer text. |
| Rewrite → voice | A result could be labelled as matching settings changed after generation started. | The suggestion retains the voice fingerprint from its request. |
| Rewrite → hashtags | Old tags survived rewrites and the suggestion hid the new tags. | The previous fix is retained: preview and accept the rewritten text and tags together. |
| Voice → existing posts | Lowering the voice hashtag count silently trimmed already reviewed posts during save/publication. | Generation uses the selected count; explicitly reviewed existing tags are preserved, within the overall 15-tag limit. |
| Zero hashtags | Changing the voice to zero hid existing tags and their removal controls. | Existing tags stay visible and removable until a rewrite or the author removes them. |
| Final preview | A source link was appended only during publishing. | Text-only source-backed posts now show that link in the final preview; edit length validation includes it. |
| Polish | AI could alter text after the final preview. | Polish produces a suggestion before save/publish. The API also rejects an unreviewed combined polish-and-publish request. |
| Failed publication | A saved draft could lose its identity when a subsequent send failed, making retry create another post. | Save and send are separate steps. The composer retains the saved post identity after failure. |
| Interrupted save | Retrying after losing the server response could create a duplicate draft. | The composer supplies a stable request ID. An additive unique database index reuses the earlier save; conflicting newer content is reported for review. |
| Images | A failed later upload or save discarded knowledge of earlier successful uploads. | Successful uploads remain attached across retries; closing during image selection is handled. |
| Composer navigation | Closing an edited post left it selected when starting a new post. | Closing the composer clears its editing target. |
| Save controls | Repeated taps could open multiple final confirmation sheets. | Save is busy while the final preview is open. |
| Approve / Send now | Reviewed-state validation rejected approved or failed posts even when their contents were unchanged. | Eligible draft, approved, failed and missed posts can be reviewed and retried. Unknown and published states remain protected. |
| My Posts | Only the nearest approved scheduled post was visible. | Other approved scheduled posts remain in the list. |
| Badge | Scheduled drafts could cause unscheduled drafts to be omitted from the count. | The badge counts all pending draft decisions. |
| Status labels | Retained clearance could hide a failed or unconfirmed result behind a green “cleared” label. | Actual failed, missed and unknown states take precedence. “Approved” alone no longer claims a publishing failure. |
| Rescheduling | Past times were accepted; moving a missed post retained a non-runnable status. | A new time must be in the future and returns the post to a draft requiring clearance. Removing a missed/approved schedule returns it to Drafts. |
| Unconfirmed publication | Recovery directed the user to the old web dashboard. | My Posts includes confirmation controls after the user checks LinkedIn. A confirmed non-publication returns an unscheduled draft and does not automatically resend. Resolution is transactional and limited to unknown posts. |
| Background send | A scheduler pass could act on a previously selected post after its schedule or hold changed. | The publish path re-reads eligibility; marking a missed post also checks its current schedule, hold and status. See concurrency limitation below. |
| Voice preview | Hardcoded music tags were displayed for every industry. | The preview uses the writer's returned tags. |
| Settings in flight | A late preview or save response could replace newer voice edits. | Stale previews are discarded; edits made during a save remain staged. |
| Unsaved settings | Back navigation silently lost staged voice, interests and delivery edits. | These pages now ask before discarding unsaved changes. |
| Writing samples | The UI permitted samples beyond the backend's limits, then silently dropped/truncated them. | The editor and API enforce 10 samples, each 80–2400 characters. |
| Timezone | The general settings endpoint stored an invalid timezone before later scheduling failed. | It validates the timezone before updating settings. |
| Optional slots | A native user could add an advanced slot but could not remove the final one. | Users with completed daily-delivery setup can remove all optional advanced slots. |
| Refresh / session | Old refresh responses could overwrite newer state or repopulate state after sign-out. | Refresh revisions reject stale responses; sign-out and expired sessions clear review/composer state and stop notification listeners. |
| Mutation errors | A failed send left the screen showing the pre-send draft state. | Error handling refreshes the saved status before showing the failure. |
| Network failures | Malformed JSON escaped normal error handling; logout and streamed upload reads could wait indefinitely. | These paths now return structured errors or use timeouts. |
| Notification startup | Setup could load before account status, causing registration to be skipped for the whole launch. | The signed-in shell waits for notification preferences and reacts when they arrive or change. |
| Notification test | Any registered device receiving the message made the current device's test look successful. | Android tests target the current registered device token. Windows alerts exclude already-cleared drafts. |
| Archive | Published history stopped at the most recent 20 posts. | Load older posts is available with an authenticated cursor endpoint. Passed-over source articles are clickable. |

## Areas traced without changing their core behavior

- Sign-in, native callback polling, the Windows loopback return, LinkedIn connection and disconnect behavior, and session ownership.
- Onboarding topics, presets, samples, revision-checked generation, sample acceptance, completion, and notification permission. Repeated completion taps are now blocked during permission handling.
- Daily preparation, same-day reuse, source discovery, scoring, writer output, generation leases, retry limits, delivery timing and the notification outbox.
- Scheduled generation, approval versus immediate publication, send claims, definite versus ambiguous failures, pause controls and daily caps.
- Account-owned media, source links, post serialization, mobile/desktop navigation and archives.
- Local launcher and the existing zero-budget billing guard. No billing, provider, deployment or credential configuration was changed.

## Remaining limitations and release work

1. **Acceptance testing remains with you.** Compilation establishes that the code builds; it does not establish that every interaction or platform notification works. Windows/browser return, Android permissions/background delivery, concurrent device edits, image uploads and actual publishing need your device verification.
2. **Concurrency is not fully serialized.** Duplicate send claims are protected and eligibility is rechecked, but post edits/cancellation and claiming a scheduled send are not yet one shared atomic operation. A very narrow edit-versus-send race still requires a dedicated concurrency change and verification before a multi-client production launch.
3. **An interrupted save is deduplicated while its composer remains open.** The new request ID is not a persistent offline draft store across app termination. Check My Posts after a crash before re-creating a post.
4. **Recovery covers recorded unknown results.** A worker that crashes leaving an aged `in_flight` ledger row without changing the post to `unknown` still needs operator recovery; the current app exposes the recorded unknown state.
5. **Google configuration and provider linking remain release work.** Google sign-in exists in code but is not configured in this installation. Google and LinkedIn identities are currently separate accounts; changing sign-in provider does not merge accounts.
6. **Localhost remains the backend.** The computer and server must remain running. Android USB testing still needs ADB reverse after reconnection. Windows notifications require ByLine to remain open or minimized. This audit does not deploy an always-on service.
7. **Some asynchronous failures still need better durable feedback.** An advanced “write one now” cycle can finish without a draft, and exhausted daily preparation retries do not yet have a dedicated user-facing result history. The source rejection history remains a recent window.
8. **Existing image review is limited.** Saved attachments are represented mainly by attachment counts, not a full persistent thumbnail gallery. Upload/retry handling was improved; an image browsing service was not added.

## Suggested acceptance sequence

- Edit a saved draft, rewrite, and verify the edited text is used. Change 7 tags → 2 → 0 and inspect suggestion, composer, saved draft and final preview.
- Enable polish and confirm it shows a suggestion before anything is saved or sent.
- Cancel editing a post, then choose Start a post; it should open a new composer.
- Prepare several scheduled drafts; clear them, change/remove a time, and confirm every post remains visible in the correct state.
- Check a known failed send can be retried. For an actual unknown result, check LinkedIn before using the new confirmation controls.
- Change voice, interests and delivery settings, then press Back without saving. Also try changing voice while a preview is in progress.
- Try a failed upload/save and confirm successful attachments remain. After reconnecting, check My Posts before re-creating work.
- Send a notification test on this phone and check the notification shade. Check Windows while open/minimized and complete browser sign-in.
- With sufficient history, load older published posts and open a passed-over source link.

## Build record

Backend TypeScript compilation, the Android debug APK build, and the Windows release build succeeded. The final Android APK was installed on the connected phone with data preserved and port 3000 forwarded. The latest Windows ZIP replaced ByLine-Windows.zip in Downloads; extract that ZIP to use the new desktop build. Neither app was opened. No test suites or live workflow tests were run.

The new draft request-ID column and unique index are additive schema changes. The existing local schema mechanism applies them when the backend next accesses the database; no manual account onboarding or database reset is needed.

````

````text
# ByLine illustrated workspace

Direction: a calm writing studio, retaining LinkedIn blue, warm white surfaces and dark readable type. Introduce original paper, pen, plant, calendar and conversation illustrations rather than stock photos or decorative statistics.

- Home: illustrated daily state, a useful writing prompt, and a warm profile cover. Existing approval, editing and delivery actions retain their behavior.
- My Posts and Archive: compact editorial headers; illustrations should support empty states without displacing the actual drafts.
- Voice, delivery, interests and composer: one compact contextual introduction per page, with consistent margins and section anchors.
- Welcome and onboarding: the same artwork family, adapted to each setup step.
- Responsive: wide headers have larger artwork; phone headers use compact artwork, and large accessibility text hides decorative art to preserve reading space.
- Assets: local Flutter vector drawing, no network images, no image-generation charges, no fake activity or metrics.
- Packaging: compile Android and Windows, install APK and replace Downloads ZIP. User handles visual and functional acceptance; do not launch apps or run tests.

Implemented: five original vector scenes (writing, voice, ideas, routine, completion), responsive editorial banners, a profile cover, an end-of-day writing prompt, illustrated empty states, matching welcome/onboarding artwork, and a light Windows title bar. All text remains separate from the artwork; decorative drawings are excluded from screen-reader output and hidden from banners at larger text scales.

Behavior: existing callbacks, post data, settings values, permissions, publishing, scheduling and backend routes are unchanged in this design pass. No network artwork or additional dependencies were introduced. The previous functional-audit limitations remain unchanged.

Validation: packaging compilation only. No apps were launched and no automated or hands-on tests were run; visual acceptance remains with the user.
````

````text
# ByLine layout and workflow review — 6 September 2026

## Plan before implementation

1. Give the native app a continuous white workspace with aligned section boundaries. Use one desktop sidebar beside the main workspace; remove the unrelated third-column routine card. Group mobile preferences and daily actions with dividers, tighter spacing, and consistent margins. Keep dropdowns, custom input, accessible contrast, and all existing actions.
2. Put the actionable draft count on My posts on Android and Windows. Keep Home free of that count. Check notification destinations and navigation state as well as the icon.
3. Return desktop browser authentication to the running app using a short-lived loopback listener and a random return path. Keep provider redirect registration unchanged, keep credentials in the verifier-protected API exchange, and handle cancellation/expired callbacks without sending native users to the legacy website. Apply this to initial sign-in and reconnection.
4. Inspect the project by workflow: authentication, onboarding, interests/sources, voice, sample acceptance, daily preparation, scheduling, editing/media, approval/skip/publishing recovery, history, notifications, settings, sessions, persistence, operator setup and budget controls. Exercise safe workflows against the isolated fixture server and inspect real service state read-only. Do not publish to LinkedIn or invoke paid-capable AI during verification.
5. Build Android and Windows, inspect actual rendered interfaces and interaction where available, reinstall Android preserving data, and replace the Windows ZIP in Downloads. Record observed results separately from automated coverage and external checks still requiring the account owner.

## Technical references

- [RFC 8252, loopback interface redirects](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8252.html#section-7.3): temporary listeners on the loopback interface. ByLine uses this only for the browser-to-app return signal; the registered provider callback stays on the backend.
- [Windows foreground activation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setforegroundwindow): Windows can deny focus changes. Restore the app and request foreground activation, with taskbar attention as a fallback.

## Findings and verification

Implementation and verification results will be recorded here as the review proceeds.

````
